The attackers also employed CENotes and LPNotes stealers, gosocks5 reverse tunnels, and advanced techniques such as the CNG Windows cryptographic API. MuddyWater mainly targeted Israeli organisations across various sectors, including engineering, local government, manufacturing, technology, transportation, utilities, and universities, as well as one Egyptian target. The group claimed no responsibility for the incident, but their involvement was confirmed by ESET researchers on 02 December 2025.

On 30 November 2025, unknown threat actors carried out an infinite mint attack on Yearn Finance's yETH product and surreptitiously withdrew around $2.8 million worth of assets, primarily ETH and Liquid Staking Tokens (LSTs), from Balancer liquidity pools. The attacker then laundered some stolen funds, approximately 1,000 ETH, through Tornado Cash. Yearn Finance confirmed the exploitation on the same day, and stated that its V2 and V3 Vaults were unaffected, with the vulnerability only existing in the older yETH application.

Blood Wolf APT targeted organisations in Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan, primarily affecting the finance, government and information technology sectors since at least June 2025, according to a report by Group-IB. The campaign relied heavily on spearphishing emails delivering official-looking PDF documents and links to attacker-controlled domains hosting malicious Java Archive files. When executed, these loaders deployed NetSupport RAT, retrieved follow-on payloads from the attackers’ infrastructure and established persistence through scheduled tasks, Windows Registry modifications and batch scripts. The Uzbekistan phase incorporated geofencing that redirected requests from outside the country to a legitimate website.

Title (Company): Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education - Unnamed External IT Service Provider
Description: Unknown threat actors deployed LockBit 3.0 ransomware against an external server used by the Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education in Gotemba City, Japan, encrypting portions of data and disrupting school operations on 18 November 2025. The affected system, hosted at an offsite data centre, contained personal information on elementary and junior high school students, including names, addresses, dates of birth and parent contact details, as well as event photos and student guidance documents. The infection was discovered when teachers reported being unable to access the school administration system. The server was immediately isolated and operations were restored from backups by 26 November 2025. Authorities, including the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications Cybersecurity Measures Office, the Personal Information Protection Commission and the Shizuoka Prefectural Police, were notified. No ransom demand was issued and no evidence of data leakage has been identified.

Unknown hackers launched a sustained DDoS attack against Turhost, Turkey’s largest domestic hosting provider, beginning on 24 November 2025. The incident rendered Turhost’s infrastructure largely inaccessible for three days, which prevented customers from reaching websites, control panels and support services. The attack, which persisted through 26 November, targeted Turhost’s service and support centres and caused widespread performance degradation despite additional mitigation measures implemented with its data centre partner. The accessibility disruptions resulted in financial losses for ecommerce platforms and other businesses reliant on Turhost’s hosting services.

Title (Company): Vereinigte Stadtwerke - Unnamed External IT Provider
Description: Unidentified perpetrators attempted to breach parts of the IT infrastructure of Vereinigte Stadtwerke (VS), a German municipal utilities provider based in Ratzeburg, in mid-November 2025 by exploiting an unnamed external IT service provider. The intrusion was detected early and stopped by the company’s protection systems and the supply systems for electricity, gas, water, heating and telecommunications, which operate on separate networks, were not affected. However, data from one of approximately 200 internal servers was partially exfiltrated. VS initiated forensic analysis and confirmed no further damage, while an investigation is under way to determine which data was exposed and whether customers are affected.

Unknown threat actors breached the systems of South Korean E-Commerce company Coupang on or around 24 June 2025, leading to the exposure of personal data from approximately 33 million customers. The exposed information included names, phone numbers, email addresses and delivery addresses, but did not involve payment data, credit card numbers or login credentials. Coupang identified the breach on 18 November 2025 and notified the authorities on 19 and 20 November, initially estimating that only around 4,500 customers had been affected. An emergency government meeting chaired by Minister of Science and ICT Bae Kyunghoon was convened on 1 December 2025. Yonhap reported the incident on 30 November 2025 and cited police sources who indicated that at least one suspect, a former Chinese national employee who had already left South Korea, had been identified, though the alleged attacker’s identity and motives remain unconfirmed.

On 11 November 2025, One Solution, a system development company, was infiltrated by unknown threat actors. This incident is a supply chain attack, where the breach at the peripheral part of the contracting structure affected the National Diet Library. The intrusion was detected by the National Diet Library on 11 November 2025, and further details were disclosed on 25 November 2025.

On 27 November 2025, South Korea's top crypto exchange, Upbit, suffered a major security breach, losing approximately 44.5 billion Korean won, about 33.3 million euros, in digital assets, primarily Solana-based tokens. The attack began just hours after its parent company, Dunamu Inc., unveiled a massive 9.3 billion euros takeover by tech giant Naver Corp. The attackers exploited a vulnerability in one of Upbit's Hot Wallets, used for fast, day-to-day transactions. The intrusion forced Upbit to halt all deposits and withdrawals on 27 November 2025. The stolen assets included over 20 tokens, prominently featuring Solana (SOL), USDC, Bonk (BONK), Jupiter (JUP), Render Token (RENDER), Orca (ORCA), and Peace Network (PYTH). Oh Kyoungsuk, CEO of Dunamu, informed the public about the attack on 27 November 2025, expressing his deep regret and reassuring customers that Upbit's assets will be fully covered to prevent any damage. Yonhao News Agency (YNA), the main national newswire of South Korea, reported that unnamed government officials suspect Lazarus, a North Korean state-linked threat actor, to be responsible for the attack.

In September 2025, a Managed Service Provider (MSP) in South Korea was breached, affecting at least 20 South Korean asset management companies. The threat actors, believed to be associated with Qilin, a large ransomware-as-a-service platform, released over 2TB of data on the dark web, combining political and propaganda messages. The breach of the MSP was the initial access vector, and the attack began with the simultaneous release of 10 financial management companies' data, followed by ransomware-focused messages, and finally returning to traditional ransomware messages. On 24 November 2025, the IT security company Bitdefender reported on the campaign discussing the possible involvement of Moonstone Sleet, a North Korean state-affiliated group. Bitdefender based this assessment on Moonstone Sleet's use of Qilin ransomware, first documented in February 2025 by Microsoft.

RomCom threat actors used the SocGholish fake-update loader to deliver Mythic Agent malware to a United States civil engineering firm on or around September 2025. Arctic Wolf Labs, which reported the incident on 25 November 2025, noted that the payload executed about ten minutes after initial exploitation and assessed the attack with medium to high confidence as linked to Russia’s GRU Unit 29155. SocGholish, a fake browser-update framework spread through compromised websites, initiated the infection chain via obfuscated JavaScript and PowerShell reconnaissance before deploying RomCom’s loader disguised as msedge.dll, which executed only when the victim’s Active Directory domain matched a hardcoded value. Arctic Wolf identified seven related command-and-control domains tied to RomCom. The end-to-end timeline from FAKEUPDATE infection to attempted Mythic Agent delivery was under thirty minutes.

Title (Company): Westminster Council  - Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea (RBKC) council
Description: Unknown perpetrators disrupted multiple London councils, including Kensington and Chelsea and Westminster, on 24 November 2025, that may have exposed residents’ data. The Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea (RBKC) said it was working with the National Cyber Security Centre and external specialists to investigate the incident and secure affected systems. Graeme Stewart, head of public sector at Check Point, told Sky News that the attack had taken several boroughs offline and highlighted weaknesses in shared infrastructure.

On 10 November 2024, Albany Gastroenterology Associates (New York, USA) was the victim of a cyber incident in which an unknown and unauthorised party gained access to their systems, gaining access to personal information of clients, including Social Security numbers (SSNs). The unauthorised access was detected on 19 November 2024, while a filing was made on 28 January 2025 with the Attorney General of Vermont.

Around 1 November 2025, INC Ransom targeted the third party emergency alert system of several hundred entities on both state and local government levels through Crisis24's OnSolve CodeRED system, which sends calls, texts, emails, and mobile alerts in the event of emergencies. INC Ransom initially breached OnSolve on 1 November and encrypted data on 10 November, disrupting CodeRED systems and ultimately leading to the temporary disruption of numerous localities' emergency alert services as several municipalities in the United States worked to migrate to new emergency alert systems after the disruption of OnSolve CodeRED. The incident also led to alerting authorities having their access to FEMA's Integrated Public Alert and Warning System revoked.  According to OnSolve/Crisis24 and INC's sample of data published on their Tor leak site, information stolen includes phone numbers, addresses, emails, usernames, and passwords for CodeRED accounts.

At some point shortly before 1 August 2023, Emennet Pasargad, a threat actor on assignment by the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) carried out a data breach against a company operating a "major SMS service" in Sweden; the hackers then sent out roughly 15,000 text messages calling for revenge against Qur'an burners in Sweden, intending to create chaos and division within Swedish society.  As a result of the breach, Swedish authorities opened an investigation and were able to determine the identities of the hackers. Despite initially pursuing legal routes of action, Swedish authorities ultimately dropped the case due to a lack of ability to extradite and/or prosecute the perpetrators outside of Swedish jurisdiction; despite this, Senior Prosecutor Mats Ljungqvist reiterated that, as long as the case is not time-barred, Swedish authorities can reopen the case at any point to pursue legal options. On 16 March 2026, the Council of the EU sanctioned "Emennet Pasargad" for compromising the Swedish SMS service.

On 23 November 2025, a breach notification from Iberia Airlines was posted that confirmed unauthorized access to the systems of one of Iberia's suppliers, which has compromised the confidentiality of certain data. It was found that data such as customer names, email address, or loyalty card identification number may have been compromised, but account login credentials and passwords have not been compromised, nor bank card information. Furthermore, in compliance with applicable regulations, Iberia Airlines notified the relevant authorities of the incident. On 25 November 2025, Everest Ransomware Group claimed to have obtained 430 GB of data, including customer names, contact details, birthdates, travel and booking information, masked card data, and marketing profiles.

On 21 March 2025, unknown threat actors compromised Delta Dental of Virginia, a dental benefits provider offering insurance plans, affecting approximately 146,000 people, including exposure of names, Social Security numbers, ID numbers, and health information. On 23 April 2025, they discovered suspicious activity associated with one email account and immediately initiated an investigation on the matter. Collected evidence showed that emails and attachments may have been accessed between March 21 and April 23, potentially exposing personal data.

On 23 November 2025, unknown threat actors compromised several official WhatsApp groups linked to cabinet ministers, senior government officers, and journalists in the Indian state Telangana by sending a fake SBI Aadhaar update message embedded with a harmful APK file. The malicious APK file allegedly gained remote control of the users' devices, including WhatsApp access, once downloaded and opened. Multiple media groups, ministers' official communication channels, the CMO WhatsApp group, and the Deputy Chief Ministers' group were believed to have come under the hackers' control. The phones of public relations officers and several journalists were also reportedly breached. The Telangana Cyber Crime police initiated verification and containment measures, while cybersecurity experts urged WhatsApp users to avoid interacting with suspicious messages or files and issued precautions such as not installing or opening any APK file received via WhatsApp or SMS, ignoring unsolicited Aadhaar or bank-related update links, enabling two-factor authentication, and reporting unfamiliar or suspicious activity immediately. The breach was reported by various media outlets on 23 November 2025, with screenshots and warnings spreading rapidly online, and the Cyber Crime police were informed about the incident, which is still under investigation.

On 17 November 2025, a DDoS attack from unknown actors temporarily crippled the website of the town of Goslar. According to a statement from the city spokeswoman, the DDoS attack took the city's website offline for "a few hours," but the attack itself was repelled and administrative services of the city remained available.

On 18 November 2025, Harvard University's Alumni Affairs and Development systems were compromised in a voice phishing attack, exposing the personal information of students, alumni, donors, staff, and faculty members, including email addresses, telephone numbers, home and business addresses, event attendance records, donation details, and biographical information. The affected groups included alumni, alumni spouses, partners, and widowswidowers of alumni, donors to Harvard University, parents of current and former students, some current students, and some faculty and staff. The university did not find any evidence that Social Security numbers, passwords, payment card information, or financial info were compromised. Harvard officials informed the public about the attack on 22 November 2025. The university is working with law enforcement and third-party cybersecurity experts to investigate the incident.

On 14 November 2025, Iberia (a Spanish airliner) suffered a cyberattack that leaked personal data of its customers due to unauthorised access to the systems of one of its technological providers. The breach compromised information such as names, surnames, email addresses, contact telephone numbers, and Iberia Club card identification numbers. Iberia immediately activated its security protocol, adopted measures to contain the breach, and notified the competent authorities. The company also informed its customers about the incident through email and recommended exercising extreme caution when faced with suspicious communications.  Following the breach, an unnamed threat actor claimed to hold 77GB of stolen airline data, including technical material on aircraft, maintenance files, and internal documents, which they offered for sale for $150,000, citing the importance of the data for industrial espionage, extortion, or intellectual property theft from China or Russia.

The Tai Hing Group, a Hong Kong-based restaurant chain, was targeted by an unknown entity on or before 19 November 2025, causing disruptions to the use of its application and electronic coupons. The company informed the authorities about the incident and established a team to investigate and enhance the security of its systems. No indication of customer personal data being compromised was found. The Tai Hing group reported the incident to the public on 21 November 2025.

On 21 November 2025, the pro-Ukraine hackivist group Ukrainian Cyber Alliance (UCA) announced on Telegram that they successfully attacked Donbas Post, a Russian-controlled postal operator in occupied eastern Ukraine. The group disrupted the company's corporate network, web platform, and email systems by wiping thousands of devices, including over 1,000 workstations, around 100 virtual machines, and several dozen terabytes of data. Donbas Post confirmed the incident in a statement and said that they restricted access to several services to contain the breach and worked to restore operations.

Title (Company): Government of the State of Coahuila
Description: On 24 November 2025, a group of cybercriminals, allegedly identified as 'Chronus', were targeted the official website of the Government of the State of Coahuila, resulting in the website being down and out of service. The portals of different secretariats, such as Finance and Government, under the domain coahuila.gob.mx, redirected to empty pages, displaying an error message 404 and 'not found' indication. Some systems considered essential, such as “Easy Pay”, used to make vehicle or tax payments, as well as other formalities of the secretariats and the Cadastre, remain in operation, although they operate under an alternate domain.

Title (Company): Attleboro Police Department - City of Attleboro
Description: On 20 November 2025, the city of Attleboro in the US state of Massachusetts suffered a cyberattack that impacted local government and police department IT systems, forcing them offline.  The incident disrupted phone lines and email services, but dispatchers made manual adjustments to ensure emergency calls were responded to without interruption. Cybersecurity experts, federal agencies, and the city's insurance provider were working with the city to resolve the outages.

Unknown threat actors breached Turkish Vodafone Net systems, accessing personal data of subscribers, employees and supplier personnel on 10 January 2026, which was later offered for sale on the Dark Web. The breach, detected on 26 January 2026, is estimated to have affected no more than 321,504 people, with leaked data including names, contact information, customer transaction details, and device information. Vodafone confirmed the incident and infromed the Personal Data Protection Authority (KVKK) about the breach.

On 20 November 2025, Rhysida launched a ransomware attack on the Cleveland County Sheriff's Office in Oklahoma, disrupting parts of the Sheriff's Office's internal computer system. The attack was reported by the Cleveland County Sheriff's Office. Rhysida took credit for the attack and listed the Sheriff's office on its data leak site.

Since 2022, the China-linked group APT24 (aka PITTY PANDA/G0011/Temp.Pittytiger) deployed BADAUDIO malware in a long-running, ongoing cyber-espionage campaign targeting Taiwan through supply chain attacks, according to a Google Threat Intelligence Group report published on 20 November 2025.  The attackers used multiple methods, including spearphishing attacks and injecting malicious JavaScript into legitimate sites, to deliver BADAUDIO malware onto victims' systems. The BADAUDIO downloader collected basic system information, encrypted it using a hardcoded AES key, and sent it as a cookie value with a GET request to fetch the payload, which in some cases was identified as Cobalt Strike Beacon.  In one incident in July 2024, APT24 compromised a Taiwanese digital marketing firm in a supply chain attack, which ultimately impacted over 1000 domains; the firm has reportedly been re-compromised several times since.

Title (Company): Rete Ferroviaria Italiana - Italferr - Almaviva - Trenitalia - Mercitalia - Ferrovie dello Stato
Description: Unknown threat actors breached Almaviva’s systems, which manage core IT functions for Italy's railway company Ferrovie dello Stato (FS) on 20 November 2025 and exfiltrated approximately 2.3 terabytes of internal data. The stolen material reportedly included technical documentation, contracts with public bodies, accounting records and full datasets belonging to multiple FS Group companies. The leak also contained personal data of passengers and personnel across subsidiaries including Mercitalia, Rete Ferroviaria Italiana, Trenitalia and Italferr. The threat actors appeared to possess prior knowledge of the environment and accessed shared folders containing operational and strategic files. The Rome Prosecutor’s Office opened an investigation and assigned the case to Cnaipic, the Postal Police unit responsible for protecting national strategic infrastructures.

The Everest ransomware group breached Brazilian energy company Petrobras on 14 November 2025, stealing a database containing more than 176 gigabytes of seismic navigation data, including over 90 GB belonging directly to Petrobras. The stolen material included detailed technical information such as vessel positioning, equipment configurations, hydrophone readings and depth measurements. The group posted two listings on its dark web leak site referencing Petrobras and partner firm SAExploration, and highlighted data from Petrobras’ Campos Basin seismic surveys, including 3D and 4D data sets. Everest demanded that a Petrobras representative contact them via the encrypted messaging platform Tox within four days.

Title (Company): Local Police of Salamanca - Council of Béjar
Description: On 20 November 2025, a hacker claimed to have obtained internal files from systems of the Council of Béjar in Spain. The Council, led by Mayor Antonio Cámara, began working with the State Administration’s Cybersecurity Operations Centre and the Civil Guard’s Criminal Intelligence Group to investigate the breach. Initial analysis suggested that only a single computer was compromised. The Council’s IT department focused on determining the origin of the irregular access and reviewing all affected equipment, while a formal complaint was prepared.

The municipality of Cabedelo in Brazil was breached by unknown threat actors on 12 November 2025, which affected the headquarters of the Secretariat of Social Assistance (Semas). The municipality of Cabedelo confirmed the incident and stated that no essential service was interrupted due to a swift response.

Inc ransomware group breached the Valley View Independent School District in Pharr in the US state of Texas, disrupting computer systems and phone lines. The district confirmed the incident but did not disclose further details. Classes continued uninterrupted and students. On 29 November 2025, Inc Ransomware claimed responsibility for the attack and said it stole 68 GB of data.

Title (Company): Avelia - Eurafibre - FullSave - Eurofiber France - Netiwan
Description: ByteToBreach exploited a vulnerability in Eurofiber's ticketing system and ATE customer portal to breach the European fiber operator on 13 November 2025, stealing data and attempting extortion. The attackers targeted Eurofiber France and its brands Avelia, Eurafibre, FullSave and Netiwan. The stolen data included SSH private keys, VPN configurations, API keys, cloud access tokens, SQL backups, source code, internal scripts, support tickets, attachments, internal messages, ID scans, screenshots, documentation, network inventories and architecture details. Researchers, including Clment Domingo, reported the incident on X, revealing that the hackers exploited a flaw in the GLPI open-source software, which had been available for update since February 2025. Eurofiber France informed the CNIL and ANSSI and filed a complaint, stating that the incident did not affect customers using services of other Eurofiber entities on platforms located in Belgium, Germany or the Netherlands.

The China-linked threat group Speccom targeted the energy sector in Central Asia in July 2025, with the presumed goal of collecting information about China-funded operations and reducing China's dependence on maritime imports. According to ESET's reporting, the group first used a backdoor called Calarat, which enabled them to deploy tools for follow-on exploitation, including a variant of the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor and the RustVoralix backdoor.

According to a publication on 18 November 2025 by Palo Alto Network's Unit42, Howling Scorpius was observed deploying Akira ransomware against a global data storage and infrastructure company. Howling Scorpius compromised the data storage company through a compromised car dealership website, which hosted a ClickFix-type malware loader disguised as a security captcha. An employee of the data company engaged with the captcha, inadvertently downloading SectopRAT malware onto the data storage company's servers, giving the attackers a foothold. The attackers established a backdoor, conducted reconnaissance, and compromised multiple privileged accounts, eventually deploying Akira ransomware across servers in three separate networks over a period of 42 days.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Between June and September 2025, FamousSparrow (also known as Salt Typhoon), a Chinese state-sponsored APT group, was observed by ESET researchers to be targeting several government entities in Latin America. In July 2025, ESET observed FamousSparrow's SparrowDoors loader and samples on the systems of government entities in Argentina, Guatemala, and Honduras, with ESET's report stating that FamousSparrow likely exploited a ProxyLogon vulnerability.  The following month, ESET detected a compromise of several systems belonging to a governmental entity in Panama, with "clear evidence" that FamousSparrow used atexec-pro, an open-source post-exploitation tool, to move laterally within the network.  FamousSparrow's victims in the campaign documented for Latin America included multiple governmental entities in Argentina, a governmental entity in Ecuador, a governmental entity in Guatemala, multiple governmental entities in Honduras, and a governmental entity in Panama.

Title (Company): Conservative People's Party (Denmark) - Social Democrats - Copenhagen Post - Red-Green Alliance/Unity List (Denmark) - Moderates (Denmark)
Description: A pro-Russian group known as NoName057(16) claimed responsibility for carrying out DDoS attacks on several Danish political parties' websites on the eve of local elections, including those of the Conservatives, the Red-Green Alliance, the Moderates and the ruling Social Democrats on 17 November 2025. The attacks temporarily prevented access to the websites on the eve of the aforementioned elections; the Danish Agency for Society Security confirmed that several websites had become inaccessible due to DDoS attacks and noted that this coincided with a forecast expressed in a security assessment published on 7 November, which stated that the threat of cyberattacks was high and that pro-Russian groups were likely to carry out such attacks. NoName057(16) claimed responsibility for the attack on their social media channels, stating that they had targeted the websites of these Danish political parties; the attacks also targeted other entities, such as the Copenhagen Post.  On 18 December 2025, the Danish Defence Intelligence Service (DDIS) officially attributed the attack to NoName057(16) and linked the group to the Russian state.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Anthropic
Description: Chinese state-sponsored group of hackers, dubbed GTG-1002, manipulated Anthropic's Claude Code model to conduct an AI-orchestrated cyber espionage campaign against 30 entities including major technology corporations, financial institutions, chemical manufacturing companies, and government agencies across multiple countries in mid-September 2025. The attackers bypassed Claude Code's protections by inducing it to believe it was performing regular defensive security activities for a company, allowing the AI to operate without recognising the illicit nature of the tasks performed. The model identified vulnerabilities, generated exploit code, collected credentials, created backdoors, classified stolen data, and prepared intelligence packages ready for use. The human operator tasked instances of Claude Code to operate in groups as autonomous penetration testing orchestrators and agents, with the threat actor able to leverage AI to execute 80-90% of tactical operations independently at physically impossible request rates. In November 2025, Anthropic published a detailed report on the cyber espionage campaign and stated that new measures were already implemented to mitigate such activities in the future.

Unknown threat actors breached Somalia's e-Visa system on 11 November 2025, exposing data of over 35,000 individuals, including many US citizens according to the US embassy in Somalia in a statement on their website on 13 November. The Somali Immigration and Citizenship Authority confirmed the breach on 16 November in a press release. The Government of Somalia set up a national-level investigation team to determine the scope of the incident. The US embassy stated that the breach resulted in the theft of data, icnluding visa applicants' names, photos, dates, and places of birth, email addresses, marital status, and home addresses.

Title (Company): Ministry of Interior (Kenya) - Ministry of Energy (Kenya) - Ministry of Education (Kenya) - Ministry of Water (Kenya) - Ministry of Labour (Kenya) - Ministry of Health (Kenya)
Description: Ahacktivist group defaced multiple ministry websites of the Kenyan government with white supremacist messages on 17 November 2025. The hackers replaced the websites for the ministries of interior, health, education, energy, labour and water, alongside several other government-affiliated platforms, with racist messages. In a press release, the Interior Ministry confirmed the incident, stating that preliminary investigations indicated the activity was suspected to have been carried out by PCP@Kenya. Following the incident, the government activated its incident response and recovery procedures, working closely with relevant stakeholders to mitigate the impact and restore access to the affected platforms.

Ringsted municipality encountered a DDoS attack making its website temporally inaccessible on 16 November 2025. The municipality informed the public about the attack through a press release the following day. The municipality said that the attack had been stopped and that the page is working again as normal. Furthermore, an investigation has been launched.

The French Pajemploi service for private employers was breached on 14 November 2025, resulting in the theft of data related to 1.2 million employees, including social security numbers, dates and places of birth. The URSSAF service, which Pajemploi depends on, discovered the incident and immediately took measures to identify the causes and strengthen protection of their information systems. The URSSAF service is a private entity in charge of public services and supervised by the Ministry for Social Security and by the Ministry for the Budget. The CNIL and ANSSI were notified, and a criminal complaint was filed with the Public Prosecutor's Office on 17 November 2025.

On or around 10 November 2025, unknown threat actors launched a cyberattack against Weda, a medical software platform used by around 85,000 healthcare professionals in France, including general practitioners, specialists, midwives and paramedical staff, to manage patient records.  The incident reportedly affected at least 23,000 users. Weda detected suspicious activity suggesting unauthorised access to certain accounts and took the platform offline as a precaution to prevent data leakage. Initial analyses indicated that partial data extraction may have occurred, though the extent of any breach remained unconfirmed. The incident caused major disruption as doctors were forced to revert to manual record-keeping.

Title (Company): Eastern Cape Department of Human Settlements
Description: The international hacking group NightSpire conducted a ransomware attack against the Eastern Cape Department of Human Settlements on 9 November 2025, compromising data related to applicants and recipients of government housing and forcing a full shutdown of departmental systems. A senior official, speaking anonymously, confirmed the incident the same day, stating that the attackers had penetrated the department’s IT environment and triggered a system-wide halt to operations.

A suspected ransomware attack paralysed the Korean Industrial Health Association’s Hanmaeum Blood Centre on 12 November 2025, disrupting its computer network and suspending blood supply operations, including donation buses. The attackers left a negotiation message on the server referencing donors’ personal information. Police launched an investigation to assess the extent of the damage and any potential data leakage.

On or around 11 November 2025, a cyber attack was carried out by the allegedly Russia-linked ransomware gang "Everest Group," which gained unauthorised access to a peripheral component of one of Italy's main energy providers, Siad Macchine Impianti. While the incident was promptly contained by Siad's internal team, ensuring full operational continuity, the Everest Group claimed to have stolen 159 GB of data and included Siad in the list of victims on their site on the dark web, publishing samples of stolen data to prove their allegations. The attack was reported by industry sites and Siad Macchine Impianti confirmed the incident.

Between July 2022 and July 2023, alleged US state threat actors within the intelligence apparatus conducted a year-long campaign targeting China's defence sector by exploiting a previously unknown zero-day vulnerability in Microsoft Exchange. The attackers seized control of a major military-industrial enterprise's email servers, compromised the firm's central domain controller, and gained access to over 50 internal devices, according to a report from CNCERT. They implanted custom malware for data exfiltration, stealing emails from 11 senior personnel, including high-level executives, containing sensitive intellectual property such as design plans for military products. The threat actors used sophisticated evasion tactics, routing operations through a global network of jump-off points in Germany, Finland, South Korea, and Singapore, and employed multilayer traffic forwarding and encryption to hide communications. According to CNCERT, the threat actors' goal was strategic data theft, resulting in a significant national security loss for China.

On 13 November 2025, the pro-Russian hacker group NoName057 claimed responsibility for a series of DDoS attacks targeting Danish government and defence websites, including the Ministry of Transport, the public sector portal Borger.dk, and the defence company Terma. The Danish Civil Protection Agency stated that it was aware of several companies and websites experiencing disruptions and operational failures due to DDoS attacks and was closely monitoring the situation in coordination with Danish military intelligence. Tobias Brun-Falkencrone, a spokesperson for Terma, confirmed that access to the company's website was disrupted. The attacks followed attacks claimed by NoName057(16) which took place the previous day and coincided with upcoming Danish local elections. On 18 December 2025, the Danish Defence Intelligence Service (DDIS) officially attributed the attack to NoName057(16) and linked the group to the Russian state.

Title (Company): Trnby Kommune - GN Store Nord - Gentofte Kommune - Gyldendal - Rdovre Kommune - Ishj Kommune
Description: The pro-Russian hacktivist group NoName057(16) claimed responsibility for a DDoS attack that disrupted websites of several Danish municipalities, including Gentofte, Rødovre, Ishøj and Tårnby, as well as private companies such as GN Store Nord and Gyldendal on 12 November 2025. The attack caused temporary outages and instability across affected sites. Minister for Societal Safety and Emergency Management Torsten Schack stated that the incident was expected and that further attacks could occur in the days leading up to the municipal and regional elections. On 18 December 2025, the Danish Defence Intelligence Service (DDIS) officially attributed the attack to NoName057(16) and linked the group to the Russian state.

In November 2025, Aleksey Olegovich Volkov, a Russian national, pleaded guilty to aiding the Yanluowang ransomware group by acting as an initial access broker, breaking into the networks of at least eight US-based organisations, including banks, telecommunications companies, and engineering firms in Pennsylvania, California, Michigan, Illinois, Georgia, and Ohio, between 2021 and 2022.  According to the affidavit filed on 28 July 2023, one of the victims, an Ohio-based telecommunications company was targeted and breached on 19 April 2022; it subsequently had its data leaked on 1 July 2022.

On 5 November 2025, Cisco updated a publication from 25 September 2025 related to an ongoing campaign earlier attributed to Chinese state-sponsored threat actors, UAT-4356, in what was dubbed "ArcaneDoor." In its 5 November publication, Cisco stated that it was observing new waves of attacks against Cisco Secure Firewalls targeting unnamed government institutions, specifically through a new attack variant exploiting the previously reported vulnerabilities CVE-2025-20333 and CVE-2025-20362 in Cisco ASA and FTD devices. The attackers exploited these vulnerabilities to gain remote access and control over unpatched systems, potentially obtaining root privileges and installing malware such as RayInitiator and LINE VIPER. While in the US CISA alerted the public of the existence of the ArcaneDoor campaign in September 2025 and in an earlier update on the exploited vulnerabilities in April 2025, Cisco's updated warning about government targets did not specify the countries in which governmental organisations were being targeted. While Cisco confirmed the compromise of several targets that were brought to the attention of Cisco through government incident response agencies assisting the affected organisations, Cisco also stated that the attacks put government and telecommunications infrastructure at broader risk of outages and takeovers, with potentially severe operational and data losses.

In November 2025, Aleksey Olegovich Volkov, a Russian national, pleaded guilty to aiding the Yanluowang ransomware group by acting as an initial access broker, breaking into the networks of at least eight US-based organisations, including banks, telecommunications companies, and engineering firms in Pennsylvania, California, Michigan, Illinois, Georgia, and Ohio, between 2021 and 2022.  According to the affidavit filed on 28 July 2023, one of the victims, a Michigan-based bank targeted on 13 December 2021, had its systems encrypted with Yanluowang ransomware, while Volkov and co-conspirators demanded $15 million in ransom. The bank paid $1 million in bitcoin and received access to its systems as a result. On 23 March 2026, a U.S. federal judge sentenced Aleksey Olegovich Volkov to 81 months in prison for his role as an initial access broker who enabled ransomware announced by the U.S. Department of Justice.

In September 2025, a threat actor, attributed to the North Korean state-sponsored KONNI Group, conducted a sophisticated spear-fishing campaign, infiltrating Android phones and personal computers using malicious software sent via the KakaoTalk messaging app. In some cases, Google Android–based smartphones and tablet PCs were remotely reset by abusing Google's "Find Hub" service, resulting in the unauthorized deletion of personal data stored on the devices. On 5 September 2025, the threat actor compromised and abused the KakaoTalk account of a South Korea–based counsellor who specializes in psychological support for North Korean defector youth, and sent a malicious file disguised as a “stress relief program” to an actual defector student. After gaining initial access, the threat actor conducted prolonged internal reconnaissance and remote monitoring, during which they collected and exfiltrated the victim’s information and key account credentials, ultimately gaining access to Google and Naver accounts. On 15 September, a separate victim’s KakaoTalk account was used to distribute malicious files en masse in a simultaneous wave. The Genians Security Centre (GSC) published a detailed report on 6 November 2025.

On 4 November 2025, hackers from the InformNapalm intelligence community, in collaboration with the Fenix cyber analysis centre, claimed a cyberattack on Russian defence company OKBM and published classified documents related to Russia's future bomber, the PAK DA, and the invisible Su57 fighter jet. The group allegedly infiltrated OKBM's internal systems, gaining deep and prolonged access that was used for months to collect information deemed of interest to Ukraine's defence forces and allied countries.

On 6 November 2025, unusual activities were detected in the municipal data network of Ludwigshafen's city administration. The city administration was subsequently taken offline and could not be reached by telephone, email, or internet as a precautionary measure. An internet forensics firm was engaged, and the investigating authorities were informed.

On 5 November 2025, a Russian hacker group known as Qilin carried out a ransomware attack on Habib Bank AG, a Swiss bank, resulting in the theft of sensitive customer data, including passport numbers, bank account balances, and source codes for internal tools, with approximately 2.5 terabytes of data and almost two million files seized. The attackers claimed responsibility for the incident on 5 November 2025, by publishing screenshots of stolen files on their website. Habib Bank AG confirmed the 'unauthorised external access' to their company network and stated that their banking services were not affected. A team, supported by cybersecurity experts, was working to determine the impact of the incident, and the bank informed relevant regulatory authorities.

On 6 November 2025, pro-Russian hacktivists NoName057(16) carried out a DDoS attack on several websites of the Belgian military intelligence service, ADIV. The attackers claimed responsibility for the attack via Telegram, referencing an interview with Belgian Defence Minister Theo Francken, where he stated that NATO would flatten Moscow if Russia attacked Brussels. The attack resulted in the temporary unavailability of the ADIV website. The attack was confirmed by a Defence Ministry spokesperson.

In October 2025, an attacker gained limited access to Haileybury College's network in Australia. The school contained the breach once the intrusion was discovered and isolated the affected systems, said Derek Scott, CEO and principal of the school, in a statement on 31 October.

On 4 October 2025, an unknown threat actor used valid credentials to breach Mino Industry's intranet via an employee's VPN account, resulting in a ransomware attack that compromised approximately 300GB of customer and personal information. The attacker gained system administrator privileges, exfiltrated data, destroyed the system, and encrypted the data, leaving behind a ransom demand. Mino Industry reported the incident to the responsible authorities, shut down its systems, and conducted a forensic investigation with an external expert. The company confirmed that the leaked information was available on the dark web on 28 October, but the related site was closed on the next day.

In July 2025, Curly COMrades, a group linked to Russian interests, utilized Windows Hyper-V to evade Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) tools and deploy custom malware undetected. The attackers created hidden Alpine Linux virtual machines (VMs) hosting custom tools like CurlyShell and CurlCat, which were used to bypass traditional host-based EDR detections. Bitdefender researchers, aided by Georgia's CERT, uncovered the attack, published in a report on 4 November 2025.  Georgia's CERT supported Bitdefender by seizing a compromised server, which was important for forensic analysis. Bitdefender assessed that the used techniques are suitable to establish covert, long-term access to victim networks.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Between April and September 2025, Russian state-sponsored hacking group Sandworm, which is linked to Russia's military intelligence service (GRU), deployed multiple versions of data-wiping malware against numerous targets in Ukraine according to the APT Activity Report published by ESET in November 2025. In April, Sandworm launched two different types of wipers against a Ukrainian university. In June and September, Sandworm deployed multiple data-wiping malware variants against Ukrainian entities active in the governmental, energy, logistics, and grain sectors.

On 6 November 2025, a federal agency, the Congressional Budget Office (CBO), which provides budget and economic information to Congress, was breached by suspected Chinese state-backed hackers. The attackers potentially accessed communications between lawmakers and researchers at the agency. The CBO spokesperson, Caitlin Emma, acknowledged the incident after it was reported by The Washington Post. The agency took immediate action to contain the incident and implemented additional monitoring and new security controls to protect its systems. Officials believed they caught the intrusion early, and an investigation was underway. US officials briefed on the hack told CNN that Chinese state-backed hackers are suspected of being behind the breach.

On 1 November 2025, hackers allegedly linked to Russia launched a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack on Poland's payment infrastructure, briefly disrupting Blik, the country's leading mobile payment system used for instant transfers and cash withdrawals. Deputy Prime Minister and Digital Affairs Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski was the first to link the incident to Russia, stating that "all strings lead to Russia" and emphasising the frequency of which Poland is targeted in cyber attacks, declaring that "This is the next stage of hybrid warfare." Blik informed the public about the incident on Monday, 3 November 2025, stating that services had been restored after temporary problems with processing payments.

On 4 November 2025, the Akira ransomware group compromised a US subsidiary of the Swiss defence company RUAG MRO Holding Ltd. in Virginia. The attack targeted the liaison office, which employs eight people and is responsible for exchanges with American institutions, suppliers, and partner companies. The Akira ransomware group claimed responsibility for the incident and threatened to publish 24 gigabytes of company data, including confidential military information, contracts, and agreements. The company stated that due to the self-sufficiency of the IT systems used there, the incident is isolated and has no impact on other systems within the RUAG Group. Moreover, no particularly sensitive data relating to employees in Switzerland has been affected. On 8 June 2026, Ruag Board President Jürg Rötheli acknowledged to the public broadcaster SRF that a ransom was paid.

On 31 October 2025, cybercriminals hacked SuperGrosz, a Polish online loan platform operated by AIQLABS, stealing personal data of at least 10,000 customers, including names, addresses, ID and tax numbers, phone contacts, employment details, and bank account numbers. The company confirmed the breach and warned that the group could potentially leak some of the data online. The company confirmed that it notified the Polish Financial Supervision Authority (KNF) CSIRT, NASK CSIRT, and the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (UODO).

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Since at least September 2025, China-linked APT Mustang Panda (UNC6384) has been observed conducting an espionage campaign against European diplomatic entities, primarily in Hungary and Belgium but also in Serbia, Italy and the Netherlands. According to Arctic Wolf Labs, the operation used spearphishing emails with lures themed around European Commission meetings, NATO workshops and multilateral coordination to deliver malicious files that exploited Windows vulnerability ZDI-CAN-25373 to deploy malware. The campaign remains ongoing and is assessed as focused on intelligence collection against the broader European diplomatic community.

An unidentified perpetrator exploited a vulnerability in the Balancer V2 protocol, causing a loss of over $120 Million on 3 November 2025. According to GoPlus Security, the Balancer V2 exploit stemmed from a precision rounding error in the Vault’s swap calculations. However, other users claiming an improper authorization and callback handling inside Balancer’s V2 vaults were the root cause for the hack. Balancer confirmed that an exploit affected Balancer V2 Composable Stable Pools and reported working on the incident.

Unknown threat actors compromised Garden Finance, a Bitcoin bridge protocol, on 30 October 2025 by exploiting one of its solvers, resulting in the theft of approximately US$11 million in digital assets. Garden Finance stated that the incident was limited to the solver’s inventory and that user funds remained unaffected, though it temporarily shut down its application to investigate. Blockchain investigator ZachXBT reported that affected assets straddled several blockchains and shared a message allegedly from Garden Finance, offering the attackers a 10% bounty for returning the stolen funds and explaining the exploit. The message suggested that the compromised solver may have been operated internally rather than autonomously. Garden’s co-founder, Jaz Gulati, confirmed that the company was working with external security experts to identify the root cause and strengthen protocol resilience.

Title (Company): University Hospital of Ghent - Telenet - Proximus - Scarlet
Description: On 05 November 2025, pro-Russian hackivist group NoName057(16) carried out a DDoS attack on the websites of Belgian telecom operators Scarlet and Proximus, as well as an internet portal of Telenet. NoName057(16) claimed responsibility for the attack on Telegram. The attack caused the websites to be temporarily disrupted for a few hours, but customer services remained available throughout. Both companies confirmed the attack and said that their systems withstood the attack and the impact was limited.

An unknown threat actor comprised the Florida-based healthcare provider Oglethorpe that operates in-patient mental health and addiction recovery treatment facilities in three states and exfiltrated sensitive information of more than 92,000 patients on 15 May 2025. The attacker had access to first and last name of patients, date of birth, driving licence number, Social Security number and medical information. The company discovered the intrusion on 6 June and reported the security incident to the Maine attorney general on 31 October 2025.

Point Lonsdale Medical Group (PLMG), a medical centre based in Victoria, Australia, experienced a cyber incident on or around 30 October 2025 after unauthorised access was gained to one of its email accounts, which was discovered when phishing emails were sent from the compromised account. The centre took immediate containment and remediation measures and notified affected recipients. While PLMG confirmed that its internal systems and patient database were not breached, a limited number of emails in the compromised mailbox were accessed, potentially exposing personal information such as names, dates of birth, addresses, medical histories, diagnoses and treatment plans.

A hacktivist group calling itself the Cyber Support Front claimed responsibility for an intrusion targeting Israeli defence contractor Maya on or around 27 October 2025. The group alleged to have stolen classified data on several advanced weapons systems, including technical information on Israel’s Iron Beam laser defence system, as well as on the Skylark reconnaissance drone, Spider air defence system and Icebreaker stealth cruise missile. The threat actors released a video purporting to show the breach and published images of Israeli military products and documents, including alleged contracts between the Israel Defense Forces, Australia and several European countries, on their Telegram channel. In early November 2025, the group posted plans for Australia's new $7 billion Redback infantry fighting vehicles online.

On an unspecified date in April 2025, a Chinese state-sponsored APT known as Tick (aka Bronze Butler, Daserf, REDBALDKNIGHT, Stalker Panda, Stalker Taurus, and Swirl Typhoon) exploited a zero-day vulnerability in Motex Lanscope Endpoint Manager, tracked as CVE-2025-61932, to hijack the systems of corporate victims "in sectors aligned with their intelligence objectives," according to a report on the activity published by Sophos Threat Intelligence.  Tick used the vulnerability to execute arbitrary commands with SYSTEM privileges on on-premise versions of the program and dropped a backdoor, known as Gokcpdoor, which established a proxy connection with a remote server and acted as a backdoor to execute malicious commands on the compromised host(s). The attack was characterised by the deployment of the Havoc post-exploitation framework, DLL sideloading, and the use of various tools such as goddi, Remote Desktop, 7-Zip, io, LimeWire, and Piping Server to facilitate lateral movement and data exfiltration. JPCERTCC and Sophos reported the attack, with Sophos detecting two different types of Gokcpdoor and observing the exploitation of CVE-2025-61932.
Techniques Used: Automated Exfiltration, Exploit Public-Facing Application, Valid Accounts

Description: The University of Pennsylvania (UPenn) in Philadelphia, PA, United States, experienced a cybersecurity incident on 30 October 2025 in which an unknown actor gained unauthorised access to several university email accounts, including those belonging to the Penn Graduate School of Education and UPenn staff. The compromised accounts were used to send offensive messages to students and alumni with the subject line “We got hacked (Action Required),” claiming data theft and criticising the university’s security and admissions policies. BleepingComputer, which reviewed one of the emails, reported that it contained highly offensive content. A UPenn spokesperson confirmed awareness of the incident and stated that the university’s incident response team was addressing it, describing the emails as “obviously fake.”

On 2 November 2025, the website of the city of Trier was targeted by a large-scale DDoS attack, which crippled its public online presence, including the website trier.de and other municipal websites for multiple days. The city confirmed the attack and said that IT systems, email traffic and digital services remained stable. The city worked with an external IT service provider to restore the pages.

TTPs linked to the Chinese state-affiliated APT groups Space Pirates, Kelp (also tracked as Salt Typhoon), and APT41 were observed in malicious activities targeting US policy-focused organisations in a campaign reported by Symantec on 6 November 2025. In one incident detected in April 2025, threat actors gained access to a non-profit organisation, aiming to establish a persistent and stealthy presence on the network. They used techniques previously documented for the Space Pirates group, including DLL sideloading via vetysafe.exe and leveraged Imjpuexc, a Microsoft file for East Asian input, to mask activity.

On 4 November 2025, the Medical Care Centre Nordoberpfalz (MVZ), specifically its sites in Tirschenreuth and Kemnath, was targeted with unspecified malware. The MVZ temporarily closed these two sites and suspended business operations as a precautionary measure, disconnecting all systems from the network. The clinics were not affected, and operations at the MVZ site in Weiden continued. A rescue team analysed the potential damage, and the MVZ was in close contact with the criminal police. The sites in Tirschenreuth and Kemnath remained closed until at least the end of the week, with all operations cancelled for that week.

Unknown threat actors carried out a cyber attack against Jennings O'Donovan, a consulting engineering company based in Ireland, which worked on a programme to aid individuals whose homes are in a process of deteriorating, in late October 2025,  According to Jennings O'Donovan, the incident involved "temporary unauthorised access to a limited part of our IT system," while the Irish government's Housing Agency warned that personal data, including addresses and contact information, could have been compromised within the course of the incident.

An unattributed hacker compromised Typus Finance, a cryptocurrency platform, in an oracle manipulation incident that allowed them to withdraw approximately $3.4 million in tokens from liquidity pools. The breach exploited a vulnerability in one of the platform's TLP contracts and caused the project’s native token to drop by around 35%.

In December 2024, an unknown nation-state actor gained initial access to the IT network of Ribbon Communications, a major telecom services provider to the US government and telecom companies worldwide. The intrusion was detected in early September 2025 and the unauthorized access of the threat actor was terminated. An investigation revealed that the attackers had gained access to files belonging to several customers stored on two laptops outside of Ribbon's main network. Ribbon disclosed the breach in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on 23 October 2025. The company is working with third-party cybersecurity experts and federal law enforcement to investigate the breach, and has yet to find evidence that the attackers accessed or stole any material information.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: In October 2025, unnamed hacktivists internet-accessible industrial control systems in Canada, including a water facility, where they tampered with water pressure values, resulting in degraded service for its community. They also targeted a Canadian oil and gas company, manipulating an Automated Tank Gauge (ATG) and triggering false alarms. Additionally, a grain drying silo on a Canadian farm was compromised, with temperature and humidity levels being manipulated, potentially creating unsafe conditions if not addressed promptly. The incidents were reported by Canadian Centre for Cyber Security without further details on 29 October 2025.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Unknown threat actors conducted a cyber espionage campaign named PassiveNeuron that targeted Windows servers of government, financial and industrial organisations across Asia, Africa and Latin America between December 2024 and August 2025. The attackers used three main tools: Neursite, a modular backdoor; NeuralExecutor, a .NET based framework; and Cobalt Strike to collect system information, manage processes, redirect network traffic and deploy additional payloads. Kaspersky’s Global Research and Analysis Team (GReAT) discovered this campaign and reported that the operators may have planted false clues including Cyrillic characters in code to confuse attribution efforts.

Sweden’s power grid operator, Svenska kraftnät, confirmed a data breach after a ransomware group, known as Everest, claimed responsibility for the attack on 26 October 2025 and threatened to leak hundreds of gigabytes of purportedly stolen internal data the day before. The incident affected a limited external file transfer solution and did not disrupt Sweden’s power supply. Chief Information Security Officer Cem Göcgören informed the public about the incident, stating that the company took immediate action and was working closely with the police and national cybersecurity authorities to determine the extent of the breach. The ransomware gang claimed to have exfiltrated about 280 gigabytes of data and said it would publish it unless the agency complied with its demands. In a press release from 6 November, Svenska kraftnät acknowledged that a small portion of exfiltrated data contained classified information related to electrical systems and contact details.

The City of Gloversville, New York, was hit by a ransomware attack in March 2025. The breach was detected on 14 March 2025 through a digital ransom note by the attackers. According to city officials, the incident compromised the personal information of current and former city employees, including payroll records, direct-deposit account numbers, and other internal data. The city reported the breach to the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the New York State Police and the U.S. Department of Homeland Security Incident Response Team, and retained external cybersecurity and legal advisors to assist in negotiations and recovery. The threat actor reportedly demanded €279,000 (US$300,000), but the city council approved a payment of €138,500 (US$150,000) in exchange for the return of the stolen data and decryption of affected systems. The investigation remains ongoing, with law-enforcement tracing the transaction and pursuing the ransomware perpetrators, believed to operate from Eastern Europe. The City of Gloversville disclosed the incident to the public on 25 October 2025.

An unidentified actor breached Ravin Academy, a cyber training centre linked to Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS), exposing personal data of over 1,000 individuals enrolled in its technical programmes on or around 22 October 2025. The academy, established by MOIS affiliates Seyed Mojtaba Mostafavi and Farzin Karimi and sanctioned by the US in 2022, confirmed the breach in a Telegram post, stating that usernames and phone numbers from a student database were compromised. Ravin Academy described the incident as an attempt to undermine Iran’s security ahead of its National Tech Olympiad, while UK-based activist Nariman Gharib reported that the leaked dataset had been made searchable online.

Unknown threat actors compromised systems of Kaufman County, TX in the United States on 20 October 2025. The attackers disabled multiple county systems including computers at the county courthouse. The incident, affecting a jurisdiction of nearly 200,000 residents, forced county officials to notify state and federal agencies while maintaining operation of the Sheriff's Office and emergency services. County Judge Jakie Allen confirmed the incident on 20 October. The FBI and state agencies engaged in incident investigation and recovery operations.

China-linked groups Glowworm (also tracked as FamousSparrow and Earth Estries) and Emissary Panda (aka UNC5221) exploited the ToolShell SharePoint vulnerability (CVE-2025-53770) shortly after its patch release in July 2025 to compromise a telecommunications company in the Middle East. The incident began on 21 July 2025 and involved webshell deployment, DLL sideloading, and the use of custom and publicly available tools. The threat actors installed backdoors including Zingdoor and ShadowPad, as well as the Rust-based KrustyLoader, to execute commands, exfiltrate data, and extract credentials. Broadcom’s Symantec Threat Hunter Team attributed the intrusion to China-based espionage activity and further noted overlaps with other campaigns exploiting the same flaw.

Title (Company): Unspecified Baby Food Manufacturer  - Unspecified Dairy Producers - Rosselkhoznadzor
Description: The Russian Federal Service for Veterinary and Phytosanitary Supervision (Rosselkhoznadzor) experienced a DDoS incident on 22 October 2025 that disrupted key information systems, including VetIS and Saturn, which are used to monitor the movement of agricultural products and chemicals. The disruption affected the Mercury electronic veterinary certification platform. According to Russian trade outlet Shopper’s, two major dairy producers and a baby food manufacturer were unable to dispatch goods for several hours due to the system’s unavailability. Industry representatives reported financial losses caused by the lack of a contingency procedure allowing shipments without digital certification. The agency reported that normal operations resumed later the same day.

On 19 October 2025, Japanese e-commerce and logistics platform Askul announced that it had suspended ordering and shipping operations due to a ransomware attack on its website. System failure occurred due to the ransomware infection, forcing the company to cancel orders and suspend shipping operations, as well as other services. On 30 October, the ransomware group RansomHouse claimed to have exfiltrated and encrypted 1.1 terabytes of data from Askul. On 31 October, the company confirmed data theft affecting customer and product supplier data. This included company names, the names of the persons in charge, email addresses, registered phone numbers and details of enquiries. On 30 July 2026, Askul announced that the names, addresses, telephone numbers, and e-mail addresses of approximately 600,000 people may have been leaked.

The hacking group Cavalry Werewolf (also tracked as YoroTrooper, Silent Lynx, and others) launched a campaign targeting Russia's public sector and key industries, including energy, mining, and manufacturing between May and August 2025. The campaign was made public by the Turkish cybersecurity firm Picus Security in a report published on 20 October 2025. Cavalry Werewolf's primary method of initial access involves spear-phishing emails disguised as official correspondence from legitimate Kyrgyz government officials, but there is evidence that they may have also used compromised real official email accounts for their operations. The phishing emails carry a RAR archive containing the custom malware, including the FoalShell reverse shell and the StallionRAT remote access trojan.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: The North Korea-aligned Lazarus group (also known as HIDDEN COBRA) targeted several European companies active in the defence industry, which some of them heavily involved in the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) sector in an advanced fishing campaign since March 2025. On 23 October 2025, ESET published a report, where they confirmed the successful intrusion for at least three companies based on telemetry data: a metal engineering company in Southeastern Europe, a manufacturer of aircraft components as well as a defence company in Central Europe. Lazarus relies on the social-engineering technique used for initial access, trojanizing open-source projects from GitHub, and the deployment of ScoringMathTea. ESET assessed these attacks to be part of the Operation DreamJob campaign. The suspected primary goal of the threat actors was likely the theft of proprietary information and manufacturing know-how. In August 2026, Check Point researchers disclosed the latest wave of attacks within Operation Dream Job which targeted defense sectors in several specifically-named countries, including France, Germany, Brazil, and India. In this latest phase, the attackers distributed a modified PDF viewer designed to open malicious PDF documents and execute a new backdoor called Troy.

An unidentified actor exploited a flaw in BetterBank’s reward logic between 26 and 27 August 2025, using a counterfeit liquidity pool to generate unlimited value due to insufficient validation. BetterBank, a decentralised finance (DeFi) protocol operating on the PulseChain network, lost approximately $5 million in digital assets, of which around $2.7 million was later returned following on-chain negotiations, leaving a net loss of roughly $1.4 million. The vulnerability had been identified in a prior Zokyo security audit just a month prior but was downgraded in severity and left unpatched, which enabled the compromise.

A convict at Romania's Târgu Jiu Penitentiary compromised the national prisoner management platform between August and October 2025, gaining unauthorised access to sensitive data including sentences, visitation records and inmate rights. The breach originated at the Dej Prison Hospital, where an inmate exploited vulnerabilities in tablets and kiosks provided for prisoners to access the National Penitentiary Administration (ANP) system. By manipulating the kiosk interface, the perpetrator escaped the ANP application's sandbox and accessed a networked printer's login page, obtaining administrator credentials belonging to a former director of the Dej complex. The attacker, identified as inmate Aurel Z., transferred the method to Târgu Jiu Prison after relocation in July. Using the stolen credentials, he granted inmates access to adult content, altered financial balances and modified sentence reduction records. He inflated balances in at least fifteen accounts, including one exceeding €1.15 million, and spent approximately €2,300 monthly. The breach involved over 300 hours of undetected administrative access and affected facilities in Timișoara and Pelendava. CEC Bank then discovered the irregularities through transaction discrepancies.

Title (Company): National Time Service Center of China
Description: Between March 2022 and June 2024, the US National Security Agency (NSA) allegedly infiltrated China's National Time Service Center, which provides high-precision time synchronization ensuring the coordinated functioning of systems underlying the operation of financial institutions, train traffic, and power grids. The NSA reportedly first gained access by exploiting vulnerabilities in the messaging function of an unnamed foreign mobile phone brand that made it possible to steal login credentials from employees of the Center. In a statement issued on 19 October 2025, China's Ministry of State Security claimed to have 'irrefutable evidence' tieing the NSA to the breach. Based on this account, the malicious activities were directed through virtual private servers in the US, Europe, and Asia in an effort to conceal their origin.  In what appeared to be an operational shift, between August 2023 and June 2024, MSS observations note the deployment of an additional suite of capabilities purportedly designed to pre-position means to "disable and sabotage" the High-Accurate Ground-based Time Service System that functions as an equivalent to satellite-supported synchronization systems. On the day of the MSS revelations, 19 October, CNCERT published a report to support these findings, outlining the use of 42 tools identified as part of the operation. The Chinese authorities claimed to have since 'cut off attack chains, upgraded protection measures, and eliminated potential risks'.

On 20 October 2025, safepay launched a ransomware attack on the Municipality of Untereisesheim, resulting in blocked access to data and systems, except for the telephone system. The perpetrators demanded a ransom for restoring access to encrypted or blocked data and threatened to publish previously stolen information. The attack severely restricted the administration's ability to perform its public duties. Investigations were ongoing by the Baden-Württemberg state cyber security agency and the state criminal police office. The municipality informed the public about the incident through a press release on 20 October 2025. On 5 December 2025, the safepay claimed responsibility for the attack on their dark net site.

On 13 October 2025, a North Central Massachusetts nonprofit healthcare system was breached by Sinobi. The intrusion affected the IT systems of Heywood Hospital and Athol Hospital, resulting in the diversion of ambulance patients and the limitation of radiology and laboratory services. Email and phone services were also disrupted. On 9 November 2025, Sinobi claimed responsibility for the attack on their dark net site.

Title (Company): Red Cross - Local administrations - UNICEF - Ukrainian President's Office
Description: A coordinated spearphishing campaign, dubbed *PhantomCaptcha*, targeted Ukrainian war relief organisations, including the International Committee of the Red Cross, UNICEF and regional administrations in October 2025. The threat actors impersonated the Ukrainian President’s Office in emails containing weaponised PDF attachments that redirected victims to a fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA page, prompting the execution of a three-stage PowerShell payload. The payload deployed a WebSocket-based remote access trojan (RAT) capable of executing arbitrary commands, exfiltrating data and delivering additional malware. The campaign used a multistage attack chain designed to exploit user trust and evade conventional security measures. SentinelOne researchers uncovered the operation on 8 October and publicly reported it on 22 October 2025. The campaign was later linked to a related operation distributing spyware through adult-themed Android APKs and fake cloud storage tools targeting users in Lviv, Ukraine.

Since July 2025, Chinese state-sponsored hacking group Salt Typhoon infiltrated a European telecommunications organization. Darktrace disclosed in a report published on 20 October 2025 that the activities involved advanced methods such as DLL sideloading to infiltrate systems while avoiding standard detection measures. Darktrace attributes the observed activities with medium confidence to Salt Typhoon. The intrusion likely began in July 2025 by exploiting a Citrix NetScaler Gateway vulnerability (CVE-2025-5777), before pivoting to Citrix Virtual Delivery Agent hosts. The hackers used living-off-the-land techniques, deploying native tools, and uploaded antivirus executable files to execute payloads via DLL sideloading. A backdoor was inserted into the telecom infrastructure, using virtual private servers for command and control over HTTP and an unidentified TCP-based control.

On 18 October 2025, the Centre Hospitalier Intercommunal de Haute-Comté (CHIHC) in Pontarlier was targeted by ransomware, which led to the encryption of part of its computer data. As a precautionary measure, the hospital's entire computer system was shut down to prevent any spread, but the hospital is operating normal. The hospital's management, in liaison with the National Agency for Digital Health (ANS), the Bourgogne-Franche-Comt Regional Health Agency, and the National Agency for the Security of Information Systems (ANSSI), analysed the extent of the incident. CHIHC informed the public about the event through a statement on 19 October 2025.

Title (Company): Royal Air Force (RAF) - UK Ministry of Defence - Dodd Group - Royal Navy
Description: On 23 September 2025, Russian cybercrime group Lynx breached Dodd Group, a subcontracting firm for the UK Ministry of Defence. The attackers gained temporary access to the company's internal systems and stole hundreds of sensitive files, including details of eight Royal Air Force (RAF) and Royal Navy bases, such as RAF Lakenheath, Portreath, and Predannack, as well as names, email addresses, phone numbers, car registrations, and other personal data of Ministry of Defence staff members and contractors with some documents labeled “Controlled” or “Official Sensitive.” The stolen data was published on the dark web. A Dodd Group spokesman confirmed the data breach, stating that only limited data had been stolen, and the company had secured and recovered its systems. A Ministry of Defence spokesperson said that they were investigating the alleged leak.

The Shelbyville Police Department in Tennessee, United States, experienced a cyber incident on 15 October 2025 that disrupted its computer systems. An investigation was initiated to determine the cause and scope of the incident. While systems for filing accident and incident reports remained functional, the department informed the public of potential delays as restoration efforts progressed.

The town hall of Ville-Elne in France and a company in Perpignan were targeted by the Qilin ransomware group on 4 and 5 October 2025. The threat actors, claimed responsibility for the incident, which disrupted the internal computer systems of the Ville-Elne municipality, including essential software.  Mayor Nicolas Garcia stated that municipal services were disrupted for a week but were nearly back to normal by 15 October, with no major data loss due to existing backups.

On 2 September 2025, unknown threat actors breached the systems of financial services company Prosper, a peer-to-peer lending marketplace, stealing personal information Social Security numbers, names, government-issued IDs, employment status, credit status, income levels, dates of birth, physical addresses, IP addresses. On 16 October, 'Have I Been Pwned' revealed that at least 17.6 million unique email addresses were affected, which has been confirmed by Prosper.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Between January and July 2025, China-linked APT group Jewelbug (aka REF7707, CL-STA-0049, Earth Alux) targeted a Russian IT service provider, as well as a South American government agency, a Taiwanese software firm, and an IT service provider in South Asia. The group remained in the network of the Russian IT service provider for five months, showing a prolonged, stealthy operation. During the attacks, the threat actor accessed code repositories and build systems, potentially enabling supply chain attacks, and exfiltrated data to Yandex Cloud to evade detection. The attackers performed credential dumping, established persistence via scheduled tasks, and cleared Windows Event Logs to hide traces. Symantec researchers reported the attack on 15 October 2025.

In August 2025, North Korean state-affiliated threat actor Famous Chollima were observed targeting a Sri Lankan organization, published in a report by Cisco Thalos on 16 October 2025. The organization was not deliberately targeted by the attackers, but it had one of the systems on the network infected, because a user was deceived by a fake job offer and installed a trojanized Node.js application called "Chessfi".  Typically, the Famous Chollima uses evasive techniques to steal data and cryptocurrency by duping jobseekers into installing malicious code on their devices. In the attack on the organization, the threat actor utilised BeaverTail and OtterCookie malware strains, which were observed to have merged and displayed new functionality in recent campaigns, including a previously undocumented keylogging and screenshotting module.
