The hackers accused Nobitex of facilitating sanction evasion and supporting the Iranian regime’s financing of terrorist organisations. On 19 June, the group move to publish the exchange’s source code and internal data. Nobitex acknowledged the breach on X, stating it had taken its website and app offline to assess the extent of the compromise. Blockchain analysis firms, including Elliptic and Chainalysis, confirmed the destruction of the funds and noted that some wallet addresses featured anti-IRGC messages.

Title (Company): Ministry of Defense (Thailand) - Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Thailand) - Bangkok Metropolitan Administration
Description: Between 28 May and 10 June 2025, a Cambodian hacktivist group known as AnonsecKh, also referred to as Bl4ckCyb3r on Telegram, launched at least 73 cyberattacks against Thai organizations. The attacks were primarily DDoS campaigns and defacement, targeting mostly Thai government or military websites, including the Ministry of Defense, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration, as well as manufacturing companies. Radware reported these incidents following a skirmish between Cambodian and Thai forces on 28 May, which resulted in the death of a Cambodian soldier.

Episource, LLC, a healthcare technology and solutions provider, was breached by an unauthorized party between 27 January and 6 February 2025, resulting in the exfiltration of protected health information, including names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, health insurance details, medical information, Social Security numbers, and birthdates, affecting approximately 5.4 million patients. The incident was discovered on 6 February 2025 due to anomalous activity, prompting Episource to shut down systems, initiate an investigation, and notify law enforcement. On 6 June 2025, Episource notified the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) about the breach.

Russian cybersecurity researchers detected the first domestic SuperCard malware attacks in May 2025, which involved a modified version of legitimate near field communication (NFC) software to steal bank data. The attackers, reportedly Chinese-speaking actors, used social engineering techniques to trick victims into downloading the malware, disguising it as a legitimate app. Once installed, the malware identified the payment system used by the victim and allowed criminals to exploit the data for fraudulent transactions. F6, a Moscow-based cybersecurity firm, reported on 17 June 2025 that the total losses from NFCGate variants in Russia amounted to 432 million rubles (approximately 5.5 million USD) in the first quarter of 2025, with over 175,000 Android devices infected. The malware was first spotted in Italy in April 2025 and was reported by Italian security company Cleafy.

Title (Company): Military and Police Criminal Justice Department (Colombia)
Description: On 15 June 2025, network infrastructure of Colombia's Military and Police Criminal Justice Department was compromised. In the course of the breach, perpetrators hijacked public information related to network services and communications, as well as administrative and jurisdictional data. Digital services were temporarily suspended, and judicial proceedings under Act No. 1407 of 2010 were suspended until further notice.

On 17 June 2025, the hacker group Predatory Sparrow, also known as Gonjeshke Darande, conducted a disruptive operation against Bank Sepah, one of Iran's leading public banks. The attack, which occurred during a military escalation between Iran and Israel, targeted the bank's infrastructure, causing disruptions to its online services and disabling ATMs across the country. The hackers claimed responsibility for the attack on social media, stating that they had destroyed all the bank's data in a coordinated attack. The group accused Bank Sepah of circumventing international sanctions and financing Iran's nuclear and missile programs. The Central Bank of Iran denied that the banking system had been affected, but widespread reports suggested otherwise. Overlapping strategic interests as well as the group's advanced capabilities and observed concern for proportionality in its disruptive operations have led to speculations that the group is associated with Israeli intelligence services.

Title (Company): NKS Superspeciality Hospital - Parmanand Multi-Superspeciality Hospital
Description: Between 10 and 11 June 2025, two hospitals in North Delhi, Parmanand Multi Superspeciality Hospital and NKS Superspeciality Hospital, were targeted in a cyberattack. Initially mistaken for a technical issue, the breach was later confirmed as deliberate following an internal IT investigation. Both hospitals alerted the police, prompting a formal probe. Technical experts are working to trace the origin and identify those responsible.

WestJet, Canada’s second-largest airline, experienced a cyberattack on 14 June 2025 attributed to the Scattered Spider threat actor. The incident disrupted access to internal systems, the mobile app and the airline’s website, briefly preventing users from logging in, though services were later restored. In response, WestJet activated internal cybersecurity teams and began working with law enforcement and Transport Canada to assess the scope of the breach and mitigate further impact.

On 9 June 2025, Inc ransomware group launched a ransomware attack against municipal systems in Thomasville in the US state of North Carolina, resulting in widespread service disruption. While essential services remained operational, many city systems were taken offline. At the time of reporting, it remained unclear whether any sensitive or personal data had been accessed or compromised. According to Deputy City Manager Eddie Bowling, suspicious activity was first detected within the city's computer systems in the afternoon of 9 June. The incident is under investigation, with state and federal authorities notified and external cybersecurity experts supporting the response.

On 12 June 2025, the website of the Argentine newspaper Ambito was defaced by a hacktivist group operating under the name '@gov.eth'. The attackers altered the website’s content, displaying images of skulls and headlines targeting former president Cristina Fernández de Kirchner. The defacement came just three days after Argentina's Supreme Court upheld Kirchner’s six-year prison sentence for corruption. The attack appears to be politically motivated, with the messaging directly referencing the high-profile conviction. No data exfiltration has been reported. The incident is under investigation.

A state-funded hacker group carried out spear phishing attacks against unnamed companies in the Danish defence industry, as reported by Defence Intelligence (FE) on 16 June 2025 in an alert. The hackers attempted to trick selected victims into taking actions that would grant access to the companies' IT systems, such as clicking on harmful links. FE confirmed that some attacks were successful and the companies' Microsoft 365 environments were compromised.

On 12 June 2025, Sweden's Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson announced that the country was under a DDoS, which had been ongoing for three days, targeting public broadcaster SVT and other key institutions, including banks and Bankid. Prime Minister Kristersson informed journalists in parliament about the attack, but did not name a specific perpetrator.

Title (Company): National Agency for Transit and Road Safety - Ministry of Public Health and Social Welfare
Description: In May 2025, Cyber Brigada PMC breached multiple databases from the National Agency for Transit and Road Safety of Paraguay and the Ministry of Public Health and Social Welfare of Paraguay. The identified data breach involves 7.4 million records of almost all Paraguayan citizens containing personally identifiable information of Paraguayan citizens. On 28 May 2025, the data is offered on the dark web for $7.4 million as ransom payment. The government did not confirm the data breach, but the website of the potentially impacted system, mentioned by the threat actor, has been shut down for one day. Moreover, the Paraguayan government announced that it would not pay the ransom. In the post on the breach forum, the attacker with the pseudonym Gatito_FBI_Nz harshly criticized the Minister of Information and Communication Technologies of Paraguay, Gustavo Villate, and claimed to be in the government's networks for weeks.

On 12 June 2025, according to OBOZ.UA, cyber specialists from the Main Directorate of Intelligence of the Defense Ministry of Ukraine, supported by cyber activists BO Team aka Black Owl hacker group, carried out a successful operation against Orion Telecom, one of the largest internet providers in Siberia, Russia. The attack, which was claimed by the BO Team hacker group in letter shared in local Telegram groups, involved a powerful DDoS attack that paralyzed Orion Telecom's networks, taking 370 servers and approximately 500 network switches out of service, and wiping backups, making it difficult for the provider to quickly restore work. The attack affected Krasnoyarsk, Irkutsk, Bratsk, and Abakan, with many Russians complaining about the lack of internet and television on social media platforms, including local Telegram groups.

On 29 April 2025, a select group of iOS user, including a prominent European journalist who requested anonymity and Ciro Pellegrino, a journalist at Italian publication Fanpage.it, were notified by Apple that they were targeted with advanced spyware. Researchers at Citizen Lab confirmed with high confidence after a forensic analysis that both victims were targeted with Paragon’s Graphite mercenary spyware, and it was very likely the same state actor. Apple confirmed that the zero-click attack deployed in these cases was mitigated as of iOS 18.3.1 and has assigned the vulnerability CVE-2025-43200.

On 6 June 2025, Russian Railways' online services were hit by a large-scale DDoS attack that made the website and mobile application inaccessible for several hours starting around 10 a.m. Moscow time. The attack was confirmed by the railway company's press service. The first anomalies were detected in the online booking systems before all digital services were affected. The physical counters at the stations remained operational, allowing ticket sales and refunds to be processed normally. The Russian railway company mobilised its IT teams to restore online services and increase security.

Between September 2024 and July 2025, Insikt Group observed a threat actor tracked as TAG-144 (aka Blind Eagle, AguilaCiega, APT-C-36, and APT-Q-98) targeting unnamed Colombian government entities using AsyncRAT and REMCOS RAT, the unit reported on 26 August 2025. Overall, Insikt Group observed five activity clusters as part of this campaign.  TAG-144 efforts identified as cluster three involved C2 IP addresses primarily communicating with the Colombian ISP UNE EPM. Similarly to other activity clusters, this activity sought to leverage legitimate internet services and the deployment of AsyncRAT and REMCOS RAT. Some of the activity tracked in Cluster Three overlapped with that of other tracked activity clusters; Insikt Group observed a malicious domain associated with Cluster Three also resolving to an IP address linked with Cluster Two.  Insikt Group noted possible connections between TAG-144 and a threat group tracked by SCILabs under the heading Red Akodon based on similar targeting patterns and TTPs. While the five activity clusters tracked by Insikt Group differ in certain tools, there also exist significant overlaps between clusters, potentially indicating related and/or evolving campaigns rather than entirely isolated activity.

Title (Company): Pastel diplomatie - Mes services étudiant - Cyclades - EduConnect
Description: A pro-Russian hacker group named Stormous hacked into educational platforms in France, compromising approximately 40,000 student accounts from Cyclades, Mes services étudiant, Pastel diplomatie and ÉduConnect. On 10 June 2025, the hackers leaked a list containing IDs and passwords for over a thousand students or parents on the darknet. With the leaked data allows access to school records, Crous files, exam results or request civil status.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Between February and July 2025, Insikt Group observed a threat actor tracked as TAG-144 (aka Blind Eagle, AguilaCiega, APT-C-36, and APT-Q-98) targeting 19 Colombian entities in government, education, transportation, and the retail sectors through a spearphishing campaign, as reported by the unit on 26 August 2025. The campaign involved the group utilizing lures and masquerading as local Colombian government authorities. Overall, Insikt Group observed five activity clusters as part of this campaign.  Activities linked to cluster one, were directed throughC2 IP addresses of several VPN servers from TorGuard and a Colombian ISP, COLOMBIA TELECOMUNICACIONES S.A. E.S.P. The group was specifically observed compromising its government victims by installing remote access trojans such as DcRAT, AsyncRAT, and REMCOS RAT. Some government victims were infected multiple times and were also linked to further activity by TAG-144 in other activity clusters, indicating lateral movement or broader targeting. While TAG-144 was active in this campaign until July 2025, its network communications ended in June 2025, which Insikt Group states could indicate that the threat actors were either evicted, completed their objectives, or switched to new objectives within other activity clusters. Insikt Group noted possible connections between TAG-144 and a threat group tracked by SCILabs under the heading Red Akodon based on similar targeting patterns and TTPs. While the five activity clusters tracked by Insikt Group differ in certain tools, there also exist significant overlaps between clusters, potentially indicating related and/or evolving campaigns rather than entirely isolated activity.

United Natural Foods (UNFI), a grocery wholesale giant, was targeted in a compromise that forced it to shut down some systems, impacting customer orders. The incident, discovered on 5 June 2025, prompted the company to take certain systems offline and implement containment measures. UNFI notified relevant law enforcement authorities and hired external cybersecurity experts to investigate the incident. The company implemented workarounds to maintain customer service continuity until affected systems are restored. UNFI filed documents with the US SEC on the same day. According to reporting by Cyberscoop, the incident's circumstances bear strong similarities with criminal group Scattered Spider.

On 12 May 2025, hackers compromised an account at the Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) and accessed and downloaded nearly 300,000 crash reports from the Crash Records Information System (CRIS). The crash records included sensitive information such as names, addresses, drivers license numbers, license plate numbers, car insurance policy numbers, details about injuries sustained during crashes, and narratives of incidents. Texas officials informed the public by sending letters to impacted individuals. The incident was reported to the public on 9 June 2025.

On 5 June 2025, Cisco Talos researchers reported that a Russia-linked threat actor targeted a critical infrastructure organization in Ukraine with a new destructive malware dubbed PathWiper. The attackers utilized a legitimate endpoint administration tool to deploy the malware, indicating they had access to the administrative console. Cisco Talos researchers noted similarities between PathWiper and HermeticWiper, a destructive tool observed in earlier targeting of critical infrastructure in Ukraine that had been attributed to the Russia-nexus group Sandworm with medium to high confidence. Based on these overlaps, Talos considers it highly likely that a Russian state-backed actor was responsible for the PathWiper campaign. The PathWiper malware scanned and identified all connected storage, including network drives, then spawned threads to overwrite key disk artifacts and files with random data, targeting NTFS structures like MBR, MFT, and others. The malicious code dismounted volumes before wiping and replaced the contents of artifacts related to the file system with random data generated on the fly. The attackers executed commands from the administrative console as BAT files, which ran a malicious VBScript that dropped and executed the PathWiper payload.

On 19 June 2024, US Dermatology Partners was breached by the Black Basta ransomware group and certain files were transferred to an external destination. The Black Basta group claimed responsibility for the incident and say to have stolen 1.8 TB of files. It is unclear if this breach was related to a previous alleged breach by BianLian, which resulted in the leak of 300 GB of files in August 2024.

An unknown group of individuals breached the systems of Istanbul Gedik University on 13 May 2025, affecting 23,269 employees, users, and students and exposing 209,421 records containing personal data. The compromised information included names, surnames, usernames, partially masked Turkish ID numbers, email addresses, institutional department information, and user traffic data. The breach was detected on 20 May 2025. The Personal Data Protection Board (KVKK) announced the incident on 4 June 2025.

Title (Company): Unnamed external service provider - MainStreet Bank
Description: MainStreet Bank reported a vendor incident that leaked customer information of about 5% of their customer base, discovered in March 2025. The bank ceased all activity with the vendor and concluded its review of the incident in late April 2025. An investigation found that MainStreet Bank's systems had not been compromised and no unauthorized transactions were conducted. The bank notified regulators and informed customers on 26 May, providing victims with tools to monitor suspicious activity. The incident was reported to the public through a regulatory filing with the SEC on 30 May 2025.

The Department of Justice in Puerto Rico was targeted in a breach in May 2025, affecting thousands of citizens and leading to the temporary suspension of services such as criminal record certificates, arms licences, and documents required by other agencies. The incident was detected on 30 May and impacted the Criminal Justice Information Office, and protocols were initiated to contain the intrusion and protect the integrity of the information.

InterLock ransomware group has carried out a ransomware attack on Texas Digestive Specialists, a Texas-based gastroenterology and surgical practice. The perpetrators claimed to have exfiltrated and leaked 263 GB of data, containing protected health information (PHI) such as lab pathology reports with patient names, dates of birth, and medical history.  According to a review by the information security observatory DataBreaches, the compromise includes data going back to August 2023.

Title (Company): Moroccan Agency for Land Conservation (ANCFCC) - Tawtik system
Description: On 2 June 2025, the Algerian hacker group "Jabaroot DZ" claimed to have extracted more than 4 terabytes of confidential data from the Moroccan Agency for Land Conservation, Cadastre and Mapping (ANCFCC), revealing sensitive information on senior Moroccan officials, including Yassine Mansouri (Director of Moroccan External Intelligence) and Nasser Bourita (Minister for Foreign Affairs of Morocco). Media reports are inconsistent about the organization from which the data was obtained; some articles claim the target was the National Agency for Land Conservation, Cadastre and Mapping (ANCFCC), while others suggest the breach might have involved the Tawtik system, a platform overseen by the National Council of the Order of Notaries. The leaked data included passports, identity cards, property deeds, and civil status documents, and was made partially accessible on the dark web.

On 3 June 2025, Telefónica, a Spanish telecommunications company, was investigating reports of an intrusion after data allegedly belonging to one million of its customers in Peru was disseminated in an internet forum. The breach was allegedly perpetrated by an individual operating under the alias of Dedale, who claimed to have a database containing information of approximately 22 million Telefónica customers. The leaked data included pesonal details such as full names, national ID numbers, mobile phone numbers, service plans, and status updates. The compromise was revealed by the cybersecurity firm HackManac on X. Telefónica announced that it was investigating the incident and that the leak had not affected users in Spain or in other markets where it maintains operations.

Title (Company): St. Marys Health System - St. Josephs Hospital - St. Joseph Hospital - Covenant Health
Description: On 26 May 2025, Covenant Health, a non-profit Catholic regional health care system sponsoring hospitals, nursing homes, assisted living residences, and other health and elder services throughout New England, was breached by an unknown threat actor, which caused disruption in three hospitals in Maine and New Hampshire. Some phones and documentation systems were disrupted, and some labs had to be closed. A spokesperson for Covenant Health confirmed that a cyberattack impacted two hospitals in Maine — St. Joseph Hospital and St. Mary’s Health System — and the St. Joseph Hospital in New Hampshire.

On 26 May 2025, Malaysian Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail's WhatsApp account was hijacked by an unknown actor who sent malicious links to the minister's contacts. The Ministry of Home Affairs confirmed the incident and urged the public not to respond to any messages or calls claiming to come from the minister. The incident is under investigation and law enforcement is working to determine the hacker's location.

On 27 May 2025, the Ukrainian IT Army was suspected to have launched a major DDoS attack against Russian provider ASVT, disrupting internet access for tens of thousands of people in Moscow and nearby areas from 27 May to 30 May 2025, and disabling ASVT's mobile app, website, and customer accounts, with the company working with Russian state agencies to restore services, and the incident was reported to the public by ASVT on 30 May 2025.

On 8 May 2025, Taiwan-based crypto money market BitoPro was targeted in an theft of crypto assets. The activities targeted hot wallets on blockchains such as Ethereum, Tron, Solana, and Polygon which recorded irregular outflows in the amount of $11.5 million, The funds were subsequently laundered through Tornado Cash and Thorchain. BitoPro confirmed the breach almost a month later after a post from the blockchain analyst ZachXBT and stated that user funds were secure and unharmed due to rapid response and moving funds from old hot wallets to new wallets during the attack. The platform is cooperating with a cyber security company and announced that new hot wallet addresses would be announced shortly.

Between 24-25 May 2025, the City of Níjar suffered an intrusion compromising the security of its computer systems and internal files. The incicent, attributed to the Devman cybercriminal group by a media outlet that refers to unnamed sources in the city council, involved ransomware and caused disruption and very likely the theft of internal information. The Civil Guard is investigating the incident. The City of Níjar has restored its services and is taking preventive measures to prevent further attacks.

ConnectWise, a Florida-based IT management software firm, was breached in a suspected state-sponsored intrusion that impacted a limited number of its ScreenConnect customers. The breach, which occurred in August 2024 and was discovered in May 2025, was linked to a high-severity zero-day vulnerability tracked as CVE-2025-3935, a ViewState code injection bug in ScreenConnect versions 25.2.3 and earlier. The threat actors, believed to be nation-state hackers, exploited this vulnerability to gain privileged system-level access and steal secret machine keys, which were used to craft malicious payloads and trigger remote code execution on the server. ConnectWise launched an investigation with forensic experts from Mandiant, contacted all affected customers, and coordinated with law enforcement. The company implemented enhanced monitoring and hardened security across its network, and no further suspicious activity was observed in customer instances.

Chinese hackers, specifically the group APT41/Brass Typhoon, used Google Calendar to aid attacks on government entities in October 2024. The attackers exploited a government website to host malware, dubbed TOUGHPROGRESS, which took advantage of Google Calendar for command and control to blend in with authentic activity. Google's Threat Intelligence Group discovered the attack and developed custom fingerprints to identify and take down attacker-controlled calendars, terminated attacker-controlled Workspace projects, updated file detections, and added malicious domains and URLs to the Google Safe Browsing blocklist. The attackers delivered event invitations containing encrypted malicious commands as spearphishing notifications tailored based on information obtained from the compromised host government site.

From 2022, the Czech Republic was targeted by a malicious cyber campaign, attributed to APT31/Violet Typhoon, a cyber espionage actor linked to the Chinese Ministry of State Security. The attack targeted a network used for unclassified communication at the Foreign Affairs Ministry. The Czech Republic summoned China's ambassador and called on China to refrain from such attacks. On 28 May 2025, the attack was made public with an attribution statement published on the website of the Foreign Affairs Ministry, which described the affected entity as part of national critical infrastructure. The EU and NATO also condemned the attack, with EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas stating that states should not allow their territory to be used for malicious cyber activities.

On 25 May 2025, Income Insurance was alerted to a ransomware attack involving DataPost, an external vendor responsible for printing and mailing documents to Income's policyholders. The attack compromised the personal and policy information of at least 146 Income Insurance policyholders, including names, postal addresses, policy numbers, and annual bonuses for the year 2024. Income Insurance immediately suspended all printing jobs with DataPost, blocked connections to DataPost, and reinforced firewall restrictions. The company is contacting customers who may be affected and is monitoring for suspicious account activity. DataPost is investigating the attack and complying with regulatory obligations. The Personal Data Protection Commission Singapore is also investigating the incident.

Around 20 May 2025, a hacker group, allegedly operating from Taiwan, infiltrated the back-end systems of an unidentified Chinese technology company based in the southeastern city of Guangzhou. The incident was disclosed by the Guangzhou Municipal Public Security Bureau's Tianhe District Branch on 20 May 2025. Following an investigation, the same office released a statement on 27 May that held a hacking group with purported links to Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) responsible for the intrusion. According to these findings, the hacking group used relatively unsophisticated techniques such as mass phishing emails, exploiting publicly known vulnerabilities, and brute-force password attacks. The group's self-developed Trojan programs were described as poorly coded, leaving behind traces that facilitated tracking and investigation by Chinese authorities. In a statement to Reuters, Taiwan's National Security Bureau responded to the accusations by claiming that the Communist Party of China manipulated "inaccurate information to confuse the outside world, so as to cover up the related cyber hacking acts".

On 25 May 2025, the website of François Bayrou, the Prime Minister of France and Mayor of Pau, was taken offline by unknown actors. As of 28 May, the site remained inaccessible. Bayrou denounced the incident, stating that it was aimed at preventing him from publishing information in the public interset and that he would file a complaint. Shortly before the incident, Bayrou had sought to publish documents through the website intended to exculpate him from accusations that he had interferred in investgations of the Bétharram case. The case centered on a series of reports about sexual abuse and physical violence at Notre-Dame de Bétharram, an educational institution run by a Jesuit congregation. Claims that Bayrou obstructed investigative efforts stem from his tenure as Minister of Education, when he was ultimately responsible for overseeing an initial inquiry into the allegations in 1996. Reports of abuse remained under criminal investigation as of 2025, with the Pau Public Prosecutor's Office having registered 200 complaints. On 14 May 2025, Bayrou had appeared at a hearing before the National Assembly to refute these allegations. Documents Bayrou had planned to release through the website included his opening statement and a chronology of events in the case.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Between July 2020 and February 2025, the Chinese state-linked hacking group TA-ShadowCricket quietly controlled over 2,000 infected systems around the world by invading the external Windows servers remote access function (RDP) or database connection (MSSQL) and installing a backdoor malware code that can control the system remotely. Affected devices have been found in various countries, including Korea, India, Vietnam, Taiwan, Germany, Indonesia, Thailand, and the United States. AhnLab and the South Korean National Cyber Security Center (NCSC) issued a joint tracking report on the cyberattack activity of TA-ShadowCricket, which was characterized by sneaking into the system and then quietly remaining in a state of silence after a long period of time. TA-ShadowCricket continues to manage its C2 servers and maintain control over thousands of compromised systems via a South Korean IP address. However, access via Chinese IP addresses has also been observed.

On 22 May 2025, the decentralized cryptocurrency exchange Cetus was targeted in a cyber-enabled theft of $223 million. The company, which runs it services on the Sui blockchain, reported an incident early in the day, telling customers on social media they paused operations of the platform's smart contract for security reasons and were investigating the issue, before confirming later that a threat actor had stolen funds. The Cetus team engaged the Sui Foundation and other ecosystem partners to track and recover the remaining funds. The incident caused significant depreciation of tokens, particularly popular in the Sui network, with 46 tokens suffering double-digit declines over the past 24 hours.

Title (Company): Not available - University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust - Not available - Not available - University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Chinese hackers exploited a remote code execution flaw in Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile (EPMM) to breach high-profile organizations worldwide, including UK National Health Service institutions, National healthcare-pharma provider in North America, and US medical device manufacturer, among others, by leveraging an exploit chain to execute code remotely on Ivanti EPMM version 12.5.0.0 and earlier via specially crafted API requests. EPMM centrally manages the security of enterprise mobile devices. The campaign developed initial access through the joint exploitation of two vulnerabilities, CVE-2025-4427 and CVE-2025-4428. The first exploitation attempts were detected on 15 May 2025, the day that Ivanti disclosed the two vulnerabilities. In a report originally published on 21 May, EclecticIQ attributed the activity with high confidence to the UTA0178/UNC5221 cluster, which is considered an Ivanti specialist. EclecticIQ subsequently revised this report, replacing references to UNC5221 with a broader attribution assessment that linked the activities to a "China-nexus espionage group".

Chinese-speaking hackers, identified as UAT6382, breached multiple local governing bodies across the United States by exploiting a now-patched Trimble Cityworks zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2025-0994) in January 2025. The hackers used a Rust-based malware loader to deploy Cobalt Strike beacons and VSHell malware, as well as web shells and custom malicious tools written in Chinese, to gain long-term persistent access to the compromised systems. The campaign was first observed by Cisco Talos, which reported that the hackers expressed a clear interest in pivoting to systems related to utilities management. The vulnerability was patched by Trimble in early February 2025, and the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added it to its catalogue of actively exploited vulnerabilities, ordering federal agencies to patch their systems within three weeks.

On 20 May 2025, the official X account of the Tanzanian police was hijacked by unknown actors and used to publish a false claim announcing the death of President Samia Suluhu Hassan. The incident triggered outrage among senior officials and led to the temporary restriction of access to X across several of the country’s major internet service providers. The Tanzanian police later confirmed that the information was fabricated and condemned its circulation as misleading and malicious. Authorities stated that they are working to identify those responsible and warned that anyone found spreading the content could face legal consequences. The incident came shortly after the president criticised foreign involvement in domestic matters, following the expulsion of several Kenyan activists who had entered the country to observe a high-profile treason trial. Although access to X was reportedly available in some parts of the country the following day, its nationwide status remained uncertain.

Russian military hackers codenamed Fancy Bear aka APT28 carried out sustained cyber attacks targeting UK defence, transport hubs, and shipping over the last two years. The attacks, which began in February 2022, targeted logistics and technology companies involved in the delivery of aid to Ukraine, as well as internet-connected cameras at Ukrainian border crossings. The campaign was linked to Russia's war in Ukraine and was carried out using a variety of covert tactics and techniques, including targeted scam emails and stolen passwords. Eleven Western countries, including the US, UK, Germany, and France, released a joint advisory on 21 May 2025 accusing the Russian military intelligence hacking group of targeting defense, transport, and tech firms involved in helping Ukraine. The attackers used various methods to compromise the networks, including exploiting specific vulnerabilities and targeting specific systems.

The departmental council of Hauts-de-Seine fell victim to an intrusion on 20 May 2025. All information systems and means of communication were deactivated. The council implemented measures to assess the impact, protect data, and restore access to the network and applications. A crisis cell was set up, and SI teams and service providers were mobilized. The breach affected the department's administration, including major cities such as Boulogne-Billancourt, Nanterre, Asnières-sur-Seine, and the business district of La Défense, causing them to operate at a slow pace. The exact cause and consequences of the incident were not communicated. The mayor of Neuilly-sur-Seine, Jean-Christophe Fromantin, indicated that telecommunications means had been cut as a precaution. The activities were reported by ICI Paris Ile-de-France and La Tribune on 20 May 2025.

On 20 May 2025, Kettering Health experienced a systemwide technology outage due to a ransomware attack by the Interlock ransomware gang, bringing down phone lines and the MyChart patient portaland leading the hospital to pre-emptively cancel some non-emergency medical procedures and divert emergency crews to other facilities on 20 May. A ransom note signed by the group Interlock threatened to destroy data and publicly publish sensitive data on the dark web if hospital officials did not reach out and negotiate within 72 hours. The group claimed on their leak site to have stolen 941 GB of data, including over 20,000 folders containing 732,489 documents with sensitive information.

On 14 May 2025, Cellcom, a Wisconsin wireless provider, experienced disruptions of its voice and SMS services for customers across Wisconsin and Upper Michigan. Data services and 911 emergency services remained available. The incident was confirmed by Cellcom CEO Brighid Riordan, who stated that the company had protocols in place to handle the situation and was working to bring systems back online. The incident did not impact personal information related to customers, and Cellcom began restoring some services on 19 May. The company is working to restore full service by 25 May.

On 14 May, Peter Green Chilled, a logistics firm supplying major UK supermarkets including Tesco, Sainsburys, and Aldi, was hit by a ransomware attack. The firm was unable to process orders, but it continued to transport activities unaffected throughout the incident. The company's managing director, Tom Binks, confirmed the incident but could not comment further. One of the affected customers, Black Farmer founder Wilfred Emmanuel-Jones, warned that if the products did not make it to supermarkets in time, they would be thrown away.

On 16 May 2025, the Danish-Swedish dairy producer Arla Foods experienced disruptions of a local IT network at a production site in Upahl, Germany. Mitigation and containment measures caused temporary production delays, potentially resulting in the cancellations of product deliveries. Arla Foods confirmed the incident to BleepingComputer, noting efforts to resume operations at the impacted facility.

On 12 May 2025, the pro-Ukrainian hacktivist group 4B1D announced to have breached systems of the Russian private hospital Lecardo Clinic.  The group claimed to have erased data from the clinic’s servers, deleting backups, encrypting and exfiltrating data, disabling more than 100 work stations in the procss. The obtained data reportedly comprises records of an estimated 52,000 patients and medical staff. Allegedly, 2,000 files from this cache had been sold on the dark web. at the time the group reported its activities. Details in the files include patient names, phone numbers, service costs, and average bill amounts. Local Russian authorities confirmed unauthorized access to the software platform used to manage patient records and medical histories, resulting in a three-day shutdown of operations at the hospital. The authorities further warned that other private care providers relying on the same software may have had their data compromised.

On 23 April 2025, the UK Legal Aid Agency suffered a compromise, resulting in the theft of a substantial amount of sensitive data, including criminal records, contact information, dates of birth, national identification numbers, criminal histories, employment statuses, and financial data. The breach is believed to have affected data dating back to 2010. The Ministry of Justice (MoJ), which oversees the agency, was informed of the breach and launched an investigation in cooperation with the National Crime Agency and the National Cyber Security Centre. In a parliamentary hearing on the incident on 19 May, Sarah Sackmann, Minister of State within the Ministry of Justice, linked the compromise to crminals, "no ifs, no buts". The agency's online digital services have been taken offline as a precautionary measure.

On 19 May 2025, a hacking group identifying as Nova obtained two terabytes of employee documents and internal emails in a breach of the Municipality of Pisa. The group claimed responsibility for the compromise when publishing 1.6 gigabytes of the stolen data on the dark web together with a ransom demand, for which they set a 14-day ultimatum. The stolen data included internal evaluations, work and holiday schedules, email conversations, as well as invoices.

On 11 May 2025, an unknown threat actor sent an email to Coinbase claiming to have information about certain customer accounts and internal documents. The attackers had paid multiple contractors and employees working in support roles outside the U.S. to collect information from internal systems, and some data, including names, addresses, and emails, was stolen. However, the hackers did not get access to login credentials or passwords. Coinbase refused to pay a ransom demand of $20 million and is working with law enforcement agencies. The company has established a $20 million reward for information on the attackers and will reimburse customers who were tricked into sending funds to the attackers. The incident is estimated to cost Coinbase between $180 million and $400 million. The breach was disclosed in an SEC filing and reported by various news outlets, including Coinbase's blog post on 15 May 2025.

On 20 May 2025, several major Russian state services, including the tax service (FNS), as well as the platforms to handle secure digital keys (Goskey), and documents (Saby), were disrupted due to a DDoS attack originating from abroad. The outages were confirmed by Saby and FNS, who reported that they were working to restore access to their systems. The attack was reported by Downdetector, an outage monitoring site, and Russian news outlet RBC.

Title (Company): Harbin Clinic - Nationwide Recovery Services - Hamilton Health Care System - Erlanger - City Government of Chattanooga
Description: Between 5 and 11 July 2024, Nationwide Recovery Services (NRS), a company hired to collect medical debt, experienced a breach that exposed sensitive information of at least 300,000 people, including financial account information, medical information, and Social Security numbers. The company experienced a network outage following the detection of suspicious activity in its information technology systems. Multiple hospitals contracting NRS services began sending out breach notifications in spring of 2025 after being informed by NRS in February 2025 that information of their patients had been affected. On 16 May, the Harbin Clinic in Georgia notified 210,140 affected people. Earlier on 14 April, the Hamilton Health Care System in Texas had informed 88,000 patients. Additional victims include the health system Erlanger of the University of Tennessee Health Science Center and the city government of Chattanooga in Tennessee.

On 16 May 2025, a DDoS attack targeted the ruling centrist party in Poland, two days before the first round of the country's presidential election. The disruption attempts started at 9:00 a.m. local time, targeting two sites associated with the Civic Platform (PO) party of Prime Minister Donald Tusk, including the party's main website and a website dedicated to fundraising for the campaign. The National Research Institute for Cyber Security (NASK) assessed that a pro-Russian was behind the blockage without identifying a specific actor. The Prime Minister's Office confirmed the incident in statements to the press and on social media. Donald Tusk in a post on X on the same day held Russia responsible for the incident.

Description: Between 2023 and 2024, ESET researchers uncovered a Russia-aligned espionage operation targeting webmail servers via XSS vulnerabilities, including a zero-day. The campaign is attributed with medium confidence to Russian state-sponsored hackers APT28, also known as APT28, Fancy Bear, Forest Blizzard, or Sofacy. The attacks started with spearphishing email leveraging an XSS vulnerability to inject malicious JavaScript code into the victim’s webmail page, which was able to steal webmail credentials, and exfiltrate contacts and email messages from the victim’s mailbox. In 2023, they only targeted Roundcube, but in 2024 it expanded to other webmail software including Horde, MDaemon, and Zimbra. For MDaemon, APT28 used a zero-day XSS vulnerability (CVE-2024-11182), which was patched in November 2024. Most victims are governmental entities and defence companies in Eastern Europe, although we have observed governments in Africa, Europe, and South America being targeted as well.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: EclecticIQ analysts assess that, in April 2025, China-nexus nation-state APTs launched high-tempo exploitation campaigns against critical infrastructure networks by targeting SAP NetWeaver Visual Compose. EclecticIQ attributed some of the activities with high confidence to Chinese state-backed APTs CL-STA-0048 and UNC5174. Actors leveraged CVE-2025-31324, an unauthenticated file upload vulnerability that enables remote code execution (RCE). The intrusions were discovered through publicly exposed directory (opendir) found on attacker-controlled infrastructure, which contained detailed event logs capturing operations across multiple compromised systems. Analysis of the open-dir infrastructure reveals a targeted campaign against critical sectors across multiple countries including critical natural gas distribution networks, water and integrated waste management utilities in UK, advanced medical device manufacturing plants, upstream oil and gas exploration and production companies in US. It also targets government ministries responsible for investment strategy and financial regulation in Saudi Arabia.

Nucor, the largest US steelmaker, was breached by an unauthorized third party who accessed certain information technology systems, forcing the company to temporarily halt production operations at some locations. The incident was disclosed via an 8K filing to the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on 14 May 2025. Nucor activated its incident response plan, took potentially affected systems offline, and implemented containment, remediation, or recovery measures. In its 8K filing from 20 June 2025, the company stated that an investigation also determined that the threat actor exfiltrated limited data from the company’s information technology systems and resulted in a temporary limitation of access to portions of the company’s information technology applications supporting some aspects of the company’s operations at some of the company’s facilities.

On 14 March 2025, an international criminal organization carried out a cyberattack on the community of Kirkel in Germany, intercepting documents containing personal data from different parts of the administration. The breach was appeared to be motivated by extortion, as the perpetrators demanded a ransom in exchange for deleting the stolen data, to which the community did not respond. The data was subsequently leaked only. The incident was reported to the public by a spokesperson on 14 March 2025.

Title (Company): Unnamed external service provider - Berliner Verkehrsbetriebe
Description: On 14 May 2025, the Berlin public transport company BVG confirmed that an external service provider had fallen victim to a data breach, resulting in the exposure of personal data belonging to up to 180,000 BVG customers. The company stated that, based on current information, details such as passwords or bank account data were not accessed. Those affected have been informed, and BVG is working closely with the compromised provider to investigate the incident.

On 22 April, the British retailer Marks & Spencer (M&S) confirmed that it was managing a cyber incident in a filing with the London Stock Exchange. The company subsequently reported disruptions to its systems, including its Sparks loyalty rewards app, that led to the suspension of online orders on 25 April. In the week following the incident, stores faced supply shortages with some food shelves remaining empty. The attackers, believed to be a criminal gang, were holding the company to ransom, and M&S was forced to resort to pen and paper to honour loyalty rewards. In a conversation with the BBC on 2 May, the ransomware-as-a-service group DragonForce claimed responsibility for targeting M&S. Already on 28 April, unnamed sources had indicated to the technology news portal Bleeping Computer that a loose network of criminals tracked as Scattered Spider, acting as affiliates of DragonForce, may have deployed its malicious encryption software. The threat actors are suspected to have breached M&S through the use of social engineering techniques, possibly as early as February 2025. According to this report by Bleeping Computer, the threat actors obtained a credential database for Active Directory Services, allowing them to gain widespread access to M&S networks and to deploy the DragonFroce ransomware to virtual machines of M&S on 24 April. On 13 March, M&S announced that a limited set of customer data had been compromised, though there was no indication at the time that the information had been leaked. Data included cumstomers’ names, email and home address, phone number, date of birth, online order history as well as partial payment card details. In the three weeks following the disclosure of the incident, the company's share price dropped by as much as 15% in value. As of 20 May, online orders remained paused without a clear timeline for resuming services. Analysts at the Bank of America estimated that M&S had been sustaining 43 million GBP of lost sales per week. In a statement from 4 May also addressing a ransomware attack against the supermarket chain Co-op and an attempted compromise of the department store Harrods, the UK National Cyber Security Centre announced its ongoing efforts to establish whether the incidents are part of a “concerted campaign by a single actor or whether there is no link between them at all.“ On 10 July 2025, the National Crime Agency announced that four people have been arrested in the UK as part of a National Crime Agency investigation into incidents targeting M&S, Co-op and Harrods.

On 13 May 2025, the Colombian National Aquaculture and Fisheries Authority (AUNAP) reported a cyberattack on its official website. In response, the agency urged the public not to access the site or interact with any links originating from it, warning of potential security risks. The technical team at AUNAP began immediate work to contain the incident and restore normal operations. While the nature and scope of the attack remain unclear, the agency confirmed that unknown actors were behind the intrusion. No data breach has yet been confirmed.

On 12 May 2025, the Karachi Port Trust (KPT) in Pakistan confirmed that their account had been hacked after a post on X (formerly Twitter) earlier on the same day falsely stated that the port suffered damage from an Indian Navy strike, amid escalating tensions between India and Pakistan. The earlier post has been deleted and the wrong information was clarified.

On April 2024, a Türkiye-backed cyberespionage group, known as Sea Turtle/Teal Kurma/Marbled Dust fka SILICON/Cosmic Wolf, exploited a zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2025-27920) in the Output Messenger application to attack users linked to the Kurdish military in Iraq. The attackers gained access to the Output Messenger Server Manager application and deployed a backdoor (OMServerService.exe) onto the victims' devices, allowing them to steal sensitive data, access all user communications, impersonate users, gain access to internal systems, and cause operational disruptions. Microsoft Threat Intelligence analysts discovered the security flaw and notified Srimax, the developer of the messaging app, who issued a software update. The attack was reported by Microsoft on 12 May 2025.

Title (Company): Chamber of Deputies (Paraguay) - Ministry of Children and Adolescents (Paraguay) - Secretariat for the Development of Repatriated and Refugee Nationals (Paraguay) - National Directorate of Meteorology (Paraguay) - National Navigation and Ports Administration (ANNP) (Paraguay) - Presidency of the Republic (Paraguay) - Ministry of Labour (Paraguay) - National Secretariat for the Administration of Seized and Confiscated Assets - Military Cabinet (Paraguay) - Ministry of Justice (Paraguay) - National Secretariat of Sports (Paraguay) - Ministry of Health (Paraguay)
Description: On 9 May 2025, Paraguay’s Ministry of Information and Communication Technologies (Mitic) confirmed a widespread cyberattack affecting at least eleven public institutions. Detected by CERT-PY, the incidents involved both website defacement and unauthorized access to sensitive data. While many of the affected entities experienced changes to the appearance of their websites, the breach at the Ministry of Health raised particular concern due to the confirmed leak of personal data from the national vaccination system. Mitic Minister Gustavo Villate stated that the attackers exploited vulnerabilities to access systems and that personal health data — including information provided by citizens during the vaccination process — was compromised. He described the breach as one of the most serious data leaks the country has faced, with possible consequences ranging from identity theft to financial fraud. The institutions targeted include the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Justice, Chamber of Deputies, Presidency of the Republic, and several others across key sectors. In response, Mitic activated its cyber incident response protocols, launched an investigation, and began working with affected entities to contain the impact and identify the full scope of the breach. On 13 May, another intrusion targeted a Paraguayan institution within the scope of the large-scale campaign against Paraguay - this time, the website of SENABICO (the National Secretariat for the Administration of Seized and Confiscated Assets) was defaced in an attack claimed by the group "CyberTeam," though it was unclear if the same group was behind the activities targeting other Paraguayan institutions.

Title (Company): Association for Police and Crime Commissioners - Arun district council - Not available - Cardiff city council - Harwich International Port - National Highways
Description: On 6 May 2025, a pro-Russian hacking group called NoName057(16) claimed to have targeted several UK websites, including local councils, the Harwich International Port, National Highways, and the Association for Police and Crime Commissioners, using a DDoS attack, temporarily making some websites inaccessible, but with limited success, as reported by various organizations, including Arun district council and National Highways. The websites were back online after a few hours. From 14 to 17 July 2025, an international law enforcement operation code-named Eastwood was launched against NoName057(16). Coordinated by Europol and Eurojust, the operation involved simultaneous actions by authorities in Czechia, France, Finland, Germany, Italy, Lithuania, Poland, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the Netherlands, and the United States, targeting individuals and digital infrastructure linked to the pro-Russian network. Operation Eastwood allowed for the deactivation of several hundred servers supporting the group’s DDoS activities. Overall, national authorities issued seven arrest warrants, including against six Russian nationals, over the suspected involvement in NoName057(16). The investigation further facilitated the arrest of two individuals in France and Spain. Law enforcement personally notified over 1,000 supporters of the group, including 15 suspected administrators, of their legal liability related to the participation in NoName057(16)‘s criminal activities.

On 27 April 2025, Masimo Corporation, a US-based medical device manufacturer, detected unauthorized activity on its on-premise network, prompting the shutdown of its systems to prevent the spread of the intrusion. Masimo activated its incident response protocols, implemented containment measures, and commenced an investigation with the assistance of third-party cybersecurity professionals. The company also notified and is coordinating with law enforcement. The incident caused the medical device maker to operate at less than normal levels, temporarily impacting its ability to process, fulfill, and ship customer orders. The investigation remains ongoing, and the full scope, nature, and impact of the incident are not yet known. This information was made public through a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on 27 April 2025.

On an unspecified date in April 2025, Esse Health, an independent physician group serving the St. Louis metropolitan area with over 100 doctors at 45 locations, was targeted in a data breach that exposed protected health information of more than 263,000 patients.

On 3 May 2025, South African Airways (SAA) was compromised, leading to temporarily disrupted access to the airline's website, mobile application, and several internal operational systems. The breach was detected on the same day and response measures were taken to mitigate its effects. The airline activated its disaster management and business continuity protocols, which successfully contained the incident and minimized disruption to core flight operations. The incident was reported to the State Security Agency, South African Police Service, and the Information Regulator of South Africa. The preliminary investigation is assessing the full extent of the incident and actively working to determine if any data was accessed or exfiltrated.

On 24 April 2025, an individual hacker targeted the German city of Ellwangen, gaining access to the city administration's systems. City officials clarified that unauthorized activity was observed on administrative systems, stating that the city administration detected an unusually high CPU load on its systems, prompting an investigation. The intrusion resulted in the preventive disconnection of all but one municipal school from the internet and the temporary suspension of an app that students and teachers use for communication. Classes, however, were able to be continued with slight technical restrictions.  On 30 May 2025, local media reported that a former student of a district school in Ellwangen is suspected to be behind the breach.

On 5 May 2025, hackers from Anonymous targeted GlobalX Air, an airline used by the Trump administration for deportation efforts. Anonymous stole flight records and passenger manifests of all flights between January and May 2025, including those for deportation, which could provide insight into who was deported, when, and to where. The hackers contacted 404 Media and other journalists about the breach, and posted a defacement message on GlobalX's website, stating they were enforcing a judge's order. The data provided to 404 Media could be verified against public reports and incidents of deportations In an SEC filing from the same day, Global Crossing Airlines Group confirmed that hackers gained access to “systems supporting portions of its business applications" and noted that none of its operations were disrupted and that it does not believe the incident will have a “material effect on the company’s financial condition.”

In February 2025, Commvault was breached, allegedly by a state-sponsored threat actor, which exploited a zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2025-3928) in their Microsoft Azure Cloud-hosted servers. The intrusion was detected by Microsoft, who notified Commvault of suspicious activity. Noting that a small number of customers were affected, Commvault reported that there was no unauthorized access to customer data and their business operations and services were not impacted.

Title (Company): Romanian Foreign Ministry - Ministry of Interior - Crin Antonescu - Romanian Constitutional Court - Nicușor Dan
Description: On 4 May 2025, a Russian hacker group known as NoName057(16) attacked several Romanian government and presidential candidates' websites using the distributed denial of service (DDoS) method on the day of the first round of the presidential election. The attack hit the website of the Romanian Constitutional Court, the main government portal, the Romanian foreign ministry site, and the websites of four presidential candidates, including Crin Antonescu and Bucharest Mayor Nicusor Dan. The hackers claimed responsibility for the activities on their Telegram channel, listing the websites of the ministries for internal affairs and justice among the targets. The National Cybersecurity Directorate informed the public about the attack on Facebook, stating that all listed websites were operational as of 2 p.m. local time. From 14 to 17 July 2025, an international law enforcement operation code-named Eastwood was launched against NoName057(16). Coordinated by Europol and Eurojust, the operation involved simultaneous actions by authorities in Czechia, France, Finland, Germany, Italy, Lithuania, Poland, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the Netherlands, and the United States, targeting individuals and digital infrastructure linked to the pro-Russian network. Operation Eastwood allowed for the deactivation of several hundred servers supporting the group’s DDoS activities. Overall, national authorities issued seven arrest warrants, including against six Russian nationals, over the suspected involvement in NoName057(16). The investigation further facilitated the arrest of two individuals in France and Spain. Law enforcement personally notified over 1,000 supporters of the group, including 15 suspected administrators, of their legal liability related to the participation in NoName057(16)‘s criminal activities.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: According to a 25 April 2025 report from Trend Micro, the APT "Earth Kurma" has been carrying out an ongoing, sophisticated cyber espionage campaign against government and government-related telecommunications sectors in Southeast Asia, specifically targeting the Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, and Malaysia since at least June 2024 and establishing persistent access to victims' systems. Trend Micro states that the threat actors used custom malware, rootkits, and cloud storage for espionage, credential theft, and data exfiltration in their campaign. According to the report, the attackers maintained prolonged, undetected access to their networks and used tools such as TESDAT, SIMPOBOXSPY, and rootkits like KRNRAT and MORIYA.

On 21 April 2025, threat actors accessed internal systems and files of Aigües de Mataró, a water supplier for Barcelona and surrounding areas. Affected data potentially included financial and personal details of customers. Also some services were disrupted. On 23 April 2025, the public was informed.

On 29 April 2025, a group of Dutch cybercriminals infiltrated and appeared to have encrypted parts of the computer systems of the City Council of Badajoz. Upon detection by the head of the municipal computer team, the servers were shut down manually according to security protocols, and since then, continuous work has been undertaken to prevent the leakage of data. The city councilor responsible for information technology reported that a message had been received, confirming the infection of the servers and allowing for tracing back the origin of the malicious activity. The cybercriminals did not send prior threats or ask for a ransom. The situation was contained by 1 May 2025. The discovery of recent backups suggests the loss of data may be lower than initially assessed. In the meantime, digital administrative procedures remained suspended until mitigation measures are lifted.

On 26 April 2025, a Pakistan-based hacker group, Team Insane PK, breached the Army College of Nursing's website, defacing its homepage with a message and images related to the Pahalgam massacre and militant Burhan Wani. This incident prompted the Indian government to issue a cybersecurity alert, directing all government ministries, departments, and agencies to strengthen their cyber defences. The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) compiled an internal report, suspecting potential imminent cyberattacks on critical infrastructure as part of a broader cyber warfare strategy. The attack was reported by various sources, including the Indian government and cybersecurity authorities, who are investigating the incident and tracing the origin and network of the hacker group.

The Rhysida ransomware group targeted the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ) in 2025, stealing and auctioning off the agency's data, including sensitive employee information. The incdient was reported by several cybersecurity websites and confirmed by the Rhysida on its dark web leak site, where they published screenshots of personal information and other files. The group claimed to have released over 2.5 terabytes of unique data, including SQL, employee data. Attempts to access and review the allegedly leaked documents were unsuccessful. The incident was publicly disclosed on 26 April 2025, with Oregon Public Broadcasting providing additional details on the breach. The DEQ spokesperson, Lauren Wirtis, stated that the claims were under investigation, but the department declined to confirm or deny the reports.

On 25 April 2025, the website of the City of Nuremberg was targeted by a DDOS attack, which made the website no longer reliably accessible. The cybercrime department of the police was notified of the incident.

On 5 December 2024, Ascension, a private healthcare system in the United States, learned that their patient information may have been involved in a potential security incident. An investigation determined that Ascension inadvertently disclosed information to a former business partner due to a vulnerability in third-party software used by the former business partner, and some of this information was likely stolen from them. The attackers gained access to a combination of personal information, including name, address, phone number(s), email address, date of birth, race, gender, and Social Security numbers (SSNs), as well as personal health information related to inpatient visits. The breach was disclosed to the public through data breach notifications sent to affected individuals and an 29 April filing with the Massachusetts Office of the Attorney General, which reported that 96 MA residents were affected.

Russian state hackers, specifically the APT28 hacking group, targeted several French institutions, including government targets, defence and industrial targets, targets in aerospace, targets in research/think-tanks, and targets in the economic and financial sector, while a French government report published on 29 April 2025 indicates that, since 2024, the targeted sectors mostly include "governmental, diplomatic, and research entities, as well as think-tanks." Notably, the French attribution of the campaign, reported by ANSSI, links APT28 to a new GRU unit. While APT28 was previously associated with GRU Unit 26165 (GRU, 85th Main Special Service Center [GTsSS]), ANSSI also linked it to GRU Unit 20728, based in Rostov-on-Don and part of the 166th Information Research Center.

On 27 January 2025, Frederick Health discovered a ransomware attack where an unauthorized user breached its systems and copied certain files from a shared server. The unknown threat actor may have accessed patient names, addresses, dates of birth, social security numbers, drivers’ license numbers, medical record numbers, health insurance information, and/or clinical information related to patients’ care.

Qilin, a Russian-based ransomware group, launched a serious cyberattack against Western New Mexico University. The incident started on April 13, 2025, and took down the university's website and other systems and services. The university used a temporary website and warned students not to use campus desktops until they were verified as safe by the IT department. The attack was reported by the university on its Facebook page, with faculty offering assignment and project extensions to support students as the university approached finals week. On 25 April 2025, Searchlight New Mexico reported that the Russian-based ransomware group Qilin is behind the attack.

On 29 April 2025, the website of the Rajasthan Education Department, in India, was hacked by the "Pakistan Cyber Force," who displayed messages related to a terrorist attack on Pahalgam days prior which killed two dozen people. The messages claimed that the attack was an inside job by the Indian government, claiming "Indian intel is fake," and made disparaging comments about a victim of the attack. The website was taken down after the breach was discovered. Education Minister Madan Dilawar condemned the attack and informed cybersecurity agencies. An investigation was launched to identify the group responsible and assess the damage.

Title (Company): Integral Port Administration (API) of Baja California Sur (BCS)
Description: The Integral Port Administration (API) of Baja California Sur (BCS) was targeted by a ransomware cyber attack that compromised its computer infrastructure and put financial information for the 2024 financial year at risk, as reported by the director general of API, Narciso Agndez Gmez, on 30 April 2025. The attack, which affected the physical servers of data processing and storage, prevented the operation of the administrative and operating systems of the company, and there is uncertainty about the total recovery of information. API manages a budget of more than 400 million Mexican pesos per year, and the impact on their computer systems poses a challenge to the fulfilment of their tax and administrative obligations. The State Government, led by governor Victor Manuel Castro Coso, asked the Congress of the State for an extension of 30 calendar days for the delivery of the Public Account, which was approved by the legislative plenary.

On 8 March 2025, Yale New Haven Health (YNHHS) faced a cybersecurity incident affecting IT services, which was quickly contained with help from cybersecurity firm Mandiant. The company declared that patient care remained unaffected. YNHHS disclosed the data breach on 11 April 2025, stating that the unknown threat actors stole sensitive patient information, including full name, date of birth, home address, telephone number, email address, race/ethnicity, Social Security number (SSN), patient type, and medical record number, impacting 5.5 million patients. The incident was reported to law enforcement, and a dedicated call centre was set up for questions. Starting 14 April 2025, YNHHS mailed letters to affected patients, offering free credit monitoring to those whose Social Security numbers were involved. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services breach portal confirmed that the incident impacted 5,556,702 individuals.

MTN Group, the largest telecom in Africa, was breached by an unknown third-party in a cyberattack that exposed the personal information of an unknown number of customers in certain markets. The South African Police Service and the country's Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation were informed, as well as other law enforcement agencies in countries where MTN operates. The company's core network, billing systems, and financial services infrastructure remained secure and operational, with no direct compromise of customers' accounts and wallets reported. MTN Group notified the public about the incident on 24 April 2025.

In February 2025, during the 9th Asian Winter Games held from 7 to 14 February in Harbin, Heilongjiang Province, Chinese authorities reported a coordinated cyber operation targeting both the event’s digital infrastructure and critical sectors across the province. According to the National Computer Virus Emergency Response Center (CVERC), the attacks involved a range of techniques, including SQL injection, arbitrary file read vulnerabilities and HTTP header spoofing. The malicious activity reportedly affected information systems related to event registration, scheduling, and logistics, as well as infrastructure in the energy, transportation, water, telecommunications and research sectors. CVERC stated that the cyber operations were traced to infrastructure allegedly linked to the United States and attributed the activity to the US government, citing indicators such as behavioral patterns, time zones and language artefacts. While Chinese officials noted that the attacks did not cause serious disruption, they indicated that the transmission of encrypted commands had been detected, which appeared to be intended to activate pre-implanted backdoors. On 15 April 2025, the Harbin Public Security Bureau publicly identified three alleged NSA operatives said to be involved in the campaign and issued warrants along with monetary rewards for information leading to their apprehension. The HPSB also claimed that the three individuals were involved in unspecified compromise attempts against Huawei. Without providing any further substantiation, Chinese state media noted findings by technical teams that purportedly pointed to the involvement of the University of California and Virginia Tech in the campaign reportedly targeting the Asian Winter Games. Although the Chinese government has presented attribution with institutional backing - including CVERC, the Foreign Ministry, and law enforcement agencies - no independent confirmation of the attack’s effectiveness or the identities of those involved has been made publicly available. The investigation remains ongoing.

On 1 May 2025, the ransomware group Qilin announced a ransomware attack on Cobb County, in the US state of Georgia, claiming to have acquired 150 GB of data and over 400,000 files, which they threatened to release on 3 May 2025 if no payment was received. The group provided 16 image files as proof, including personal information on employees and members of the public. The independent incident news portal DataBreaches reported the incident and sent an email inquiry to the county, which had previously confirmed a ransomware incident but had not acknowledged the scope of the attack.

On Friday, 25 April 2025, the capital portal of the state of Berlin, berlin.de, was targeted by a comprehensive DDoS attack. The attackers behind the cyberattack were unclear. The incident was also reported to have affected the Berliner Polizei, with some of their pages being partially affected. The Internetwache der Polizei remained accessible. The Senate Chancellery announced on Instagram that it was a DDoS attack. The systems affected included berlin.de, service.berlin.de, daten.berlin.de, itdzberlin.de, content management system Imperia, and the intranet.

On 28 April 2025, pro-Russian hackers from the group NoName057(16) launched a coordinated Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack on multiple Dutch municipalities and provinces, rendering the websites of over twenty local governments inaccessible for several hours. The attack, which was claimed by the group, caused significant disruption but did not compromise critical infrastructure or steal any data. The group stated that their actions were in retaliation for the Netherlands' support for Ukraine. The attack was confirmed by Sebastiaan Quekel, a spokesperson from the NoordHolland province. The Dutch government worked to resolve the situation, with some websites remaining offline. The VVD party called for stronger cybersecurity measures to protect against future threats, and the AIVD warned of the increasing instability in the world. From 14 to 17 July 2025, an international law enforcement operation code-named Eastwood was launched against NoName057(16). Coordinated by Europol and Eurojust, the operation involved simultaneous actions by authorities in Czechia, France, Finland, Germany, Italy, Lithuania, Poland, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the Netherlands, and the United States, targeting individuals and digital infrastructure linked to the pro-Russian network. Operation Eastwood allowed for the deactivation of several hundred servers supporting the group’s DDoS activities. Overall, national authorities issued seven arrest warrants, including against six Russian nationals, over the suspected involvement in NoName057(16). The investigation further facilitated the arrest of two individuals in France and Spain. Law enforcement personally notified over 1,000 supporters of the group, including 15 suspected administrators, of their legal liability related to the participation in NoName057(16)‘s criminal activities.

On 4 October 2024, Onsite Mammography, a healthcare service provider in Massachusetts, was breached by an unauthorized third party. According to the investigation, an unauthorized actor gained access to the individual's email account for a brief window of time. The investigation further revealed that the unauthorized actor only had access to the email account and did not have access to any other systems within the Onsite network. On 21 April 2025, Onsite Mammography informed the public about the incident

On 29 April 2025, the German city of Stuttgart was targeted by a DDoS attack, which caused the city council's website to be temporarily unavailable. The attack, attributed to the Russian group NoName057(16), started on 29 April, and the city administration blocked traffic to the site offline citing technical problems. The site was accessible again by the afternoon. A city spokesperson confirmed the incident, clarifying that the website had been flooded with requests and traffic from a number of bots or a botnet, causing the servers to fail. From 14 to 17 July 2025, an international law enforcement operation code-named Eastwood was launched against NoName057(16). Coordinated by Europol and Eurojust, the operation involved simultaneous actions by authorities in Czechia, France, Finland, Germany, Italy, Lithuania, Poland, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the Netherlands, and the United States, targeting individuals and digital infrastructure linked to the pro-Russian network. Operation Eastwood allowed for the deactivation of several hundred servers supporting the group’s DDoS activities. Overall, national authorities issued seven arrest warrants, including against six Russian nationals, over the suspected involvement in NoName057(16). The investigation further facilitated the arrest of two individuals in France and Spain. Law enforcement personally notified over 1,000 supporters of the group, including 15 suspected administrators, of their legal liability related to the participation in NoName057(16)‘s criminal activities.

On 25 April 2025, Canadian electric utility Nova Scotia Power and its parent company Emera suffered an intrusion that impacted their IT systems and networks.
