The companies discovered unauthorized access to certain parts of their Canadian network and servers, and immediately activated their incident response and business continuity protocols. They engaged leading third-party cybersecurity experts and took actions to contain and isolate the affected servers. Law enforcement officials were notified. The incident disrupted IT systems, including customer support lines and an online customer portal. On 2 May, Nova Scotia Power disclosed that it had temporarily suspended billing. As of 28 April 2025, the companies were still working to restore services. The incident was disclosed to the public by Nova Scotia Power through a social media post on 28 April 2025, and by Emera through a press statement on 25 April 2025. Although the companies did not share technical details about the incident, experts speculate that it may have been a ransomware attack. At the time of reporting, no ransomware gang had publicly claimed responsibility for the compromise. In an update from 14 Mai 2025, Nova Scotia Power confimed that on or around March 19, 2025, certain customer information stored on the impacted servers was accessed and later taken by an unauthorized third party. he types of impacted personal information varied by individual customer and depended, in part, on the information provided by each customer. This may have included one or more of the following: name, phone number, email address, mailing and service addresses, Nova Scotia Power program participation information, date of birth, and customer account history (such as power consumption, service requests, customer payment, billing, and credit history, and customer correspondence), driver’s license number, and Social Insurance Number. For some of our customers, bank account numbers (for pre-authorized payment) may also have been impacted, if this information was provided by these customers.

Title (Company): Intermunicipal System of Drinking Water and Sewerage Services (SIAPA)
Description: In April 2025, unidentified hackers locked computer systems of the Intermunicipal System of Drinking Water and Sewerage Services (SIAPA) in the Mexican state of Jalisco and demanded a ransom for its release. Affected systems were restored within a week of detecting the incident. Authorities initiated an investigation to establish responsibility for the breach. Jalisco Governor Pablo Lemus Navarro reported that no ransom was paid.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Threat actors associated with the Lazarus group (also tracked as Labyrinth Chollima/HIDDEN COBRA/Guardians of Peace/Diamond Sleet fka ZINC) breached six companies in South Korea between November 2024 and February 2025 using a watering hole attack strategy and an exploit for a vulnerability in a file transfer client. The campaign, tracked as Operation SyncHole by Kaspersky researchers, targeted multiple organizations in the software, IT, finance, and telecommunications sectors. The hackers used an exploit that was known by the vendor at the time of the investigation, but it had been leveraged before in other attacks. The attack started with targets visiting legitimate South Korean media portals that Lazarus had compromised with server-side scripts for profiling visitors and redirecting valid targets to malicious domains. Kaspersky researchers reported its observations to the Korea Internet Security Agency (KrCERT) and the vendor addressed it in an update.

On 5 May 2025, by the group Pakistan Cyber Force targeted the website of Armoured Vehicle Nigam Limited (AVNL), a defence PSU under the Department of Defence Production. The attackers defaced the homepage with the Pakistan national flag and images of the Al Khalid tank. The website was taken offline to prevent further propagation or malware insertion. No sensitive internal production or design documents were accessed, but a thorough cybersecurity audit was conducted as a precautionary measure.

In April 2025, the National Assembly site of Senegal was hacked. The website was replaced by a home page in Korean. The consequences of the attack included the website being out of service for several days.

On 29 March 2025, the Piura Tax Administration Service (SATP) was the victim of a cyber attack, where cybercriminals hacked into the computer systems and asked for a ransom to release the system. The attack was later confirmed by SATP manager Manuel Reyna. The incident occurred on 29 March, and emergency actions were taken immediately. The system could be restored and fully stabilized by 31 March after 48 hours. The attack caused the paralysis of the systems, preventing the collection of taxes, but the SATP assured that there was no danger to citizens.

On 2 May 2025, hackers stole critical data from the Jammu Municipal Corporation (JMC) website. JMC is a civic body established to develop municipal infrastrucutre in line with the needs of the population of Jammu, a city located in Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir, which itself is part of the disputed Kashmir region. The threat actor stole certificates and exfiltrated databases, which likely contained citizen data, including Aadhaar numbers that identify residents in India's biometric ID system, property records, tax details, administrative documents, and urban planning files. Indian intelligence officials disclosed the incident, with one unnamed intelligence source noting that the inicident followed "patterns of Pakistan-backed cyber operations aimed at destabilising Indian administrative infrastructure".

On 2 May 2025, hackers launched a ransomware attack against Georgia's Coweta County School System, affecting 23,000 students across 29 K-12 school causing operational issues. The incident was reported to the Georgia Emergency Management Authority and Homeland Security. The school district's IT system was alerted to unusual activity and took systems offline. The district is working with cybersecurity experts, federal, and state authorities to investigate whether student and employee information was accessed. The Nitrogen Ransomware Gang claimed responsibility on 26 May 2025.

In April 2025, the official Facebook account of the Salta Police was breached. The General Directorate of Cybersecurity was able to restore control of the account, eliminate unauthorized posts, and restore security after activating digital security protocols and conducting an investigation.

Title (Company): Local Police of Rome - Unkown cloud provider
Description: On 16 April 2025, an external cloud service provider for urban traffic officers in Rome was hit by a cyber attack, causing the tablets and cell phones of the officers to malfunction. The officers were forced to improvise and use old notepads to issue fines. The IT issues began on the 16 April 2025 and lasted until at least 18 April 2025. The unionist Gabriele Di Bella, provincial secretary of the Ugl union, reported the incident. The attack affected the cloud network that allows storing online data of motorists identified for traffic violations by the local police.

On 17 April 2025, a cyber attack occurred on the Wallonia Public Service (SPW) computer system, breaching the information systems. The incident, which was detected on the same day, forced the authorities to shut down all internet connection. Microsoft was contracted by the Walloon government to remediate the incident and restore services. The decision was taken in consultation with the CCB (Centre Cybersecurity Belgique). The SPW spokesman, Nicolas Yernaux, and Minister Adrien Dolimont's office informed the public about the incident.

SK Telecom, South Korea's largest wireless telecom company, holding almost 50% of South Korea's mobile phone service, was breached by unknown actors who accessed the Universal Subscriber Identity Module (USIM) information of SKT's customers through a data theft operation that occurred on the night of 19 April 2025. Later, it was discovered that the first malware infiltration occurred already on 15 June 2022. The company detected the infection at 23:00 and promptly reported it to the Korea Internet Security Agency (KISA) the following morning. SK Telecom reportedly sanitised the impacted systems, isolated the suspected hacking device, and enhanced defensive measures to prevent damage to customers and confirmed the leak of data. The company also offered impacted customers a free subscription to the SIM protection service. The breach was reported to the Personal Information Protection Commission on 22 April 2025. The government launched an emergency response system and is investigating the cause of the attack. No threat actors have taken responsibility for the breach. On 19 May 2025, the Ministry of Science and ICT published a report confirming that the subscriber identification numbers (IMSI) and authentication keys (Ki) of approximately 26.95 million USIMs, including those of SKT and budget phone subscribers and IoT lines and even personal information such as names, dates of birth, phone numbers, and email addresses had been leaked. The total leaked data volume amounts to 9.82 GB. Multiple media outlets are reporting that a China-nexus group tracked as Red Menshen and Earth Bluecrow is responsible for the compromise based on the use of the BPFDoor malware associated with the actor.

On 13 February 2025, the Baltimore City Public Schools system was affected by a ransomware attack launched by the Cloak ransomware gang. The attack resulted in the theft of information belonging to roughly 25,000 individuals, including current and former employees, volunteers, and contractors. Files also were related to around 1.5% of the student population (roughly 1,150 students). The stolen records likely contained Social Security numbers, drivers license numbers, or passport numbers for employees, while student data stolen included call logs, absenteeism records, and/or maternity status for students. The incident was reported by various news outlets, including The Baltimore Banner and 11 News WBALTV, and was confirmed by the school system in a data breach alert published on 22 April 2025. The school system did not pay a ransom. Law enforcement was contacted, and cybersecurity firms were hired to help the school system recover from the attack. Victims were offered two years of credit monitoring services, and a call centre was set up to answer questions about the incident.

In April 2025, Kaspersky observed an unidentified threat actor targeting various large organizations in Russia, spanning the government, finance, and industrial sectors.  The threat actor used a backdoor, masquerading as a secure networking software update for ViPNet, distributed inside LZH archives, which contained malicious files, including msinfo32.exe, which loaded the backdoor into memory. The backdoor allowed attackers to steal files from infected computers and launch additional malicious activities. Kaspersky solutions detected this threat as HEURTrojan.Win32.Loader.gen. The ViPNet developer confirmed intrusion activity against some of their users and issued security updates and recommendations for customers.

On 18 April 2025, the website of Wan Hai Lines, a Taiwanese freight shipping line, was targeted in what appeared to be a DDoS attack by unknown actors who prevented access to the website. The company's spokesperson, Su Limei, disclosed the disruption in a Taipei Stock Exchange filing on the same day.

On 21 April 2025, Afflelou, a French manufacturer of optical and acoustic devices such as glasses and hearing aids was targeted by threat actors exploiting a security flaw in one of its external providers to obtain personal data belonging to thousands of the company's customers; impacted data included names, dates of birth, postal and email addresses, telephone numbers, and purchases, though the company confirmed that no medical data or financial information (e.g., bank account information) was obtained during the breach. The company informed the affected customers by email and took corrective action with the assistance of cybersecurity experts, also notifying the National Commission on Informatics and Liberty (CNIL) in accordance with the GDPR.

On October 27, 2024, Laboratory Services Cooperative (LSC), a Seattle-based nonprofit organization, identified suspicious activity within its network and immediately engaged third-party cybersecurity specialists to determine the nature and scope of the incident, notifying federal law enforcement. The investigation revealed that an unauthorized third party gained access to portions of LSC's network and accessed/removed certain files, exposing sensitive information of roughly 1.6 million people, including personal identifiers, medical information, insurance information, and billing and financial data. The breach mainly affects individuals who had lab tests done through select Planned Parenthood centres that rely on LSC for their testing. LSC informed the public about the attack through a statement on April 10, 2025, and the Maine's AG Office was also notified.

On 18 April 2025, the government of Abilene, Texas, detected a breach that caused the city to shut down some of its systems. As a precaution, the city's IT staff took certain systems offline, while ensuring the continuous operation of emergency services. The intrusion resulted in disruptions to the city's card payment systems, requiring citizens to pay with cash, checks or online. The city pledged not to shut off utilities for past-due accounts. The incident was originally disclosed on 21 April. On 16 May, the Qilin ransomware group claimed responsibility for the attack and demanded a ransom payment within one week.

DaVita, a dialysis firm, was hit by a ransomware attack that encrypted some elements of its network, prompting the company to implement measures to limit the effect of the breach. The company discovered the incident on Saturday, April 12, 2025, but could not estimate the duration or extent of the disruption at that time. DaVita informed the public about the attack on the same day through a regulatory filing. On 24 April 2025, the Interlock ransomware gang claimed the attack. The group alleged to have stolen 1.5 terabytes of data from the healthcare company, or nearly 700,000 files of what appear to be sensitive patient records, information on user accounts, insurance, and even financial details.

Western Sydney University (WSU) was breached by a threat actor who compromised one of the university's single sign-on (SSO) systems between January and February 2025, resulting in the unauthorized access of demographic, enrolment, and progression information for approximately 10,000 current and former students. The university disclosed the incident on 11 April 2025.

A cyber attack occurred in Poland, exposing national identity documents and prosecutors' information, and was carried out against EuroCert, a company that issues qualified certificates, with the authorities investigating to minimize the exposure of sensitive data. The incident was a ransomware attack that was detected on 12 January 2025, and resulted in the encryption of files stored on EuroCert's servers. The affected data may include email addresses, phone numbers, PESEL numbers, names, dates and places of birth, citizenship, ID card or passport information, usernames, and passwords. The Polish police and CERT Polska initiated an investigation into the incident.

On 1 April 2025, the town hall of the French municipality of Loon-Plage was hit by a ransomware attack, which encrypted files. The attack spread to five computers and disrupted a series of municipal services. The municipality did not respond to a ransom demand and restored most services by 10 April.

On 8 April 2025, a hacker identifying as GOV.ETH breached Profile.com's publishing systems, editing several notes on the home page, uploading a photo of Argentina's President Javier Milei's identity card, and leaving aggressive messages against Jews and the President. The hacker, who claimed responsibility for the compromise, promoted their Telegram channel and reported previous violations, including the official page of the Argentine government. GOV.ETH, a self-described Socialist National, declared to have chosen Profile.com as a target over its identified vulnerabilities which they planned to expose. In an anonymous conversation with Profile.com, GOV.ETH suggested potential future targets, including the news portal Clarn, and expressed admiration for Adolf Hitler and Benito Mussolini, while repudiating President Milei and US President Donald Trump.

On 28 March 2025, a ransomware attack was carried out by an unknown actor on Sensata Technologies, a Massachusetts-based industrial tech manufacturer, impacting the company's systems and operations, including shipping, receiving, manufacturing production, and various other support functions. The attack, which was reported to the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on 6 April 2025, resulted in the company taking its network offline and contacting law enforcement. Cybersecurity experts were called in to assist with the recovery effort, and a preliminary investigation found evidence that files were taken from the company's environment. On 23 May, Sensata Technologies determined that sensitive information had been stolen, including full name, address, social security numbers (SSN), and medical information. The company informed current and former employees.

Title (Company): Moroccan Ministry of Economic Inclusion, Small Business, Employment and Skills
Description: On 8 April 2025, Jabaroot DZ, a group claiming to be a collective of Algerian hackers, targeted the official website of the Moroccan Ministry of Economic Inclusion, Small Business, Employment and Skills, specifically the National Social Security Fund (CNSS), by exploiting vulnerabilities, including through SQL injections, file modification, and remote code execution, which was previously warned about by a Moroccan expert on Facebook on 3 April. The attack temporarily disrupted access to the ministry's digital platform and leaked internal information, including the list of Moroccan employees, on a Telegram channel. The hackers claimed their activities were a response to Morocco's alleged harassment of Algerian social media accounts. CNSS confirmed the breach on 9 April 2025, but claimed that many of the allegedly leaked documents are "false, inaccurate or distorted". An OSINT investigation by Moroccan cybersecurity researchers, published on the blog Hack4 living on 9 April, identified links between the group and a cybersecurity specialist living in Germany, possibly of Tunisian origin.

On 8 April 2025, the Chicoloapan City Council's official social network accounts were hacked, resulting in the publication of inappropriate content on at least six social networks. The attackers uploaded explicit videos, generating reactions and outrage among followers. The municipal government confirmed the hack, filed a complaint with the police, and worked with cybersecurity specialists to resolve the incident. The authorities asked the population to report offensive publications and avoid sharing or interacting with false publications. This incident occurred after another hack was registered on the official Chicoloapan government page a few days prior.

On 9 April 2025, a joint advisory by the UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) and several international partners was published, outlining the methods and activities of Chinese state-sponsored hackers who have been observed in an ongoing campaign deploying two forms of previously-identified spyware, MOONSHINE and BADBAZAAR, against targets deemed of strategic interest for Chinese intelligence authorities. Namely, the spyware has been utilised in the ongoing campaign to snoop on Uyghur, Tibetan, and Taiwanese individuals and civil society organizations. According to the advisory, the spyware enables intruders to access the microphones and cameras, messages, photos, and location data of infected devices. The group utilised spyware-infected apps, including "Tibet One" and "Audio Quran," as well as other apps geared towards targeted victims' interests (i.e., apps using the languages of victims or purportedly "cultural" apps) and spread them through social media, as well as official app stores, since at least December 2021. Furthermore, popular platforms like WhatsApp and Skype were used to target individuals and organisations worldwide who are tied to activities considered by the Chinese state to pose a threat to its stability. NCSC Director of Operations Paul Chichester stated that the NCSC is warning at-risk populations to only use known app stores, check apps once installed and routinely review permissions, report questionable messages and files and carefully inspect shared files and links on social media.

On 8 April 2025, the Czech Prime Minister, Petr Fiala, denounced a cyberattack on his X account and that of his political coalition SPOLU, where, according to him, attackers from abroad published false messages, including one about a Russian attack on Czech soldiers near the Russian enclave of Kaliningrad and another post about retaliation for US tariffs. The post about the attack on Czech soldiers was confirmed by a government spokeswoman, Lucie Ješátková, to be false. The Czech Republic Police were informed and an investigation was launched to identify the perpetrators.

On 14 March 2025, a mutual insurance company from Venado Tuerto, Argentina, was the victim of a financial cyber theft when an administrative employee was targeted while using the digital banking system. The attackers, whose identities were not disclosed, used a popup window to trick the employee into providing credentials, allowing them to freeze her access to the system and to transfer 29 million pesos (roughly US$27,000) from the insurance company to an account at another bank. The incident was reported to the police by the affected employee and was investigated by the Public Prosecutor's Office. Following an investigation, the criminals' bank account was blocked, and the judge ordered the bank to retransfer the stolen funds to the original account.

Title (Company): Municipality of Saint-Justin - Saint-Lon-le-Grand - MRC of Maskinongé - Municipality of Saint-Sévère
Description: On 30 March 2025, at 5:00 AM, the regional county municipality (MRC) of Maskinongé (Canada) was targeted by cyber criminals, resulting in the paralysis of a part of its computer systems for over a week. The municipalities of Saint-Lon-le-Grand, Saint-Sévère, and Saint-Justin were also affected as a result of the incident. Prefect Paul Carbonneau confirmed that a ransom was demanded by the threat actors. The security authorities of Québec was notified of the incident and opened an investigation.

A 6 April 2025 report from the Ukrainian CERT reports that threat actors tracked by the CERT as UAC-0226 are impersonating Ukrainian drone manufacturers and state agencies to target strategically vital "centers of innovation development in the military sector, military formations, Ukrainian law enforcement agencies, and local governments, especially those located along the country's eastern border" in an ongoing campaign since at least February 2025. According to the CERT, UAC-0226 is using phishing lures related to demining, UAV production, administrative fines, and compensation for destroyed property to trick their victims into opening XLS documents containing malicious macros facilitating access for UAC-0226 to victim systems.

In March 2025, unknown hackers stole 9GB of data from the city hall of Thaon-les-Vosges, France, in a ransomware incident, with the hackers demanding several million euros, which the city hall did not pay.  Several weeks later, on 8 April 2025, hackers allegedly released the stolen data, which included hundreds of internal documents. The documents allegedly contained personal details such as names, identities, and personal contact details of employees and elected officials. The leak was reported by an online media outlet, Zataz, who observed that the data included files changed between 2017 and 2024, while the most recent files were dated 3 March 2025, suggesting that exfiltration occurred after this period.  The French cybersecurity agency ANSSI was alerted about the incident and launched an investigation.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: On 8 April 2025, Microsoft released information about a zero-day in the Windows Common Log File System (CLFS) that was actively exploited by a group tracked as Storm-2460 in a series of ransomware attacks against various organisations worldwide. According to Microsoft, targeted institutions included victims in the IT and real estate sectors in the United States, the financial sector in Venezuela, a Spanish software company, and the retail sector in Saudi Arabia. The attackers used the PipeMagic malware to exploit the vulnerability (CVE-2025-29824), which has a CVSS score of 7.8, allowing them to escalate privileges and gain access to sensitive data.

Title (Company): Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) - Not available
Description: Unknown hackers breached the US Treasury Department's Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) in June 2023 and maintained this access until 12 February 2025, obtaining over 150,000 emails, including highly sensitive information relating to the financial condition of federally regulated financial institutions and allowing the unidentified threat actors to spy on bank regulators, after breaking into an email system administrator's account at the OCC.  Bloomberg first reported the incident, and the OCC notified the US Congress of a major information security incident on 8 April 2025, stating that the system administrative account compromised in the breach was disabled on 12 February 2025.

Title (Company): Insignia Financial - REST - AustralianSuper - Hostplus - Australian Retirement Trust
Description: In early April 2025, an unknown threat actor attacked some of the country's largest profit-to-member superannuation funds with millions of members each and managing tens or hundreds of billions—including AustralianSuper, Hostplus, REST and Australian Retirement Trust, and Insignia Financial breaching over 20,000 accounts in these attacks. AustralianSuper, which manages the retirement savings of over 3.5 million members from over 472,000 businesses, totalling over $365 billion, confirmed that the attackers breached at least 600 accounts using stolen credentials. The Association of Superannuation Funds of Australia (ASFA), Australia's advocacy body for the superannuation industry, said today that "a number of members were affected" resulting in some compromised data even though the "majority of the attempts were repelled."

On 29 March 2025, Spectos GmbH, a third-party data collection and analytics service provider for Royal Mail, was breached by a threat actor using the handle 'GHNA' on BreachForums, who gained access to customer data, including personally identifiable information of Royal Mail customers, by using credentials of a Spectos employee compromised in a 2021 info stealer malware incident according to the cybersecurity company Hudson Rock. The breach resulted in the leak of over 144GB of data, including 16,549 files, containing customer personally identifiable information, internal Zoom meeting video recordings between Spectos and Royal Mail Group, delivery and post office location datasets, Mailchimp mailing lists, and a WordPress SQL database for mailagents.uk. Royal Mail confirmed that there was no impact on their operations.

On 31 March 2025, the Stell Hospital in the French city of Rueil-Malmaison was hit by a ransomware attack, which infected all of the hospital's computer systems, forcing the facility to operate without digital assistance. The hospital's IT team responded urgently, insulating the networks to contain the attack, and an emergency fund was used to deploy new equipment and reconstruct a semblance of operation. The National Police is investigating. The hospital's management instructed staff to change passwords and to be vigilant, and security protocols were strengthened. The incident impacted the hospital's operations, with caregivers using paper and pen, and care slowed down.

The INC ransomware gang infiltrated the State Bar of Texas, a bar association with over 100,000 licensed attorneys and the second-largest of such professional unions in the US, between 28 January and 9 February 2025, as discovered on 12 February. According to the association, INC gained unauthorized access during this period and stole information, including full names and other personal details redacted in the filing with the Texas Attorney General's office. INC ransomware gang took responsibility for the incident and leaked samples of allegedly stolen files, including legal case documents, on the dark web on 9 March 2025. The association publicly disclosed the breach on 3 April 2025.

Title (Company): Revenue Administration (Türkiye) - General Directorate of Population and Citizenship Affairs - Turkish Employment Agency - Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change - Presidency of Social Security Institution - Adana Yuregir Municipality - Altinbas University - Tinaztepe University - Nisantasi University - Ministry of National Defense - Ministry of Health - Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge and Northern Ring Motorway Operation - Ministry of Education (Türkiye) - Dumlupınar University
Description: According to an indictment on 3 April 2025, on unnamed dates in 2021, a gang of cyber criminals in Türkiye stole personal information of 101 million citizens through intrusions into the systems of 17 public institutions in Türkiye. The targeted institutions included the Department of Health, Ministry of Environmental Urbanism and Climate Change, Ministry of National Education, and the Ministry of National Defense, among others. The hackers hid the data on virtual servers from abroad, and the incident was reported by Mesut Haan Benli of Hurriyet on 3 April 2025.

A China-linked espionage actor, tracked as UTA0178/UNC5221, exploited a critical Connect Secure remote code execution vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2025-22457, in Ivanti Connect Secure (“ICS”) VPN appliances version 22.7R2.5 and earlier, to deploy malware, including TRAILBLAZE, BRUSHFIRE, and SPAWN, since at least mid-March 2025. The vulnerability, due to a stack-based buffer overflow weakness, was patched by Ivanti on 11 February 2025, with the release of Ivanti Connect Secure 22.7R2.6. Ivanti disclosed the vulnerability to the public on 3 April 2025.

Title (Company): Jackpot Junction - Lower Sioux Indian Community - Lower Sioux Health Care Center
Description: The Lower Sioux Indian Community in Minnesota was targeted in an incident that disrupted the local healthcare facility, government center, and casino, specifically Jackpot Junction, which is controlled by the tribe. The attack, discovered on systems connected to the casino, forced the tribe to activate incident response protocols and take measures to contain the incident, including taking some systems offline. Government officials first notified the public of issues on 28 March 2025. The tribe worked with third-party experts to address the incident and provided temporary phone numbers for essential services. The attack was claimed by the RansomHub ransomware gang and occurred in late March 2025, with the tribe warning residents on Wednesday, 3 April 2025, about the disruptions caused by the incident.

On 21 March 2025, the ransomware group PLAY targeted the Regionale Verkehrsbetriebe Baden-Wettingen (RVBW), demanding a ransom and threatening to publish stolen data by 6 April 2025. The RVBW refused to pay the ransom and isolated their IT infrastructure, cutting off external connections and conducting a security check on all computers. The attack resulted in the encryption of some data, but no customer data was affected. The incident had no impact on the RVBW's bus operations, but some digital signs at bus stops were temporarily out of order. The RVBW is working with the Swiss federal criminal police to investigate the attack and improve their IT security measures. The incident was first reported on 3 April 2025.

In August 2022, hackers accessed certain systems of Advanced Computer Software Group Ltd's health and care subsidiary via a customer account that did not have multifactor authentication (MFA), resulting in a ransomware incident that put the personal information of 79,404 people at risk. The attack caused disruption to critical services such as NHS 111, and other healthcare staff were unable to access patient records. The Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) investigated and fined Advanced £3.07m for security shortcomings on 29 March 2025, noting gaps in the deployment of MFA, a lack of comprehensive vulnerability scanning, and inadequate patch management.

On 2 April 2025, unidentified threat actors targeted the computer system of the Civic Platform, a Polish political party led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. Tusk identified an "eastern source," possibly Russia or Belarus for the malicious activity and linked the incident to "foreign election interference." Several leaders of Civic Platform, including the head of the Prime Minister's Chancellery, Jan Grabiec, also confirmed the incident, which allegedly affected the computers of both the Civic Platform office employees and the election headquarters; he also asserted that there was "concrete evidence pointing to the modus operandi of the Eastern secret services," without providing further details. Grabiec stated that the attackers utilized the Civic Platform's website to access the systems used by the party's electoral apparatus, which are used to coordinate the presidential campaign. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Digital Affairs, Krzysztof Gawkowski, stated that the police were working to investigate, while no data theft was detected due to rapid action by the Polish services.  The attack occurred just before the first round of the presidential elections, scheduled for 18 May 2025, and was seen as an attempt to influence the campaign and destabilize electoral preparations. The Polish Minister of Digital Affairs, Krzysztof Gawkowski, later confirmed that the attack was carried out by groups related to the Russian Federation and Belarus.

On 21 March 2025, the ransomware group RansomHub published a post on the darknet claiming to have stolen 92 gigabytes of data from a US subsidiary of MAN Truck & Bus, according to a MAN spokesperson. RansomHub claimed responsibility for the attack, but did not disclose the exact nature of the stolen data, and while MAN did not officially comment on the incident and the nature of stolen data, the company responded to an email from CSO that "a cybercriminal" had accessed the systems of the US subsidiary, while also stating that the central IT systems of MAN were unaffected and that the subsidiary is taking immediate action to remedy the effects of the incident.

On 31 March 2025, Russia's state-owned railway, RZD, was targeted by a DDoS attack, which temporarily disrupted its website and mobile application. The attack was reported by RZD on Tuesday, and ticket sales remained operational at physical offices.

On 31 March 2025, the website of the Moscow subway system was defaced and the system itself disrupted by unknown hackers, possibly in retaliation for an attack against Ukraine's national railway operator the week prior. The website of the Moscow metro system displayed a message made to look as if it had been authored by Ukraine's national railway operator, Ukzaliznytsia, which itself was the victim of a cyberattack the week before. The post mimicked the defacement message left on the Ukrainian railway system's website. According to transport officials, the website of Moscow's metro system was inaccessible due to "technical maintenance". Officials did not confirm outside interference. This lack of public confirmation contrats with reports by Roskomnadzor, Russia's internet regulator, of disruptions and observations from passengers on 31 March about service disruptions that prevented them from topping up their subway cards remotely or recharging cards at stations. The transport authority did not immediately provide any assessment as to whether these disruptions had a connection to the defacement.

On 11 September 2021, Canadian citizen Aubrey Cottle, also known by his moniker "Kirtaner," a hacker and early member of the hacktivist group Anonymous, breached the Texas Republican Party's website, defacing it with conspiracy theory-related texts. He managed to gain access to the website through its hosting provider, Epik. In addition, Cottle downloaded personal information from an Apache backup web server owned by the Texas chapter of the Republican Party, which was later released publicly via BitTorrent as a 180-gigabyte file of stolen data. Cottle gained access to the website through a breach of its hosting provider, Epik. The FBI identified him through his social media posts, including a TikTok video taking credit for the hack. The FBI used these posts to subpoena records from a Discord channel Cottle had created, where he had discussed the hack and claimed to have root access to Epik's network. On 30 August 2022, the Ontario Provincial Police raided Cottle's home, seizing 20 terabytes of data, including emails and a solid-state drive containing personal data obtained during the breach. In March 2025, the Department of Justice unsealed charges against Cottle, who was charged with identity theft and faces a maximum sentence of five years in prison.

Tokiwa Industry, a supermarket chain of the Japanese department store chain Tokiwa, was the victim of a disruptive cyber incident on 30 March 2025, according to a press release by the company from 1 April.  According to Tokiwa, the incident was discovered on 30 March as the product ordering system of Tokiwa Industry was taken down, while several systems of Tokiwa were allegedly encrypted by the unknown hackers. Tokiwa clarified that no customer information had been permanently deleted and no leak of personal information had been detected. The disruption caused Tokiwa Industry to shut down all 23 stores in Japan's Oita Province while recovery efforts and an investigation were underway.

The China-linked threat actor Earth Alux has been observed by Trend Micro researchers in a report published on 31 March 2025 to be targeting various key sectors, including government, technology, logistics, manufacturing, telecommunications, IT services, and retail in both the Asia-Pacific and Latin American regions, since at least 2023. TrendMicro's report states that Earth Alux initially focussed its efforts on the Asia-Pacific region, but since mid-2024 has been observed targeting South America as well.  The campaign involves exploiting vulnerable services in internet-exposed web applications to drop web shells, such as GODZILLA, which facilitated the deployment of additional payloads, including backdoors dubbed VARGEIT and COBEACON. VARGEIT was used to load tools directly from its command-and-control server to a newly spawned process of Microsoft Paint for reconnaissance, collection, and exfiltration, while COBEACON was employed as a first-stage backdoor. The threat actors also utilized a loader component code-named RAILLOAD, which was executed using DLL sideloading, and a persistence and timestomping module referred to as RAILSETTER.
Techniques Used: Automated Exfiltration, Exfiltration Over C2 Channel, Exploit Public-Facing Application

Description: Sometime after 22 January 2025, unknown threat actors compromised servers of the US software company Oracle, specifically older servers belonging to Cerner, a US healthcare IT company acquired by Oracle in 2022 and later renamed to Oracle Health. The threat actor copied patient data to an outside location, in an attempt to extort multiple medical providers in the United States. The FBI launched a probe into the incident as reported by Bloomberg News on 28 March 2025, citing a person familiar with the matter. Oracle became aware of the breach around 20 February 2025 and notified customers about the breach. According to the notification, the breach affected data on former Cerner servers that had not yet been migrated to Oracle's cloud storage. At the time of reporting it remained unclear how many patient records were affected and which healthcare providers were subsequently targeted as part of the extortion scheme. In January 2026, Munson Healthcare, another US-based healthcare provider, confirmed that its data was stolen through the breach of Cerner.

On the night of 25 to 26 March 2025, unknown threat actors targeted the servers of the Municipality of Maria Enzersdorf in Austria. The incident disrupted the municipality's IT systems, but all analogue services, including citizen support at the town hall, the public works department, and local kindergartens, continued to operate normally. Specialist firms were engaged to address the issue, and the relevant authorities, including law enforcement and the data protection officer, were informed

China-nexus group FamousSparrow deployed an upgraded version of the proprietary backdoor SparrowDoor to target a US-based trade organization and a Mexican research institute in July 2024. The threat actors gained initial access via exploitation of outdated Microsoft Exchange and Windows Server endpoints, infecting them with webshells. The new malware version features improved code quality, encrypted configuration, and stealthy command-and-control switching, as well as parallel command execution and a plugin-based architecture. ESET researchers reported the activities on 26 March 2025.

The largest South African chicken producer Astral Foods told investors on 24 March 2025 that it suffered a cyberattack on 16 March 2025, causing “downtime in processing and deliveries to customers” that resulted in lost revenue and backlogs. Astral Foods said it lost about 20 million rand worth of profits, equivalent to around $1 million. At the date of this announcement, on 24 March 2025, Astral Foods stated that all business units are operating normally following the recovery of our systems. Astral confirmed that no confidential information or sensitive data of customers, suppliers or individual stakeholders was compromised as a result of the intrusion.

Unknown actors gained remote control over computers belonging to the municipality of Merlevenez in Morbihan, France, by installing spyware. They attempted to place large orders to companies, including for telecommunication allowances worth €25,000 from Bouygues and for computer and multimedia equipment worth over €125,000 from Lenovo, by usurping the identity of the General Manager of Services, Gwenal Chauvel. The breach was discovered on 12 March 2025 when the companies, distrustful of the large-volume orders, contacted the Director General of Services. The hackers also tried to change the bank details to receive outstanding payments. The town hall of Merlevenez filed a complaint for computer hacking and identity usurpation. The incident was publicly disclosed on 27 March 2025.

On 22 March 2025, an individual hacker, claiming to be part of a larger hacking group with the acronym CNE, which contains a racial slur [and is therefore only referenced by the acronym here], accessed NYU's IT systems without authorisation, took control of the systems directing web traffic to NYU's website, and defaced the NYU homepage, exposing admissions data on approximately 1 million students. The hacker claimed to have redacted personal information but actually leaked full names, addresses, phone numbers, grade point averages, email addresses, and citizenship status. NYU spokesperson John Beckman informed the public about the incident, stating that the university's IT team worked with a cybersecurity consultant to regain control of the system and redirect traffic back to its real website in less than three hours. The incident was reported to law enforcement authorities, and the university is working to provide notice to anyone whose personal information was subject to unauthorised access. The hacker claimed the intrusion was in response to the Supreme Court decision in 2023 striking down affirmative action, aiming to prove that schools are not abiding by the ruling. [Note on threat actor identification: The full name of the allegedly associated hacker is listed in the initiator category solely for documentation purposes. The European Repository of Cyber Incidents strongly opposes reproducing offensive terms that may form part of the name by which threat actors refer to themselves.]

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: According to a Cisco Talos Intelligence threat report from 20 March 2025, the China-linked APT group UAT-5918 is targeting core Taiwanese infrastructure, including major industries like telecommunications, healthcare, information technology, and other critical infrastructure sectors in a persistent espionage campaign tracing back to at least 2023. According to Talos, the group specializes in establishing under-the-radar long-term access in victims' networks and has been observed infiltrating vulnerable web and application servers to open multiple points of entry to victim organisations. In the report, Talos links the UAT-5918 to other Chinese state-sponsored APTs, including Volt Typhoon, Flax Typhoon and Dalbit, with the majority of TTPs overlapping with Volt Typhoon.

On the morning of Tuesday, 25 March 2025, unknown hacker(s) stole approximately $13 million worth of digital currency from Abracadabra Finance, a decentralised cryptocurrency platform. Only after the transactions were executed did Abracadabra catch the exploit. The company acknowledged the incident on social media, stating the issue was sourced back to a product called "cauldrons," which are isolated lending markets that allow users to borrow against various cryptocurrencies. In the wake of the theft, Abracadabra initiated an investigation alongside experts. The blockchain security company Chainalysis tracked the stolen funds, which included 6,260 ETH ($12.9 million). Abracadabra Finance offered a bug bounty to the hacker of 20% of the stolen funds.

Title (Company): Malaysia Airports Holdings Berhad (MAHB) - Kuala Lumpur International Airport
Description: Malaysia Airports Holdings Berhad (MAHB) was the victim of a ransomware incident by Qilin who demanded US$10 million on 23 March 2025. The attack resulted in several systems of MAHB being shut down, while spillover effects were allegedly felt for Kuala Lumpur International Airport, which saw severe flight delays and information screens disrupted. Check-in and baggage claims were also allegedly impacted, according to Malaysian media. A former Malaysian Member of Parliament Wee Choo Keong claimed that systems at KLIA were "down for more than 10 hours". However, a joint statement released by MAHB and the National Cybersecurity Agency (NACSA) disputed this, saying KLIA had no system disruptions as a result of the attack. In the meantime, an investigation was initiated into the impact.

On 27 June 2024, unknown cybercriminals breached the systems of a long-term care facility, Hillcrest Convalescent Center in North Carolina (USA), and stole the data of 106,000 patients. The data included sensitive personal information from patients, such as name, date of birth, Social Security number, patient data, medical information, treatment information, health insurance information, and Health Care Provider information, according to Hillcrest's notice of the data breach. Hillcrest released their advisory on 3 March 2025, following the conclusion of an investigation into the incident in February 2025.

On 21 March 2025, a DDoS attack was launched against Russian provider Lovit, targeting its critical infrastructure and resources, including its mobile app, official website, and personal accounts of users. Roskomnadzor reported the attack on 24 March 2025. TASS informed the public about the incident.

In mid-March 2025, Kaspersky detected a wave of infections by previously unknown and "highly sophisticated" malware which was utilised in an ongoing phishing campaign allegedly by state-sponsored actors targeting Russian entities, particularly educational institutions and media outlets. Kaspersky dubbed the operation "ForumTroll" due to its targeting patterns and phishing theme. The attackers sent personalized phishing emails related to a scientific and expert forum called "Primakov Readings;" the emails contained malicious links that, when clicked, infected the victims' devices via a Google Chrome zero-day exploit chain, specifically exploiting the CVE-2025-2783 vulnerability, which Google fixed on 25 March 2025, following disclosure by Kaspersky. The malware was designed to run in conjunction with an additional exploit for remote code execution. On 27 October 2025, Kaspersky published further reporting on Operation ForumTroll, stating that it is like that tools and infrastructure used by the threat actor are linked to the Italian spyware company Memento Labs (formerly operating as Hacking Team).

As reported on 12 February 2025, the University of Notre Dame Australia (Fremantle) was breached by the Fog ransomware group in January 2025, resulting in the theft of 62.2 GB of data, including student medical documents, employee and student contact details, and confidential documents, with the Fog ransomware group claiming responsibility in February 2025 for the attack.

On 15 March 2025, unknown threat actors caused network and communication outages affecting the administration of Strafford County in the US state of New Hampshire, limiting services such as email and phone services, and a local nursing home's access to county systems holding medical data. Strafford County Commissioner Chair George Maglaras informed the public about the disruption through statements to the media.

Ukraine's state-owned railway company, Ukrzaliznytsia (UZ), experienced an outage of its online sytems on 23 March 2025, as disclosed by the company on Telegram. Later, the company confirmed that it was a cyber attack. UZ described the incident as a systemic, non-trivial, and multilevel disruption but ruled out any effects for rail traffic. Cargo documentation was switched to paper-based processes until the online system could be restored. Online ticketing services were unavailable, increasing waiting times at ticket counters. Several international travelers with electronic tickets issued by UZ that could not provide proof of pruchase because of the disruptions were reportedly fined by Hungarian railway workers when transiting through Hungry.

Title (Company): European Sea Ports Organisation (ESPO) - City of Enghien - Federal Public Service Economy - MyGov.be - Municipality of Wezembeek-Oppem - Walloon Parliament - Municipality of Sint-Genesius-Rode - Municipality of Wemmel
Description: The Russia-linked hacktivist group NoName057(16) launched DDoS-type attacks against several official Belgian websites, including the e-government portal MyGov.be and the website of the regional Walloon Parliament, on 24 March 2025. On its Telegram channel, the group declared that the operation was carried out in response to a new aid package of €1 billion adopted by Belgium in support of Ukraine. Belgian Defence Minister Theo Francken pledged the package to Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky during a meeting in early March. The Walloon Parliament stated that the disruption attempt only briefly interfered with access to the website.  The following day, on 25 March 2025, NoName057(16) launched several more DDoS attacks on Belgian websites, including the websites of the Federal Public Service Economy, the European Sea Ports Organisation (ESPO), the Municipality of Sint-Genesius-Rode, the Municipality of Wemmel, the Municipality of Wezembeek-Oppem, and the City of Enghien.  From 14 to 17 July 2025, an international law enforcement operation code-named Eastwood was launched against NoName057(16). Coordinated by Europol and Eurojust, the operation involved simultaneous actions by authorities in Czechia, France, Finland, Germany, Italy, Lithuania, Poland, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the Netherlands, and the United States, targeting individuals and digital infrastructure linked to the pro-Russian network. Operation Eastwood allowed for the deactivation of several hundred servers supporting the group’s DDoS activities. Overall, national authorities issued seven arrest warrants, including against six Russian nationals, over the suspected involvement in NoName057(16). The investigation further facilitated the arrest of two individuals in France and Spain. Law enforcement personally notified over 1,000 supporters of the group, including 15 suspected administrators, of their legal liability related to the participation in NoName057(16)‘s criminal activities.

The China-nexus group Weaver Ant collected data from a major Asian telecommunications provider's network over a period of at least for years stretching from 2021 to 2025. The group compromised Zyxel CPE routers of Southeast Asian telecommunication providers to hide traffic and infrastructure. The threat actor established a foothold on the network by using an AES-encrypted variant of the China Chopper web shell, and introduced a more advanced, custom-build web shell known as INMemory to execute payloads in memory. Weaver Ant used data exfiltration methods such as passive network traffic capturing via port mirroring, and linked web shells together in a technique called web shell tunneling to create a covert command-and-control network inside the victim's infrastructure. The group moved laterally using SMB shares and high-privileged accounts, and collected configuration files, access logs, and credential data. To remain undetected, the group disabled logging mechanisms. The breach was reported by Sygnia on 24 March 2025, which attributed the attack to a state-sponsored actor citing the group's the use of an Operational Relay Box (ORB) networkof mostly composed of hijacked Zyxel routers, backdoors previously linked to Chinese threat groups, and the operation of Weaver Ant during GMT 8 business hours.
Techniques Used: Automated Exfiltration, Exploit Public-Facing Application, Valid Accounts

Description: Hackers compromised government systems of Union County in the US state of Pennsylvania in an incident discovered on 13 March 2025. The breach resulted in the theft of personal information, particularly affecting individuals involved with County law enforcement, including Social Security numbers and drivers license numbers as well as information on court-related matters and other County business. Federal law enforcement was notified, and forensic experts were hired to help with the recovery process. The County published a notice on 21 March 2025 warning its more than 40,000 residents about the incidents.

On 27 February 2025, unidentified hackers carried out a cyber attack on Harvest, a financial software provider. The attack resulted in a data leak affecting two French banks, MAIF and BPCE. Exposed information included marital status, marital and professional status, identity, title, account number, and outstanding balance of a limited number of customers. Jrme Notin, CEO of Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr, informed the public about the attack and disclosed measures to be taken against phishing and identity usurpation on 24 March 2025. The attackers did not claim the incident.

Title (Company): Presidency of the Republic of Costa Rica
Description: On Friday, 21 March 2025, the official YouTube account of Costa Rican President Rodrigo Chaves was hijacked by unidentified perpetrators, who replaced the profile's content with a logo labelled 'Strategy' alongside a bitcoin symbol and uploaded videos related to cryptocurrency transactions. The incident, which lasted several hours, was resolved late Friday night after experts from the president's office, the science and technology ministry, and Google worked together to regain control. The incident was reported by various news outlets, including Reuters, on 21 and 22 March 2025. The YouTube profile of the Presidential House, with over 75,000 followers, was affected, and old videos, such as the National Chain and live broadcasts, were kept on the profile, but content of the home screen was changed to show videos promoting cryptocurrency.

Title (Company): Islamic Republic of Iran Shippping Lines (IRISL) - National Iranian Tanker Company (NITC)
Description: On 21 March 2025, the supposedly Iranian, anti-regime hacktivist group Lab Dookhtegan claimed to have carried out a cyber attack that disrupted communications on 116 Iranian cargo ships. The attack targeted the communication network of two Iranian companies, National Iranian Tanker Company (NITC) and Islamic Republic of Iran Shipping Lines (IRISL), which are sanctioned by the US Department of the Treasury, the UK, and the European Union. The companies are responsible for supplying munitions to Houthi rebels in Yemen. Lab Dookhtegan did not provide specific information on its uses of TTPs, but as Cydome noted, open-source reporting indicates the group likely exploited vulnerabilities in the maritime satellite communication systems that these ships rely on. The hackers interfered with communications between ships, ports, and external third parties, affecting 50 NITC vessels and 66 IRISL vessels. Cydome further state that based on the information presented by the hackers, they were able to take full control of the communications system, with elevated credentials, full access to the ships’ networks and ability to remotely execute malicious code. The owners would take weeks to restore their communications systems fully. The high degree of automation and coordination in the attack suggests advanced capabilities, including prior reconnaissance of the fleet's IT infrastructure. Iran International also reported on the purported event.

Title (Company): German Society for Eastern European Studies (DGO)
Description: The German Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution warned German NGOs about Russian espionage efforts in March 2025. The warning was sent to dozens of foundations, associations, and organisations. The Russian state-sponsored hacking group, allegedly linked to the Russian state, gained unauthorized access to the email accounts of the German Society for Eastern European Studies (DGO) and monitored their communication for several months, after the DGO was labelled as an 'extremist organisation' by the Russian Ministry of Justice on 1 July 2024. The DGO's managing director, Gabriele Freitag, described the incident as an 'escalation' by the Russian state. The intrusion was reported by NDR, WDR, and SZ, and was disclosed to the public on 21 March 2025. The warning also mentioned that Russia increasingly restricts the scope of action of foreign organisations by listing them as 'undesirable' or 'extremist', often accompanied by hacker attacks on their IT systems. The Deutsche Gesellschaft für Auswärtige Politik (DGAP) was also declared an 'undesirable organisation' by Russian authorities.

Between 20 April and 22 April 2024, an unknown threat actor infiltrated the systems of US sperm donation and cryopreservation firm California Cryobank (CCB). On 14 March 2025, CCB confirmed a 2024 data breach that resulted in threat actors accessing customer information. A subsequent investigation found affected files included bank account and routing numbers, payment card numbers, and health insurance information.

On 23 March 2025, it became public that Cerballiance Laboratory was affected in the theft of several thousand personal data, including names, first names, email addresses, and cell phone numbers. The intrusion was detected around 13 March 2025. As a result, the hackers obtained a security code allowing them to access certain personal data, in order to sell it on the black market. The management of Cerballiance reassured customers that health and Social Security data were not compromised. Cerballiance`s IT staff stopped the breach and contacted victims individually. A complaint was filed, systems and passwords were strengthened.

Title (Company): Buquebus Turismo - Ministry of Social Development (Mides) - National Directorate of Civil Aviation and Aeronautical Infrastructure (Dinacia)
Description: An unidentified threat actor breached the Ministry of Social Development (Mides) and leaked hundreds of documents, including 264 internal documents and 275 scans of national identity documents, one of which contained data on teenage pregnancies with the names of expecting parents. Upon releasing the documents on 19 March 2025, the hacker claiming to be in possession of access credentials for Mides systems that they planned to leak. At the time of reporting, this claim had not been independently verified. Mides confirmed that they are aware of the leak and are investigating the attack in collaboration with the Agency for Electronic Governance and the Information and Knowledge Society (Agesic) and in compliance with applicable regulations regarding the protection of personal data.

In 2024, the China-aligned MirrorFace APT group carried out cyberespionage activity against a Central European diplomatic institute in relation to Expo 2025, which will be held in Osaka, Japan, and a Japanese research institute by using a customized AsyncRAT and reviving the ANEL backdoor. ESET researchers detected the activity and presented these findings at the Joint Security Analyst Conference (JSAC) on January 2025. On 8 January 2025, the Japanes government attributed the cyberattack to MirrorFace.

On 19 March 2025, the X account of Argentine national deputy José Luis Espert was taken over by an unknown group to promote the $LIBRA cryptocurrency. Espert's advisor, Jimena Aristizbal, confirmed the incident and reported that the team had lost access to the account. The hackers are believed to have used AI tools to generate material portraying Espert as supporting new cryptocurrencies. Espert regained control over the account within several hours.

Atchison County in Kansas detected and responded to a cyber incident that impacted its computer network, prompting the closure of its offices on Tuesday, 18 March 2025, as announced by county officials on social media.

Title (Company): National Directorate of Civil Aviation and Aeronautical Infrastructure
Description: On 18 March 2025, a group of right-wing hackers known as La Pampa Leaks, potentially from Argentina, compromised the official website of the National Directorate of Civil Aviation and Aeronautical Infrastructure (DINACIA) in Uruguay. The attackers exposed personal information of Uruguayan President Yamandu Orsi, including one of his phone numbers, and threatened other leaders and officials. The hack occurred on the anniversary day of the Uruguayan Air Force. The attackers claimed to have intercepted emails and had access to sensitive information, which they threatened to make public. Local journalist Eduardo Preve reported the attack. The government reported a 'security incident' and the Cybercrime Unit of the National Police and the Agency for Electronic Governance and the Information and Knowledge Society (Agesic) worked to identify the origin of the attack and its perpetrators. The attack was first reported by local media, including El Observador and Underline, and was later confirmed by President Orsi in statements to the press. On 30 March 2025, an 18-year-old was charged with 180 days of pretrial detention for hacking the websites of state agencies and private companies including the website of the DINACIA.

On March 17, 2023, China's state security ministry (MSS) accused four individuals linked to Taiwan’s military of cyberattacks and espionage. According to the MSS, the suspects are part of Taiwan’s Information, Communications, and Electronic Force Command unit (ICEFCOM), which has allegedly targeted China’s infrastructure, including power grids and telecommunications, since 2023. Beijing claims ICEFCOM hired hackers and cybersecurity firms for cyber warfare, using phishing attacks and disinformation campaigns under aliases like Anonymous 64. More specifically, the MSS stated that their tactics include infiltrating China’s critical infrastructure, sending phishing and propaganda emails, stealing login credentials to hijack online platforms for counter propaganda, and using bots on social media to spread disinformation, manipulate public opinion, and suppress dissent. However, China provided no concrete evidence for the attribution claim. Taiwan’s Premier Cho Jung-tai dismissed the accusations as fabricated to justify Beijing’s own cyber activities against Taiwan. After the MSS statement, three Chinese cybersecurity firms—QiAnXin, Antiy, and Anheng Information—released reports on APT-Q-20, a suspected Taiwan-linked cyber group active since 2006. The group allegedly targets Chinese government, military, and research institutions for sensitive data.

On March 2025, unknown hackers attacked The Municipality of Murca in the early hours, which interrupted the access to various platforms and digital services of the municipality. Further details on the extend of attack itself and the time until all services running normally are still missing.

On 28 February 2025, unknown hackers accessed the Play Bridge Vault and stole over 8.6 million WEMIX tokens. The company publicly disclosed the hack on 4 March, four days after discovering it. An unknown group of attackers managed to infiltrate Wemix’s NFT platform Nile after stealing an authentication key for monitoring purposes. The attackers spent two months designing their operation while deploying transaction protocols.

On 11 March 2025, a ransomware leak page for Edesur Dominicana, a power distribution company in the Dominican Republic, was published by the hacker group Hunters International including screenshots of potentially stolen data. The leak indicates that data has been exfiltrated from the organization but specifies that the data is not encrypted. Dominicana confirmed an intrusion of its systems on the same day.

On March 2025, unknown hackers breached the network of the Pelham School District. Superintendent Chip McGee said the district will be offline for the next two weeks while an investigation continues into what happened and workers get everything back online. In the meantime, students remained without have access to their Chromebooks and teachers were without access to their Google Drive file repositories and email inboxes.

Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said on 17 March 2025 that an old phone and email account of hers were hacked by unknown hackers. The president clarified that the personal telephone number active on the hacked device had already been leaked in February 2024, when she was a presidential candidate. Sheinbaum noted during a daily press conference that she had given the required warnings when she became aware of the hacking, and added that the email account was old and the phone is no longer used for "personal communication" but to talk to her supporters. It is not yet known to what extent the phone was compromised or whether any emails were stolen. The compromises occured shortly after Mexico agreed to handing over 29 drug traffickers to the United States on February 27.

The North Korean APT37 was observed distributing spyware through five fake utility apps, targeting Korean and English-speaking end users. The campaign started as early as in 2022, while the latest malware samples were collected in 2024. Lookout Threat Labs, in its report from 12 March 2025, indicated that the spyware remained active. Lookout linked the campaign to APT37 with medium confidence and also indicated that the infrastructure used in the KoSpy espionage campaign is likely shared with APT43 (Kimsuky), another North Korean threat actor. The spyware, known as KoSpy, was hidden in utility apps, including apps alleged to be a 'File Manager', a 'Software Update Utility' app, and 'Kakao Security', among other lures; it was distributed through the Google Play Store and third-party app stores. KoSpy collected extensive data from users who downloaded the apps, including SMS message data, call logs, location, files, audio, and screenshots. The threat actor also used a two-stage command-and-control infrastructure, retrieving initial configurations from a Firebase cloud database.

On 11 March 2025, a ransomware attack was carried out by unidentified hackers against the Department of Health Services for the state of Yap in Micronesia, resulting in all computers used by the government health agency being taken offline in order to "prevent further damage". The department worked with private IT contractors and other government agencies to restore services and determine the extent of the infiltration, without clarifying whether any data was actually encrypted, wiped, or stolen. Email communication and digital health systems were also shut down in response to the attack, but services continued with slower operations.

The Swiss locations of Dutch grocery store chain Spar, plus its partner TopCC stores, were the victims of a disruptive cyber incident that occurred on the night of 13-14 March 2025. The incident shut down computer systems and payment terminals, plus the goods ordering system of Spar. The attack was reported by Swiss media company Blick, which stated that Spar immediately called on specialists and filed a complaint, informing the Swiss Federal Data Protection and Transparency Officer. The incident was announced on Spar's website and social media channels on Saturday, 15 March 2025, with the company stating it is striving to restore its business as quickly as possible.

On 9 February 2025, the ransomware organisation CrazyHunter, which has been observed targeting primarily Taiwanese targets in healthcare, attacked Mackay Memorial Hospital in Taipei, according to a notice from the Taiwanese Ministry of Health and Welfare on 11 February. As a result, 500 computers were disrupted and allegedly over 16.6 million patient data was encrypted and stolen (32.5GB) from Mackay and its partner organisations across Taiwan.  On 28 February, an allegedly CrazyHunter-affiliated user of a hacker forum claimed to have the data, which was subsequently published and included names, ID numbers, mobile phone numbers, home addresses, and medical records included within this patient data. However, on 13 March 2025, another group named "Babuk" published 120GB of data allegedly from the hospital as well. TeamT5, a Taiwan-based cybersecurity company, promptly responded to the incident at Mackay and provided IoC intelligence, assisting the hospital in completing thorough scans of its environments. TeamT5 also linked the incident to CrazyHunter, though has not commented on Babuk's claims.

Following another incident at Mackay Memorial Hospital in Taiwan on 9 February 2025, CrazyHunter ransomware gang, which primarily targets Taiwanese organisations (specifically healthcare), launched another ransomware operation against Changhua Christian Hospital in Taiwan, in early March 2025. While the specifics of data stolen or encrypted were not clear, TeamT5 Threat Intelligence linked the attack to CrazyHunter's Mackay attack, which involved the encryption and exfiltration of data, as well as the disruption of hundreds of computers; similarly, the Taiwanese Ministry of Health and Welfare indicated that systems had been infiltrated by CrazyHunter, without clarifying further specifics. In the meantime, the Ministry of Health and Welfare coordinated with the Cybersecurity Administration to repair damaged systems; as of 4 March, secondary systems remained down as a result of the attack. The Ministry of Health and Welfare also referred to the back-to-back incidents as "systematic."  It should be noted that the exact date of the incident was not clarified, including the actual month; certain Taiwanese publications linked it to the end of February (28.02), while other publications and the TeamT5 report claimed it took place in "early March."

On 11 March 2025, the internet service provider TurkNet's database was targeted by an unknown hacker. The company confirmed the hack involving data theft but stated that it did not cover the financial information of the customers and TurkNet user passwords. In the statement from the company, it was noted that there were no interruptions due to the incident. A member of a Dark Web forum named "Hades_hgs", who claimed to be the hacker, posted a list of many user data including the name account, phone number, Turkish ID number, and open address.

In mid 2024, Mandiant discovered threat actors deployed custom backdoors on Juniper Networks’ Junos OS routers. Mandiant attributed these backdoors to the China-nexus espionage group UNC3886. They used a used a zero-day exploit that is now tracked as CVE-2025-21590 to install six custom backdoors. Mandiant worked with Juniper Networks to investigate this activity and observed that the affected Juniper MX routers were running end-of-life hardware and software. Although Juniper did not release fixes this time, the vendor published a bulletin that includes mitigation recommendations and updated signatures for its Juniper Malware Removal Tool (JMRT). Mandiant has not identified any technical overlaps between activities detailed in this blog post and those publicly reported by other parties as Volt Typhoon or Salt Typhoon. Juniper Networks has released emergency security updates to patch a Junos OS.

In early March 2025, New Zealand-based Vercoe Insurance Brokers fell victim to a ransomware attack carried out by the DragonForce group. The attackers claimed to have stolen over 60GB of data, disrupting the brokerage’s IT systems. Upon detecting the breach, Vercoe Insurance Brokers took immediate action, engaging external cybersecurity experts and notifying the Office of the Privacy Commissioner and the Financial Markets Authority. While all systems have since been restored, investigations into the extent of the data compromise are ongoing. Clients and relevant stakeholders have been informed, and the company has committed to notifying affected individuals if personal data is confirmed to have been exposed.

In early March 2025, the City of Lorient in France was targeted by unnamed actors stealing non-sensitive data from the city administration. This data included names, professional email addresses, and the administrative responsibilities of 5,000 people of former employees and 1,500 current workers. The compromise was disclosed by Steven Lehuédé, Deputy Director General of the City of Lorient, who warned of potential identity theft and advised users to be vigilant against fraudulent correspondence.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: In January 2025, Silk Typhoon was observed exploiting a zero-day vulnerability in the public facing Ivanti Pulse Connect VPN (CVE-2025-0282) uncovered by Microsoft Threat Intelligence. They identified that Silk Typhoon fka HAFNIUM, a Chinese espionage group, targeted common IT solutions, such as remote management tools and cloud applications, to gain initial access to organizations. The group exploited unpatched applications to elevate their access and conduct further malicious activities. After compromising a victim, Silk Typhoon fka HAFNIUM used stolen keys and credentials to infiltrate customer networks, where they abused deployed applications, including Microsoft services, to achieve their espionage objectives. In late 2024, the group shifted tactics to broaden access and enable follow-on attacks against downstream customers of its initial targets, specifically targeting IT management companies. Silk Typhoon fka HAFNIUM performed reconnaissance using stolen API keys and leaked corporate passwords, and gained access through password-spray attacks, zero-day exploits, and unpatched third-party services. The group primarily targeted IT providers, identity management platforms, privileged access management, and remote monitoring and management tools, and moved from on-premises to cloud environments by stealing Active Directory credentials and targeting Entra Connect servers. Silk Typhoon is targeting a wide range of sectors and geographic regions, including information technology (IT) services and infrastructure, remote monitoring and management (RMM) companies, managed service providers (MSPs) and affiliates, healthcare, legal services, higher education, defense, government, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), energy, and others located in the United States and in the rest of the world. Microsoft Threat Intelligence informed the public about the attack on 5 March 2025.
Techniques Used: Exploit Public-Facing Application, Trusted Relationship, Valid Accounts

Description: The government of Mission, Texas, was breached by cybercriminals, who targeted portions of their network, exposing all data held on city systems, and requiring systems to be taken offline. Emergency services remained operational. The attack started on 28 February 2025. The city declared a state of emergency. Mayor Norie Gonzalez Garza notified Texas Governor Greg Abbott. Law enforcement was contacted to investigate. The city government notified residents of the incident on 5 March 2025.

On Monday, 10 March 2025, the Dark Storm hacktivist group, a pro-Palestinian group that launched in 2023, claimed responsibility for a massive cyberattack against X (fka Twitter), causing multiple worldwide outages. According to security analysts, Dark Storm conducted five DDoS attacks against X, in varying lengths; the group posted screenshots and links to the checkhost.net site as proof of the attack on their Telegram channel. Furthermore, external cyber experts such as those with Cisco's ThousandEyes confirmed that network conditions also pointed to the attack being DDoS.  X owner Elon Musk confirmed that the outages were caused by a "massive cyberattack," alleging that the attack was carried out by a large, coordinated group or a country; later in the day, Musk linked the attack to Ukraine in an interview with Fox Business, saying that Ukrainian IPs were observed in the attack but offering no evidence to support his claims. However, other independent security analysts argued that the severity of the attack was likely due to many of the X origin servers not being properly secured by Cloudflare DDoS protection, and further contributing to the severity was the fact that the attack was likely from a Mirai botnet. Such a botnet, comprised of infected, old (unpatched) cameras and DVRs all acting together to launch the DDoS attacks, would also contradict Musk's claims that Ukrainian actors could have been behind the attack since Ukrainian IPs were observed; a botnet would have IPs from many places, not just Ukraine. Importantly, one anonymous security researcher from a "prominent firm" pointed out that Ukraine was not even in the top 20 IP address origins involved in the X attacks.
