Interestingly, some security analysts, such as those at Orange Cyberdefense, believe there may be a link to the Russian Federation, as evidenced by previous targeting patterns and coalitions built with Russian groups such as Killnet, Bluenet Russia, or the (potentially Russian) Anonymous Sudan group. As a result of the attack, X enabled DDoS protections from Cloudflare, which now shows a captcha when suspicious IP addresses connect to the site. The outages were also tracked by Downdetector, which reported tens of thousands of user reports from the US and over 8,000 reports from the UK. Alp Toker, director of Netblocks, suggested that the outages were consistent with a denial of service attack targeting X's infrastructure at scale.

On 5 February 2025, Japanese telecommunication services provider NTT Communications Corporation discovered that its facilities had been subjected to unauthorized access. By 6 February 2025, it was confirmed that some information might have been compromised. The hackers breached NTT's Order Information Distribution System, which held details on 17,891 corporate customers, including customer name, customer representatives' name, contract number, phone number, email address, physical address, and service usage information. NTT blocked the threat actors' access to the breached system by 6 February 2025, but the investigation revealed that the attackers had pivoted to another device on NTT's network by 15 February 2025. This device was promptly disconnected to prevent further lateral movement. NTT made a public announcement on its website on 7 March 2025, informing the affected corporate customers about the data breach.

On 15 December 2024, the Rhysida ransomware gang breached the systems of Sunflower Medical Group, a Kansas healthcare provider. The gang accessed sensitive information of nearly 221,000 patients, including names, addresses, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, driver's license numbers, medical information, and health insurance information. The breach was initially discovered on 7 January 2025. A cybersecurity firm was hired to investigate, revealing that the hackers had been inside their systems since mid-December and made copies of Sunflower's files. Sunflower Medical Group notified regulators in Maine, Vermont, and California, and posted a notice on its website. The company sent letters to all victims with valid addresses and offered one year of credit monitoring services. The Rhysida ransomware gang took credit for the attack in January 2025, threatening to leak the stolen data if a ransom of about $800,000 was not paid.

Title (Company): National Information Resources Service - e-Government Standard Framework Portal - Korea Internet & Security Agency's (KISA) - National Tax Service
Description: Between March 4 and March 10 in 2025, RipperSec, a pro-Palestinian hacktivist group, attacked the South Korean government's site with a DDoS attack. Rippersack claimed responsibility, stating their motivation as 'Stop weapons support in Israel', and encouraged other hackers to target Korean government sites. The group shared capture screens of temporary access problems on the IRS site and provided instructions on Telegram to attack Korean government sites. Affected sites include e-Government Standard Framework Portal, the Korea Internet & Security Agency's (KISA) Protection Country, the National Tax Service and the National Information Resources Service (IRS). Earlier, in November, a South Korean media outlet reported that South Korea was the eighth-largest arms exporter to Israel from October 2023 to September 2024, with sales worth at least $900,000 (about 1.3 billion won).

Beginning in November 2024, Blind Eagle/ APT-C-36 conducted a series of ongoing campaigns targeting Colombian institutions and government entities, delivering malicious .url files that exploited the vulnerability CVE-2024-4345 six days after Microsoft had patched the vulnerability. They targeted Colombian judicial institutions and other government or private organizations, resulting in high infection rates, with over 1,600 victims affected during one campaign around 19 December 2024. Check Point Research discovered and disclosed the campaigns.

On 6 March 2025, Papara, one of Turkey's leading electronic money companies, was subjected to a major DDoS attack, resulting in partial cuts in services, but no user accounts or data were affected. The company's tech teams quickly intervened to solve the problem, with officials stating that security was a top priority. Users experienced errors, such as "I'm sorry, we can't serve now" and "Your information is being controlled," while trying to access the application. The incident was reported to the public through the company's official statement on 7 March 2025.

On 7 March 2025, the Concello de Vigo's website was disrupted in a cyber attack attributed to the pro-Russian group TwoNet, which targeted Spain in response to its support for Ukraine. The attack, executed in two waves, used a DDoS  attack to overload the servers and render them inaccessible. The incident was confirmed by municipal sources and the National Institute of Cybersecurity (INCIBE) and was later claimed by TwoNet on its Telegram channel. While the attack caused temporary website outages, it did not affect the Municipal Electronic Headquarters or compromise personal or confidential data.The municipal website resumed normal operations after a few hours, with disruptions limited to the early morning and midday.

On 5 March 2025, unknown hackers exploited a vulnerability in 1inch’s older smart contract, stealing $5 million. The attack targeted a third-party market maker, TrustedVolumes, rather than individual users. After negotiations, the hacker agreed to return most of the stolen funds in exchange for a bug bounty. The breach stemmed from a flaw in the Fusion v1 resolver smart contract, which allowed unintended transactions. 1inch detected the incident at 18:00 UTC and quickly deployed security measures to stop further exploitation by updating its resolver contracts.

Title (Company): National Cryptological Center - Ministry of Inclusion, Social Security and Migration - Ministry of Defense - Ministry of Foreign Affairs - Royal Elcano Institute - Newtral
Description: On 2 March 2025, the pro-Russian group TwoNet claimed responsibility for a DDoS cyber attack on the Newtral website and several Spanish state departments, including the Ministry of Defense, the Ministry of Inclusion, Social Security and Migration, the National Cryptological Center, and the Royal Elcano Institute. The National Institute of Cybersecurity identified the attack through a Telegram publication. TwoNet stated the attack was in response to Spain's support for Ukraine. The group threatened to continue attacking government sites and big companies if Spain's support for Ukraine did not cease. TwoNet also claimed to have attacked the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and threatened to carry out massive DDoS attacks against Spain's state and government websites over the next month. The Incibe and Newtral investigated the incident, which caused isolated stability problems on the Newtral website, resolved after taking necessary measures.

Unknown hackers targeted the network of the German municipal utility in Schwerte, North Rhine-Westphalia, in early March 2025, impacting the city administration. In response, officials severed digital connections to the municipal utility to prevent further damage. As a result, all citizen services, including applications for passports and certificates of good conduct, were temporarily unavailable. The town hall and city offices were also unreachable by email. Stadtwerke Schwerte is working with external service providers to restore services, though the duration of the disruption remains unclear. Essential utilities and company websites have not been affected.

Unknown hackers targeted the Missouri Department of Conservation on 28 February 2025. The agency, responsible for issuing hunting and fishing permits and managing nearly 1 million acres of public land, has activated its Incident Response Team to assess the breach. Cybersecurity teams are investigating suspicious activity on a data server, with third-party experts assisting in determining the full impact. While it remains unclear if personal data was compromised, affected stakeholders will be notified if necessary.

On 2 March 2025, Poland's space agency (POLSA) suffered a network breach, which was detected by state cybersecurity services, leading to unauthorized access to POLSA's IT infrastructure. The agency disconnected its network from the internet, and its website remained inaccessible as of 3 March. Poland's Digital Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski confirmed the incident and announced that specialists were working to identify the attackers behind the breach.

On 24 February 2025, a group of pro-Russian hackers claimed a cyber attack on the Liguria Region's portal. The Security Operation Center of Liguria Digitale activated emergency procedures and implemented containment measures, limiting the impact to just three minutes of disservice. The incident was reported on 24 February 2025, and experts stated that no further serious consequences were detected.

Title (Company): Enna Magazine - City of Verona - Province of Ragusa - Province of Enna - Province of Trapani - City of Catania - Regione Puglia - City of Adrano - Province of Caltanissetta
Description: On 25 February 2025, the pro-Russian hacker group 'NoName057(16)' carried out a series of DDoS attacks against various local authorities in Italy; targets included Province of Trapani, Province of Ragusa, Province of Caltanissetta, Province of Enna, Enna Magazine, Region Apulia (Puglia), City of Catania, City of Adrano, and the City of Verona, according to NoName's Telegram site, which was reported by FalconFeeds. The attacks resulted in the affected municipalities' websites being inaccessible, but affected entities reassured citizens that no data was accessed. The attacks occurred in response to a speech given by the President of Italy, Sergio Mattarella, which took place nine days prior. On the other hand, the attack on Puglia was linked specifically to the mayor of Bari being “close to Kyiv”. Italy's National Cybersecurity Agency alerted the targets and authorities, providing suggestions for mitigation of impact.  From 14 to 17 July 2025, an international law enforcement operation code-named Eastwood was launched against NoName057(16). Coordinated by Europol and Eurojust, the operation involved simultaneous actions by authorities in Czechia, France, Finland, Germany, Italy, Lithuania, Poland, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the Netherlands, and the United States, targeting individuals and digital infrastructure linked to the pro-Russian network. Operation Eastwood allowed for the deactivation of several hundred servers supporting the group’s DDoS activities. Overall, national authorities issued seven arrest warrants, including against six Russian nationals, over the suspected involvement in NoName057(16). The investigation further facilitated the arrest of two individuals in France and Spain. Law enforcement personally notified over 1,000 supporters of the group, including 15 suspected administrators, of their legal liability related to the participation in NoName057(16)‘s criminal activities.

On 28 February 2025 at 07:10 am, the official website of the Italian municipality of Pescara was targeted by a DDoS attack allegedly launched by Russia-affiliated NoName057(16) group. The attack was reported by the Municipality of Pescara in a note without providing the identity of the attacker. The Municipality announced that the page was restored and briefly usable again later in the day. A complaint regarding the incident was lodged to the Italian Data Processing Center that will submit the results of initial screening to the National Cybersecurity Agency and the Postal Police for a detailed report.  News portal of the Abruzzo region reported that the campaign was launched following statements by Italian President Sergio Mattarella marking the third anniversary of Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Beside targeting the website of the Municipality of Pescara, NoName057(16) is suspected to have launched a wave of DDoS attacks on municipal sites of Rome, Milan, Catania, and Verona, and the regions of Lazio, Piedmont, Apulia, and Valle d'Aosta. However, it is reported that the attacks had no effect and the sites are reachable. From 14 to 17 July 2025, an international law enforcement operation code-named Eastwood was launched against NoName057(16). Coordinated by Europol and Eurojust, the operation involved simultaneous actions by authorities in Czechia, France, Finland, Germany, Italy, Lithuania, Poland, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the Netherlands, and the United States, targeting individuals and digital infrastructure linked to the pro-Russian network. Operation Eastwood allowed for the deactivation of several hundred servers supporting the group’s DDoS activities. Overall, national authorities issued seven arrest warrants, including against six Russian nationals, over the suspected involvement in NoName057(16). The investigation further facilitated the arrest of two individuals in France and Spain. Law enforcement personally notified over 1,000 supporters of the group, including 15 suspected administrators, of their legal liability related to the participation in NoName057(16)‘s criminal activities.

On 25 February 2025, SentinelLABS reported on an ongoing campaign by Ghostwriter, a Belarusian-government linked cyberespionage group. According to SentinelLABS, the campaign, which was in preparation from July-August 2024 and began officially at least in November-December 2024, targets the Ukrainian government and Belarusian opposition groups/figures. The attackers used weaponised Excel documents with obfuscated VBA macros to deliver malicious payloads through phishing attacks which were/are geared towards Ukrainian interests to generate a sense of urgency and make a victim click on the lure, after which Ghostwriter deployed its PicassoLoader and Cobalt Strike payloads, enabling them to establish command-and-control and access victims' data.  The campaign coincides with the Belarus presidential elections (26 January 2025), suggesting an effort to conduct cyberespionage while suppressing political opposition and achieving Belarusian political goals.

On 19 February 2025, the Cyber Resistance / Ukrainian Cyber Alliance, a group of pro-Ukraine hacktivists, carried out a cyberattack on CarMoney, a Russian microfinance company. CarMoney confirmed earlier this week that it had suffered a cyber incident, forcing it to shut down all systems after attackers sent spam messages to customers claiming the company was closing its business, donating its proceeds to charity and writing off all debts. The organization has not attributed the attack to Ukrainian hackers or disclosed the full extent of the breach.  The hackers said their attack destroyed CarMoney’s infrastructure and compromised “terabytes of data.” While CarMoney has assured clients and investors that no personal data was affected, the hackers claim they obtained information on a large number of borrowers, including members of Russian military units and intelligence officers. The hackers shared screenshots on Telegram but the data’s  authenticity could not be independently verified. While CarMoney’s website remains operational, customers have reported ongoing payment service disruptions and difficulties accessing their accounts.  CarMoney, one of Russia’s largest microfinance firms, issues short-term loans secured by vehicles. According to independent Russian media, Putin’s ex-wife, Lyudmila Ocheretnaya, controls the company through a network of offshore entities.

On 24 February 2025, Kaspersky reported a new, ongoing campaign targeting unnamed industrial organisations in the Asia-Pacific region, with a particular focus on Chinese-speaking targets, as evidenced by the tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) utilised, such as leveraging Chinese-language search engines and apps.  Kaspersky was initially tipped off to the campaign through reports from victims of attacks on government agencies and industrial organisations in the APAC region, and upon investigating, realised that the attackers were utilising a multi-stage, long-term, complex procedure to install malware (FatalRAT), which was delivered via zip files in Telegram, WeChat, and by email. The zip archives were disguised as invoices or legitimate tax filing applications for Chinese-speaking individuals and contained the FatalRAT first-stage loader packed using tools make detection and analysis more difficult. According to Kaspersky, the targets were primarily from Taiwan, Malaysia, China, Japan, Thailand, South Korea, Singapore, the Philippines, Vietnam, and Hong Kong; in any case, the vast majority were from China, while the victims included targets in IT, telecoms, healthcare, construction, manufacturing, governments, logistics and transportation, and finance. While Kaspersky and other IT companies are thus far unable to identify the specific group behind the attack, Kaspersky attributes it with medium confidence to Chinese-speaking initiators.

On 19 February 2025, Paratus Namibia, a telecommunications operator in Namibia, reported a cyber attack on its internal computer system, which disrupted some of its information systems and affected its operational processes. The company was investigating the extent of the security breach at the time of the report on 24 February 2025, but no further information about the incident has been disclosed.

Title (Company): Diputación de Ciudad Real - Empresa Municipal de Transportes de Madrid - City of San Sebastian - Ayuntamiento de Hondarribia - Junta de Comunidades de Castilla - Ayuntamiento de Donostia - Ayuntamiento de Irun - Tranvía de Zaragoza - Chamber of Commerce of Madrid - Port of Barcelona - Diputación de Gipuzkoa - Diputación de Albacete - Diputación de Girona - City of Valladolid - Toledo City Council - Diputación de Bizkaia - Basque Government - Provincia de Huesca - City of Barakaldo - Ayuntamiento de Zaragoza - Comunidad Autónoma de Castilla-La Mancha
Description: Between 3-5 March in 2025, the Russian hacktivist group NoName057(16) launched a DDoS attack on several Spanish websites including Toledo City Council, Basque Government, the Diputación de Bizkaia, the Junta de Comunidades de Castilla y León, the Port of Barcelona, the EMT of Madrid, Chamber of Commerce of Madrid, the City of Valladolid, San Sebastian, Barakaldo, Ayuntamiento de Donostia, Ayuntamiento de Irun, Diputación de Gipuzkoa, Ayuntamiento de Hondarribia, Ayuntamiento de Zaragoza, Tranvía de Zaragoza, Provincia de Huesca, Comunidad Autónoma de Castilla-La Mancha, Diputación de Albacete, Diputación de Girona, Diputación de Ciudad Real, Diputación de Toledo. On X, the hackers claimed that the attack was a response to a statement of Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez expressing support for Ukraine. From 14 to 17 July 2025, an international law enforcement operation code-named Eastwood was launched against NoName057(16). Coordinated by Europol and Eurojust, the operation involved simultaneous actions by authorities in Czechia, France, Finland, Germany, Italy, Lithuania, Poland, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the Netherlands, and the United States, targeting individuals and digital infrastructure linked to the pro-Russian network. Operation Eastwood allowed for the deactivation of several hundred servers supporting the group’s DDoS activities. Overall, national authorities issued seven arrest warrants, including against six Russian nationals, over the suspected involvement in NoName057(16). The investigation further facilitated the arrest of two individuals in France and Spain. Law enforcement personally notified over 1,000 supporters of the group, including 15 suspected administrators, of their legal liability related to the participation in NoName057(16)‘s criminal activities.

Title (Company): Palau Ministry of Health and Human Services
Description: The Qilin Ransomware Group claimed to have compromised the Palau Ministry of Health and Human Services (MHHS) on 17 February 2025, and threatened to release internal data by 27 February. The MHHS confirmed being a victim of a cyber attack on 18 February 2025, and stated that work to determine the extent of the breach was ongoing. The ministry runs Belau National Hospital, an 80-bed facility that serves the country’s nearly 20,000 residents spread across hundreds of islands. The hospital remained open, and patients were encouraged to continue seeking care as usual. The ministry was unable to confirm whether patient data had been affected at the time. The group published some of the stolen information on 28 February. In a statement, the Health Ministry confirmed that patient data was compromised as result of the cyberattack and may include billing summaries for Belau National Hospital patients between from 2018 to 2022. Personal information like names, addresses, phone numbers and data on diagnoses and procedures were likely exposed.

On Monday, 3 March 2025, Russian telecom Beeline was targeted by a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack, resulting in internet disruptions for some of its over 44 million subscribers. Users in Moscow and surrounding regions reported difficulties accessing the company's mobile app, website outages, notification failures, and internet disruptions. This was confirmed by Beeline and reported by outagetracking services, including Downdetector, and Russia's communications watchdog, Federal Service for Supervision of Communications, Information Technology and Mass Media- Roskomnadzor. Beeline stated that its specialists had identified the issue and taken measures to stabilize services.

On 24 February 2025, Infini Neobank was hacked, resulting in the theft of $49.5 million USDC, which was then transferred to the Ethereum network. The attacker traded the stolen USDC for Ethereum-based DAI and purchased 17.696 ETH, later transferring it to the address 0xfcc8...6e49. The attack was likely carried out by obtaining a private key, with the private key to the address 0xc49b...e3e1 possibly being leaked. The stolen assets were transferred to wallets associated with TornadoCash, an anonymization protocol. An Infini developer, who secretly retained executive authority after the project was completed, is thought to be behind the attack. An official police report has been filed, and a member of Infini's team claimed that the engineer who committed the theft had been identified and reported to the police.

Title (Company): Faculté libre de droit et d’économie-gestion (FACO - École de Psychologues Praticiens (EPP) - École de psycho-pédagogie (EFPP) - Penninghen School of Art Direction and Interior Architecture - École nationale de la statistique et de l’analyse de l’information (ENSAI) - École nationale de la statistique et de l'administration économique (ENSAE Paris)
Description: A hacker, known as 'st0jke', infiltrated several French higher education institutions, including the École de Psychologues Praticiens (EPP), the Faculté libre de droit et d’économie-gestion (FACO), the Penninghen School of Art Direction and Interior Architecture, the École de psycho-pédagogie (EFPP), the École nationale de la statistique et de l'administration économique (ENSAE Paris), and the École nationale de la statistique et de l’analyse de l’information (ENSAI), compromising data of thousands of students and teachers. Stolen data has been advertized for sale in clandestine forums, with the EPP's database being offered for $2,500, FACO's data for $1,500, and EFPP data for $1,000.

In or around early February 2025, a hacker, known by the alias Rey and a member of the HellCat ransomware group, breached the systems of Orange Group, a French telecommunications operator. Rey allegedly maintained persistent access within the Orange systems for roughly a month, before finally exfiltrating data on 23 February 2025 and leaking it days later after a ransom was not paid. The affected data was mostly from the Romanian branch of Orange and includes 380,000 unique email addresses, as well as 12,000 (6.5GB) of administrative documents such as invoices and contracts, as well as customer and employee information. The breach was carried out by exploiting compromised credentials and vulnerabilities in the company's Jira software and internal portals. BleepingComputer reported on the incident and received a statement from Orange Group, who confirmed the breach and stated that they were committed to protecting the data and interests of their employees, customers, and partners. The company also stated that there was no impact on customer operations and that they were cooperating with relevant authorities to address the matter.

Between June and October 2024, a ransomware campaign tracked by Orange Cyberdefense as Green Nailao targeted European healthcare organizations. The attackers exploited a vulnerability in Check Point Security Gateways (CVE-2024-24919) to steal user credentials and access virtual private networks (VPNs) using legitimate accounts. The hackers subsequently deployed ShadowPad and PlugX backdoors, commonly associated with Chinese cyberespionage groups, as well as a new ransomware strain called NailaoLocker. Orange Cyberdefense describes NailaoLocker as relatively unsophisticated and poorly designed, encrypting files and leaving a ransom note demanding payment in Bitcoin via a ProtonMail address. The observed activities mark the first time that ShadowPad has been linked to the delivery of ransomware. A medium-confidence assessment by Orange Cyberdefense associated the campaign with Chinese intrusion sets, pointing to multiple possible objectives, including the opportunistic use of ransomware as means for additional revenue generation or as a false-flag tactic to cover up efforts to obtain sensitive data.
Techniques Used: Exploit Public-Facing Application, Replication Through Removable Media

Description: The Rainbow District School Board in the Greater Sudbury region of Ontario, Canada, was breached by cyber criminals in early February 2025, resulting in the theft of sensitive personal information. The breach, detected on 7 February 2025, affected people who worked for the board as early as 2010 and students who attended a school in the Rainbow District School Board as early as 2011. Stolen information included social insurance numbers, bank account information, and medical information belonging to staff and students. The board reported the incident to the Greater Sudbury Police Service and the Ontario Provincial Police. The incident was announced by the board on 20 February 2025. In February 2026, the media Sudbury.com reported that a freedom of information request revealed the ransomware cyber incident affecting the Rainbow District School Board cost the board more than $680,000.

Multiple government services of Anne Arundel County in the US state of Maryland were disrupted following a network intrusion disclosed on 23 February 2025. Describing the situation a week after the start of the incident, County Executive Steuart Pittman said that while 911 and 311 call centers were operational, many services were still impacted by the shutoff of internet access.  “County officials are working diligently with the Anne Arundel County Office of Information Technology, public safety officials, cybersecurity specialists, and each department to conduct a full investigation,” he said. The county is also home to several prominent federal institutions, including the National Security Agency and the US Naval Academy.

Title (Company): Appomattox County - Appomattox County Public Schools
Description: Networks of Appomattox County Public Schools and Appomattox County, Virginia  were breached by an unknown entity in the week of 18 February 2025. The incident was discovered and reported by the school district and county. Outside cybersecurity experts were contacted to help secure their systems and investigate the cause. The incident resulted in the closure of Appomattox County Public Schools on Tuesday and the remainder of the week due to winter weather. The county and school district enaged in collaboration with state and federal authorities on the investigation.

Nichino Ryokka, Ltd., a Japanese company specialising in agricultural chemicals, was breached by an unknown attacker on 11 February 2025. The ransomware attack led to the encryption of some data regarding corporate information and personal information, though it is unclear if this personal information was customers' or employees'; in any case, the company assured the public that none of this data was believed to be exfiltrated. The company announced this incident on 14 February 2025, after conducting an investigation, and is currently responding to the incident with the help of outside experts, with plans to increase its cyber security response in the future.

On 22 February 2025, hackers took control of the official X account of Myanmar's military junta leader Min Aung Hlaing and used it to promote a fake crypto coin, branding it as Myanmar's national crypto currency. The hackers shared and deleted several crypto money wallet addresses, and later claimed the launch had been postponed, raising suspicion among crypto traders.

In early December 2024, an unidentified hacker group launched a ransomware attack on the Semyonishna dairy plant, the largest dairy processing plant in southern Siberia, reportedly in connection to the plant's support for Russian troops in Ukraine; the plant had recently donated drones and humanitarian aid for Russian troops in Ukraine. The attackers used LockBit ransomware and remote access software AnyDesk to spread the malware across the company's network, which lacked antivirus protection. The attack caused the company's printers to churn out leaflets condemning the company's contributions to the Russian army, thus also disrupting the company's ability to label products. The plant's management, led by Valery Levitsky, director of Sayanmoloko, reported that operations had returned to normal by December 2024. The FSB's regional office and local news website Kommersant reported on the incident.

On 20 February 2025, the cybercriminal group RansomHub claimed it had breached Riverdale Country School, an elite prep school in the Bronx in New York City and was holding its data for ransom. RansomHub, which formed in February 2024, posted the school's website along with a countdown clock on its dark web site, alleging that it had stolen 42 GB of data. The group warned that the school had just over five days to comply with its demands or it would release the data. The data potentially includes personal information about students and their families, vaccination records, academic records, health data, and staff payroll. RansomHub typically employs multiple extortion tactics against its victims, including encrypting data and exfiltrating it to servers under the group's control.

Title (Company): Ministry of Education and Culture of the State of Colima
Description: On 21 February 2025, an unidentified actor began to release records allegedly obtained from a compromise of the Ministry of Education and Culture of the State of Colima on a dedicated leak site. To stop the release of additional documents containing personal details of administrators, teachers, and students, the actor demanded state authorities take action against officials within their ranks that the hacker without further evidence claimed had engaged in criminal acts against minors and had links to drug trafficking. The Office of the Attorney General of the State of Colima was informed, and an investigation was initiated. The Cybernetics Police of the Ministry of Public Security was requested to support the investigation.

On 23 January, the Bundeswehr University in Munich has been attacked by hackers. According to an unknown source within the University, a significant amounts of data from various areas were copied or leaked by attackers. This includes real names and passwords, work and stored private email addresses, login data or course content. Data such as private account and cell phone numbers or addresses are also affected. According to current knowledge, the attackers are said to have gained access to the university's central IT services using a leaked user ID. The Bundeswehr's Cyber ​​and Information Space Command confirmed the incident upon request. "The Bundeswehr's networks are not affected by this," said a spokesman. According to current knowledge, no data was deleted or illegally encrypted.

JabaRoot DZ claimed to have hacked the database of the Ministry of Justice of Morocco in June 2025, compromising personal information of Justice Minister Adbellatif Ouahbi and nearly 5,000 judges and 35,000 judicial personnel. The breach appears to be linked to previous activities by the group targeting the National Security Fund (CNSS) and the National Agency for Land Registry, Cadastre and Cartography (ANCFCC). JabaRoot DZ framed their own activities as part of a mission to confront political corruption in Morocco.

On 17 February 2025, Ecuador's National Assembly was targeted by two cyberattacks. The National Assembly reported the incident and stated that it was able to quickly identify and counteract the situation, alerting citizens and public institutions that these attacks attempted to breach confidential information.

On 14 February 2025, Genea Fertility, a major Australian IVF clinic, was breached by a cyber attack, resulting in delayed treatments. The attackers accessed Genea's data, but the extent of the breach and the type of data compromised is still being investigated. Genea Fertility detected suspicious activity on its network and immediately took steps to contain the incident, including disabling some of its systems. The clinic is working to restore its systems and inform individuals if their personal data has been impacted. Genea Fertility disclosed the attack on its website. The incident was reported by multiple sources, including ABC journalists, and Genea Fertility is collaborating with the public relations firm Porter Novelli to investigate the damage.

In March 2024, the China-linked threat actor Winnti, also known as APT41, targeted Japanese companies in the manufacturing, materials, and energy sectors in a cyber espionage campaign dubbed RevivalStone. The campaign, detailed by Japanese cybersecurity company LAC, involved custom tools, including the Winnti malware, which has a unique rootkit for hiding and manipulating communications, and stolen digital certificates. The attackers exploited an SQL injection vulnerability in an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system to drop web shells, such as China Chopper and Behinder, on the compromised server. They performed reconnaissance, collected credentials for lateral movement, and delivered an improved Winnti malware version. The intrusion reached a managed service provider (MSP) by leveraging a shared account, and the company's infrastructure was weaponized to propagate the malware to three other organizations. The campaign was linked to tools like DEATHLOTUS, UNAPIMON, PRIVATELOG, CUNNINGPIGEON, WINDJAMMER, and SHADOWGAZE. Researchers Takuma Matsumoto and Yoshihiro Ishikawa from LAC disclosed the attack, also tracked by Trend Micro as Earth Freybug, by Cybereason as Operation CuckooBees, and by Symantec as Blackfly.
Techniques Used: Exploit Public-Facing Application, Trusted Relationship, Valid Accounts

Description: A group of Chinese cybercriminals conducted large-scale cyberattacks targeting telecommunications towers and banks in Kuwait at least since 13 February 2025 but potentially earlier, leading to the Kuwaiti government to dismantle the group on the 13th following alerts from banks and telecommunications companies. According to the Kuwaiti Ministry of Interior, the criminal gang, composed of Chinese nationals, used advanced electronic devices planted within mobile vehicles to penetrate telecommunications networks and broadcast fraudulent messages impersonating banks, enabling them to steal bank account data and thus to seize funds.  Security teams within the Department of Combating Cybercrime identified the source of the suspicious signals, traced it to a vehicle in the Farwaniya area, and apprehended the driver, a Chinese national. Further investigation revealed additional devices and technical tools used to analyse the compromised data, and the accused confessed to collaborating with others in hacking communication networks. The accused were referred to the relevant authorities for legal action, as reported by Al Jarida newspaper.

On 20 February 2025, the British large medical firm HCRG Care Group, operating under the name Virgin Care and a member of the TWENTY20 Capital, was attacked by the Medusa ransomware group, which seized more than 2TB of sensitive data, including government documents, employee personal information, sensitive medical records, financial information, passports, and birth certificates, after hacking into HCRG's system. Samples of the data appeared on a dark web leak site. Medusa demanded $2 million in ransom. The company admitted to have been targeted by ransomware but was unable to determine the specifics of the hackers' claims. HCRG worked with public security experts to determine the cause of the accident and reported the incident to the ICO and other directors. No further suspicious activity was detected since initial action.

Title (Company): Ministry of Interior (Italy) - Transport Authority - Intesa San Paolo bank - Malpensa airport - Linate airport - Ministry of Finance (Italy) - Port of Taranto - Guardia di Finanze - Ministry of Enterprises and Made in Italy (Italy) - Port of Trieste
Description: On 17 February 2025, the pro-Russian group NoName057(16) carried out a cyber attack on Italian banking and transport companies. The targeted companies included Intesa San Paolo bank, airports of Linate and Malpensa, the Transport Authority, and the ports of Taranto and Trieste. Further targets included the websites of ministries (Ministry of Enterprises and Made in Italy), the Financial Police (Guardia di Finanze), and certain sub-sites of the Ministries of the Interior and Finance. The attack was in response to statements made by the President of the Republic, Sergio Mattarella, on 5 February 2025, comparing Russia's aggression against Ukraine to the Third Reich project in Europe. The group used DDoS actions to conduct the attack. NoName057(16) claimed responsibility for the attack through a message on their Telegram channel. The National Cybersecurity Agency alerted the affected entities and initiated mitigation actions in collaboration with the victims' technicians. Local media reported on the incident. From 14 to 17 July 2025, an international law enforcement operation code-named Eastwood was launched against NoName057(16). Coordinated by Europol and Eurojust, the operation involved simultaneous actions by authorities in Czechia, France, Finland, Germany, Italy, Lithuania, Poland, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the Netherlands, and the United States, targeting individuals and digital infrastructure linked to the pro-Russian network. Operation Eastwood allowed for the deactivation of several hundred servers supporting the group’s DDoS activities. Overall, national authorities issued seven arrest warrants, including against six Russian nationals, over the suspected involvement in NoName057(16). The investigation further facilitated the arrest of two individuals in France and Spain. Law enforcement personally notified over 1,000 supporters of the group, including 15 suspected administrators, of their legal liability related to the participation in NoName057(16)‘s criminal activities.

On 9 June 2025, the official X account of Paraguay’s President Santiago Peña was hacked by an unknown cybercriminal group that leveraged a compromised staffer email account linked to the X account. The compromise was reported by Gustavo Villate, head of the Ministry of Information and Communications (Mitic), at a press conference on the same day. The hacking allegedly was part of a fraud attempt to collect cryptocurrency through advertising. The Computer Emergency Response Team (Cert-PY) intervened immediately, recovering the president’s account.

On 14 February 2025, the Bavarian state government was breached, affecting the State Chancellery and the State Ministry of Digital Affairs. The Landesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik (LSI) confirmed it as a DDoS, causing temporary unavailability of some websites, but no data was lost or encrypted. The Bavarian State Criminal Office is investigating, with possible connections to the Munich Security Conference not yet confirmed, and the prosecution process to be handed over to the police after technical analysis is completed. The hacktivist group NoName057(16) claimed responsibility for the activity on its Telegram account.  From 14 to 17 July 2025, an international law enforcement operation code-named Eastwood was launched against NoName057(16). Coordinated by Europol and Eurojust, the operation involved simultaneous actions by authorities in Czechia, France, Finland, Germany, Italy, Lithuania, Poland, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the Netherlands, and the United States, targeting individuals and digital infrastructure linked to the pro-Russian network. Operation Eastwood allowed for the deactivation of several hundred servers supporting the group’s DDoS activities. Overall, national authorities issued seven arrest warrants, including against six Russian nationals, over the suspected involvement in NoName057(16). The investigation further facilitated the arrest of two individuals in France and Spain. Law enforcement personally notified over 1,000 supporters of the group, including 15 suspected administrators, of their legal liability related to the participation in NoName057(16)‘s criminal activities.

A cyber attack targeted Kenya's Business Registration Services (BRS) in 17 February 2025, exposing the business dealings of President William Ruto and former President Uhuru Kenyatta's families. The attack leaked company names, directors, shareholders, and business owners' IDs, phone numbers, and house details. The incident was reported by Firstpost Africa on 17 February 2025.

On 8 February 2025, Medusa Ransomware Group claimed to have breached SimonMed Imaging, a US-based diagnostic imaging company, stealing over 212 GB of sensitive data and exposing private information of more than 132,000 individuals, including patients and employees, before demanding a $1 million ransom in Bitcoin. The group posted 45 proof files online. A company representative said the breach occurred last week, but SimonMed “interrupted” hackers and “no data was encrypted.” Clinical systems were not impacted by this “unauthorized activity". Furthermore, "to immediately contain the situation, we temporarily took some systems offline, resulting in some operational slowdowns.”

On 13 February 2025, the Caisse des Dépôts, a French financial institution, was the subject of a cyberattack in which the personal data of approximately 70,000 people, including 1,000 elected officials, were stolen. The attackers used fraudulently obtained connection identifiers to access the platform and remove sensitive information, including social security numbers, names, dates and cities of birth, and mailing addresses, from the Ircantec pension fund scheme. The victims were informed of the breach via email, and the Caisse des Dépôts blocked the fraudulent connections, strengthened account creation controls, and notified its partners to set up alert systems. A complaint was filed, and a report was made to the National Commission on Informatics and Liberty (CNIL) in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). The attack was first reported by Franceinfo and later confirmed by the Caisse des Dépôts to Figaro on 13 February 2025. Additionally, Chronopost, a subsidiary of the La Poste group, was also targeted in a separate cyberattack at the end of January 2025, resulting in the theft of personal data of 210,000 customers, including surname, first name, postal address, signature, and sometimes telephone number.

On 12 February 2025, the offices of Virginia Attorney General Jason Miyares were targeted by a cyberattack, which was detected early and resulted in minimal damage. The attack took nearly all systems offline, including email, VPN access, and internet connectivity to the office's network. The FBI and Virginia State Police are investigating the incident. Cybersecurity expert Alex Nette noted that the attack may have been motivated by a desire for information, as the attorney general's office often files nonpublic legal briefs. The incident was reported by the Richmond Times-Dispatch and CBS 6 on 13 February 2025. A ransomware group, known as Cloak, has confirmed its involvement in an attack. On 20 March, Cloak publicly listed the Virginia attorney general’s website on their Tor-based data leak platform, accompanied by a message stating, “The waiting period has expired. Compromised data can be downloaded from the leak page.”

On 13 February 2025, Shva, a company providing communications for credit card transactions in Israel, experienced disruptions due to a cyber attack, specifically a denial of service attack, which prevented payments from being cleared. The attack started at around 11am and was initially thought to be a communications malfunction, but was later confirmed as a cyber incident. Check Point chief of staff Gil Messing and Panorays cofounder Demi BenAri reported that the attack involved bombarding the payment server with a large number of requests, causing it to crash. Messing suggested that the attack may have been carried out by a state actor, possibly with the assistance of smaller entities, and that the goal of the attack was to create a cognitive effect rather than steal data or money. The incident was reported by several customers and was disclosed by Shva, with updates provided on the company's website.

In late 2024, Cinnamon Tempest fka DEV-0401/Emperor Dragonfly/Bronze Starlight, a Chinese state-sponsored threat actor, ran a ransomware scam against an Asian software and services firm. The attackers demanded $2 million in ransom, with a discount to $1 million if paid within three days. They used the RA World ransomware variant and exploited a known Palo Alto PANOS vulnerability (CVE-2024-0012) to breach the infrastructure. The attackers obtained administrative credentials from the company's intranet, stole Amazon S3 cloud credentials from its Veeam server, and used them to steal data from its S3 buckets before encrypting computers. Symantec's Threat Hunter Team reported this incident on 13 February 2025.

Title (Company): Kewadin Casinos - Sault Tribe - Sault Tribe
Description: A ransomware attack was carried out by an unknown entity on the Sault Tribe in Michigan, beginning on 10 February 2025. The attack impacted multiple computer and phone systems across tribal administration, including casinos, health centers, and various businesses. The tribe was forced to temporarily close many departments and businesses. The attack had a devastating impact on the tribe's health division, with all scheduled appointments cancelled, but emergency walk-ins were still accepted. Gaming operations at the five Kewadin Casinos locations were halted until further notice. Chairman Austin Lowes disclosed the incident on the tribal Facebook page on 10 February 2025, and declined to provide more information due to the ongoing investigation.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Storm-2372, a group assessed with medium confidence to align with Russia's interests and tradecraft, conducted a device code phishing campaign that started in August 2024. The attackers targeted governments, NGOs, IT services and technology, defense, telecommunications, health, and energy/oil and gas sectors in Europe, North America, Africa, and the Middle East using a specific phishing technique to trick users into logging into productivity apps and capturing login tokens to access compromised accounts. Microsoft reported the cyberattack on 13 February 2025.

The Papua New Guinea tax office, specifically the Internal Revenue Commission (IRC), was hit by a ransomware attack on 28 January 2025, resulting in a system outage that affected its Standard Integrated Tax Accounting System (SIGTAS), internet networks, phones, and email communications. The attack may have exposed sensitive data belonging to Australian companies and individuals. The IRC engaged a private company to assist in its recovery. Australia offered cybersecurity experts to support the PNG government. The incident was reported by ABC News on 13 February 2025. The attack remained under investigation, with unclear details on who was behind it and the nature and volume of any leaked information.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Between December 2024 and January 2025, Salt Typhoon, also known as RedMike, breached the confidentiality and integrity of information systems of telecoms and university networks by exploiting two vulnerabilities, CVE-2023-20273 and CVE-2023-20198, in Cisco IOS software, which runs on Cisco routers and switches. The hackers targeted over 1,000 Cisco devices worldwide, and configured the hacked devices to connect via GRE tunnels to maintain access and steal data. Recorded Future reported the incident on 13 February 2025, having tracked the group's activities.

On 27 January 2025, West Virginia's Harrison County school district was breached by a cyber attack, upon which the district shut down its network, however, it did not disclose whether any data was exfiltrated.

Title (Company): GSP-Finance - GSP-Processing - Gazprom-Automation - GSP-2 - GSP-Service - Gazstroyprom - GSP-Fuels and Lubricants - Infoservice Region - Vector Vostok - GSP-6 - GSP-Center - GSP-Mechanization - GSP-Oil and Gas Processing - GSP-Investments - GSP-7 - SSK Gazregion - GSP-1 - GSP-Technologies - Gazstroyprom-Auto Transport Enterprise - GSP-4 - GSP-5 - GSP-Complectation - Sphere Group
Description: Ukrainian hackers with the Ukrainian Main Directorate of Intelligence (GUR) and the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) managed to gain access to the systems of one of Russia's largest state-owned energy companies, Gazstroyprom, by using insider access, according to anonymous statements from military intelligence officials. The attack took place between 7 and 8 February 2025, according to RBC Ukraine's reporting. According to RBC, unnamed sources within the military linked the attack to Gazstroyprom's importance for the Russian war effort; as part of the attack, over 120 servers of Gazstroyprom and 22 of its subsidiaries were disabled. Furthermore, 2 petabytes (2000 TB) of data were destroyed, and the computers of over 10,000 employees of Gazstroyprom and its subsidiaries were "rendered inoperable," with the estimated damages reportedly being in the tens of millions of dollars.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: According to a Microsoft report published on 12 February 2025, Russian state sponsored hacking group Sandworm, also known as "Seashell Blizzard," has been conducting a cyber campaign dubbed “BadPilot”, targeting Ukraine and multiple Western countries. The group has been observed establishing long term persistence on compromised systems, stealing credentials, and performing lateral movement. While earlier phases of the campaign (2021 to 2023) focused on Ukraine, European countries, and regions in the Middle East and Asia, Microsoft reported a shift beginning on 24 February 2024, with Sandworm now targeting the United States, United Kingdom, and Australia. This recent phase has adopted a "spray and pray" approach, hitting both strategic and non strategic organisations. Targets include sensitive sectors such as energy, oil and gas, telecommunications, shipping, and arms manufacturing, as well as international government institutions, sectors potentially aligned with Russian strategic interests. The campaign has primarily exploited vulnerabilities in ConnectWise ScreenConnect (CVE 2024 1709) and Fortinet FortiClient EMS (CVE 2023 48788) to gain access.

The Port of Ostend, in Belgium, was the victim of an unauthorised intrusion by unknown actors on the night between the 10th and 11th of February 2025.  According to the Port's authorities, the unknown actors breached the "Ensor" system, which enabled them to gain access to data relating to ship arrivals and departures, as well as crew lists, though authorities clarified that no critical data was in this system. In the meantime, the Port has enlisted external experts to help mitigate the impact of the data breach.

On 11 February 2025, decentralised money lender zkLend was breached by an unknown actor/actors who exploited a smart contract flaw, specifically a rounding error bug in the mint() function, to steal 3,600 Ethereum, worth $9.5 million as of 13 February 2025. The attack was detected on the same day, with zkLend warning on X about the cybersecurity incident. The EthSecurity Telegram channel reported that the threat actor(s) manipulated the 'lendingaccumulator' to exploit the rounding error during ztoken mint() and withdraw() to repeatedly deposit and withdraw wstETH. Starkware confirmed that the vulnerability was not part of Starknet technology but rather an application-specific bug. The threat actor(s) attempted to launder the crypto through the RailGun privacy protocol but were blocked due to protocol policies. zkLend has offered the hacker a deal to return 90% of the stolen Ethereum, keeping 10%, in exchange for not facing liability for the attack. The hacker has until 13 February 2025, at 7:00 PM EST, to respond, after which zkLend will pursue legal action.

Sarcoma ransomware group claimed responsibility for a cyber attack against a Chinese subsidiary of Unimicron, a Taiwanese printed circuit boards (PCB) maker and one of the world's largest, on 30 January 2025, subsequently publishing samples of stolen files and threatening to leak a total of 377 GB of SQL files and documents if a ransom is not paid by 20 February 2025. The incident was disclosed by Unimicron in a bulletin on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (TWSE) portal on 1 February 2025, with the company stating that the impact was "limited."

The Russian state-sponsored hacking group Sandworm group has been observed by EclecticIQ to be deploying malicious Windows activators and fake Windows updates to target Windows users, particularly in critical infrastructure, in Ukraine. The ongoing campaign has operated since at least late 2023, with the most recent (observed) attack occurring on 12 January 2025. In the campaign, Sandworm uses trojanised Microsoft Key Management Service (KMS) activators and a new version of the BACKORDER loader to infect victims' devices with DarkCrystal RAT (DcRAT) malware. According to EclecticIQ, Sandworm's goal is to collect sensitive information, including keystrokes, browser cookies, and system information, and send it to attacker-controlled servers. In the most recent attack of 12 January 2025, malware was observed being used in data exfiltration attacks against unnamed Ukrainian targets, with the attackers using typosquatted domains to infect victims.  EclecticIQ threat analysts, in their report on 11 February 2025, linked the attacks to the Sandworm based on overlapping infrastructure, consistent tactics, techniques and procedures (TTPs), and frequently used ProtonMail accounts, while other aspects indicating a Russian build environment further strengthened their attribution.

Handala Hackers, a group with suspected ties to Iranian intelligence, claimed responsibility for a cyberattack against Israel's police force, exfiltrating 2.1 terabytes of sensitive data, including personnel records, weapons inventories, medical and psychological profiles, legal case files, weapon permits, and identity documents, and leaked 350,000 files on 9 February 2025 and 10 February 2025, despite the Israeli police denying direct penetration of their systems, with an investigation underway to confirm the extent of the incident, which included email addresses, gun licenses, officer photos, personal contact details, classified documents, and personal information about suspects and convicted criminals, and allegedly obtained access to the personal files of police officers and breached the servers of the Israeli Ministry of National Security.

On  January 2024, Eric Council Jr., a 25-year-old man from Alabama, carried out a SIM swapping attack on the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) account on X. He and his co-conspirators posted a fake announcement that Bitcoin ETFs were approved. This caused Bitcoin's price to jump up by 1,000 USD and then plummet by 2,000 USD after SEC Chairperson Gary Gensler tweeted that the announcement was fake. The SEC confirmed the next day that the SECGov X account was compromised through a SIM-swapping attack targeting the phone number of the person in charge of the X account. Council used a fraudulent identification card to impersonate the victim and gain access to the victim's cellular phone number. He was paid 50,000 USD in Bitcoin by his co-conspirators. The incident was reported by SEC Chairperson Gary Gensler on X. The Justice Department disclosed the details of the attack. Council pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit aggravated identity theft and access device fraud and is scheduled to be sentenced on 16 May 2025, facing a maximum penalty of five years in prison.

Title (Company): Laho.fr - Lesaides.fr - Chamber of Commerce and Industry (France)
Description: The Chamber of Commerce and Industry (CCI) of the Hauts-de-France region was presumably breached by a pro-Russian cyberattack on Thursday, 6 February 2025, following another attack on the night of 31 January to 1 February 2025. The attack targeted the official site of the CCI and two other sites, laho.fr and aides.fr. The same group of hackers claimed responsibility for the attack. No data loss was reported, and the system recovered by the end of the morning. The CCI lodged a complaint with the gendarmerie and informed the National Information Systems Security Agency (ANSSI) about the incident.

Title (Company): Council of the Department of Nord (France)
Description: The employment site of the Nord Department's Council in France was breached by unknown attackers in an incident disclosed on 7 February 2025, resulting in the theft of user data including civil status, identification, personal life, and work life information, but not bank data, as reported by La Voix du Nord, with the council warning users of potential phishing attempts and identity deception. The stolen data includes name, first name, age, reference bodies, territory, and work structure details.  National Commission on Informatics and Liberty was informed.  The Department invites recipients to remain vigilant as the illegally obtained data is likely to be made available to third parties to obtain other confidential information or benefits by phishing techniques or attempts to deceive third parties using their identity and ties with the Department of Nord.

A ransomware gang attacked the University of The Bahamas on 2 February 2025, shutting down the internet and telephone systems, disrupting email, classes, and online applications used by the university's 5,000 students across three campuses. The university confirmed the ransomware attack on 3 February 2025, and worked with law enforcement to contain the incident. Personal information was impacted, and students were urged to change their passwords. In-person classes continued, but deadlines for applications and assignments were extended, and cash was accepted at school kiosks due to credit card machines being down. The university's telephone systems were offline until temporary mobile numbers were provided. The school's website returned to service on 7 February 2025. The University of The Bahamas informed the public about the attack through a statement on 7 February 2025, and implemented a phased approach to network restoration with enhanced security protocols.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: On 5 Februar 2025, a pro-Russian hacker group, Noname057(16), attacked seven Ukrainian websites, including those of companies involved in military aircraft repairs and the production of military weapons and equipment, such as Ukroboronprom, Zaporizhzhia State Aviation Repair Plant, MiGremont, Antonov JSC, and JSC Kyiv Radar Plant, by using distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks, as claimed by the group via their X account. The attack was reported by authors Jess Daly and Seven, exposing the identities of Russia's 'Digital Army' as part of Russia's relentless cyber attacks on Ukraine and its NATO Allies since Russia's full-scale invasion. From 14 to 17 July 2025, an international law enforcement operation code-named Eastwood was launched against NoName057(16). Coordinated by Europol and Eurojust, the operation involved simultaneous actions by authorities in Czechia, France, Finland, Germany, Italy, Lithuania, Poland, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the Netherlands, and the United States, targeting individuals and digital infrastructure linked to the pro-Russian network. Operation Eastwood allowed for the deactivation of several hundred servers supporting the group’s DDoS activities. Overall, national authorities issued seven arrest warrants, including against six Russian nationals, over the suspected involvement in NoName057(16). The investigation further facilitated the arrest of two individuals in France and Spain. Law enforcement personally notified over 1,000 supporters of the group, including 15 suspected administrators, of their legal liability related to the participation in NoName057(16)‘s criminal activities.

On 1 February 2025, the Kaveri portal, operated by the Karnataka Stamps and Registration Department, was hit by a suspected Artificial Intelligence-based DDoS attack. The attack involved flooding the portal with around 20 lakh (2 000 000) searches, causing technical issues and disrupting property registration services. The portal's search strength of around 2.5 lakh (250 000) queries per day was exploited by the attackers, who used AI to pile the portal with search requests for documents such as Encumbrance Certificate (EC). The attack was detected after the portal was unable to handle the increased traffic, resulting in a significant drop in property registrations, from 8,500-9,000 daily to 556 on 1 February 2025. The Department of Egovernance was informed, and assistance was sought to track those responsible. Dayananda K A, Inspector General of Registration and Commissioner of Stamps, reported the attack to The Indian Express. The portal was fully restored by Wednesday evening, 5 February 2025, with property registration numbers returning to normal levels, reaching 7,225 with a revenue of around Rs 62.59 crore (625,9 million Rs)/ 6.94 million EURO.

Title (Company): Francesco Cancellato - Giuseppe Caccia - Francesco Nicodemo - Not available - Luca Casarini
Description: On Friday, 31 January 2025, WhatsApp alleged that nearly 90 journalists and civil society members using the messaging app were targeted by Israeli spyware owned by Paragon Solutions. The targets were alerted of a possible breach of their devices, with WhatsApp having high confidence that the 90 users in question had been targeted and possibly compromised. The alleged attacks were disrupted in December, but it is unclear how long the targets may have been under threat. WhatsApp sent Paragon a cease and desist letter and is exploring its legal options. A WhatsApp spokesperson reported the attack, stating that this is the latest example of why spyware companies must be held accountable for their unlawful actions. On March 19, the Canadian Research Institute The Citizen Lab published a report which mapped Paragon’s infrastructure, identifying deployments in countries including Canada, where potential links to the Ontario Provincial Police were found. Citizen Lab’s findings aided Meta in detecting and mitigating the described infiltrations. In November 2025, the Italian political adviser Francesco Nicodemo revealed that he was one of the victims targeted with Paragon. On 5 March 2025, the Naples and Rome prosecutors investigating the Paragon case confirmed in a technical report, which is not yet public, that Graphite software was used against the journalists Caccia, Casarini and Cancellato.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Silent Lynx, a Kazakhstan-origin threat actor, was linked to cyber attacks targeting entities in Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan, including embassies, lawyers, government-backed banks, and think tanks, between 27 December 2024 and 5 February 2025. The attacks commenced with spearphishing emails containing RAR archive attachments that delivered malicious payloads, granting remote access to compromised hosts. The payloads included a malicious C binary and a decoy PDF file, which ran a PowerShell script using Telegram bots for command execution and data exfiltration. Seqrite Labs detected the attacks and reported them to the public on 5 February 2025, noting tactical overlaps with YoroTrooper, a threat actor linked to attacks targeting the Commonwealth of Independent States countries.
Techniques Used: Automated Exfiltration, Drive-by Compromise, Phishing, Valid Accounts

Description: On 7 February 2025, a group of hackers, calling themselves TalibLeaks, carried out a massive cyber attack against the Taliban government of Afghanistan's computer systems. They published over 50GB of stolen documents and files online. The leaked records included claims that the Taliban had imprisoned over 1400 women and 16,000 men. Approximately 80 foreign nationals were also said to be being held in Taliban prisons. The leak came from 21 Taliban ministries and government agencies, including the Afghan Food & Drug Administration, Afghan Telecom Regulatory Authority, and the Ministry of Justice. The hackers stated that all files were taken in the past 12 months from compromised Taliban government networks. The Taliban's Ministry of Communications confirmed the leak, but claimed that most files had been publicly accessible for years and that no systems had been hacked. The hackers posted a note on Twitter, stating 'GDPR does not apply in Afghanistan, just like there are no women's rights.' The leak was reported on 7 February 2025.

On 31 October 2024, the city of McKinney, Texas, was breached by a cyberattack, which was discovered on 14 November 2024. The attackers gained unauthorized access to the city's government systems, exposing sensitive information of 17,751 residents, including names, addresses, Social Security numbers, drivers license numbers, credit card information, financial account data, and medical insurance information. The city's IT team severed any unauthorized activity and contacted the FBI, Department of Homeland Security, and Texas Department of Information. The city began sending breach notification letters to victims on 5 February 2025, and is providing one year of identity protection services. The incident was reported by the city of McKinney in breach notification letters and on the government website, and notices were filed with regulators in Maine, Texas, Vermont, and other states.

On the weekend of 5 January 2025, the Ausgleichskasse des Verbandes Swissmem was targeted by a ransomware attack, despite having comprehensive security measures in place. The attackers encrypted access to servers and data, and stole around 10% of the total data. The AK Swissmem informed the Eidgenössischen Datenschutz- und Öffentlichkeitsbeauftragten and the Bundesamt für Cybersicherheit about the incident and filed a criminal complaint with the Kantonspolizei Zürich. The attack was reported by the AK Swissmem on their website on 5 February 2025. The attackers have not published any of the stolen data, and there is no evidence of misuse. The AK Swissmem has set up a hotline for customers and informed affiliated companies, employees, and pensioners. The attack did not affect customer systems, and no money was stolen or transferred. The AK Swissmem resumed normal operations on a newly set up platform since 9 January 2025.

On 23 January 2025, Ecuador's public procurement system suffered a cyber attack, affecting 920 recruitment processes. Computer offenders accessed user credentials, modified key information, and deleted files, especially in the error validation phase. The attackers used malware specialized in extracting information from vulnerable systems, with the theft of keys and data coming from a computer with an IP address located in Guayaquil. The National Public Procurement Service (Sercop) reported the incident to the Attorney General's Office (FGE) on 25 January 2025, and submitted a technical report on 30 January 2025. The attack caused delays in the platform, complicating the execution of public procurements at the national level, and raised concerns about the vulnerability of state computer systems.

OOn 4 February 2025, the crypto exchange XeggeX suffered a cyberattack in which the CEO's account was compromised, preventing users from accessing their accounts and assets. XeggeX officials attributed the disruption to a security breach but assured users that funds remained secure despite the incident. Following the attack, the exchange successfully locked wallets to protect user assets. The XeggeX team announced that they were actively working to resolve the issue and restore access to affected accounts. The incident was acknowledged on the exchange’s website and social media channels, with the company stating that operations were temporarily suspended but would resume soon. However, the attack raised concerns among investors and users, with some speculating that it could be an orchestrated rug-pull fraud.

Tata Technologies Ltd., an Indian public multinational tech firm, was hit by a ransomware attack that impacted the company network on 31 January 2025. The attack, reported to India's national stock exchange, temporarily affected some of the company's IT assets. Client delivery services remained fully operational. As a precautionary measure, some IT services were suspended, but have now been restored. A detailed investigation is underway in collaboration with cybersecurity experts. No major ransomware groups have claimed the attack, and it is unclear if the attacker managed to steal any data from the company.

On 27 January 2025, a cyber attack was launched against the websites of German railway providers Metronom, Erixx, and Enno, resulting in their websites being inaccessible. The attack, suspected to be a DDoS attack, involved a botnet sending numerous requests to the websites, causing them to collapse due to overload. The affected websites include www.dermetronom.de, www.erixx.de, and www.derenno.de. Metronom spokesperson Simon Mrtens informed the Abendblatt about the incident. Despite countermeasures being taken, the websites were expected to remain restricted until the weekend. The attack did not affect customer data, and train operations continued normally. Customers were advised to use alternative information channels. The incident was reported by the Abendblatt on 30 January 2025.

Between 11 January and 1 April 2024, the EMBARGO ransomware gang breached the systems of NorthBay Healthcare, a regional healthcare system in California. The gang gained access to sensitive information, including national insurance numbers, passport numbers, financial information, medical data, health insurance data, and credit and debit card numbers. The attack affected 569,012 people and forced the hospital to turn away patients and cancel appointments. Those affected received identity protection services for one year. The data breach was detected on 11 September 2024 and affected users were notified on 29 January 2025.

Medusa ransomware group compromised and stole data from Hospital de Alta Complejidad El Cruce “Néstor Kirchner” in Florencio Varela, Buenos Aires Province in January 2025. The attack, carried out by one of Medusa’s affiliates, compromised and lost over 760GB of sensitive data. As a result, the hospital’s IT department has taken its official website offline to contain the incident. Medusa is demanding a ransom of $200,000 in Bitcoin for deleting the stolen files, with a payment deadline set for February 6. The file tree published on Medusa’s blog on the Tor network reveals more than 650,000 lines of data, including files containing Protected Health Information (PHI), such as diagnostic images and laboratory test results linked to patients’ names. Additionally, the leaked data includes Personally Identifiable Information (PII), such as dates of birth, passport numbers, driver’s licenses, and full addresses.

On 30 January 2025, hackers attacked the municipality of Torre del Greco, causing a computer blackout that lasted over 24 hours. The attack, which occurred from Thursday afternoon to the next day, resulted in a lack of internet connection and slowed down work in all sectors, including the urban police. The registry offices were forced to close and Mayor Luigi Mennella postponed a junta session. Specialist technicians investigated the cause of the attack, which was suspected to be either a failure, sabotage, or a hacking attempt.

On 2 January 2025, Community Health Center (CHC), a US healthcare provider, discovered that a skilled criminal hacker had gained access to its network in mid-October 2024, resulting in a data breach that impacted the personal and health data of 1,060,936 patients. The hacker stole files containing patients' personal and health information, including names, dates of birth, addresses, phone numbers, emails, Social Security numbers, medical diagnoses, treatment details, test results, and health insurance information. CHC reported the breach to Maine's attorney general and hired investigators to assess the incident's impact and secure its systems. The hacker did not encrypt any compromised systems, and the security breach did not impact CHC's operations. CHC believed they stopped the hacker's access within hours, and there was no current threat to their systems. The breach was made public on 31 January 2025.

On 26 January 2025, New York Blood Center Enterprises (NYBCe) was hit by a ransomware attack, disrupting critical blood donation services across the US. The attack was identified and confirmed by NYBCe and third-party cybersecurity experts. Law enforcement was notified. No information was provided about the identity of the perpetrator or whether any data was accessed. The incident was disclosed by NYBCe in a statement on 29 January 2025. New York State Senator Dean Murray also informed the public about the attack and its impact on a scheduled blood drive on 30 January 2025. NYBCe provides blood donations and products to 70 area hospitals and serves over 75 million people across the country.

On 30 January 2025, Ukraine's cyber forces, specifically a group from Military Intelligence , launched a DDoS attack on the digital infrastructure of Russian companies Gazprom and Gazprom Neft, on the anniversary of the Heroes of Kruty battle. The attack, which started on 28 January 2025, targeted online services of enterprises that support the Russian army, resulting in Gazprom customers being unable to access their personal accounts, use the company's online services, pay for fuel with fuel cards, or accumulate and redeem bonus points on their accounts. Ukrainian intelligence services claimed responsibility for the attack, stating it was a tribute to the heroes of Kruty.

The Town of Apex in the United States experienced a ransomware attack on 2 July 2024, which compromised several of the town's systems, including utility billing. The town immediately launched an investigation, engaged the services of the North Carolina Joint Cybersecurity Task Force, and reported the incident to federal law enforcement. The town has been working to restore systems in a secure manner and has made significant progress, but the incident response process has required extensive time, labor, and resources. The town has also been providing updates on the incident and has informed the public that emergency services were not interrupted and remained operational throughout the incident

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Bitdefender Labs has identified an ongoing cyber-espionage campaign orchestrated by the threat actor UAC-0063 targeting organizations in Central Asia and Europe. Initially focused on government institutions in Central Asia, the group has expanded its operations to include embassies in Germany, the UK, the Netherlands, Romania, and Georgia, aiming to exfiltrate sensitive data from high-value targets.  The attackers gained initial access by weaponizing stolen Microsoft Word documents from previously compromised victims, exemplifying a supply chain attack strategy. These malicious documents deployrf the HATVIBE loader and other malware, including DownEx, DownExPyer (also known as CHERRYSPY), and PyPlunderPlug, a USB-based data exfiltrator. To evade detection, the attackers delivered the weaponized documents via phishing emails that contain download links rather than direct attachments. Upon opening the documents, users encountered blurred pages and misleading warnings urging them to enable macros, which triggered malware execution. CERT-UA has assessed with moderate confidence that UAC-0063 is linked to the Russian cyber-espionage group APT28 (BlueDelta). Still, no definitive technical evidence existed to confirm this connection for Bitdefender Labs.  In September and October 2024, multiple alerts detected weaponized documents uploaded from Kazakhstan likely exfiltrated from Kazakh embassies based on metadata. On November 21, 2024, the latest attack attempt involved a malicious document hosted on a compromised server, which was sent via phishing emails. On April 4, 2024, a newly compiled version of DownExPyer was deployed against a target in Romania, while on January 12, 2023, the PyPlunderPlug USB exfiltration tool was found on a compromised system in Germany.
Techniques Used: Automated Exfiltration, Drive-by Compromise, Phishing, Valid Accounts

Description: On 28 January 2025, the strassen.gr.ch website, run by the Civil Engineering Office of the Canton of Graubünden in Switzerland, was the victim of a cyber attack. The attack occurred between 10:00 and 15:30, making road map data inaccessible.

On 15 November 2019, the Rouen University Hospital Centre was targeted by a large-scale cyberattack. The IT department noticed the encryption of their data at 7 p.m..
