A PowerShell dropper observed on the device deployed two encoded files, delivering the Tavdig backdoor and a Symantec binary, enabling further reconnaissance. Secret Blizzard, another actor, used Tavdig to install the KazuarV2 backdoor for persistence and subsequent operations. Microsoft was still investigating whether Secret Blizzard leveraged access to Storm-1837's backdoor or purchased access, which would indicate cooperation. Microsoft assumed that Secret Blizzard likely wanted to exploit this access to gain further strategic access at the ministerial level. The background to this cyber incident was an incident published a week earlier in the first part of the report, which is also available here. In that incident, Secret Blizzard compromised the infrastructure of Pakistani threat actor Storm-0156 to gain access to Afghan government entities' computer systems.

Between March and April 2024, the Russian state-sponsored actor Secret Blizzard, also known as Turla, was observed leveraging the Amadey bot malware to deploy a known backdoor called Kazuar on target devices associated with the Ukrainian military. The attack involved commandeering Amadey bots to deploy a backdoor known as Tavdig, which was then used to install an updated version of Kazuar. The Microsoft threat intelligence team reported the cyber attack on 11 December 2024. Microsoft was still investigating whether Secret Blizzard leveraged access to Storm-1837's backdoor or purchased access, indicating cooperation in the form of Malware-as-a-Service (MaaS). Microsoft assumed that Secret Blizzard likely wanted to exploit this access to gain further strategic access at the ministerial level. The background to this cyber incident was an incident published a week earlier in the first part of the report, which is also available here. In that incident, Secret Blizzard compromised the infrastructure of Pakistani threat actor Storm-0156 to gain access to Afghan government entities' computer systems.

On 9 December 2024, unknown threat actors launched a cyber attack on Anadolu Insurance's mobile application, Sigortam Cepte. The attackers gained unauthorized access to the notification message service but did not affect the databases. Anadolu Insurance publicly disclosed the attack on social media and in statements, assuring users that their personal data was secure and no data leakage occurred. The application was temporarily shut down as a precautionary measure but was reopened the following day.  The attack was detected when users received abusive and fraud-related notifications, including a false promise of double repayment if Bitcoin was sent to a specified address.

Title (Company): WK Kellogg Co - Hertz - Western Alliance Bank - Cleo
Description: A zero-day vulnerability in Cleo's managed file transfer (MFT) software products LexiCom, VLTrader, and Harmony has been actively exploited by hackers to breach corporate networks and steal data since at least 3 December 2024. The flaw allowed unrestricted file uploads and downloads, leading to remote code execution. This vulnerability (CVE-2024-50623) affected versions 5.8.0.21 and earlier and bypassed a previous patch released in October 2024. Cybersecurity company Huntress wrote in its report of 9 December 2024 that at least ten organizations in industries like consumer goods, food, trucking, and shipping have been impacted, with the most vulnerable systems in the United States. Furthermore, Huntress wrote that the patch offered by Cleo does not work. Cybersecurity expert Kevin Beaumont commented on the cyber incident on Mastodon on 10 December 2024 and said the Termite ransomware group had a zero-day exploit for those affected products. The Clop ransomware group claimed responsibility for the cyber incident on 15 December 2024.

Title (Company): Unspecified US Government Agency - Unspecified US Energy Company - Unspecified Global Organisations - Sophos
Description: Guan Tianfeng (also known as GbigMao) and his employer Sichuan Silence Information Technology Company compromised approximately 81,000 Sophos firewalls worldwide, including over 23,000 in the United States and 36 protecting US critical infrastructure, between 26 July 2018 and May 2020. According to a US Department of Justice indictment unsealed on 10 December 2024, victims included a US energy company active in oil production and a US government agency. The indictment stated that Sichuan Silence sold services and data acquired through the intrusions to Chinese companies and government entities. The threat actors exploited a zero-day SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2020-12271) with the intent of exfiltrating data and potentially deploying Ragnarok ransomware. Sophos discovered the intrusion, which it named the Asnarök attack after the deployed trojan, on 22 April 2020 following reports of unusual database field values. Sophos issued a hotfix on 23 April 2020, patching the vulnerability, removing malware and preventing ransomware deployment. Post-exploitation analysis revealed experimental vulnerability testing dating back to February 2020, linked to the Double Helix Research Institute in Sichuan, China. On 10 December 2024, the US Department of Justice indicted Guan Tianfeng on charges of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and computer fraud. The US Department of the Treasury simultaneously designated Sichuan Silence Information Technology Company and Guan Tianfeng under sanctions.

The Japanese corporation Ito En confirmed on 6 December 2024, that its U.S. subsidiary was hit with ransomware. The company is the largest producer of green tea in Japan and has subsidiaries in the U.S., Australia, China and Indonesia. The company said a third party attacked Ito En North America as they discovered on 2 December 2024, that some file servers were encrypted. The company said the file servers have been isolated from the network and are currently being restored using backup data from before the attack. Additionally, the information leak is being investigated.

On 21 November 2024 at the latest, unknown threat actors launched a ransomware attack on Artivion, a leading manufacturer of cardiac surgery devices. The attack encrypted some of its systems and stole data from compromised systems. The company took certain systems offline, initiated an investigation, and engaged external advisors to assess, contain, and remediate the incident. The attack disrupted Artivion's corporate operations, order processing, and shipping, but most disruptions have been addressed.  Artivion disclosed the incident in a Monday 8-K filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on 9 December 2024. Artivion explained that it is working to securely restore its systems as quickly as possible and evaluate any notification obligations. The company also believes it will incur additional costs not covered by insurance.

Unknown threat actors launched a ransomware attack on Kurita America, a US subsidiary of Japanese water treatment company Kurita Water Industries, headquartered in Minnesota. This resulted in the encryption of multiple servers, potentially leaking customer, business partner, and employee data to third parties. On 29 November 2024, an alert from the security systems triggered the investigation. The main servers were already restored, and business operations were not disrupted, as reported by the company on 7 December 2024.

Ukrainian intelligence agency HUR executed a DDoS attack against Russia's Gazprombank, one of Russia's largest banks. The attack caused users to experience difficulties accessing services and disrupted financial operations tied to Russia's war efforts in Ukraine. Cyber specialists from Ukraine’s military intelligence (HUR) successfully attacked Gazprombank's systems, a source in the agency told the Kyiv Independent on 5 December 2024. The attack reportedly rendered Gazprombank’s website inaccessible in France and Germany, with its mobile application also experiencing outages.

On 9 December 2024, unknown threat actors carried out a DDoS cyberattack against the municipal websites of presumably multiple Danish municipalities. The ones confirming outages included Albertslund, Dragr, Esbjerg, Frederiksberg, Frederikshavn, Greve, Guldborgsund, Haderslev, Hedensted, Horsens, Ikast-Brande, Mariagerfjord, Mors, Nstved, Aabenraa, and Aarhus. The Municipality of Vejle confirmed the DDoS attack on Facebook, causing its website outage. The pro-Russian hacktivist group NoName057(16) announced DDoS attacks on 9 December 2024, against several Danish municipalities, including Aarhus, Esbjerg, Helsingor, Vejle and Horsens.

Title (Company): Council of Professional Colleges of Veterinaries of Castile and Len
Description: On 19 October 2024, unknown threat actors carried out a cyber attack on the Council of Professional Colleges of Veterinaries of Castile and León, compromising the personal data of 2.6% of users registered in the company’s animal identification system database. The stolen data included first name, last name, NIF, address, phone numbers, and email addresses. The breach was detected on 21 October 2024 and reported by the Directorate-General for Agricultural and Livestock Production of the Department of Agriculture, Livestock and Rural Development. The stolen data raises concerns about its potential use for identity impersonation crimes. The Council of Professional Colleges of Veterinaries of Castile and León has notified the Spanish Agency for Data Protection and filed a complaint with the National Police on 3 November 2024.

On 2 December 2024, Pembina Trails School Division, located in Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada, was hit by a ransomware attack, resulting in some of its systems, including phone lines, being taken offline. The division's network system was still down on the following day. Pembina Trails staff were informed of the attack on Tuesday, and the division was working on a fix. The specific nature of the cyber security incident and whether any personal data may have been exposed was not revealed. Outside experts were brought in to investigate, and the division was restoring interrupted services and investigating the incident. The division's information technology staff detected unusual activities in the network system on the morning of 2 December. The attack was reported by Supt. and CEO Shelley Amos in a letter to staff and parents, and later commented on by technology analyst and journalist Carmi Levi, who praised the division's quick response to the incident. Levi noted that the attack followed a depressingly familiar trajectory, reflecting a growing realization within the cybercriminal community that schools, school boards, and other public-facing institutions make for highly desirable targets. Levi also stated that the district will ultimately have to share specific guidance on what exactly happened, what's being done to recover from this event, and what steps will be taken to harden its systems, staff, and students against future attacks.

In Late November 2024, unknown threat actors carried out a cyber attack on Watsonville Community Hospital, California, causing a network outage that shut down the hospital's internet connection and electronic systems. The attack, which started last week, is still ongoing, and an investigation by third-party IT specialists is underway to determine the type of attack and if any personal information has been compromised. The hospital's emergency, inpatient, and outpatient services remain open, but patients are experiencing delays in the emergency room due to the manual use of paper patient charts. The incident was disclosed by hospital spokesperson Nancy Gere on 7 December 2024.

On 4 December 2024, PIH Health, a California hospital network, was breached by a ransomware attack launched by unknown threat actors, disrupting its network and IT systems across multiple facilities, including PIH Health Downey Hospital, PIH Health Good Samaritan Hospital, PIH Health Whittier Hospital, urgent care centers, physicians' offices, home health, and hospice services. Despite the attack, urgent care centers and emergency rooms remained operational. Critical systems such as patient health records, laboratory, pharmacy, radiology, patient registration, and other IT tools were taken offline. Phone service was also disrupted for most locations. PIH Health enlisted third-party cyber forensic specialists to determine the extent of the attack and potential data compromise. The incident was publicly disclosed by PIH Health on its website on 4 December 2024.

On 21 November 2024, unknown threat actors carried out a sophisticated cyberattack on White Lake Township Hall in Oakland County, Michigan, compromising the township's financial transactions and impacting a new issue of infrastructure bonds related to a 50 million USD  civic center project. The attack, which was detected on the same day, has put the project on hold. White Lake Township Police Chief Daniel Keller and Township Supervisor Rik Kowall informed the public about the attack. The incident is under active investigation by federal authorities and impacted financial institutions, who are coordinating with the White Lake Township Police Dept.

On 30 November 2024, the 8Base ransomware group launched a cyber attack on Croatia's Port of Rijeka, exfiltrating sensitive data, including contracts, accounting information, invoices, receipts, certificates, employment contracts, and other personal and confidential documents. The stolen data will subsequently be published on the group’s Tor leak site if the port declines to meet the ransom demand. Despite the breach, CEO Duško Grabovac assured the public that the port's operations remained unaffected. On Februar 2025, the leak site of the 8Base group was seized and at the same time, four European nationals suspected group members were arrested in Thailand.

On 4 December 2024, BT Group's BT Conferencing business division was breached by the Black Basta Ransomware Gang, who claimed to have stolen 500GB of sensitive data, including financial, corporate, and personal information, such as passport copies, and threatened to leak it unless a ransom is paid. The attackers published folder listings and screenshots of documents as proof. BT Group took impacted servers offline, stating that the incident was restricted to specific elements of the platform and did not affect live BT Conferencing services or other BT Group or customer services. The breach was reported by BleepingComputer and Hackread.com, and BT Group is working with regulatory and law enforcement bodies to investigate the incident. Black Basta added BT's btci.com and btconferencing.com domains to their data leak site.

The Pakistani-based threat actor Storm-0156 (also known as SideCopy or Transparent Tribe) compromised Afghan government networks between December 2022 and mid-2023, using CrimsonRAT and Waiscot malware to gain access to these systems. This campaign focused on espionage, collecting sensitive information from Afghan government entities. Storm-0156's activities align with its broader objective of targeting South Asia's government, military, and industrial systems for intelligence. Additionally, in another cyber incident, the Russian state-sponsored hacking group Turla infiltrated the Pakistani threat actor and used that access to infiltrate the Afghan government.

In June 2024, the China-linked threat actor known as MirrorFace launched a spear-phishing campaign targeting individuals and organizations in Japan, delivering backdoors known as NOOPDOOR and ANEL. The campaign used emails with links to Microsoft OneDrive, containing booby-trapped ZIP archives with themes related to interview requests and Japan’s economic security. The attackers used three infection vectors, including macro-enabled Word documents and Windows shortcut files, to deliver a malicious dropper called ROAMINGMOUSE, which acted as a dropper for ANEL and NOOPDOOR components. The backdoors were used to capture screenshots, upload/download files, load executables, and run commands via cmd.exe. Trend Micro reported the attack and provided technical analysis. The campaign was ongoing as of December 2024. In January 2025, the Japanese government attributed the campaign to MirrorFace.

Between December 2022 and October 2024, the Russian state-sponsored hacking group Secret Blizzard (also known as Turla) breached the infrastructure of Pakistani threat actor Storm-0156. It hijacked their command and control servers to gain access to already compromised networks of the Afghan government. Turla deployed their malware tools, TwoDash and Statuezy. The attackers also targeted the Pakistani threat actors, gaining access to valuable data such as malware tools and stolen credentials and data. Lumen's Black Lotus Labs and Microsoft's Threat Intelligence Team tracked this campaign and reported that Turla's operation was primarily used to deploy backdoors on Afghan government entities. The attackers' approach allowed them to gather intelligence stealthily without exposing themselves or their toolset, shifting blame and complicating attribution efforts.
Techniques Used: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel, Valid Accounts

Title (Company): Hidalgo Laboratory - Stamboulian Health Services - Rossi Center
Description: Around 23 November 2024, the Rossi Group, which includes Rossi, Stamboulian and Hidalgo Laboratory medical centers, suffered a ransomware cyberattack by the FOG group, which paralyzed the systems, lowered websites, and prevented patients from doing studies and taking turns. The attackers encrypted information and asked for a cryptocurrency ransom in return, but no deadline was given, and the company did not enter into negotiations. According to the company's CEO, Omar De Fornari, no patient data was compromised, but forensic analysis has not confirmed this.

On 25 November 2024, Unknown Threat Actors launched a ransomware attack against ENGlobal Corporation, a major energy industry contractor, by illegally accessing and encrypting some of its data files, limiting employee access to its IT system and hindering operations. ENGlobal Corporation reported the incident to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, has started an internal investigation, and has hired external cybersecurity experts to address the issue. On January 27, 2025, ENGlobal Corporation updated its first report and added that the incident disrupted access to key business applications, including financial and operational reporting systems, for approximately six weeks. However, as of January 27, 2025, all operations and corporate functions have been fully restored, and the Company believes the threat actor no longer has access to its systems. Additionally, the affected IT system contained sensitive personal information, and the Company plans to notify impacted individuals and relevant regulatory authorities in compliance with federal and state laws.

Unknown threat actors encrypted the electronic systems of three medical practices and their branches at the Hofer Medical Center in Germany on 25 November 2024, reported the Frankenpost on 26 November 2024. Since then, the electronic systems have been non-functional. Countermeasures and the consequences for patients are currently being assessed.

A ransomware attack targeted a server managed by DBP, Inc., a medical transcription vendor contracted by the Veterans Health Administration (VHA). The attack potentially exposed the protected health information (PHI) of 2,302 Veterans, including full names, medical record information, and Social Security numbers. The attack involved encrypting and possibly copying files stored on the server, but it did not compromise the VA electronic health record system. DBP, Inc. responded by disconnecting the compromised server from the internet, purchasing new hardware, and implementing enhanced security controls.

A significant cyberattack has targeted the UK Ministry of Defence (MoD), resulting in the theft and leak of nearly 600 employee passwords on the dark web. inews first reported on this cyber incident on 29 November 2024. The breach, attributed to suspected Russian hackers, exposed sensitive information of military personnel, civilian staff, and defence contractors. The stolen credentials provided access to the Defence Gateway portal, a critical platform for communication, HR services, and health records, though it does not store classified information. Affected employees are primarily UK-based, with others stationed overseas in Iraq, Qatar, Cyprus, and mainland Europe. Initial investigations suggest hackers exploited vulnerabilities in personal devices used to access the platform, bypassing its multi-factor authentication system. Although no direct evidence links the attack to the Kremlin, the tools used indicate state-sponsored involvement, aligning with previous high-profile cyberattacks on Western institutions. The MoD, in collaboration with the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), is investigating and working to mitigate potential harm. This incident occurs amidst heightened UK-Russia tensions, underscoring growing concerns over cyberattacks and espionage activities targeting critical national infrastructure.

On 28 November 2024, unknown threat actors carried out a malware cyberattack on Dewan Farooque Motors Limited (DFML), crashing the company's IT servers and corrupting its data. The attack led to the postponement of the DFML board of directors meeting, which was originally scheduled for 28 November 2024. The incident was disclosed by DFML in a stock filing on 30 November 2024, and reported by Dawn, a Pakistani English-language newspaper, on the same day. The company stated that the restoration of its information system and financial data, including that of the first quarter ending 30 September 2024, is necessary and will take considerable time.

In mid-November 2024, a cyber attack by South East Asian threat actors, who refer to themselves as 'Waste', breached the confidentiality of Uganda's central bank, 'Benki Kuu ya Uganda', by infiltrating the bank's IT infrastructure and transferring 62.4 billion Ugandan shillings, equivalent to around 16 million euros, from an account. The Ugandan newspaper Daily Monitor reported the attack on 28 November 2024. The central bank managed to recover more than half of the stolen amount. The police initially led the investigation but were later taken over by the country's secret services. An external company was also commissioned to carry out an investigation. President Yoweri Museveni was involved in the case.  Uganda’s biggest independent newspaper, Daily Monitor, reported that the theft may have involved collusion by insiders. According to a report in the online Monitor, “security agencies are treating it as an ‘inside job’, that was the result of collusion between the Bank of Uganda, the Finance Ministry’s Treasury Department and the Accountant General’s Office.”

The Russia-aligned cybercrime group 'RomCom' exploited two zero-day vulnerabilities, one in Mozilla Firefox and the other in Microsoft Windows, in November 2024, ESET disclosed in a technical report. The vulnerabilities in question are CVE-2024-9680, a use-after-free breach in the Firefox Animation component, and CVE-2024-49039, a vulnerability of privilege escalation in Windows Task Scheduler. The attackers used a fake website to redirect potential victims to a server hosting the malicious payload, which combined the two flaws to achieve code execution and release the RomCom RAT. The attack chain involved social engineering for the distribution of malicious URLs, and the exploit was activated if the site was visited by a vulnerable version of the Firefox browser. The attackers were able to execute arbitrary code without any interaction from the user, leading to the installation of the RomCom backdoor on the victim's computer. The attack was attributed to RomCom, also known as Storm-0978, Tropical Scorpius, UAC-0180, UNC2596, and Void Rabisu, which has a history of cybercrime and espionage operations dating back to at least 2022. The US government has recommended avoiding memory-unsafe languages to prevent this type of flaw. ESET telemetry data shows that most of the victims who visited the site hosting the exploit were in Europe and North America.
Techniques Used: Content Injection, Drive-by Compromise, Exploit Public-Facing Application, Phishing

Description: The hacktivist group NoName057(16) conducted a denial-of-service attack targetinghe Coroners Court of Victoria on 25 November 2024. Threat researcher Dark Web Informer reported the incident, which was later confirmed by the Coroners Court of Victoria. A spokesperson for the court stated that while the attack disrupted its public website, there was no unauthorized access to sensitive systems, including case records, employee data, or financial information. Immediate actions were taken to mitigate the impact and restore service. This incident is part of a broader campaign by NoName, a ransomware group implicated in global DDoS-for-hire schemes. .

On 27 November 2024, the Costa Rican Petroleum Refinery RECOPE was targeted by unknown threat actors in a ransomware attack, forcing the institution to resort to manual fuel sales. The attack was detected in the early hours of the same day, prompting the activation of security protocols and an ongoing analysis of the attack's impact. RECOPE reported the incident in a press release on the same day, assuring customers that supply and service were unaffected. In collaboration with the Computer Security Incident Response Center of the Cybersecurity Directorate of the Ministry of Science, Innovation, Technology and Telecommunications of Costa Rica (Micitt), the institution's technical team is working to resolve the situation and strengthen security systems. RECOPE's president, Karla Montero, made a public call for calm while experts analyzed the attack's impact.The unknown perpetrators demanded a ransom of 5 million US dollars.

On 27 November 2024, an unknown threat actor launched a ransomware attack on the city of Hoboken, causing widespread issues and service shutdowns ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. The attack resulted in the suspension of online city services, cancellation of municipal court and street sweeping, but waste collection and recreational programs continued. The Hoboken Police Department, City administration, and IT department are investigating the attack. No group has claimed responsibility for the incident.

Title (Company): National center for Human rights of the Republic of Uzbekistan - KMG-Security - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Between July 2024 and November 2024, the Russian state-sponsored threat actor TAG-110 carried out a cyber-espionage campaign targeting human rights groups, private security companies, and educational institutions in Central Asia, East Asia, and Europe. The attackers used custom malware, including the Hatvibe loader and the Cherryspy backdoor, delivered through malicious Microsoft Word email attachments, to infect at least 62 unique victims, primarily in Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, Turkmenistan, and Kazakhstan. The campaign, which is believed to have been ongoing since at least 2021, aimed to gather insights into geopolitical events in neighbouring countries and reinforce Russia's military efforts in Ukraine. The attacks were attributed to TAG-110 by Recorded Futures Insikt Group, noting an overlap with a group tracked by CERT-UA as UAC-0063. CERT-UA, based on medium confidence, has linked UAC-0063 to the Russian cyber-espionage group APT28, believed to be operated by GRU Unit 26165, but has stopped short of equating the two threat actors.

On 23 October 2024, the RansomHub gang breached the confidentiality and availability of the information systems of the City of Coppell, Texas with a ransomware attack. The City of Coppell reported widespread technology issues, including an internet outage, unavailable WiFi at city facilities, and disruptions to library services, permitting and inspection platforms, and the municipal court. The City of Coppell announced the attack on 23 October 2024 and by the RansomHub gang on 25 November 2024. The City Manager of the City of Coppell, Mike Land, informed the public about the attack and its potential impact on the data of individuals and vendors. The City of Coppell restored some of its operations by 1, 15 and 20 November 2024.

Title (Company): National Institute for Agricultural and Food Research and Technology (INIA-CSIC)
Description: Unknown actors encrypted at least one device in the network of the Spanish National Institute for Agricultural and Food Research and Technology (INIA-CSIC) since at least 12 November 2024, both anonymous sources and the spokeswoman for the Ministry for Digital Transformation and Civil Service reported to the Spanish daily El Pais on 26 November 2024. In an internal e-mail dated 12 November 2024, the INIA-CSIC secretariat announced that a computer problem had occurred. On 16 November 2024, those in charge also admitted that the problem was a cyber attack. At the time of reporting, 26 November 2024, the cyber incident was considered resolved, although access restrictions for employees remained in place.

In 2024, the Chinese cyber-espionage group Flax Typhoon infiltrated Paraguayan government networks, intercepting emails and accessing the email server. The United States Embassy in Paraguay and the Ministry of Information and Communication Technologies (MITIC) publicly disclosed the incident on 26 November 2024. The attack was first detected by the Ministry of Information and Communication Technologies (Mitic), after which the Paraguay government requested the help of U.S. experts. These details were given by the Director of Cybersecurity and Information Protection at MITIC, Jorge Levera,  in ABC Paraguay on 26 and 27 November 2024. He said that in April 2024, they noticed external traffic when the workplaces were not occupied. As a result, MITIC reportedly recognized that the e-mail server was accessed without authorization and found out in collaboration with the U.S. Southern Command that e-mails were intercepted in May and September 2024. In the media reports, Levera speaks of a front company in China that offers its services to other companies and the Chinese government. The attackers' source IP was traced back to China, and while the reasons behind the attack are still unknown, it is presumed that the company may have sold the data to the Chinese government. Meanwhile, in its press release, the U.S. Embassy in Paraguay refers to Flax Typhoon.

The Termite ransomware group disrupted the managed services hosted environment of supply chain management and software provider Blue Yonder since at least 21 November 2024, Blue Yonder reported in an incident notification for the first time on 22 November 2024. The incident involved a ransomware attack, and at least at the coffee chain Starbucks, the incident disrupted the system they use to track and manage their employees' schedules. The retailer Wm Morrison Supermarkets was also affected. In December 2024, the Termite ransomware group claimed to have exfiltrated 680 GB of data, including databases, email lists "for future attacks" (over 16,000 entries), miscellaneous documents (over 200,000), reports, and insurance documents. On 29 January 2025, Morrisons supermarkets reported that the cyberattack on its technology supplier, Blue Yonder, in November disrupted product availability and impacted Christmas sales. CEO Rami Baitieh explained that the attack forced the shutdown of the company’s warehouse management system, resulting in a temporary loss of visibility over fresh produce and fruit and vegetable stock levels.

The Bank of France was allegedly breached by the Near2tlg hacker group, who claim to have stolen sensitive data, including employee identities, customer bank accounts and transaction history, internal reports, financial strategies, and confidential communications, which were put up for sale on Telegram and BreachForums for $10,000, with sample documents including position papers and administrative reports on 23 November 2024. However, the full scope of the intrusion remains unclear. On Monday, 25 November, the communications department of the Banque de France told Ouest-France that “there was no attack on the secure information system”. However, the Banque de France acknowledges that “there was occasional external access to an HR (human resources) extranet. But no sensitive personal or financial data was compromised”. The institution has closed the extranet site affected by this cybercriminal visit.

In 2022, Russian state-sponsored hackers, specifically Unit 26165 of the 85th Main Special Services Center, also known as APT 28, Forest Blizzard, Fancy Bear and GruesomeLarch, breached a Washington, D.C.-based organization, named Organization A in Volexity's report, focused on Ukraine by exploiting Wi-Fi connectivity, using a new attack technique dubbed a 'nearest neighbour attack'. The attackers initially attempted a password-spray attack against a public entry point but were hampered by a multi-factor authentication requirement. They then compromised at least two nearby organization's networks, named Organisations B and C in Volexity's report, using credentials originating from a password-spray attack in January and February 2022. Starting from these two organizations close to the actual target, they connected to the victim's Wi-Fi network, as the target's Wi-Fi system didn't require multi-factor authentication. Volexity detected the hacking campaign on 4 February 2022, when hackers began exfiltrating data through compressed files, using Microsoft's native Cipher.exe utility to evade detection. Following Volexity's initial comprehensive analysis and countermeasures at an unspecified point, Volexity discovered that the hackers could reaccess Organisation C's network approximately one month after the initial countermeasures. The breach was first reported at the 2024 Cyberwarcon conference in Arlington, Virginia, and was disclosed by Steven Adair, a researcher and the president of Volexity and Ars Technica, on 22 November 2024.  The attackers claimed no responsibility for the incident.
Techniques Used: Drive-by Compromise, Exploit Public-Facing Application, Wi-Fi Networks

Description: On 4 October 2024, Hackers breached U.S. satellite maker Maxar Space Systems and accessed personal data belonging to its employees, including name, social security number and the employee number. The company informs in a notification to impacted individuals. On 11 October 2024, immediately after discovering the unauthorized access, the company took action to prevent the hackers from reaching further into the system. The company said: “Our information security team discovered that a hacker using a Hong Kong-based IP address targeted and accessed a Maxar system containing certain files with employee personal data.”

In mid-november 2024, unknown threat actors launched a cyber attack against Occitanie’s agricultural chambers, resulting in data theft and encryption of computer systems. The attack was disclosed to the public on 21 November 2024 with the Chamber stating that the situation was under control and that partially operations were already possible. The National Information Systems Directorate (DNSI) and the National Information Systems Security Agency (ANSSI) are working to restore all services as soon as possible. The Chamber has lodged a complaint with the authorities. The incidents bears similarities to an incident which affected the departmental chamber of Haute-Garonne.

Unknown threat actors breached the Haute-Garonne Chamber of Agriculture's information systems, stealing and encrypting data. The attack, which began 17 November 2024, was reported by the organization's president, Denis Carretier, and director, Jol Cassagne, who informed the public about the attack. The National Information Systems Directorate DNSI and the National Information Systems Security Agency ANSSI are working together to reestablish all services as soon as possible. A complaint has been lodged with the authorities. The incident coincided with another affecting the higher regional chamber of Occitane.

Title (Company): Federal Intelligence Service - Bundeskriminalamt (BKA) - Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution
Description: On 22 November 2024, DDoS attacks against the websites of German security authorities, including the Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA), the Federal Intelligence Service (BND), and the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV) were launched. The attacks rendered the websites offline for several hours without any compromise of the IT systems. The apparently pro-palestianian group Mr Hamza claimed to be behind the attack.

On 21 November 2024, unknown hacktivists breached The Real World platform associated with Andrew Tate. The threat actors exploited a critical security vulnerability and leaked over 794,000 usernames, nearly 325,000 email addresses, and private chat messages. Additionally, the primary chatroom was flooded with pro-feminist and LGBTQ emojis, temporarily banning users, and deleting attachments. The incident was first reported by DailyDot and DDoSecrets.

Over 2,000 Palo Alto Networks firewalls were hacked in November 2024, exploiting recently patched zero-day vulnerabilities CVE-2024-0012 and CVE-2024-9474 in PAN-OS. The attackers gained administrator privileges and deployed web shells on compromised devices, granting persistent remote access. Palo Alto Networks and their Unit 42 tracked the exploitation activity, and Shadowserver researchers reported that approximately 2,000 devices were hacked, primarily in the US (554) and India (461), followed by Thailand (80), Mexico (48), Indonesia (43), Turkey (41), the U.K. (39), Peru (36), and South Africa (35). The incident was publicly disclosed by Palo Alto Networks and Unit 42. IP addresses 136.144.17.173, 239.218.251, and 216.73.162 were identified as being associated with the malicious activities. Palo Alto Networks initially warned customers on 8 November about restricting access to their next-generation firewalls due to an unspecified remote code execution flaw, and the company has observed a notable increase in threat activity following the public release of technical insights by third-party researchers on November 19, 2024. The attackers' identities and motivations remain yet unknown.

On 18 November 2024, a INPS Servizi S.p.A., a subsidary of the Italian National Institute of Social Security INPS, suffered a ransomware attack, breaching its computer security and encrypting sensitive data. The attack is suspected by experts to be conducted by ransomware group Lynx, an apparent re-organisation of INC Ransomware group. The incident had no impact on the computer systems of the INPS, but the website of INPS Servizi as well as management applications provided to the INPS were inaccessible at time of reporting. However, the Contact Center, the main service provided by INPS Servizi, was not hit by the attack and remains operational. Following the incident, INPS is providing active technical and advisory support to facilitate the rapid restoration of the IT systems of INPS Servizi SPA.

Title (Company): Canton of Schwyz - Backslash - Municipalities in the canton of Aargau - Canton of Glarus
Description: On 24 November 2024, Unknown Threat Actors carried out a DDOS cyber attack on Backslash, a Swiss website provider. The attack resulted in 318 communal websites and the websites of the cantons of Schwyz and Glarus being inaccessible, including those of 68 municipalities in the canton of Aargau. The Federal Office for Cybersecurity BACS reported that there was no evidence of an infringement of the integrity or confidentiality of data of the authorities and municipalities concerned. The attack had no influence on the transmission of the voting results from the municipalities to the canton, following referenda held on that day.

On 19 November 2024, the threat actor named near2tlg claimed to have breached the confidentiality of at least one customer account on the digital patient record system Mediboard by usurping a privileged account. Mediboard is an open-source web application used by many healthcare institutions. The threat actor stole sensitive personal data of 758,912 French individuals, including names, dates of birth, postal and e-mail addresses, telephone numbers, medical prescriptions, physician information, death declarations, mutual card histories, and external identifiers. The hacker claimed the data leak on the BreachForums hack site and published an excerpt. Softway Medical Group, the developer of Mediboard, stated that the breach was not related to Mediboard itself but rather a result of compromised identifiers used by a person to access the system of one of Mediboard's customers. The Softway Medical Group did not host the health data concerned.

On Monday, 18 November 2024, the Lozère Chamber of Agriculture was targeted by unknown threat actors in a cyberattack that severely disrupted its functioning by limiting access to computer systems. The incident was publicly disclosed on 20 November 2024.

In November 2024, unknown threat actors breached the confidentiality of Direct Assurance, a subsidiary broker of the Axa group, by hacking into a supplier's computer system, resulting in data theft from approximately 6,000 customers and 10,000 prospects, including RIBs. Axa France confirmed the attack and notified the National Commission on Informatics and Freedoms, deploying measures to block further leaks and informing affected customers.

On 19 November 2024, unnamed South Korean drone research and development institutes were targeted by a ransomware attack. The attackers sent a private email with a malicious file attachment to South Korean drone research and development companies, universities and institutions. The email bypassed the defence systems of some small businesses, resulting in the infection of classified PCs and USB software. The National Intelligence Service (NIS) is investigating the attack and checking the servers of companies and research agencies to determine the extent of the damage.
Unknown hackers gained access to and encrypted the network of the German municipality Bergen auf Rügen, police reported.

Title (Company): Legal Counsel of the Federal Executive Branch CJEF
Description: On 15 November 2024, the RansomHub ransomware gang, claimed to have breached the Mexican government's official website, specifically targeting the Legal Counsel of the Federal Executive Branch CJEF, and exfiltrated 313GB of confidential information, including contracts, administrative information, financial data, emails, and personal details of federal officials, which was later posted as a sample on their website, with a ransom deadline of 25 November 2024. On 20 November 2024, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum confirmed that her government is investigating the alleged cyberattack and is awaiting a detailed report. The cybercriminals RansomHub removed the 206 gigabytes of confidential information belonging to the Mexican Presidency's legal counsel that had been published on the dark web on 28 November 2024. According to Manuel Rivera, director of the cybersecurity company Nekt Group, the attack was supported by local partners who could be employed or ex-employed by the Department itself.

EMBARGO ransomware group launched a ransomware attack on American Associated Pharmacies (AAP), a U.S. healthcare organization managing over 2,000 pharmacies across the U.S. The attackers allegedly stole 1.469 TB of AAP's data, scrambled AAP's files, and demanded a ransom payment. AAP reportedly paid the cybercriminals $1.3 million for decryption and now faces another $1.3 million demand to prevent its data exposure. The EMBARGO ransomware group uses endpoint detection and response (EDR) killing tools and a Rust-based ransomware kit. Check Point and the Register reported the attack. AAP posted a statement on its website about the incident, informing users that all passwords associated with APIRx.com and RxAAP.com had been reset, and limited ordering capabilities for API Warehouse had been restored at APIRx.com.

On 16 November 2024, Morocco Hebdo, a Moroccan web platform, was targeted by a Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) cyber attack, allegedly carried out by Algerian threat actors, in an attempt to silence the platform. The attack occurred after the publication of a cover file on the increasingly belligerent gestures of the Algerian regime against Morocco. Morocco Hebdo reported the incident in a press release on 18 November 2024, stating that their technical teams had established the attack's origin as coming from Algeria. The attackers aimed to bring down the website by overwhelming it with requests in a short period. Morocco Hebdo disclosed the attack and attributed it to Algerian threat actors.

On 17 November 2024, unknown threat actors carried out a flash loan attack on Polter Finance, a decentralized loan-and-receiving platform, resulting in a $12 million loss. The attack was linked to an accidental price error in the SpookySwap BOO market, which Polter Finance had just launched. The platform's operations were halted, and the price of POLTER dropped by 86% from $0.125 to $0.0171. Polter Finance's anonymous founder reported the attack to the Singapore police on the same day and confirmed his identity using a digital identity system called Singpass. The founder claimed that the attack resulted in the theft of $12 million worth of crypto assets. Polter Finance established a partnership with the Security Alliance Information Sharing and Analysis Centre (SEAL-ISAC) to track down the attacker and is working to recover the stolen funds.

Between 21 August 2024, and 23 August 2024, Unknown Threat Actors gained access to American Neighborhood Mortgage Acceptance Company LLC's (AnnieMac) network, potentially viewing and/or copying files containing sensitive personal information, including names and Social Security numbers, of 171,074 customers.

Unknown threat actors breached the confidentiality of the Library of Congress's IT systems, gaining access to email communications between congressional offices and some library staff, including the Congressional Research Service, from January to September 2024. The Library of Congress informed lawmakers and notified law enforcement about the security breach, and an investigation is ongoing. The library has mitigated the vulnerability used by the adversary and taken measures to prevent such incidents in the future.

An undisclosed hacker exploited a vulnerability in the Thala DeFi platform on 15 November 2024 and withdrew tokens with a total value of 25.5 million dollars. Thala, a decentralized finance protocol on the Aptos blockchain, was quickly able to identify the attacker, negotiate a bounty and recover the assets that had been frozen in the meantime.  The protocol's codebase is currently undergoing a comprehensive review and re-audit of all affected and related packages, and Thala said in a statement that it will return all stolen funds to user accounts once it has re-audited its codebase.

A cyber attack was carried out by the Indonesian Cyber Attack (Indohaxsec) group, which supports Russia, targeting the German Federal Statistical Office (Destatis). The attackers presumably breached the system used for data exchange between Destatis and German companies, stealing sensitive data, including names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, and login credentials of companies that exchange statistical data with Destatis. The stolen data was offered for sale on the darknet for $250. The attackers claimed responsibility for the attack and published a preview of the stolen data, including contact information and several companies' login credentials. The attack is believed to have occurred despite the system being updated just a few months prior. The affected companies were not informed about the data breach at the time of publication. Indohaxsec had previously announced on Telegram that they would target Germany and had collaborated with the pro-Russian hacker group NoName05716.

On September 5-8, 2024, unknown threat actors launched a ransomware attack on Great Plains Regional Medical Center in Oklahoma, compromising personal data of 133,000 individuals, including sensitive information such as name, demographic information, health insurance information, clinical treatment information, drivers license number, and/or Social Security number. The attackers accessed and encrypted files on the systems and copied some of them. The incident was reported to the US Department of Health and Human Services by the Oklahoma Medical Center. The organization quickly restored its systems and returned to normal operations, but a limited amount of patient information was not recoverable. No ransomware groups claimed responsibility for the security breach. The incident was publicly disclosed by the organization through a notice of security incident on their website and reported to the US Department of Health and Human Services on 19 November 2024.

On 21 February 2025, the Dubai-based cryptocurrency exchange Bybit became the victim of smart contract attack, resulting in the theft of crypto assets worth $1.46 billion, the largest amount obtained in a single compromise to date. The threat actors tapped Bybit's ETH cold wallet by manipulating a transaction through a sophisticated attack that masked the signing interface and altered the underlying smart contract logic. The attacker gained control of the affected ETH cold wallet and transferred its holdings. Crypto fraud investigator ZachXBT reported that the exploiter split 10,000 ETH out of the roughly 401,346 ETH stolen to 48 addresses. The analyst was also among the first to link the compromise to the North Korean state-sponsored group Lazarus. Bybit CEO Ben Zhou confirmed the incident, stating that the exchange had enough liquidity to honor withdrawals and continue operations, with all other cold wallets being secure and client funds safe. Zhou speculated that the source of the compromise could have been the wallet provider Safe, which Bybit uses for its Ethereum cold wallet. Safe wrote that they had not found evidence that the official Safe frontend was compromised, but temporarily paused certain functionalities out of caution. Bybit had reserve assets of over $16 billion before the hack and secured bridge loans to cover 80% of the stolen ETH. Ethereum temporarily lost 4% of its value when news of the incidents became public. On 26 February 2025 the FBI also attributed the ByBit hack to TraderTraitor (Lazarus).

On 13 November 2024, the Department of Reunion's computer systems were targeted by a cyberattack claimed by the group Termite, resulting in a limited data leak. The attack was stopped due to the rapid intervention of the computer teams, and a crisis cell was mobilized to assess the consequences and restore computer networks. A complaint was filed with the authorities, and a notification was sent to the National Commission on Informatics and Freedoms (CNIL). The Department's President, Cyrille Melchior, publicly disclosed the attack and informed the public about the progress of the actions put in place.

On or around 23 May 2024, Chinese state-sponsored hacking group TAG-112 compromised two websites linked to the Tibetan community, Tibet Post and Gyudmed Tantric University, by inducing visitors to download a malicious executable file disguised as a security certificate, which loads Cobalt Strike Beacon malware to the user's computer.  The attack, reported by Insikt Group on 12 November 2024, was likely aimed at gathering information and surveillance rather than destructive attacks. Insikt Group informed the university and the news website of the hack, and Gyudmed Tantric University has remedied the problem starting this week, while the news website remained compromised. Recorded Future attributed TAG-112 as a subgroup of the well-known Chinese state-sponsored proxy TAG-102, also known as Evasive Panda.

On or around 1 November 2024, unknown threat actors breached the confidentiality and integrity of the City of Sheboygan's network through an external, unauthorized access. The attackers left a ransom message. The City of Sheboygan secured the network and started a forensic review. Local cybersecurity expert Brian Collins, co-founder of PanaTech, commented on the attack, stating that the city likely lacked active monitoring of network activity and that it is harder to identify when someone has breached firewalls nowadays. The city stated that it had not discovered evidence that any sensitive personal information has been compromised by this incident. Public safety services were responding to all emergent and nonemergent requests for service with limited interruptions, and city employees with internet access could communicate with each other online as all cloud-based services were up and working. The incident was reported by TMJ4 News on 11 November 2024.

On an unspecified date in October 2024, an international hacker group, identified as INC Ransomware group, launched a ransomware attack on the Hungarian Army's procurement agency, VB. The attackers demanded a ransom of $5 million (€4.7 million) from the Hungarian state in exchange for not publishing the stolen data. Screenshots of military secrets, including details of the Hungarian Army's defense capabilities and military equipment procurement, were leaked on the Darknet on 6 November 2024. The attack was first publicly disclosed by Ferenc Fresz, an IT security expert, on his Facebook page. The Hungarian Ministry of Defense confirmed the attack, stating that an international hacker group had targeted the VB's IT systems. The incident was reported by online portals Hang.hu and HVG.hu on 14 November 2024.

Title (Company): HYP Credit Guard - Maccabi Health Aid Fund - Rav Kav Kav Online
Description: On 10 November 2024, unknown threat actors carried out a cyber attack on HYP, a company providing payment solutions in Israel. The attack affected multiple organizations, including the Maccabi Health Aid Fund and the Rav Kav Kav Online public transport system, causing disruptions to credit card payments. Channel 12 TV broadcaster and Sevenot Ahronot reported the incident. HYP confirmed the attack and stated that their systems returned to normal after the incident was mitigated.

Title (Company): Soreq Nuclear Research Center - Not available
Description: On 5 November 2024, Handala, believed to be affiliated with Iranian intelligence, claimed to have breached the accounts of several senior Israeli officials, including a nuclear scientist who worked at the Soreq Nuclear Research Center and was involved in the SARAF particle accelerator project, and a former major general who previously headed the military's cyber operations before serving as Defense Ministry director-general, and leaked their details, photos, and documents, including screenshots from the SARAF particle accelerator project, some of which date back to 2014-2015, with the hackers threatening to release their full cache of documents in the future. The leak also included personal materials belonging to a current Israeli ambassador and a former military attach in the United States, as well as information about family members of senior Israeli officials. The Israeli daily Haaretz reported on this on 11 November 2024 and assumed, at least in the case of the Israeli nuclear scientist, that the relevant data was stolen from his phone or email rather than from the Soreq Nuclear Research Center.

Unknown Threat Actors launched a ransomware attack on the Houston Housing Authority (HHA) on 21 September 2024, encrypting the agency's virtual servers. Although the HHA's firewall initially appeared to have thwarted data theft, the hackers later claimed to have obtained sensitive data from the agency. The HHA's IT director, Roy Spivey, and board chair, Jody Proler, assessed the agency's security vulnerabilities and formed an action plan, which included a $311,000 expenditure to bolster network security, adding two-factor authentication on all desktop servers, enhanced firewalls, more robust file recovery, and continuous monitoring across the agency's systems. The HHA plans to notify residents, staff, and vendors about the breach as it proceeds with its heightened cybersecurity efforts.

Title (Company): Joint Chiefs of Staff (South Korea) - People's Power Party (South Korea) - National Information Resource Service (South Korea) - Ministry of Interior and Safety (South Korea) - Korea Electric Power Corp. (KEPCO) - Ministry of Environment (South Korea) - Ministry of Defence (South Korea) - National Association for Court Management (South Korea) - Korea Road Traffic Authority (KoRoad)
Description: Pro-Russian hacker group disrupted the websites of a variety of South Korean public organizations beginning on November 5, the hacker group itself claimed. Under the campaign name "Operation South Korea," the hacker group evidently disrupted the websites of the South Korean Ministry of National Defense, the Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS), the Ministry of Environment, the National Information Resource Service (NIRS), the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Safety, Korea Road Traffic Authority (KoRoad), Korea Electric Power Corp. (KEPCO) and the People's Power Party (PPP), the Ministry of Science and Information and Communication Technology (ICT) confirmed on Nov. 6, 2024. The National Association for Court Management (NACM) website was the target of DDoS attacks on November 7, 2024.

Title (Company): Not available - MIT Technology Review Magazine
Description: The hacker known as Intel Broker breached MIT Technology Review Magazine via a third-party contractor, leaking nearly 300,000 user records on Breach Forums on 4 November 2024. The data includes full names, email addresses, and activity details, posing risks for phishing and targeted scams. Intel Broker, notorious for recent attacks on high-profile organizations, alleges that the data includes Personally Identifiable Information. Hackread.com analyzed the leaked data and can confirm it includes personal details, which, while not as sensitive as financial data, could be leveraged in phishing attempts or targeted scams. The leak does not appear to contain highly sensitive information like social security numbers or financial data, but the compromised data is still a privacy risk, as it could be exploited for phishing scams or identity verification attacks. MIT Technology Review, an esteemed publication from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is known for its analysis of emerging technologies and their impact on society. This data breach potentially exposes readers and contributors who engaged with the platform, a situation that may lead to reputational challenges for the publication, as well as privacy concerns for its user base. Hackread.com disclosed the attack on 4 November 2024.

Chinese state-sponsored hacking group Volt Typhoon compromised Singaporean telecom provider Singapore Telecommunications (SingTel) in June 2024. Bloomberg reported this on November 5, 2024, based on two unnamed people involved in the matter. One of these people also attributed the cyber incident to the Chinese state-sponsored hacking group Volt Typhoon. According to the statements, the Singaporean telecommunications provider Singapore Telecommunications (SingTel) discovered suspicious data traffic in a specific end router and, therefore, malware in the network.  The sources assumed that the cyber incident against SingTel could be considered an initial attempt at other cyber incidents, probably in the United States, or as a starting point for future cyber incidents, also probably against targets in the United States. In June 2024, a cyber incident occurred, with the Chinese state-sponsored hacking group Salt Typhoon attacking many US telecommunications providers.

The Hellcat ransomware gang compromised Schneider Electric, a multinational energy management company. A likely member of the ransomware group, who goes by the name 'Grep' or 'greppy', disclosed on X on 3 November 2024 gaining unauthorized access to one of Schneider Electric's internal project execution tracking platforms hosted within an isolated environment by using openly accessible login credentials and a MiniOrange REST-API. The attackers claimed to have over 40 gigabytes of data from the company's JIRA platform, including projects, issues, and plugins, along with over 400,000 rows of user data, totalling 75,000 unique email addresses and the names of Schneider Electric employees and customers. The attackers demanded a $125,000 ransom in Monero. Schneider Electric reported the incident, which marks the third time in the past 18 months that ransomware groups attacked the company, following incidents in January 2024 and June 2023. Schneider Electric disclosed the incident on 5 November 2024.

Embargo Ransomware Gang launched a ransomware attack on Memorial Hospital and Manor, an 80-bed hospital in Bainbridge, Georgia, on 2 November 2024, disrupting the hospital's Electronic Health Records (EHR) system, which was discovered early Saturday morning when employees saw notifications of potential risks found by the virus protection software, and the hospital has since reverted to paper-based processes while evaluating options to restore and recover its EHR, as disclosed by the hospital in a statement on Facebook on 3 November 2024. The Embargo ransomware gang claimed responsibility for this ransomware attack on November 5, 2024 and also claimed to have stolen 1.15 TB of data.

On 3 November 2024, the day of the second round of the presidential elections in the Republic of Moldova, the servers of the Central Electoral Commission (CEC) were targeted by a cyber attack, according to the statement made on Sunday by Angelica Caraman, the CEC president, in a press conference. These attacks affected the speed of the voting registration application at polling stations, thus hampering the verification and registration process. It was observed a slowing down of the functionality of the program that registers voters at the ballot box resulting most likely from a DDos attack.

Between 2020 and 2024, Chinese state-sponsored threat actors compromised at least 20 Canadian government networks, stealing valuable data to advance Chinese Communist Party (CCP) strategic, economic and diplomatic interests, and provide them an advantage in China-Canada bilateral relations and commercial matters. The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre) confirmed the compromises in its National Cyber Threat Assessment 2025-2026, published on 31 October 2024. The Cyber Centre noted that the threat actors targeted information to support the People’s Republic of China’s (PRC) malign influence and interference activities against Canada’s democratic processes and institutions. All known federal government compromises have been resolved, the Cyber Centre confirmed. The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre) disclosed the attack in its National Cyber Threat Assessment 2025-2026, published on 31 October 2024.

M2, a cryptocurrency exchange based in the United Arab Emirates, was the victim of a large-scale cyber crypto theft in the early morning of 31 October 2024 in which an unknown hacker gained access to multiple crypto wallets.  According to blockchain analysts and M2 itself, the hack was detected within 16 minutes and remedied, with all lost funds being repaid to the impacted wallets.

The Russia-linked hacker group NoName057(16) launched a DDoS attack on several UK local authorities, claiming on X to have hacked Portsmouth City Council; Bournemouth, Christchurch & Poole (BCP) Council; Medway Council; Exeter City Council; Burnley Town Council; and Middlesborough Council in early November 2024.  While not all attacks were confirmed by the relevant authorities, the Portsmouth City Council and BCP Council confirmed that their websites were disrupted by the attack, with other councils also experiencing temporary outages as they worked to take systems offline. The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) provided guidance to the affected councils, and no user or resident data were reported to be at risk.

The German pharmaceutical wholesaler AEP, based in Alzenau, Lower Franconia, was the victim of a disruptive cyberattack on 28 October 2024. According to AEP, unknown hackers encrypted some of its systems, resulting in the company only being reachable through telephone and email. As a result of the attack, pharmacies' services were limited; in the meantime, AEP declared that they had taken "necessary and far-reaching measures" and were consulting external IT experts for assistance.

According to a 30 October 2024 report by Unit42, North Korean state-sponsored hacking group Andariel (aka Jumpy Pisces, Onyx Sleet, fka PLUTONIUM/Silent Chollima/G0138/DarkSeoul) infiltrated an unnamed target in May 2024, leading to persistent access and data theft by the group from May to September 2024. Following the theft of data, Unit42 indicates a potential collaboration with the Play ransomware group, since Play ransomware was deployed against the target at the end of September 2024.  In late May 2024, Andariel compromised the unnamed organisation's network via a compromised user account, and then extracted registry dumps and deployed Mimikatz for credential harvesting. The threat actors solidified their presence on the network over the next few months, establishing command-and-control, stealing data, creating malicious services, establishing Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) sessions, and uninstalling endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools. In early September 2024, an unknown actor gained access to the same compromised user account and carried out "pre-ransomware activities" (credential harvesting, privilege escalation, etc.) according to Unit42. By the end of the month, Play ransomware was deployed onto the victim's servers.   Unit42 links Andariel to Play with medium confidence due to the fact that Andariel had access to the account up until the day before the deployment of Play ransomware. However, Unit42 also states that Andariel could have simply sold access to the compromised user account to Play, rather than coordinate with the group directly.

An unidentified threat actor, using the alias 'kzoldyck', breached the systems of Peruvian financial services provider Interbank, formally the Banco Internacional del Perú Service Holding S.A.A., and leaked 3.7 TB of stolen information online, including personal info, credit card details, CVVs, passwords, and API credentials, related to 3 million customers, after a two-week ransom negotiation failed, with Interbank confirming the data breach and disclosing the incident on October 31, 2024, and assuring customers that their funds were not impacted by the security incident, while the company resumed its mobile and online platforms after recent outages. The Public Prosecutor's Office in Peru initiated preliminary proceedings for the hacking of Interbank, and the Office of the Prosecutor in Cybercrime will investigate the alleged leak of data that affected several of the clients of that bank.

Unknown threat actors compromised sensitive information from the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) during the 2024 tax season, affecting tens of thousands of Canadians. Exploiting client identifiers linked to H&R Block Canada, the attackers accessed CRA tax accounts, modified bank details, filed hundreds of false statements, and diverted $6 million before detection. The CRA’s investigation revealed suspicious repayment patterns, including refunds to shared bank accounts and centralized mailing addresses. Internal investigations by CRA and H&R Block found no breaches in their systems, attributing the increase in attacks to emergency COVID-19 benefits introduced in 2020. With over 31,000 privacy violations and $190 million in suspected fraudulent payments, the CRA has since bolstered security measures, offering credit protection solutions to victims. The incident was publicly disclosed through a joint Radio-Canada and CBC investigation on 31 October 2024.

According to CertiK, an unknown hacker gained access to private keys within the network of SUNRAY, a cryptocurrency platform, at the end of October 2024. Access to the private keys enabled the hacker to steal almost $3 million USD from SUNRAY, which were then transferred to other crypto accounts. According to SUNRAY, an investigation was initiated in order to solve the problem of compromised data within the theft.

Title (Company): Landmark Admin - Liberty Bankers Insurance Group
Description: On 23 October 2024, Landmark Admin, LLC (“Landmark Admin”) filed a notice of data breach with the Attorney General of Maine after discovering that hackers were able to encrypt and remove data from Landmark Admin’s system. One of the affected customers is the Liberty Bankers Insurance Group, which data is included in the breach. In this notice, Landmark Admin explains that the incident resulted in an unauthorized party being able to access consumers’ sensitive information, which includes their names; addresses; Social Security numbers; drivers’ license numbers; state identification card numbers; passport numbers; bank account and routing numbers; medical information; health insurance policy numbers; dates of birth; and life and annuity policy information. Upon completing its investigation, Landmark Admin began sending out data breach notification letters to all 806,519 individuals whose information was affected by the recent data security incident. On 13 May 2024, Landmark Admin detected suspicious activity within its IT network. The following day, Landmark Admin determined that an unauthorized party had attempted to access its network and was able to regain access to its IT network on 17 June 2024, including certain files containing confidential consumer information. Thus, the unauthorized activity on Landmark Admin’s systems occurred between 13 May 2024 and 17 June 2024.

Title (Company): Gymnasium Marktbreit -  Staatliche Berufsschule Kitzingen-Ochsenfurt -  Armin-Knab-Gymnasium - Realschule Kitzingen - Erich-Kästner-Schule - Staatliche Realschule Dettelbach - Fachoberschule / Berufsoberschule Kitzingen
Description: Unknown threat actors attacked seven secondary schools in the district of Kitzingen on Wednesday, 23 October 2024, by breaching the IT systems of the state schools in Kitzingen and Dettelbach, the Armin-Knab-Gymnasium in Kitzingen, the Gymnasium Marktbreit, as well as the vocational school, the FOS/BOS and the Erich-Kästner-Schule in Kitzingen, causing partial encryption of the IT systems by ransomware, with no signs of data exfiltration initially, but a possible breach of data protection reported by the schools, with the Landratsamt Kitzingen disclosing the incident on 25 October 2024, and cooperating closely with the criminal police of Würzburg, the Commissioner for Cybercrime and the Bavarian State Office for Information Security to deal with the incident, and the Bavarian State Ministry of Education and Culture having established a security framework for IT security in schools. The attack was also reported by the media on 6 November 2024, with the Landratsamt Kitzingen confirming that the attackers had stolen data from one of the schools, and that the data was personal data, with the victims to be informed as soon as the analyses of the data have been completed, and no publication of the data could be established as before.

Title (Company): Italian Revenue Agency - Sistema di Indagine (SDI) - Bank of Italy
Description: The Italian private investigation company Equalize gained access to the databases of the Italian law enforcement agencies, the Italian Revenue Agency, and the Bank of Italy and stole data beginning in 2019, reported the Milanese public prosecutor, Francesco de Tommasi, in the course of the investigation's disclosure on 25 October 2024. The Milan, Bari and Perugia public prosecutor's offices were involved in the investigation. They brought charges against around 60 people for membership in a criminal organisation to abuse access to a computer system, corruption, disclosure of official secrets, abusive wiretapping and aiding and abetting. The focus is on the private investigation company Equalize and its circle, which is said to have consisted of hackers, computer consultants, private intelligence agencies and police officers. The managing director of Equalize and former police officer Carmine Gallo; the chairman of the Fondazione Fiera Milano, Enrico Pazzali; Gallo's business partner, Nunzio Samuele Calamucci; and the owners or members of associated companies, Massimiliano Camponoro and Giulio Cornelli, were placed under house arrest. Carmine Gallo was wiretapped for having contacts with the mafia and for having 800,000 entries of the database of the Italian law enforcement agencies, SDI.  The stolen data was primarily intended to be used to harm competitors or political opponents of Pazzali or people associated with him. Furthermore, the stolen data was sold to clients with the same interest, including large companies and professional and law firms.

According to the Indian software company Seqrite, an unspecified threat actor targets various sectors in espionage campaign "Operation Cobalt Whisper" since May 2024. The new campaign targets the defence and research sectors in South Asia, particularly Pakistan and Hong Kong, but with growing interest in India. The focus is on engineering researchers and professors, using sophisticated lures like decoy documents related to electrotechnical societies and energy infrastructure. The campaign employs the post-exploitation tool Cobalt Strike, indicating a methodical approach to cyber-espionage. Seqrite further lists the following victims:  Defense Industry, Electrotechnical Engineering, Energy (Hydropower, Renewable Energy), Civil Aviation, Environmental Engineering, Academia and Research Institutions, Medical Science Institutions, Cybersecurity Researchers.

Slovenian media sites reported that the University of Maribor was hit by ransomware on 23 October 2024 after 8 pm, according to a statement the university published on its own website. It stated that the cyberattack happened in the evening and was reported to SI-CERT. Due to the disruptive nature of the attack, the computer services of the university were partially or completely inaccessible at the time of reporting.  According to unnamed sources by DELOS, all data, also the University back-ups, are said to have been encrypted by the attackers, complicating the recovery process.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: In a Joint Cybersecurity Advisory released on 19 February 2025, the FBI, CISA, and the Multi-State Information Sharing and Analysis Center (MS-ISAC) warned of a continuous ransomware campaign by the China-based Ghost actors. Tracing back to 2021, the campaign has targeted organizations in over 70 countries through vulnerabilities in Internet-facing services (such as CVE-2018-13379, CVE-2010-2861, CVE-2009-3960, CVE-2021-34473, CVE-2021-34523, CVE-2021-31207). Victims include critical infrastructure, schools, universities, healthcare, government networks, religious institutions, technology, and manufacturing companies, as well as small and medium-sized businesses. Based on the frequent rotation of ransomware payloads, the actors have tracked under a range of names, including Cring, Crypt3r, Phantom, Strike, Hello, Wickrme, HsHarada, and Rapture. The Advisory concludes that Ghost actors do not typically exfiltrate large amounts of data of sensitive quality, such as intellectual property or personally identifiable information.

Unknown threat actors, believed to be affiliated with the Chinese government, compromised the email account of a World Uyghur Congress (WUC) staff member on 21 October 2024, and sent a notification to all registered attendees of the WUC general assembly in Sarajevo, falsely claiming that the event was postponed. The WUC released copies of the forged emails on its social media accounts to notify attendees that the information was incorrect. The incident occurred ahead of the 24-27 October general assembly of the WUC, an international organization of the ethnic group's diaspora from more than 25 countries in Central Asia, the Middle East, Europe, and North America. While the Chinese Embassy in Sarajevo firmly denies any allegations regarding their involvement in the incident.

Criminal actors compromised the systems of US-based OnePoint Patient Care, a pharmacy specializing in hospice and palliative care, exposing the personal data of 795,916 individuals between 6 and 8 August 2024. The breach affected names, addresses, medical records, diagnoses, prescriptions, and, for some, Social Security numbers. OnePoint detected suspicious network activity on 8 August, initiating an investigation and containment measures with forensic experts. The incident, while not affecting operations, was later linked to the Inc Ransom ransomware group, which leaked stolen data after the company declined to pay the ransom. Impacted individuals have been advised to monitor credit and financial activity for suspicious transactions. OnePoint notified their customers on 21 October 2024.

In October 2024, Stormous ransomware group compromised the Transak company, which provides an 'onamp' service for many famous blockchain companies, by exploiting a data leak caused by employees using laptops for non-work purposes, affecting some 93,000 unique users, including passports, ID cards, and personal photos, and is now trying to negotiate with the company, demanding $30,000 to remove the stolen data, which includes classified private documents, government identifications, addresses, financial statements, and personal photos of users, with the company classifying the damage as 'low or moderate' due to the lack of sensitive information such as social security numbers and credit card details, and the CEO, Sami Stairt, stating that the company is not interested in negotiating with the ransomware group.

Various sources reported that Hackers have used the vulnerability (CVE-2024-47575) to compromise FortiManager devices since at least 23 September 2024. A possible vulnerability in FortiManager first became public in a Reddit conversation on 19 October 2024, after Fortinet may have privately notified these individuals. On 23 October, cybersecurity researcher Kevin Beaumont published a post on the Medium website naming a vulnerability in the FortiManager protocol. In the same post, Beaumont criticized Fortinet's reluctance to disclose the vulnerability and attributed the exploitation to nation-state actors. The following day, 24 October 2024, Fortinet published the vulnerability notification for the first time. On the same day, Mandiant also published its technical report and wrote that over 50 devices had been compromised since at least 27 June 2024. The vulnerability allowed a compromised FortiManager device to issue arbitrary commands. Mandiant attributed this incident to the group UNC5820, which exfiltrated the configuration data of the FortiGate devices managed by the compromised FortiManager.
