According to Delta Prime, the attack took place around 6:00am and involved the Arbitrum chain; according to Delta Prime, the attacker took control of a private key for its admin wallet, allowing the hacker to redirect legitimate transactions to a malicious account, which enabled them to steal almost $6 million.

Cybersecurity giant Fortinet has confirmed it suffered a data breach after a threat actor with the moniker ‘Fortibitch’ claimed to steal 440GB of files from the company's Microsoft Sharepoint server. Fortinet is one of the largest cybersecurity companies in the world, selling secure networking products like firewalls, routers, and VPN devices. The threat actor claims to have tried to extort Fortinet into paying a ransom, likely to prevent the publishing of data, but the company refused to pay. Fortinet confirmed that customer data was stolen from a "third-party cloud-based shared file drive." Fortinet wrote in a statement on their website that there is no indication that "this incident has resulted in malicious activity affecting any customers and did not involve any data encryption, deployment of ransomware, or access to Fortinet’s corporate network." Furthermore, Fortinet’s operations, products, and services have not been impacted, and no evidence of additional access to any other Fortinet resource is found.

Title (Company): Taiwan Stock Exchange - Unspecified central government agencies - Unspecified local tax authorities - Maritime and Port Bureau - Unspecified private banks - Unspecified military units - Unspecified financial and securities organizations
Description: During 11-15 September 2024, the pro-Russian hacker group ‘NoName057(16)’ carried out a series of DDoS attacks on 45 Taiwanese entities. The most prominent of these was carried out against the Taiwan Stock Exchange (TWSE), which left its website briefly unavailable after trading hours. The disruptions, which also targeted other government and financial websites, came in response to recent remarks by Taiwanese President William Lai. Lai had suggested that China should reclaim land from Russia's Far East, which the hacktivist group cited as a reason for its campaign. NoName057(16) reported support for its activities from the hacker collective RipperSec, that previously engaged in pro-Palestinian operations. While the TWSE website experienced delays, the exchange clarified that the incident did not affect trading systems. The hackers aimed to disrupt the websites of a range of Taiwanese organizations, with similar DDoS attempts reported for airports and local tax bureaus. Taiwan's Minister of Digital Affairs Yennun Huang linked NoName057(16) and RipperSec to the campaign in a press briefing on 14 September.

On 8 September 2024, unknown hackers breached the IT systems of the French city of Isbergues, disrupting multiple municipal services. The city suspects that personal data may have been stolen during the attack, and the French data protection authority (CNIL) has been notified. Authorities are investigating the breach with support from the Hauts-de-France Cyber Incident Response Center (CSIRT) and the national gendarmerie.

Hackers which are likely from DPRK stole approximately USD 20 million in cryptocurrencies from hot wallets of Indoensian cryptocurrency trading platform Indodax since at least 10 September 2024, Indodax first reported in the early morning of 11 September 2024. Some observers of the cryptocurrency scene on X also reported on the same day that the hackers began converting the stolen cryptocurrencies into established cryptocurrencies. The observers also put forward various theories as to how this cyber incident could have come about, including the compromise of the withdrawal system or the signature machine. According to the co-founder of Indodax the attackers exploited a vulnerability to gain access. The long disruption of the Indodax platform is due to maintenance measures, ensuring that no more exploits exist in their systems.  Additionally, the CEO stated in a written statement that an analysis conducted by a crypto security agency indicated that the attack was (perpetrated) by an actor affiliated to the DPRK (Democratic People's Republic of Korea).

Unknown hackers are demanding ransom from Colombian energy provider Air-e since 2 September 2024.  The attackers were able to bypass several of Air-e's security measures, which shows how sophisticated the attack was.  Despite significant efforts by Air-e to restore the systems, their service is still impacted. Customers are still not able to pay their service fees online.  Air-e informed the Attorney General's office about the attack, which is now leading the investigations.

An Iranian-nexus hacking group attacks Iraqi entities over several months in 2024. According to Check Point Research, this campaign targets different Iraqi entities, including government networks. This campaign features a custom toolset and infrastructure for specific targets and uses a combination of techniques commonly associated with Iranian threat actors operating in the region. This toolset employs command and control (C2) mechanisms, including a custom DNS tunnelling protocol and a tailor-made email based C2 channel. The C2 channel uses compromised email accounts within the targeted organization, indicating that the threat actor successfully infiltrated the victim’s networks. The Veaty and Spearal Tactics, Techniques and Procedures (TTPs) are very similar to two other malware families, Karkoff and Saitama, which are attributed to the same APT34 actor, indicating that this campaign is implemented by a similar nexus threat actor.
Techniques Used: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol, Exfiltration Over C2 Channel, Phishing

Description: The hacker group RansomHub claims to have breached the systems of the University of Genoa in Italy and stolen 18 GB worth of data on 9 September 2024.  The stolen data originated from the department of mathematics. To prevent the data from being leaked, the university has to pay the ransom until 23 September 2024. The amount of the ransom was not specified.  The police started their investigation on 10 September 2024.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Free Russia
Description: Between April and June 2024, the Kremlin-linked cyberespionage group COLDRIVER aka Star Blizzard conducted a spear-phishing campaign targeting civil society members, NGOs, and the US-based Free Russia Foundation, a pro-democracy think tank. The group focused on organizations operating in Eastern Europe, sending phishing emails containing malicious PDF links designed to compromise victims' systems. COLDRIVER impersonated trusted contacts to lure targets into downloading the malicious PDFs. Once accessed, victims' devices were scanned, and data was transmitted to command-and-control servers hosted on virtual private servers from Hostinger International Limited. The group used Proton Mail accounts to maintain anonymity throughout the operation. In addition to NGOs and media outlets in Russia and Belarus, the campaign notably targeted the Free Russia Foundation in the beginning of September 2024, leading to the theft of over 2,500 email chains and 13GB of sensitive documents. These included grant reports, internal correspondence, and personal information, which were subsequently leaked on a Telegram channel. The leak is believed to be linked to COLDRIVER’s continued efforts to destabilize pro-democracy entities.

All the personal data, from ID numbers to home addresses, of 108 million Turkish citizens registered with official institutions appears in a data breach, detected by Free Web Turkey in 2023, which sued the Ministry of the Interior for neglecting its data protection obligations. The stolen data, which included 82 million home addresses and 134 million GSM numbers, was uploaded to Google Drive. When the National Cyber Incident Response Center (NCCRC) realised the data had been stolen, it contacted Google and asked for help in removing the data.

US-based Highline Public Schools in Washington recently suffered a significant cyberattack, forcing the temporary closure of multiple schools in on 9 September 2024. The district confirmed that unknown threat actors gained unauthorized access to their network, disrupting critical systems and impacting school operations.

According to Kaspersky, a new APT called "Librarian Ghoul" targets Russian companies and research institutes from the defense sector with espionage in 2024. Among the targeted entities are research institutes of various types; companies in the aerospace and aviation industries; manufacturers of equipment for the gas processing, petrochemical, nuclear power and defence industries; manufacturers of diving equipment, communication and radar systems, control and cash register equipment, automotive components, automated process control systems, telecommunication equipment; secure communications equipment; semiconductor devices and power modules (translated from Russian). Librarian Ghouls sends malicious RAR archives containing .SCR files with names that mimic Office documents. When the victim runs the file, the malware downloads additional payloads to the computer, collects data of interest from the archives and sends it to the attackers. Kaspersky already reported on the group's activities in July 2024, but still does not attribute it to a certain state or region.

According to a 13 May 2025 report by Trend Micro, since April 2024, the Chinese-speaking threat group Earth Ammit has been targeting Taiwanese military and satellite industries, plus Taiwanese drone supply chains, in a campaign dubbed "TIDRONE." This campaign, according to Trend Micro, has been observed using malware toolsets CXCLNT and CLNTEND. Before that, Earth Ammit's activities also focused on unspecified entities in Korea and Canada in the "VENOM" campaign, but also payment services in Taiwan. Trend Micro's research indicates the attackers have certain interest in military-related industry chains, particularly in the manufacturers of drones, coming from Taiwan. The observed TTPs show a substantiate evolution of the group's malware arsenal and that they optimized their attack chain. According to the report, the group likely moved to the lateral movement stage at the time of reporting, while having used other techniques some time ago for initial infiltration. Furthermore, the group uses two backdoors throughout its operations, namely CXCLNT and CLNTEND. Trend Micro states that the Earth Ammit's tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) can reasonably link it back to other China-linked APT groups; according to their report, the company states that the TTPs and threat profile bear resemblance to the Chinese APT Dalbit, while the timezone the group is active in corresponds with the GMT+8, used in China, Taiwan, and other east Asian countries. Given the sensitivity of data hold by the targeted drone manufacturers, espionage seems as the most reasonable operation motive.

Unknown threat actors attacked Charles Darwin School in Biggin Hill, Westerham (United Kingdom) in September 2024. Since they were experiencing IT issues, they found out that the school has become a victim of ransomware. Due to the attack, the school must remain closed on 9 September till 11 September. Within that time, the staff devices can be removed and cleansed. The school is currently available by phone only.

Payment gateway provider SLIM CD, based in Coral Springs, Florida, suffered a major data breach between August 2023 and June 2024, potentially compromising the sensitive personal and financial information of over 1.7 million customers. The breach exposed names, addresses, and credit card details, including card numbers and expiration dates. SLIM CD confirmed unauthorized access to their network but has not disclosed the specific method of the attack. Experts suspect phishing, malware, or social engineering tactics may have been involved.

Transport for London's (TfL) computer systems have been targeted in an ongoing cyber attack in September 2024. Until now, there is no evidence customer data had been compromised and there was currently no impact on TfL services. However, the Dial-a-Ride assisted transit service for disabled people was temporarily suspended. One source close to the matter told the Register: "The TfL hack was their Cisco VPN getting popped." The Register put the suggestion to TfL that attackers may have gained access through a Cisco or Netscaler appliance. The alarm was raised when TfL spotted some suspicious activity during routine monitoring. Access was subsequently limited, and a 17-year-old was arrested in connection with the hack on 5 September. On 20 September, TfL began sending letters to around 5,000 customers whose data "may have been accessed". On 18 August 2025, Two teenagers charged over Transport for London cyberattack. The hack caused a damage of  £39m.

Tewkesbury Borough Council confirmed on 5 September 2024 that it has been the victim of a cyberattack. Suspicious activity was noticed on the council's systems in the afternoon a day before. After internal investigations, the decision was taken to shut the online systems down. The cause and source of the attack is not yet known. Investigations so far have shown there has been no loss of data from the systems. And partner organisations have confirmed their own systems are safe.

For several days in September 2024, unusual incidents have been observed on the community's internal computer network from French Val-de-Reuil. Investigations carried out by the City's services, supported in their research by the National Agency for Information Systems Security, have made it possible to determine the cause. They show that a cyberattack of unknown origin targeted the City Hall's servers. Until proven otherwise and in the current state of the analyses, no leak of personal or confidential data has been detected. For a period of 24 to 48 hours, the telephone and Internet lines of the City's services are therefore suspended.

In late August, Planned Parenthood suffered a cyberattack causing a disruption and sensitive data may be stolen. Planned Parenthood is a non-profit organization that provides sexual health care services. It is not yet known whether any personal information about patients might have been stolen, but that could potentially be devastating. The group behind the attack, Ransomhub, has claimed responsibility on their leak site. The listing on the leak site shows financial information, court papers, and insurance certificates.

Title (Company): Not available - Société française du radiotéléphone (SFR)
Description: French cybercriminal group, French Hackers Squad, stole personal information from around 50,000 people and companies via an unnamed partner of the French telecommunications company SFR on 7 June 2024, the hacker group claimed on 27 August 2024 on various platforms. It is unknown how the theft occurred; the stolen data included surnames and first names, telephone numbers, addresses and email addresses. The hacker group claimed to have logged into the relevant database.

The Sarawak (Malaysia) affiliate of Swinburne University of Technology, a public Australian research university, was the victim of a ransomware attack by RansomHub at the end of August 2024 which led to the compromise of personal information. While the university is an affiliate of the Australian university, it is administered by the Sarawak local government. The university was posted on RansomHub's leak site on 30 August, and RansomHub included a number of pieces of data to prove the attack: this included a letter of completion to a student, an advanced standing application, bank details, a blank form, and a scan of the passport of a Malaysian former student. The theft was confirmed on 2 September; the university claimed that other data of this nature was also stolen, including sensitive personal information. While RansomHub claimed that 366GB of data were stolen on its leak site, the university stated that the total scope of the theft was not yet clear.

Allegedly, three people disrupted the Ekomobil traffic application of the Izmit Metropolitan Municipality in the Turkish province of Kocaeli on 30 August 2024, various media reported on the same day. The three people, with the initials A.A., M.K.S. and A.D., were arrested the following day, on 31 August 2024. Bomb threats are said to have been displayed on the screens of the public transport vehicles themselves. In the applications themselves, the hackers allegedly referred to themselves as Jund-al-Aqsa and announced that they would target all ‘local Zionists’.

The websites of several French cities, municipalities, and companies were hit by DDoS attacks by the pro-Russian hacker group Noname057 between 2 and 3 September 2024, leading to several disruptions. According to the group's Telegram, the attacks were part of Noname's "DDoSia Project," in which "Russophobic countries" (i.e., countries supporting Ukraine in its war against Russia) were all to be targeted. The attacks led to the disruption of websites of city/municipal administrations and other organisations, among them: Reims (both the city and the Greater Reims administrative region); the University of Reims Champagne-Ardenne and the metropolitan region of Nantes. On 4 September 2024, the hacktivist group claimed to have disrupted the websites of the city of Angers and the Angers Loire Association of Municipalities, which both confirmed on the same day.

Octave, a French software publisher specializing in the retail sector, which hosts the data for the Amiens philately publisher's website, suffered a cyberattack on the night of August 15-16, 2024. As a result, all the group's data was encrypted, and the hackers demanded a ransom, causing the philately publisher's website to be taken offline. In total, eight independent publishing distributors are affected. Direct consequences include the inability to process orders placed before this date and to generate shipping notices and invoices. The company confirmed the hack and tries to recover the systems in the next weeks. The director estimates that the losses caused by the incident "amount to several tens of thousands of euros".

Unknown hackers targeted the website of the Brandenburg branch of the German AfD party on 27 August 2024, rendering it offline for several days due to a sustained DDoS attack. René Springer, chairman of the AfD Brandenburg state association, believes a sophisticated and well-funded threat actor is responsible for the attack.

Title (Company): Young Consulting - Blue Shield of California
Description: BlackSuit Ransomware Group gained access to Young Consulting Data between 10–13 April 2024.  Young Consulting, a software company that develops integrated software solutions for the underwriting, marketing and administering of medical stop-loss insurance, experienced technical difficulties within its computer environment on 13 April 2024. Further investigation determined that an unauthorized actor gained access to Young Consulting's network between 10 April and 13 April 2024 and downloaded copies of certain files. The information involved in the breach varied by individual but included names, dates of birth, Social Security numbers and insurance policy and claim information. Blue Shield, a provider of healthcare plans in California, was affected by this data breach and directed affected patients to view Young Consulting's breach notice for more information. The BlackSuit ransomware group claimed responsibility for the attack that resulted in the data breach.

On 1 September 2024, the German hospital operator Wertachkliniken, which manages the Bobingen and Schwabmünchen clinics, was targeted by unknown threat actors in a cyberattack that severely disrupted its IT systems. The attack led to the encryption of virtual servers, blocking access to critical data and forcing the hospitals to operate under limited, analogue conditions. The IT department, with the support of external experts, is actively working to resolve the issue. Authorities have been notified, and the police are investigating the incident. As a precaution, surgeries scheduled for Monday at the Bobingen clinic have been cancelled.

On 19 August 2024, the North Korean hacker group Citrine Sleet exploited the Chromium zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2024-7971) to conduct remote code execution (RCE) attacks on 19 August 2024. Targets were initially directed to the Citrine Sleet-controlled exploit domain voyagorclub[.]space. Upon connection, the zero-day RCE exploit for CVE-2024-7971 was deployed. Once code execution was achieved in the sandboxed Chromium renderer process, shellcode containing a Windows sandbox escape exploit and the FudModule rootkit was downloaded and executed in memory. The sandbox escape leveraged CVE-2024-38106, allowing the main FudModule rootkit to run in memory. This rootkit uses direct kernel object manipulation (DKOM) techniques to bypass kernel security mechanisms, operating entirely from user mode while performing kernel tampering via a kernel read/write primitive. CVE-2024-7971 is a type confusion vulnerability in the V8 JavaScript and WebAssembly engine, affecting versions of Chromium prior to 128.0.6613.84. Google released a patch for this vulnerability on 21 August 2024, and users are strongly advised to update to the latest version of Chromium. This marks the third exploited V8 type confusion vulnerability patched in V8 this year, following CVE-2024-4947 and CVE-2024-5274. In response to this nation-state actor activity, Microsoft has directly notified targeted or compromised customers, providing critical information to help secure their environments.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Between April and July 2024, the Iran-linked cyberespionage group APT33, also known as Peach Sandstorm and Refined Kitten, conducted a series of infiltrations targeting critical organizations in the government, defense, satellite, and oil and gas sectors in the United States and the United Arab Emirates. The group deployed a new multi-stage backdoor malware named Tickler as part of these operations. APT33 gained initial access to the targeted networks through password spray attacks, attempting to breach multiple accounts using a few commonly used passwords to evade detection. The attackers also used social engineering tactics, particularly focusing on the education sector to procure operational infrastructure, including setting up fraudulent Azure tenants using compromised accounts. The Tickler malware, disguised as legitimate PDF files, was used to establish a foothold in the compromised systems. The malware collected network information and communicated with command-and-control (C2) servers hosted on Microsoft Azure infrastructure, which Microsoft later identified and disrupted. In addition to maintaining persistence within the networks, the attackers utilized the SMB protocol for lateral movement, allowing them to move across the compromised systems. Microsoft has since shared indicators of compromise (IoCs). APT33’s activities are linked to intelligence collection efforts on behalf of the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). On 18 September 2024, Brad Smith, vice-chairman and president of Microsoft Corporation, reported to the United States Senate Select Committee on Intelligence that the US government sector affected was at least or exclusively a county government in a disputed swing state. The hacking group managed to access an account belonging to the county government, but it is unclear whether the incident was related to the elections.

In the last week of August, the German air navigation service provider, Deutsche Flugsicherung (DFS), experienced a cyberattack in late August 2024. According to a spokesperson from DFS, the hackers infiltrated the IT infrastructure, causing disruptions to office communications. However, it is important to note that air traffic control operations remained unaffected throughout the incident. The extent of any potential data access is still under investigation. Various media outlets have suggested that the Russian APT28 group may be involved in the attack. In December 2025, the federal government of Germany attributed the attack to the Russian group "Fancy Bear" (aka APT28) and summoned the Russian ambassador.

Alcampo, one of the main chains of hypermarkets and supermarkets in Spain, has been the victim of a cyberattack that has affected its normal operation on 25 August 2024. The incident generated complications in key systems and processes affecting the ordering systems of Alcampo stores, which has caused supply problems that have affected the availability of some products in the establishments. In addition, it is speculated that the attack may also have affected the implementation of promotions and the production of periodical brochures that the chain publishes. However, the company has denied that these specific areas are compromised, stating that a contingency plan has been activated to mitigate the effects of the attack. The company has implemented technical and organizational measures to ensure the continuity of its operations, although it recognizes that these are being carried out in a more complex way than usual.  The company is working closely with cyber crime experts and has filed a complaint with the competent authorities to investigate the attack.

Google’s Threat Analysis Group published a blog post on 29 August 2024 that details watering hole attacks channeled through Mongolian government websites. The report with moderate confidence ties the campaign to APT29, a group that’s been linked to Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service, also referred to as Cozy Bear or Midnight Blizzard. The campaigns occurred from November 2023 to July 2024. Google stated that the hackers used “n-day” exploits that were first used by major commercial spyware producers. A cookie stealer framework is employed to acquire authentication cookies from prominent websites such as LinkedIn, Gmail and Facebook.

Title (Company): Kingsoft Corporation - Not available - Not available
Description: The South Korean cyber espionage group APT-C-60 exploited several 0-day vulnerabilities in Chinese email software and the Chinese office software WPS Office beginning on 30 April 2024, reported both the Chinese IT security company HunterLab on 12 August 2024 and the Slovakian threat intelligence company ESET on 28 August 2024. The first report by HunterLab refers to the exploitation of vulnerabilities in Foxmail, 126 and 163's email software and Kingsoft Corporation's WPS Office. HunterLab attributed this incident to the Fake Hunter APT from South Korea, whose goal is said to have been to gather intelligence related to relations between China and South Korea. The various software is said to have been used to compromise government officials' computers, trade personnel, non-governmental organisations and scholars. ESET's second report only refers to the two vulnerabilities (CVE-2024-7262; CVE-2024-7263) in WPS Office. ESET attributed this incident to the South Korean cyber espionage group APT-C-60. APT-C-60 is said to have targeted East Asian countries using the SpyGlace backdoor as a payload.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), and the Department of Defense Cyber Crime Center (DC3) released a joint Cybersecurity Advisory (CSA) to warn network defenders that, as of August 2024, a group of Iran-based actors continues to exploit US and foreign organizations. This includes organizations across several sectors in the US (including in the education, finance, healthcare, and defense sectors as well as local government entities) and other countries (including in Israel, Azerbaijan, and the United Arab Emirates). The FBI assesses a significant percentage of these threat actors’ operations against US organizations are intended to obtain and develop network access to then collaborate with ransomware affiliate actors to deploy ransomware. The actors’ initial access is usually obtained via exploiting a public-facing networking device, such as Citrix Netscaler (CVE-2019-19781 and CVE-2023-3519), F5 BIG-IP (CVE-2022-1388), Pulse Secure/Ivanti VPNs (CVE-2024-21887), and, more recently, PanOS firewalls (CVE-2024-3400). After infiltrating victim networks, the actors collaborate with ransomware affiliates (including NoEscape, Ransomhouse, and ALPHV [aka BlackCat]) in exchange for a percentage of the ransom payments by providing affiliates with access to victim networks, locking victim networks, and strategizing to extort victims. The actors also conduct what is assessed to be a separate set of malicious activity—stealing sensitive data from victims, likely in support of the government of Iran.

The criminal groups IntelBroker and EnergyWeaponUser claimed to have targeted the semiconductor company AMD on 28 August 2024. The stolen data includes user credentials, internal resolutions, and detailed case descriptions. AMD has said that it is aware of the claims made by the cybercriminal organization and is working with law enforcement and a third-party hosting partner to investigate the situation and is also assessing the extent of the data breach. This breach follows a similar incident in June 2024, where the company's employee data was compromised.

Japan's leading French-based pharmaceutical company Sanofi has announced a data breach affecting information of 330,000 Japanese medical workers and employees. From July 10 to 14 2024 it was found that an external third party had been accessing part of the company's database.

RansomHub Group compromised networks of the British company Banham Poultry on 18 August 2024 and obtained personal details of staff. Said information include National Insurance numbers, copies of passports and bank details. Banham Poultry, refused to say whether the cyberattack involved ransomware, but in an email to staff it added: "In most instances the criminals responsible are looking to gain money from companies rather than individuals."

The Qilin group listed CODAC Behavioral Healthcare, a non-profit health care treatment organization, as one of their latest victims on 28 August 2024. Within the stolen data are financial information, pictures of ID cards, a list of staff members - including their Social Security Numbers - and healthcare cards.  This attack is very similar to the one on pathology lab services provider Synnovis in June 2024.

The Venezuelan National Electoral Council (CNE) was allegedly hit by a DDoS attack on 26 August 2024, which impacted the availability of its website and related services. According to the state-run Venezuelan Television (VTV) channel, the attack took place against the centres which host the website of the CNE and was tracked to IP addresses outside of Venezuela, though it was unclear where exactly the attack took place from.  The attack follows a previous alleged attack on the CNE earlier in August. Prior to this new attack, the CNE's website had been reactivated in preparation to publish the electoral results by the time it was attacked on 26 August.

The Malaysian hacktivist group RipperSec disrupted the website of the French comparison website PriceBank on 25 August 2024. The DDoS attack was carried out in response to the imprisonment of Telegram founder Pavel Durov and as part of the #FREEDUROV campaign.

China-linked APT Volt Typhoon exploited a zero-day vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2024-39717, in Versa Director, to deploy a custom webshell on breached networks, allowing the threat actors to intercept credentials in plain text. Versa Director is a centralized management and orchestration platform used primarily by Internet Service Providers (ISPs) and Managed Service Providers (MSPs) to manage and monitor Software-Defined Wide Area Networks (SD-WANs). Researchers at Lumen’s Black Lotus Labs discovered a zero-day vulnerability in Versa Director on June 17. Black Lotus Labs detected unusual traffic indicating the exploitation of several US Versa Director servers between June 12 and mid-July 2024. The initial access to these compromised systems was likely through port 4566, typically used for high-availability (HA) pairing between Versa nodes. Black Lotus analysis of global telemetry identified actor-controlled small-office/home-office (SOHO) devices exploiting this zero-day vulnerability at four US victims and one non-US victim in the Internet service provider (ISP), managed service provider (MSP) and information technology (IT) sectors. Black Lotus linked the activity to Volt Typhoon with moderate confidence.

Title (Company): Confederation Paysanne - La Voix du Nord - National Agency for the Safety of Medicines and Health Products (ANSM) - Public Service in France
Description: Hacktivists disrupted multiple French websites with DDoS attacks following the arrest of Telegram Founder Pavel Durov on 24 August 2024. Shortly after Durov’s arrest at Le Bourget Airport in Paris, numerous hacktivists began to publicize their intention to retaliate, calling on their followers to target certain French websites in a cyberattack campaign called “opDurov.” Multiple French government and non-government websites have gone offline in a DDoS Attack.

State-sponsored hacktivist group People's Cyber Army of Russia in collaboration with the pro-Russian hacktivist group disrupted the website of the Supreme Court of France and the Administrative Court of Paris on 25 August 2024, the hacktivist group announced on the same day on 25 August 2024. The DDoS attack was carried out in response to the imprisonment of Telegram founder Pavel Durov and as part of the #FREEDUROV campaign.

The Italian National Research Council, Italy's largest public research institution, was allegedly the victim of a data theft by the criminal actor SilkFin, which took place on 25 August 2024. SilkFin claimed to have stolen the data and subsequently leaked a 5.1MB .SQL file onto a breach forum, which contained sensitive data related to research projects and researchers. As some data was related to ongoing projects and users both domestically and globally, researchers worry of the potential for further attacks on other research institutions by actors abusing the stolen data.

Rhysida ransomware group targeted the Port of Seattle, which also operates the Seattle-Tacoma (Sea-Tac) International Airport, with a cyberattack on 24 August 2024. The outages began early Saturday and took down several systems. While the full scale of the outage has not been made public, the Port of Seattle websites, email and phone systems were also affected.  Security operations at Sea-Tac Airport were not impacted with 72,000 people flying out on Sunday, although the baggage sorting systems and some terminal screens at Sea-Tac Airport were disrupted. Travellers have been advised to allow extra time for their stay at the airport, use mobile applications for check-ins, and be prepared for longer-than-usual security lines and baggage claim wait times. On 13 September, Port of Seattle confirmed that Rhysida ransomware group was behind the cyberattack. They also confirmed that Rhysida accessed and encrypted parts of their computer systems, disrupting key services like baggage handling, check-in kiosks, ticketing, Wi-Fi, and parking. Port of Seattle also stated that they refused to pay the ransom, for this reason the ransomware group may publish stolen data.

Title (Company): bloom hearing specialists - Brad Hutchinson Hearing - HearClear Audiology
Description: An unknown threat actor infiltrated the systems of Australian national hearing services provider Bloom Hearing and infected internal systems with ransomware on 5 July 2024.  Bloom Hearing acknowledged the incident on 21 July and published a statement confirming the theft of data on 21 August. The company runs several ear clinics in Australia under its own name, as well as the HearClear Audiology and Hutchinson Audiology clinics.  The stolen data includes medical and financial data of current and former patients, as well as current and former employees and contractors. Bloom Hearing also offers hearing services through the federal Health Department's Hearing Services Program, which provides subsidised hearing services to veterans, pensioners and their dependents. This enabled the hackers to access patients' veteran status and concession card details.

An Essex primary school says its IT system has been compromised during the summer holiday in 2024. Systems were shut down and the start of the school year was delayed by a day. Canvey Island Infant School has reported the incident to the National Cyber Security Centre of the United Kingdom.

Title (Company): Syndicat des Énergies et de l'Aménagement numérique de la Haute-Savoie (Syane)
Description: The state-sponsored hacktivist group People's Cyber Army of Russia disrupted the website of the Federation of Energy and Digital Infrastructure of Haute-Savoie (Syane) on 25 August 2024, the hacktivist group itself announced the following day on 26 August 2024 on Telegram. The DDoS attack was carried out in response to the arrest of Telegram founder Pavel Durov in France on 24 August 2024 and as part of the #FREEDUROV campaign.

On 1 July 2024, the Israeli cybersecurity firm Sygnia disclosed its discovery of a China-nexus threat actor exploiting a zero-day vulnerability in Cisco network appliances. In subsequent reporting on 22 August, Sygnia detailed that the state-sponsored group Velvet Ant leveraged a command injection vulnerability in the command line interface of Cisco’s Nexus-series switches (CVE-2024-20399). The software flaw allowed the threat actors to gain direct access to the underlying Linux OS on which the operations of the switches are based. When used with valid administrator credentials to access the switch management console, the exploit enables threat actors to run arbitrary scripts on the compromised devices. Sygnia reported the vulnerability to Cisco in April 2024 after it had detected its abuse in the wild as part of an investigation of a multi-year espionage campaign conducted by Velvet Ant.

Unknown hackers compromised the domain and X account of the Fur Affinity social network beginning on 20 August 2024, Fur Affinity itself announced on 21 August 2024. The hackers are said to have compromised the respective DNS server via DNS hijacking so that access to Fur Affinity's domain was redirected to malicious websites. In addition, the X account of Fur Affinity and its recently deceased founder, Sean 'Dragoneer' Piche, have been taken over. Fur Affinity recovered control of their X account.

Title (Company): Chaika-Service - PJSC I.S. Brook INEUM - LLC Kontur-NIIRS - MTC - None - Yandex - Rostelecom - Beeline
Description: Members of Ukraine's Main Intelligence Directorate (GURMO) with assistance from Ukrainian hacktivists targeted Russian communication and Internet service providers on 24 August 2024. According to Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform, the operation was conducted to coincide with Ukraine's Independence Day on 24 August and was aimed at the Internet service provider Rostelecom as well as the mobile operators MTC and Beeline in addition to online services of Yandex.  Additional targets included the Chaika-Service automobile factory, aircraft equipment producer LLC Kontur-NIIRS and the supplier of hardware and software supplier PJSC I.S. Brook INEUM, which support the Russian armed forces. The operation allegedly also targeted the cloud and file storage of the Internet providers Mail.ru, VDSina, and Quidex as well as the resources of lighting equipment manufacturers, diesel stations, hosting providers, and ballistic protection manufacturers. Ukrinform cited GURMO sources that claimed the operation reached 33 target servers and 283 work stations at factories. According to these reports, 21 websites were shut down and 15 cloud and file storage repositories were deleted, erasing 70 terabytes of data.

Unknown actors hit Swisscom, a major Swiss telecommunication provider, with a DDoS attack on 23 August 2024. Connectivity disruptions affected payment service provider Twint between 11:30 and 16:00. Other e-banking and other online services were briefly unavailable during this period.  Swisscom was able to redirect malicious traffic on the afternoon of 23 August.

Title (Company): Korea Research Institute for Vocational Education and Training (KRIVET)
Description: The threat actor operating under the pseudonym Intelbroker hacked a career information website of the Korea Research Institute for Vocational Education and Training (KRIVET), which is part of the Ministry of Education, and offered 1.6 million records pertaining to CareerNet members for sale. Intelbroker advertised the information which dates to before April 2018 as for sale for $20,000. KRIVET confirmed the compromise in a statement on 20 August. Although the managing institute stated that credentials stolen during the breach were encrypted, security experts noted that the encryption did not meet common security practices and could be broken.

Unknown hackers took over the Facebook account of the electoral tribunal of the Mexican state of Tamaulipas on 21 August 2024, the electoral tribunal reported on its website. In addition, the president of the electoral tribunal is said to have been the victim of an armed attack on the same day.

Malwarebyte Labs reports unknown attackers infected the online stores of hundreds of companies using the e-commerce platform Magento with a digital skimmer in August 2024. Digital skimmers are snippets of code that have been injected into online stores, and they can steal the user's credit card number, expiration date and CVV/CVC as the user type it in. Within a few days, over a dozen attacker-controlled websites were identified that were set up to receive the stolen data. Among the victims are a European beer manufacturer and a Canadian university.

On 21 August 2024, unknown hackers gained control of McDonald’s official Instagram account and the personal X account of the company's senior markeing director. The hackers used this access to promote a fraudulent Solana-based cryptocurrency scheme. The attackers posted links to a fake "Grimace" meme coin, tricking followers into transferring funds through the Solana blockchain, believing they were investing in a McDonald’s-branded cryptocurrency. The scam resulted in over $700,000 in stolen funds. McDonald’s quickly regained control of its Instagram account and removed the fraudulent posts. The company issued an apology and is cooperating with law enforcement to investigate the breach.

Unknown hackers targeted the New Caledonian Internet service provider Lagoon with Ransomware. On 19 August, the company announced on social media that it had been the target of ransomware the day before. The cyberattack paralysed Lagoon's computer systems, and the hackers demanded a ransom in exchange for not leaking exfiltrated data. Lagoon's website was unavailable. In addition, several subscribers have reported difficulties, including the complete loss of their Internet connection.

Unknown hackers targeted Microchip Technology Inc. (USA) with a cyberattack. The company, which supplies chips to the US defense industry, detected suspicious activity on its information technology systems on August 17, 2024. It was later confirmed that an unauthorized party had breached certain servers and disrupted some business operations. Upon discovering the breach, Microchip implemented measures to contain the incident, including isolating compromised systems, shutting down certain operations, and launching an investigation with external experts. The company’s manufacturing facilities are operating below normal capacity, affecting its ability to fulfil orders. The full scope and impact of the cyberattack remain uncertain as the investigation is ongoing.

Unknown hackers disrupted a Russian telecommunications operator on 21 August 2024, the Federal Service for Supervision of Communications, Information Technology and Mass Media of Russia (Roskomnadzor, RKN) reported on the same day. According to the report, a Russian telecommunications operator was hit with a DDoS attack at 14:00 on 21 August 2024. This led to a one-hour disruption of short messaging services in Russia, such as Telegram and WhatsApp, until the attack was repelled.

Gen Threat Labs uncovered and reported a zero-day vulnerability in the AFD.sys driver (CVE-2024-38193) to gain unauthorized access to unspecified sensitive system areas in early June 2024. The vulnerability was actively exploited by the North-Korea-linked Lazarus APT group and has now been fixed by Microsoft.

On 29 July 2024, Swiss industrial company Hoerbiger Holding, known for its expertise in compression technology, drive technology, and safety systems, was targeted by the Akira ransomware group. The attackers infiltrated the company’s network, stealing and encrypting over 50 GB of sensitive data, including employee information, customer data, contracts, and financial records. The attack also disrupted production at several locations. Hoerbiger confirmed that the ransomware attack compromised two out of 800 global servers, while core systems such as Microsoft 365, ERP, CRM, and HR platforms remained unaffected due to external hosting. In response, the company has restored its production facilities and is working to rebuild its IT infrastructure with strengthened security measures.

Ukrainian cyber hacktivists from the BO team targeted the Russian Internet provider Vega in August 2024. They took down more than 1173 of the provider’s switches and 10 of the company’s servers, and the information on them was completely destroyed. As a result, the provision of Internet and communication services to a number of strategic enterprises of the city has been blocked for five days in a row. Amongst others, the All-Russian Research Institute of Technical Physics (VNIITF), a developer of nuclear munitions, is affected by the incident. The hacktivists obtained potentially sensitive information from this plant, including personal data and internal documents including on arrangements designed to help the Institute circumvent sanctions.

According to a report by CheckPoint Research, Fucosreal, an Agent Tesla threat actor, used the Agent tesla stealer in a spam campaign for the purpose of data exfiltration against several industries from China, India, the UAE, and the Philippines in March 2024. Among the affected sectors are the Diamond industry, Metallurgical industry, Glass manufacturing, Environmentally friendly packaging, Ocean freight shipping, Wallpaper manufacturing and Aluminum industry. The threat actor distributed a malicious TAR archive, which contained the Agent Tesla stealer in the spam campaign and used the Telegram Bot API for data exfiltration.

Unknown attackers gained access to the systems of US oilfield services firm Halliburton around 21 August 2024.  The company, headquartered in North Houston, Texas, confirmed that a third party managed to access internal systems according to an SEC filing from 23 August.  The firm plays a major role in the oil and natural gas supply chain, including the maintenance of oil production facilities. According to Reuters, the incident impacted systems on the company's North Houston campus, as well as global connectivity networks.  In November 2024, Halliburton announced that the ransomware attack had cost it $35,000.

Unknown attackers targeted the systems of the British Virgin Islands Electricity Corporation (BVIEC) with ransomware on 19 August 2024. The attack was conducted on the heals of the tropical storm "Ernesto" which already put pressure on BVIEC to restore damaged parts of the electricity grid.  According to the General Manager of BVIEC, Dr. Neil Smith, ransomware of the Akira strand was used in the attack. The incident was discovered on 19 August. Further investigations revealed that the initial intrusion took place several months earlier.  The attack affected internal as well as external operations of BVIEC. Online payments were also impacted by the incident and customers had to pay in person.

Unknown attackers gained access to the systems of French Paris-Saclay University and deployed ransomware on 11 August 2024. The incident impacted all internal servers of the university, causing outages to the institution's email services, the intranet, shared work spaces and certain business applications. The university communicated details of the intrusion on its website ten days after it was first detected, disclosing the involvement of ransomware. Following internal protocols and government directives, the university stated that it was not planning to make any ransom payments. Together with the French cybersecurity agency ANSSI, a university response team launched an investigation to determine the point of entry into the network. On 20 August, the university filed a complaint with the departmental gendarmerie of Palaiseau. On October 9, the ransomware group RansomHouse claimed to have stolen 1 TB of data from the University of Paris-Saclay.

Earth Baku, a hacking group associated with the Chinese-state-sponsored APT41, expanded its geographical reach by pursuing targets in Germany, Italy, United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Thailand since late 2022, according to a report by Trend Micro from 9 August 2024. Previously, the group had predominantly focused on the Indo-Pacific region. The group targeted the following sectors: government, media and communications, telecom, technology, healthcare and education. Suspected but non-confirmed target geographies also included Georgia and Romania. Throughout those activities, Earth Baku updated its tactics, using public-facing applications like IIS servers as entry points for attacks. They then deploy sophisticated malware, including the loaders StealthVector and StealthReacher, and the modular backdoor SneakCross. In the post-exploitation stage, Earth Baku uses reverse tunneling tools to maintain control and deploys the MEGAcmd tool, likely for data exfiltration.
Techniques Used: Automated Exfiltration, Exfiltration Over Web Service, Exploit Public-Facing Application

Description: The Alabama Cardiology Group (USA) suffered a data breach from June 6 until July 2, 2024, which affected 281,000 individuals, according to a breach notification to federal regulators on 2 August 2024. The notification further stated that the hackers obtained sensitive information and that the incident involved a network server. The practice further revealed in an online statement that they became aware of the breach on 2 July. The incident affected various types of personal information, including Social Security numbers, health insurance details, financial data, and medical records such as diagnoses and lab results. Alabama Cardiology Group was likely targeted through credential abuse, possibly due to weak or reused passwords, and a lack of multifactor authentication, according to Mike Hamilton, founder and CISO of Critical Insight.

Unknown threat actors targeted the website of the Venezuelan National Assembly on 16 August 2024. Due to the attack, the website is currently not accessible and official notes and communiqués will be disseminated on the Telegram messaging platform as an interim measure. According to the minister of science and technology, at least 106 government agencies have been targets of the digital attacks since the presidential elections on 28 July.

Jesse Kipf, a 39-year-old US citizen from Kentucky, gained access to the Hawaii death registry and faked his death intending to escape his child support payments beginning in January 2023, the US Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Kentucky reported in its press release on 20 August 2024. In the case of the Hawaii death registry, Kipf used the username and password of a doctor in another state to gain access to it. Kipf also gained unauthorised access to other unnamed death registries, private business networks, and government and corporate networks with the aim of selling access on the darknet. The failure to make maintenance payments and the damage to the affected computer networks totalled $195,758.65. The US District Court for the Eastern District of Kentucky sentenced Kipf to 81 months imprisonment for computer fraud and aggravated identity theft.

On 7 November 2024, Finastra detected suspicious activity on its internally hosted file transfer platform, which led to the discovery of a large-scale data breach. Using the nickname 'abyss0', an unknown threat actor had stolen over 400 gigabytes of data, including customer information, and began selling it on the cybercrime community BreachForums on 8 November 2024. This actor also tried to sell the stolen data before, on 31 October 2024. Therefore, the breach is believed to have occurred at least a week before detection, with the threat actor gaining access to Finastra's file-sharing system through compromised credentials. Finastra notified its customers, including 45 of the world's top 50 banks, and implemented an alternative secure file-sharing platform to ensure continuity. The company is still investigating the root cause and scope of the breach and has been sharing Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) and updates with its customers. KrebsOnSecurity reported the incident on 19 November 2024.

Unknown threat actors infiltrated the management tools of French telecom provider Free, accessing personal data associated with certain subscriber accounts. While Free reported that no passwords, bank card details, or communications content were compromised, the precise scope and timing of the breach remain undisclosed. In response, Free has lodged a criminal complaint and alerted the National Commission for Information Technology and Civil Liberties (CNIL) and the National Agency for the Security of Information Systems (ANSSI). On October 21, 2024, an unnamed user on BreachForums put the stolen data from Free up for sale. Although no bank card details were released, over 5 million International Bank Account Numbers (IBANs) were allegedly stolen as part of the attack, with the hackers releasing a sample (100,000) of these numbers on BreachForums. The Paris judicial court has ordered Telegram to reveal the identity of a hacker behind a ransomware attack on October 31. Free and Free Mobile reported that a cybercriminal identified as "[Z] [L]" sent three messages on October 21 through their internal platform for personal data protection, followed by a fourth message addressed to the "president of the Iliad group," Xavier Niel, via Telegram. The hacker demanded a ransom of €10 million in cryptocurrencies. Telegram has been given 48 hours to provide identifying information, such as IP addresses, the phone number used to create the account, and civil identity details. On 6 December 2024, cybersecurity researcher Clément Domingo (also known as SaxX on X) uncovered that an internal agent likely provided their OpenVPN credentials to a third party, potentially the hacker. That way, the hacker leveraged stolen VPN credentials to infiltrate Free's secure network. Masquerading as IT personnel, the attacker manipulated other employees through social engineering to gain additional credentials, enabling the hacker to access vast customer data. This leak is said to have been known among certain employees, but none of them dared to disclose it to their superiors. According to French media, a 17 year old suspect was indicted in January 2025 in relation to the hack, while in March 2025, Free was targeted in sanctions proceedings by the French National Commission for Information Technology and Civil Liberties.

On 9 August 2024, a hacker gained unauthorized access to the Google G-Suite accounts of San Francisco-based cryptocurrency firm Unicoin, locking all employees out of key systems, including G-Mail and G-Drive, for nearly four days. The breach disrupted operations until 13 August 2024, when Unicoin regained control of its accounts. While no evidence of stolen digital assets has been found, the breach led to discrepancies in the personal data of employees and contractors, particularly within the accounting department. Additionally, traces of hacked messages were identified in certain managers' email accounts. Unicoin continues to investigate the incident and its potential impact on operations, while also terminating a contractor who had forged their identity during the ongoing investigation.

POLADA, the Polish Anti Doping Agency, was the victim of a data theft by Beregini, a Russian hacker group which POLADA linked to the "services of a foreign state," in the during the Paris Olympics in 2024, with data being leaked on 6 August. According to Beregini's Telegram statement, the subsequent leak of data included the "complete database of Polish athletes," indicating that several Polish athletes were using doping with the knowledge of POLADA. However, Polish media and POLADA both stated that, while data was actually stolen, the data was manipulated by the Russian hackers and then released online as part of a disinformation campaign, saying that "none of the mentioned athletes obtained a positive result and none of the dates presented correspond to anti-doping controls." POLADA indicated that there would be an investigation alongside the police, CERT Polska, the Office for Personal Data Protection, and the Ministry of Sport and Tourism, while simultaneously asking citizens to not spread "propaganda of a hostile country."

At the end of July 2024, Kaspersky identified an active series of targeted cyberattacks on dozens of computers of Russian government organizations and IT companies. In these attacks, attackers infected devices using phishing emails with attachments containing malicious shortcut files. When clicking on the shortcuts, malware was installed, which subsequently received commands through the Dropbox cloud storage. Using this software, the attackers downloaded additional Trojans onto infected computers, in particular tools used by APT31, as well as an updated CloudSorcerer backdoor.

CERT-UA warned on 12 August 2024 of an ongoing phishing campaign from threat actors tracked as UAC-0198, which targeted local and state-level government computers.  CERT-UA stated that the attack was enabled through UAC-0198 impersonating the Security Service of Ukraine (SSU), which sent phishing emails with a link downloading a "Documents.zip" file, which, if the file was opened, would inject MESHAGENT malware into the computer, giving the attackers hidden, unauthorized access to the computer. According to CERT-UA, over 100 computers, including within these governmental sectors, were infected with the malware in the course of the campaign as of 12 August 2024.

Unknown attackers target Australian Evolution Mining Company with Ransomware on 8 August 2024. The company stated that despite the disruption the ransomware attack caused to its IT systems, it does not anticipate it will have any material impact on operations. Mining operations continued uninterrupted, indicating that the unknown threat actors did not reach production-critical workstations.

Rhysida Ransomware Group targeted Sumter County Sheriff’s Office (Florida, USA) on 6 August 2024. The agency acted quickly to cut off all access from the attacker, but the cyberattack has temporarily disrupted access to certain records, although law enforcement services remain unaffected. The Rhysida group claimed responsibility for the attack and demanded a ransom of 7 Bitcoins, approximately $425,000, to restore access.

On 9 January 2024, the East Valley Institute of Technology (EVIT) in Arizona was hit by a ransomware attack carried out by the LockBit group, potentially compromising the personal, health, and financial information of 208,717 individuals. The Lockbit hackers accessed EVIT’s network using compromised credentials and encrypted critical systems, demanding a ransom, which EVIT refused to pay. The breach exposed potentially sensitive information, including social security numbers, disciplinary files, medical records, information about diagnoses and allergies, as well as financial account details.

North Korean hackers targeted a South Korean defense contractor in early 2024. Local media, citing defense and police sources, reported that a subcontractor for a major defense technology company had been hacked, leading to the leak of technical data about the South Korean military’s Baekdu and Geumgang surveillance aircraft. South Korean officials suspect that North Korea orchestrated the breach of the company that produces operation and maintenance manuals for military equipment, reflecting its renewed focus on small subcontractors whose security level tends to be lower than big manufacturers.

Unknown hackers disrupted the Ohio School Boards Association's website and email on 8 and 9 August 2024.  The hack was discovered on the afternoon of 8 August 2024 when members were no longer able to access the OSBA website.  Over 700 school boards and around 3500 board members across Ohio are being served by the OSBA.  The head of the OSBA told news media that the association typically does not store any personal information like financial information or social security numbers. As of now, there is no reason to believe that any sensitive data from members has been compromised. She also ruled out the possibility of a ransomware attack, but there could be a connection to the cyber incident at the City of Columbus, Ohio, three weeks earlier.

An unknown actor conducted an DDoS attack on Russia's Kursk region on 8 August 2024. The unnamed hackers targeted government and business websites, as well as critical infrastructure services, making some of them temporarily unavailable, Russian state media reported. This incident coincided with Ukrainian military advancements in the Kursk region.

Unknown actors hacked into the email system of an Indian supplier of electrical and telecommunication towers and other equipment with customers worldwide on 9 August in 2024. The attackers sent a fraudulent message to the company's client, falsely indicating a change in banking details. After a deal with a client from the UAE, the client confirmed the payment, but the company later discovered the funds were not credited to their account. The hackers impersonated the company, instructing the client to transfer an amount of 920 million rupees (roughly USD 10.9 million) to an account at the National Bank of Australia.

An unknown attacker conducted an DDoS attack on the website of the Port of Tyne near Newcastle (United Kingdom) on 6 August in 2024. The Port of Tyne confirmed its site was down for some time and restored website availability soonafter.

Unknown hackers targeted Brussels Institute for Journalism and Communication (IHECS) with ransomware on 2 August 2024. The threat actors gained access through a phishing operation and exfiltrated data from the university's computer system before encrypting drives. The attack was discovered on 2 August and a crisis team has since been set up and a company specialising in cybercrime has been called in.

According to the City of Killeen, (Texas, USA) the BlackSuit ransomware group gained access to the city's systems on Wednesday, 7 August 2024.  The city says most of the affected systems are internal, but citizens may experience a delay in essential services at the Utility Collections division. Upon discovery of the breach, the city took steps to secure their systems to prevent further access. As a precautionary measure, Killeen disconnected from the Bell County Network to contain the spread of the attack. As of now, the city does not believe that personal or financial information of citizens has been exfiltrated but recommends monitoring personal bank accounts and to report any suspicious activity.

A hacker group known as the Mexican Mafia hacked into the Mexico City Judicial System (PJCDMX)'s website and stole data of 162,439 users in early August 2024; it proceeded to leak all of their login credentials on 6 August 2024 in a document leaked on a hacking forum and simultaneously sent to media sources, with the group's leader, named "Pancho Villa," alleging that he had "thousands of terabytes" more data. Ultimately, almost 300,000 records were leaked in the document, but out of these, 162,439 were unique identifiers (emails, passwords, usernames), suggesting roughly 140,000 were duplicates. Among the actual data stolen and leaked were hundreds of credentials from government employees, such as those from the Judicial Branch of the State of Mexico, the Mexican Social Security Institute, the Superior Court of Mexico City, and the Institute for Social Security and Services for State Workers, as well as data belonging to users of educational institutions.

Nexera, a cryptocurrency blockchain infrastructure protocol, was the victim of a financial theft from an unknown hacker on 7 August 2024. The attack, which was outlined by a blockchain security firm, saw the theft of roughly $1.2 million in NXRA coins, as well as over $500,000 in USDT stablecoin. The attack was enabled by an exploit within Nexera's proxy contract - a central point of blockchain infrastructure protocols - which allowed the hacker to take control of it and withdraw all NXRA coins. Nexera was forced to halt trading and pause NXRA contracts so that, ideally, the stolen money could not be exchanged for other cryptocurrencies.

Unknown hackers breached Systems of mobile device management company Mobile Guardian on 4 August 2024, which impacted users globally, the attackers remotely wiped a small percentage of devices, according to the company. Mobile Guardian’s investigations found that there had been a global cybersecurity incident involving unauthorised access to its platform that affected its customers globally, including those in Singapore. Based on preliminary checks, about 13,000 students in Singapore from 26 secondary schools had their devices wiped remotely by the perpetrator. There is currently no evidence that the perpetrator had accessed user files. As a precautionary measure, the Ministry of Education of Singapore has removed the Mobile Guardian Device Management Application from all iPads and Chromebooks. Efforts are underway to safely restore these devices to normal usage. This attack is similar to an incident on April 19th 2024, also involving Mobile Guardian and Schools in Singapore.

The Iranian state-sponsored group APT42 compromised the campaign of US presidential candidate Donald J. Trump beginning in July 2024. On 10 August 2024, news outlet Politico reported receiving internal campaign communications from an individual using the alias "Robert", including documents related to the vetting process of vice presidential candidate JD Vance. On 8 August 2024, Microsoft Threat Analysis Center published a report noting that a US presidential campaign had been subject to spear-phishing attempts by Iranian actors with ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). Trump campaign spokesperson Steven Cheung subsequently confirmed the campaign was affected. On 11 August 2024, Trump acknowledged the incident but claimed only publicly available information had been obtained. On 14 August 2024, the Google Threat Analysis Group published a technical report on APT42 and its phishing campaigns against US and Israeli targets in 2024, confirming recent media reports of incidents against US election campaigns. The report noted that the personal Gmail account of a high-ranking political advisor had been compromised and attributed the incident to Cluster C of APT42. On 19 August 2024, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) issued a joint statement officially attributing the breach to Iranian threat actors. On 18 September 2024, the FBI, ODNI and CISA announced that Iranian threat actors had sent stolen and unpublished material, including email text, to members of Biden's election campaign in late June and early July 2024 and to US media outlets since June 2024. On 26 September 2024, the US Department of Justice unsealed an indictment against three Iranian nationals allegedly affiliated with the IRGC in connection with the operation.

​On 6 August 2024, IT and phone systems at McLaren Health Care hospitals were disrupted following an attack linked to the INC Ransom ransomware operation. McLaren hinted the hospitals had lost access to patient information databases when advising patients to bring detailed information about their current medications to appointments, including physician orders and printed results of recent lab tests. Employees at McLaren Bay Region Hospital in Bay City have shared a ransom note warning that the hospital's systems have been encrypted and stolen data will be published on INC RANSOM ransomware gang's leak site if a ransom is not paid. The incident is still under investigation. McLaren stated that it had brought its operations fully back online by 27 August. On 5 May 2025, the hospital finished its investigation that confirmed the data of  743,000 patients was affected by the data theft.

Unknown threat actors conducted a ransomware attack on the internal network of the US city of Flint on 14 August 2024. Due to the attack, several services are currently unavailable such as the online or credit card payments of water, sewer, and taxes. E-Mail and phone services are also experiencing gaps in service. Whether internal data such as resident or employee personal data was accessed is still under investigation.

An unnamed ransomware actor encrypted data from the network of a Swiss farm, the Luzerner Zeitung first reported on 5 August 2024. According to the report, hackers encrypted Vital Bircher's farm's Windows network in Hagendorn near Zug and demanded CHF 10,000 to decrypt it. The farmer refused to pay the ransom. Due to the encryption of the Windows network, the farmer could no longer access the data from his milking robot, which was responsible for his 70 cows, and the milking robot could no longer feed data into the network. Due to this lack of data, the farmer was unable to recognise that a cow was pregnant and needed help, so the calf to be whelped died in the womb, and the mother cow subsequently had to be euthanised. The ransomware attack cost the farmer around CHF 6,400 as he had to buy a new computer and pay for veterinary costs.

A group of hackers redirected visitors of the website of the National Party of Uruguay to a website controled by the attackers that showed a statement threatening Senator Graciela Bianchi. The actors further claimed to possess compromising WhatsApp messages from the senator. According to Macarena Rubio, president of the board of directors of the National Party (PN), the political party filed a complaint with the Cybercrime Unit of the police. According to the statements of the nationalist leader, the objective of the action is to be able to “identify those responsible”. The incident was also announced on Breach Forums.

The newly emerged Brain Cipher Group hit the network of the Réunion des Musées Nationaux, with ransomware which includes around 40 French museums, on the night of 3-4 August 2024, during the Summer Olympics. The group's payloads are based on LockBit 3.0. The attribution stems from French IT-media reports, that did not disclose their sources. According to an initial press release, no data extraction has been detected, but the French news outlet Le Parisien reports that financial data has been encrypted, and a ransom is being demanded. The incident is still under investigation and the French cyber agency has been informed.

North Korean APT Group Andariel targeted South Korean construction and machinery companies in April 2024, according to a joint report from the South Korean National Cyber Security Centre, the National Intelligence Service, and others. According to intelligence agencies, the campaign is twofold: on the one hand, Kimsuky has been targeting the websites of construction agencies with malware hidden in authentication services when a user logs into the website. This allowed Kimsuky to infect the computers of local governments, public institutions, and other construction companies in January 2024. The joint campaign from Andariel started in April. The group exploited vulnerabilities in VPNs to install remote control malware into the systems of construction and machinery companies in South Korea. In this move, the hacker group is said to have succeeded in stealing machine and equipment-related blueprints. The NCSC links the joint Kimsuky-Andariel campaign to North Korea's "Local Development 20x10 Policy," meant to facilitate the building of modern industrial facilities in the DPRK.

Unknown actors disrupted multiple emergency dispatch centres in Highland Lakes and across Central Texas with a DDoS robocall attack on 4 August 2024, authorities reported the following day. The DDoS attack involved automated calls from fake phone numbers that disrupted the emergency dispatch centres' telecommunications network. The callers could not hear each other, addresses were not displayed, or the calls did not go through at all. The switching centres belonging to the Capital Area Council of Governments (CAPCOG) are located in Burnet, Llano, Travis, Williamson, Fayette, Caldwell, Lee, Blanco, Hays and Bastrop Counties.

North Korean APT Group Kimsuky targeted South Korean construction companies in supply chain attack in January 2024, according to a joint report from the South Korean National Cyber Security Centre, the National Intelligence Service, and others. According to intelligence agencies, the campaign is twofold: on the one hand, Kimsuky has been targeting the websites of construction agencies with malware hidden in authentication services when a user logs into the website. This allowed Kimsuky to infect the computers of local governments, public institutions, and other construction companies. The joint campaign from Andariel started in April. The group exploited vulnerabilities in VPNs to install remote control malware into the systems of construction companies in South Korea. In this move, the hacker group is said to have succeeded in stealing machine and equipment-related blueprints. The NCSC links the joint Kimsuky-Andariel campaign to North Korea's "Local Development 20x10 Policy," meant to facilitate the building of modern industrial facilities in the DPRK.

Title (Company): Santa Ana de Motril Hospital - Virgen de las Nieves Hospital - Andalusian Health Service (SAS) - Clinico San Cecilio
Description: An unnamed actor stole personal information of approximately 50,000 health professionals from the Andalusian Health Service (SAS) and various associated health service providers since at least 9 July 2024, the Andalusian Health Service reported on 5 August 2024. According to the report, the cyber incident was discovered on 9 July 2024 on the websites of various healthcare providers, including the Clinico San Cecilio, the Virgen de las Nieves Hospital in Granada, and the Santa Ana de Motril Hospital. However, other healthcare providers from the Southern Health Management Area and the Granada district are also said to be affected.  The incident was discovered when an anonymous actor contacted the aforementioned healthcare providers and informed them that they had identified a vulnerability that they would exploit if they did not receive a ransom. Whether the actor making contact and the actor stealing the data are the same remains under investigation.  The personal information included names and surnames, ID cards, telephone numbers, professional categories, corporate email, corporate user credentials and encrypted passwords. The hacker demanded $2,500 in Bitcoin for not disclosing the stolen information.

At the end of July 2024, the Indian Banking Technology Service Provider C-Edge was hit by a RansomEXX group with ransomware, which affected nearly 300 Indian banks, especially cooperative and rural regional banks. The incident's coverage was communicated by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), which temporarily isolated the affected banks from the country’s retail payments system to prevent the spread of the attack. Since the attack was contained within C-Edge’s systems, the impacted banks are now able to resume payments via the United Payments Interface (UPI) and other payment systems managed by the NPCI. Cyber-security firm CloudSEK reported that the attack was carried out by the ransomware group RansomEXX, being facilitated by a misconfigured Jenkins server at Brontoo Technology Solutions, a partner of C-Edge, according to Brontoo Technologies filed report to CERT India.

An unattributed cybercriminal group sent various remote access Trojans via TryCloudflare tunnels from February to July 2024, Proofpoint reported in a technical report on 1 August 2024. According to the report, the cybercriminal group used the function of TryCloudflare Tunnel to create a one-time tunnel without having to create an entire account for it. The cybercriminal group used this to send hundreds to hundreds of thousands of messages in different languages to targets containing remote access Trojans. These included AsyncRAT, VenomRAT, GuLoader, Remcos and, from June to July 2024, almost exclusively Xworm.  In a traceable incident on 28 May 2024, a remote access Trojan was successfully deployed against legal and financial organisations.

According to President Maduro, the Venezuelan National Electoral Council was allegedly targeted with DDoS after the Presidential election on 28 July 2024, which he stated as the reason for why the authorities have not released detailed vote counts at that time. Furthermore, he blamed Elon Musk for the attack and argued that the election system has been hacked as part of a plot against him. However, the hacking collective Anonymous also claimed the hack for itself. There have been no external verifications of the DDoS operation, but the Venezuelan state airline Conviasa was also disrupted a few days later. The US network security provider Netscout reported on 31 July of an observed tenfold increase in DDoS attacks against Venezuelan websites on July 29. On 14 August, the Chilean hacker Astra gave an interview to the medium Publimetro and claimed responsibility for the cyber incident on what was supposed to be the National Electoral Council. In the interview, Astra, also the leader of the hacker group Cyber Hunters, explained that they had discovered an unsecured ghost machine used to rig the elections. Astra said that they blocked this ghost machine from accessing the electoral system and stole the database it contained, with entries for 19 million residents, many of whom were already deceased. Astra also announced that the cyber incidents against Maduro will become more frequent and automated.

Cisco Talos disclosed an espionage campaign that compromised a Taiwanese government-affiliated research institute that started as early as July 2023. The company attributed the campaign, which delivered the ShadowPad malware, Cobalt Strike and other customized tools for post-compromise activities, due to technical overlaps with medium confidence to the Chinese APT41, which is widely perceived as state-sponsored.
