The attack was confirmed in a statement to Bangor Daily News on 25 March 2026, stating that it had recently experienced a network disruption and was investigating the incident with cyber incident specialists.

Unknown threat actor breached Papardo hospital in Messina on 24 March 2026, disrupting its systems and causing chaos in healthcare activities. The attack, which was first noticed on the evening of 24 March, blocked access to the computer system used for administering therapies to hospitalised patients and the central system for booking visits. The hospital filed a complaint with the Postal Police and informed the Prefecture, the Questura, and the Privacy Guarantor about the incident.

Unknown threat actor launched ransomware attack on the Port Of Vigo in the Northwestern Spanish autonomous province of Galicia on 24 March 2026. The attackers managed to compromise systems belonging to health and border inspection, as well as the port authority website. However, the attack was detected and staff prevented it from spreading to systems controlling operations. The attackers demanded a ransom, but any attempt at negotiation was cut off. The port continued to work manually and within its own network.

Unknown threat actors breached MetroWest Community Federal Credit Union, a financial institution based in Framingham, Massachusetts, between 1 and 3 September 2025. The attackers exfiltrated personal data of over 20,000 customers, including names, addresses, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, financial account numbers, driver's license numbers, taxpayer identification numbers and payment card numbers. MetroWest FCU discovered the breach on 1 January 2026 and disclosed the incident on its website on 11 March 2026.

Unknown threat actor compromised HR software COMPASS of French Ministry Of National Education on 15 March, accessed the personal data of approximately 243,000 National Education agents, mostly trainee teachers from primary and secondary schools, leveraging the login details of an external account. The stolen data included names, first names, postal addresses, contact details, and periods of absence. The data of tutors, including names, first names, and professional landlines, was also compromised. The intrusion was detected four days later, on 19 March 2026, by the ministry's operational centre for information system security. The Ministry of National Education informed the National Agency for the Security of Information Systems (ANSSI) and the National Commission for Information Technology and Liberties (CNIL), and a complaint was filed in Paris.

Unknown perpetrators conducted a DDoS attack against Nuup Bussii, a bus company in Greenland, on 23 March 2026. The company disclosed the attack on Facebook, stating that their webpage was unstable due to an ongoing cyberattack.

The Akira ransomware group claimed responsibility for an attack on INP Switzerland, an energy supply services provider, on the night of 25 to 26 February 2026. Akira claimed to have stolen 9 GB of data and threatened to publish it. INP Switzerland confirmed the occurrence of an attack but did not attribute it to a specific actor.

Title (Company): US Military Personnel - Unspecified Journalists - Current and Former US Government Officials - US Political Figures
Description: Cyber actors associated with Russian intelligence services conducted global phishing campaigns targeting commercial messaging application (CMA) accounts, including those of current and former US government officials, military personnel, political figures and journalists. The FBI and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) disclosed the campaign in a Public Service Announcement on 20 March 2026. The campaigns aimed to bypass encryption by compromising individual user accounts rather than the encryption of the applications themselves. The attackers gained unauthorised access to thousands of individual CMA accounts, enabling them to view victims' messages and contact lists, send messages and conduct additional phishing against other CMA accounts. On 26 June 2026, CISA published an update on their previous announcement stating that the campaign is ongoing and the attackers use new variants of phishing messages.

Title (Company): DeKalb County Jail - DeKalb County Sheriff's Department
Description: Unattributed threat actors deployed ransomware against the DeKalb County Sheriff's Department and Jail in Georgia on 14 March 2026, compromising the main computer server and affecting essential systems including email and detention management software. Correctional officers first noticed the issue early Friday morning when booking software suddenly stopped functioning. The authorities were able to recover detention-related data with the help of their booking vendor. Sheriff Patrick Ray reported the incident to the FBI and Tennessee Bureau of Investigation (TBI).

Iran-linked threat actors conducted a wave of attacks against over 50 Israeli small businesses in the weeks before 22 March 2026, destroying data and compromising approximately 50 security cameras. Yossi Karadi, Director-General of the Israel National Cyber Directorate, disclosed the attacks to reporters on 24 March 2026. Karadi stated that most targeted companies had existing cybersecurity vulnerabilities and that most victims have since restored operations. He added that Iran had not infiltrated or disrupted critical infrastructure such as energy grids, banks or hospitals.

Unidentified perpetrators breached Westport Fuel Systems, a Canadian company specialising in alternative fuel systems and components for the transportation industry, on 17 March 2026. The attackers gained unauthorised access to certain parts of the company's network, business applications and business and employee information.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Unspecified oil refinery
Description: Between November 2025 and February 2026, a Libyan oil refinery, a telecommunications operator, and a state institution were targeted in a cyber espionage campaign. The attackers used AsyncRAT malware, a modular backdoor, and gained initial access to the systems through spear phishing emails with bait documents related to Libyan current events, including a file titled 'Leaked CCTV footage - Saif al-Gaddafi's assassination', referencing the killing of Saif al-Gaddafi on 3 February 2026. The attack was revealed by an analysis published by the IT security company Symantec on 20 March 2026.

Unknown threat actors breached the General Secretariat of Catholic Education (Secrétariat Général de l'Enseignement Catholique) in France on 21 March 2026, which resulted in the leakage of personal data of 1.5 million people, including 800,000 primary school students, their families and 40,000 teachers. The compromised data included names, addresses, email addresses, telephone numbers and dates of birth. The General Secretariat reported the incident to the relevant authorities, including the Ministry of National Education, and informed headteachers, teachers and parents of affected pupils. Deputy Secretary-General Stéphane Gouraud disclosed the attack in a statement on 21 March 2026.

Title (Company): Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority
Description: The ransomware group WorldLeaks claimed responsibility for an attack on the City of Los Angeles and its Metro system on 19 March 2026. The group added the city to its data leak site on 20 March 2026 and claimed to have stolen 159.9 GB of data. The attack forced the transit agency to limit access to internal administrative computer systems which disrupted station arrival displays. Riders faced issues adding funds to TAP cards online or via support. Rail and bus services continued to run normally. Metro stated that no customer or employee data was affected and continued security checks to restore full access.  On 9 April 2026, the Iranian threat actor Ababil of Minab also claimed to have hacked the LA Metro (LACMTA). The group allegedly gained administrative access to virtualization infrastructure, web servers, and an operational rail yard management system. Ababil of Minab claimed the data destruction of 500 TB of data and the exfiltration of 100 TB of sensitive data. On 26 May 2026, the Israeli IT security company Gambit published a technical report in which they link the threat actor to Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS).

In 2025, Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) discoverd a suspected Russian espionage group UNC6353 having compromised Ukrainian websites, ranging from industrial equipment and retail tools to local services and ecommerce websites, and leveraging them to deliver a sophisticated iOS exploit toolkit to selected iPhone users from a specific geolocation. The exploit kit, dubbed Coruna, includes several n-day vulnerabilities (CVE-2024-23222, CVE-2022-48503, and CVE-2023-43000) for multiple iOS versions (not the latest version). Coruna was first observed in February 2025, where is was used by a customer of a surveillance company. In a campaign in July 2025, Coruna was spread by infected Ukrainian websites (watering hole attack). CERT-UA was notified to clean up all compromised websites.

Unknown threat actors deployed ransomware against the municipal administration of Matten near Interlaken, Switzerland, on 14 and 15 March 2026, resulting in the encryption of some data. The affected data was later fully restored.

Title (Company): Brazil’s Ministry of Mines and Energy - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: TGR-STA-1030 (aka UNC6619), a state-aligned group that operates out of Asia, attacked government organisations in 37 countries in or around early 2025. The group used phishing campaigns and exploited known vulnerabilities to gain access to the victims' networks using a wide range of common tools, exploitation kits and proof-of-concept code for N-day exploits. Unit 42 first identified UNC6619 upon investigating a cluster of malicious phishing campaigns targeting European governments in early 2025, but identified actor infrastructure dating as far back as January 2024.

Unknown threat actors breached Intuitive Surgical, a US-based surgical robotics firm, via a phishing attack before 13 March 2026. The attackers compromised an employee's credentials to gain access to the company's internal business administrative network, accessing customer and employee data. Intuitive Surgical disclosed the incident in a statement on 12 March 2026.

Suspected China-based state-sponsored actors, designated as CLSTA1087, carried out a targeted espionage operation against Southeast Asian military organizations since 2020. The attackers used custom-developed tools, including the AppleChris and MemFun backdoors, and a custom Getpass credential harvester, to collect highly specific files concerning military capabilities, organizational structures, and collaborative efforts with Western armed forces. The attackers' objective was highly targeted intelligence collection, rather than bulk data theft. Unit 42 informed the public about the attack on 12 March 2026.

On 10 March 2026, French Breaches, an independent website dedicated to the monitoring and documentation of data leaks in France, revealed that personal information of 310,000 young beneficiaries of the "Young Region Card" from the Occitanie Region have been stolen and are sold on the dark web. According to the French Breaches website, the supporting screenshots, the leaked database contains personal information including the name, first name, date of birth, postal address and e-mail, telephone number, school, school level, administrative file number, administrative status, date of registration and the contact details of the legal representatives. On 12 March, a spokesperson of the Occitanie Region confirmed to France 3 that it was notified by a service provider on 5 March that a "security incident on the computer system of the Youth Card" had occurred, without being able to specify the number of people affected.

In late 2025, researchers from Lookout Threat Labs discovered DarkSword, a full iOS exploit chain for recent iOS versions that was distributed from a compromised Ukrainian government website. DarkSword leverages several vulnerabilities including multiple zero-day vulnerabilities (CVE-2025-31277, CVE-2026-20700, CVE-2025-43529, CVE-2026-20700, CVE-2025-14174, CVE-2025-43510, CVE-2025-43520). Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) attributed the activities to the suspected Russian espionage group UNC6353. DarkSword aims to extract an extensive set of personal information including credentials from the device and specifically targets a plethora of crypto wallet apps. Since at least November 2025, GTIG has observed multiple commercial surveillance vendors and suspected state-sponsored actors utilizing DarkSword in distinct campaigns. The attack was carried out from a domain domains tied to the probable Russian threat actor UNC6353, as it was discoverd by Google earlier in 2025.

On 10 March 2026, Loblaw Companies Limited, the largest food and pharmacy retailer in Canada, announced that hackers breached a portion of its IT network and accessed basic customer information, exposing names, phone numbers, and email addresses of customers, prompting a forced logout for customer accounts, while payment, health, and password data appeared unaffected.

On 12 March 2026, the ShinyHunters hacking group breached the systems of Canadian telecommunications and business services firm Telus, stealing at least 700 terabytes of data, which reportedly included personally identifiable information, call data and recordings, FBI background check information, and source code from multiple business divisions. Telus was informed about the incident and subsequently started an investigation with the support of cyber forensics experts and law enforcement. The company stated that all business operations remained fully operational and there was no evidence of disruption to customer connectivity or service. The incident was confirmed by a Telus spokesperson.

Title (Company): Herzliya Train Station - Shalom Train Station
Description: On 11 March 2026, unknown threat actors compromised advertising signs in the passenger halls at Herzliya Station and Shalom Train Station in Tel Aviv. It was reported that Iranian hackers took control of the signs and posted messages claiming that the stations were expected to be attacked by Iranian missiles and instructing the public to evacuate immediately.

Title (Company): Ministry of Emergency and Disaster Management in Syria - Not available - Not available
Description: In early March 2026, the suspected China-aligned threat actor UNKInnerAmbush conducted a phishing campaign targeting Middle Eastern government and diplomatic organizations by sending emails from a likely compromised email address 'uzbembishelcat.kg' and linking to a Google Drive URL. The attackers purported to share sensitive information, including images from the US Department of Foreign Affairs and evidence of Israel's alleged plans to attack Gulf oil and gas infrastructure. The attack was reported by Proofpoint Threat Research on 11 March 2026.

On 5 March 2026, a suspected Pakistan-aligned actor, known as UNKRobotDreams, sent spear-phishing emails to India-based offices of Middle East government organisations. The emails were sent from an Outlook free-mail address impersonating India's Ministry of External Affairs, using the subject 'Gulf Security Alert Iran Retaliation Impacts' to increase credibility and urgency. Proofpoint reported the incident on 11 March 2026.

On 11 March 2026, Iranian-linked hackers, claiming to be from the 'Handala' group, breached the website of the Academy of the Hebrew Language, rendering it inaccessible. The hackers displayed a threatening message in English, stating 'No need to learn Hebrew. You will soon not need it anymore' alongside the logo of the 'Handala' group. The attack was reported by several sources, including the Times of Israel, and was commented on by Barak Dan, the scientific secretary of the institution, who emphasized the symbolic dimension of the cyberattack.

In the night of Saturday, 7 March 2026, hackers disrupted critical IT systems of the provincial hospital in Szczecin, Poland, by using ransomware, forcing staff to switch to manual documentation. The attackers, whose identity remains unknown, demanded a ransom of several million dollars to restore access to vital data. Poland's Defence Minister, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, informed the public about the attack on Wednesday, 13 March 2026, and announced that a team from the Territorial Defence had been sent to the hospital to support efforts to restore normal operation.

On or around 11 March 2026, hackers, suspected to be of Russian origin, breached the Workers Samaritan Federation (ASB) in Saarland, gaining access to a server containing customer data and that of current and former employees. The attackers threatened to publish the stolen data. The ASB isolated the affected server and worked with IT forensics experts to close the security gap. Despite the cyberattack, all services, including the rescue service and patient care, continued as usual. The relevant data protection and security authorities were informed. The incident was reported by several news outlets on 11 March 2026.

On 5 March 2026, unknown threat actors compromised the Middlesex London Health Unit’s (MLHU) systems in Canada, resulting in the shutdown of several systems, including regular phone lines and software. The incident was reported to Ontario's privacy commissioner and health ministry. In collaboration with cybersecurity experts from CFC Response and Norton Rose Fulbright, as well as external legal counsel and law enforcement agencies, several computer and phone systems were restored between 6 and 8 March 2026. The incident's impact on patient data is still being determined, with Williams stating that the MLHU will notify individuals if any personal data was affected. The public was informed of the attack via a press release from the MLHU on Friday, 8 March 2026.

On 11 March 2026, Iranian hackers allegedly compromised the networks of Stryker, a United States medical tech company, resulting in a major outage that affected the company's global operations in Europe, Asia, and the US. The attack, which occurred overnight, left thousands of people unable to work and all IT systems down, including at its Cork base, which employs 4,000 people. The incident was reported to the public by Stryker’s employees complaining on social media on 11 March 2026. On the same day, Stryker also issued a statement disclosing the global network disruption. The Iranian-linked group Handala claimed responsibility for the attack on 11 March 2026.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Dahua - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: On 28 February 2026, Iranian threat actors compromised IP cameras manufactured by Hikvision and Dahua, in countries including Israel, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, the UAE, Cyprus, and Lebanon. The research suggested that Iran leverages camera compromise for operational support and battle damage assessment related to missile launches. The hacking activity was observed before and after the US-Israel attacks, with similar targeting patterns seen during the 12-day war between Israel and Iran in June 2025. The attackers exploited critical vulnerabilities in the software of the targeted cameras, using popular VPN services and Virtual Private Servers (VPS) to hide their identities. Check Point Research reported the attack on 4 March 2026.

On 12 March 2026, the municipality of Epe was breached via a phishing attack, resulting in the leak of approximately 800 gigabytes of data. Around 600,000 files of various sizes were comprimised, including personal data such as names and addresses. The attackers targeted the municipality's internal network drive. The municipality reported the incident to the Dutch Data Protection Authority and informed the public about the data leak through their website and the press on 14 March 2026.

On 1 March 2026, China-linked threat actors, including Camaro Dragon group,  targeted unspecified entities in Qatar with malware disguised as Middle East conflict news. The attackers used tools like PlugX and Cobalt Strike to target the Gulf's energy industry and military targets amid rising regional tensions. They sent out files disguised as photos and news articles, which, when opened, contacted a hacked server to pull down more data and used DLL hijacking to secretly run the PlugX backdoor. The malware allowed hackers to steal files, record keystrokes, and take screenshots. The group also targeted Qatar's vital oil and gas industries using a password-protected file named 'Strike at Gulf oil and gas facilities.zip', which delivered a new loader program written in Rust, hiding its malicious code inside a component of NVDA, a legitimate open-source screen reader for the blind. Check Point Research detected and reported the incident, revealing that these hackers began their operations on 1 March 2026.
Techniques Used: Exploit Public-Facing Application, Phishing, Replication Through Removable Media

Description: On 9 March 2026, unknown threat actors launched a ransomware attack on the Community College of Beaver County, encrypting campus data and demanding a ransom. The attack, described as an encryption-based cryptolocker attack, cut off access to crucial systems, including grades, transcripts, and financial records. The college worked with outside specialists and their insurance company to manage the fallout, but it was unclear if any personal data had been taken. The attack was reported on 9 March 2026.

On 17 February 2026, unknown Chinese threat actors breached the Federal Bureau of Investigation's (FBI) networks. The affected system contain sensitive data related to court-authorized wiretaps, pen registers, and FISA warrants, along with personal information on active FBI targets. The hackers exploited the infrastructure of a commercial internet service provider used by the FBI and utilised sophisticated techniques to penetrate the federal network. The incident was detected by the FBI and reported to Congress on 8 March 2026. The National Security Agency (NSA) and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) were involved in the investigation. The Wall Street Journal reported that unnamed U.S. investigators believe that the intruders are affiliated with the Chinese government. On 1 April 2026, Politico reported that the FBI hack is considered as a "major incident" and it is believed hackers successfully compromised a huge amount of sensitive data stored directly on FBI systems.

In January 2026, a threat actor, attributed with moderate confidence to North Korea, targeted multiple cryptocurrency companies, from staking platforms, to exchange software providers, to the exchanges themselves, and stole propriety source code with hardcoded credentials, as reported by Ctrl-Alt-Intel on 2 March 2026. The attackers used stolen AWS credentials and React2Shell vulnerability (CVE-2025-55182) for initial access and stole backend programs, confidential information, and exchange software from companies providing 'staking' services for virtual currencies. They also accessed internal systems using obtained authentication information for cloud services, such as AWS, and collected high-value information, including database connection information and API keys. The attackers used a server based in South Korea and a Korean VPN service to camouflage their tracks.

On 19 November 2024, TriZetto Provider Solutions, an American healthcare technology company owned by Cognizant, was breached, affecting over 3.4 million individuals, with exposed data including insurance and medical information, such as names, addresses, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, health insurance member numbers, and other demographic, health, and health insurance information. The breach was discovered after suspicious activity was detected in a web portal used by some of its healthcare provider customers on 2 October 2025. The incident was disclosed by TriZetto Provider Solutions in a filing with Maine’s attorney general on 6 February 2026.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: In late 2025, APT36, a Pakistani threat group also known as Transparent Tribe, unleashed an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted malware propagation campaign, targeting Indian government entities, diplomatic missions, and defence-related organisations in South Asia. The group used AI-powered development tools to generate large volumes of mediocre-quality malware variants, written in various programming languages. The threat actors leveraged trusted cloud services, including Slack, Discord, Supabase, and Google Sheets, for command and control to make detection more difficult. The campaign was made public by Bitdefender researchers on 5 March 2026. Malware samples were identified between late December 2025 and late January 2026. Bitdefender assess with medium confidence that the observed malicious activity is linked to APT36, also known as Transparent Tribe.

Title (Company): Arndt Freytag von Loringhoven - Not available - Not available
Description: In early 2026, Russian state hackers infiltrated WhatsApp and Signal groups containing Dutch officials and military personnel by posing as the Signal Support chatbot and using the 'linked devices' function to gain access to sensitive information. The attackers likely targeted journalists and other individuals of interest to the Russian government, in addition to Dutch public servants and military personnel. The attack was conducted solely through social engineering. The Netherlands General Intelligence and Security Service (AIVD) and the Military Intelligence and Security Service (MIVD) confirmed the attack in a joint statement on 9 March 2026 and said that the Russian hackers likely gained access to sensitive information through this campaign. On 12 March 2026, the German media The Spiegel reported that the former BND VP Arndt Freytag von Loringhoven was among the victims. On 20 March, the French Cyber Crisis Coordination Center (C4) published a warning note stating they have observed a resurgence in attack campaigns targeting the instant messaging accounts of political figures, high-ranking officials, and government executives. Sectors with a strong government presence are specifically targeted. In their note, C4 directly referenced the publication by Dutch intelligence services as a credible source and stressed the connection to Russian state-sponsored hackers.

Unknown threat actors deployed ransomware against Foster City, California on 19 March 2026, halting most municipal services after staff discovered the malware on city networks in the early hours. Emergency services, including 911 and police dispatch, remained functional. The Foster City Police Department's business phone lines were temporarily down and a Planning Commission meeting was cancelled. The city disclosed the incident in a statement on their website on the same day.

Unknown perpetrators breached the networks of Lucas County, Ohio in mid-March 2026, disrupting key public-facing portals including the auditor's real estate system. The incident impacted several county applications such as the AREIS property search and dog licensing portal. County officials confirmed the incident and took some systems offline after learning of the breach. Multiple services were down from 15 March 2026 until at least 17 March 2026.

In April 2026, home security firm ADT confirmed a data breach by ShinyHunters, which listed the company on its website as part of a "pay or leak" extortion attempt. The breach impacted 5.5M unique email addresses along with names, phone numbers and physical addresses. ADT also advised that "in a small percentage of cases, dates of birth and the last four digits of Social Security numbers or Tax IDs were included" and that it had contacted all affected people.

In April 2026, the hacking group ShinyHunters claimed they had breached Amtrak. The group typically compromises organisations' Salesforce instances before demanding a ransom and later, if not paid, dumping the data publicly. They subsequently published the alleged data which contained over 2M unique email addresses along with names, physical addresses and customer support records.

In April 2026, the notorious hacking collective ShinyHunters claimed they had obtained a substantial volume of data belonging to the Carnival cruise operator and attempted to extort the organisation to prevent the data from being leaked. The following week, the group published the data publicly, which contained 8.7M records with 7.5M unique email addresses. The data contained fields indicating it related to the Mariner Society loyalty program run by Holland America, a cruise line brand under Carnival, and included names, dates of birth, genders and data relating to status within the loyalty program. Carnival acknowledged a phishing incident involving a single user account and advised they were working to better understand the scope of the unauthorised activity.

In March 2026, the anime streaming service Crunchyroll suffered a data breach alleged to have impacted 6.8M users. The exposed data is reported to have originated from the company's Zendesk support system where "name, login name, email address, IP address, general geographic location and the contents of the support tickets" were exposed. A subset of 1.2M email addresses from an alleged 2M record dataset being sold was later provided to HIBP.

In March 2026, Hallmark suffered an alleged breach and subsequent extortion after attackers gained access to data stored within Salesforce. The data was later published after the extortion deadline passed, exposing 1.7M unique email addresses across both Hallmark and the Hallmark+ streaming service, along with names, phone numbers, physical addresses and support tickets.

In April 2026, education company McGraw Hill confirmed a data breach following an extortion attempt. Attributed to a Salesforce misconfiguration, the company stated the incident exposed "a limited set of data from a webpage hosted by Salesforce on its platform". More than 100GB of data was later publicly distributed, containing 13.5M unique email addresses across multiple files, with additional fields such as name, physical address and phone number appearing inconsistently across some records.

In April 2026, the NSFW AI girlfriend platform My Lovely AI suffered a data breach that exposed over 100k users. The data included user-created prompts and links to the resulting AI-generated images, along with a small number of Discord and X usernames.

In April 2026, the hacking collective ShinyHunters claimed to have obtained data from Pitney Bowes as part of a broader extortion campaign that also named several other organisations. After negotiations allegedly failed, the group publicly released the data which included 8.2M unique email addresses, along with names, phone numbers and physical addresses. A subset of the data also included Pitney Bowes employee records with job titles.

In April 2026, the music trivia platform SongTrivia2 suffered a data breach that was subsequently published to a public hacking forum. The data contained a total of 291k unique email addresses sourced from either Google OAuth logins or accounts created on the site, the latter also containing bcrypt password hashes. The data also included names, usernames and avatars.

In March 2026, the personal development and achievement media brand SUCCESS suffered a data breach. The incident exposed 250k unique email addresses along with names, IP addresses, phone numbers and, for a limited number of staff members, bcrypt password hashes. The data also included orders containing physical addresses and the payment method used. In SUCCESS' disclosure notice, they advised their system had also been abused to send offensive newsletters with quotes falsely attributed to contributors.

In April 2026, online training company Udemy was the victim of a “pay or leak” extortion attempt perpetrated by the ShinyHunters group. The data was subsequently leaked publicly and contained 1.4M unique email addresses belonging to customers and instructors. The data also included names, physical addresses, phone numbers, employer information and instructor payout methods including PayPal, cheque and bank transfer.

North Korean state-sponsored group BlueNoroff aka APT38, a sub-group of the Lazarus Group, breached the devices of Cryptocurrency and Web3 executives through fake video conferences on Zoom and Microsoft Teams between January and March 2026. The attackers took over Telegram accounts of well-known people in the crypto industry and used old chat logs to appear trustworthy, before inviting victims to meetings via manipulated Calendly links. During these meetings, the attackers played pre-recorded videos of the compromised individual, before claiming technical issues and convincing the victim to download files containing Remote Access Trojans (RATs). This gave them full access to the computer and allowed the attackers to empty crypto wallets and steal sensitive data. The incident was reported in a technical brief by ArticWolf on 27 April 2026.

The hacking group Payload Ransomware encrypted the systems of the Rural Municipality of Gimli forcing the municipality to hire a security firm on 28 April 2026. The attack was reported by Ransomware.live and resulted in the cancellation of the Rural Municipality's council meeting and the inability to process bill payments at its office. The Winnipeg Free Press reported on the incident on 29 April 2026.

Unknown threat actors carried out a ransomware attack on Adams County, Mississippi on 17 April 2026. The attack disrupting online business for over a week, affecting records access and non-cash payments. The disruption locked county workers out of their systems, unable to access digital civil and circuit court records and accept non-cash payments. The attacker appeared to have entered through a sanitation department computer running an outdated vulnerable operating system, Windows 7. The county sent out a countywide alert on 20 April 2026 to alert residents to the outage of local government services. The Board of Supervisors approved emergency IT work to overhaul the county network and provide around-the-clock network monitoring, totaling an overall cost of around US$250,000.

An unknown threat actor compromised Itron, a Washington-based public company that provides utility technology products and services for energy and water resources management, in April 2026. On 13 April, the company was notified that an unauthorized third party had gained access to certain parts of its system. The incident was made public in a FORM 8-K report on the same day. Itron said that it took action to remediate and remove the unauthorized activity and has not observed any subsequent unauthorized activity within its corporate system.

Title (Company): Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare
Description: A group of hackers using the pseudonyms Izanagi, Gordonfreeman and Cantpwn stole data from the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare's Tu Empleo portal, which was later put up for sale on internet forums on 26 April 2026. The stolen data encompasses 2,000 records, including sensitive data such as ID numbers, addresses, phone numbers, and users CVs. Guatemalan President stated that the theft occurred through an old programming code (API), which has already been removed. The hackers claimed responsibility for the cyberattack and requested a payment of two Bitcoins to cease further attacks on the State. The theft was reported by the ministry on the night of 26 April 2026, reporting that investigations and technical adjustments to its systems are ongoing.

An unknown threat actor built AI-automated exploitation framework Bissa Scanner and leveraged React2Shell vulnerability to compromise over 900 victims in multiple countries in early 2026. On 22 April 2026, researchers published a report on an AI-assisted exploitation platform Bissa Scanner, which used Claude Code and OpenClaw to support mass scanning, exploitation, and credential harvesting. The focus of the operation was the exploitation of React2Shell (CVE-2025-55182), resulting in the scanning of millions of targets, over 900 confirmed compromises, and the collection of tens of thousands of exposed environment files. The researchers highlight three different victims: A mid-sized tax resolution and financial advisory firm, a large digital-asset, payments, and enterprise finance company, and a mid-sized payroll, HR, and stablecoin payments platform.

An unknown threat actor breached the systems of Hutt City Council in New Zealand using phishing emails in March 2026. This exposed the identity of five people and financial information of 732 people to the threat actor. The council confirmed the incident and reported the incident to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner and informed all those affected, who were contacted and notified of the steps to be taken in response. RNZ reported the attack on 29 April 2026.

PhantomCore exploited TrueConf video conferencing software vulnerabilities to breach the networks of Russian organizations since September 2025. The group leveraged an exploit chain comprising three vulnerabilities (BDU-2025-10114, BDU-2025-10115, and BDU-2025-10116) to execute commands remotely on susceptible servers. The attackers used various tools, including PhantomPxPigeon, PhantomSscp, MacTunnelRat, and PhantomProxyLite, to establish a foothold in the breached environment, conduct reconnaissance, and harvest credentials. The attackers, primarily aimed at the internal processes of a compromised organization and stay in the victim’s infrastructure for a long time, gradually expanding their presence on the network. In some cases, the attackers carried out encryption of both virtual machines and physical servers, as well as workstations of ordinary users. The group targeted public and private organizations of a wide range of industries in Russia, and their attack chains also used phishing lures for initial access. The activities were made public by researchers from the Russian security company Positive Technologies on 20 April 2026.

A threat actor calling themselves KikoRivera, breached the Andalusian Public Ports Agency (APPA), a part of the Andalusian Regional Government in Spain, by using a Remote Code Execution (RCE) in April 2026. The threat actors gained remote access to the system and extracted 18.8 GB of critical data, including seven complete databases, source code, 2,600 records of personal data and encryption keys. The incident was detected on 26 April 2026 and was reported to the National Police. The Andalusian Digital Agency (ADA) was also informed to apply relevant protocols. A complaint was filed and mandatory communication was made to the Data Protection Agency. The incident was made public by Antonio Delgado, Global Head of Cybersecurity at Affinitas Education, on his LinkedIn profile.

Unknown threat actors compromised the website of Sir David Davis, Conservative MP for Goole and Pocklington, inserting links redirecting users to Southeast Asian gambling pages on 23 April 2026. After the website was restored, it was subjected to a DDoS attack comprising 142 million requests and consuming nearly 800 GB of data within 24 hours. Sir David Davis stated that much of the suspicious activity was traceable to China. The incident was disclosed by Sir David Davis in the House of Commons. Deputy Speaker Nus Ghani addressed MPs on the matter, advising members to contact the Parliamentary Security Department (PSD) for security advice.

Unknown threat actors stole US$2.5 million from the Sri Lankan Finance Ministry in January 2026 by intercepting emails related to debt transactions between the Government of Sri Lanka and Australia. A payment owed to Australia disappeared after hackers broke into the ministry's email server. Four senior officers at the Public Debt Management Office (PDMO) were suspended following the breach. The Sri Lankan government disclosed the incident on 23 April 2026 and was seeking assistance from foreign law enforcement agencies. Australia's High Commissioner in Sri Lanka, Matthew Duckworth, confirmed that Australian officials were assisting the investigation.

ShinyHunters ransomware group breached medical device company Medtronic in the United States in April 2026. The hackers accessed data in certain corporate IT systems, claiming to have stolen over 9 million records containing personally identifiable information and internal corporate data. Medtronic disclosed the incident on its website on 24 April 2026, stating that the breach did not impact customers or products and that business operations remained unaffected. ShinyHunters listed Medtronic on its leak site on 18 April 2026 and threatened to release the stolen data unless the company engaged in negotiations for a ransom payment by 21 April 2026. After the date, Medtronic disappeared from the leak site without further comments.

The hacker group LAPSUS$ claimed responsibility for an alleged data breach involving AstraZeneca, a multinational pharmaceutical and biotechnology company in March 2026. The group alleged that they had obtained approximately 3GB of internal data, including source code, cloud infrastructure configurations, employee-related information including secrets and access credentials and cloud infrastructure configurations. The hackers attempted to sell the data.

On 23 April 2026, a group of hackers calling themselves "True Muslim Afghans" breached the Indian media network OneIndia, broadcasting a political message that denounced the current Interim Afghan Government and the Taliban's shifting policies. The hackers utilized the compromised broadcast channels to display the Afghan flag and condemn the growing proximity between the Taliban and the Indian establishment.

Unknown threat actors breached Banco Rendimento, a foreign exchange, credit and payments institution based in São Paulo, on 21 April 2026. The bank's information security team identified the incident on the morning of 21 April 2026 and contained the operation at an early stage. The attack affected some client access channels and some accounts. Banco Rendimento officially disclosed the incident in a formal note to the market on 22 April 2026.

Title (Company): Julia Klöckner - President of the German Bundestag
Description: Unattributed threat actors compromised the signal account of Germany’s Bundestag President Julia Klöckner through a Signal-based phishing campaign in April 2026. The attack was likely part of a larger phishing-campaign targeting sensitive individuals in security agencies and political positions. German authorities previously stated that the campaign is likely conducted by a state-sponsored group. The incident was reported by Der Spiegel and Politico. Chancellor Friedrich Merz was included in the targeted Signal group chat but was not compromised. Media reports cited unofficial government officials to attribute the attack to Russia. In February 2026, the BSI and BfV have issued a warning concerning phishing attempts via massengers platforms.

Chinese state-linked APT group GopherWhisper infiltrated Mongolian government institution since July. The group used a set of custom backdoors and abused popular cloud-hosted services such as Slack and Discord for command and control (C2). Researchers at ESET discovered the backdoors in 2025 and analysed the communication gaining insight into the group's internal operations and post-compromise activities. ESET'S report was published on 23 April 2026.

The ransomware group Blackwater breached Minidoka Memorial Hospital in Rupert, Idaho, on 5 April, resulting in a cyber incident that temporarily affected certain internal systems and limited imaging services, leading to some emergency patient transfers. The hospital disclosed the incident in a Facebook post and stated that they continue to treat patients. In an update on Facebook, the hospital said that full imaging access was restored by 19 April 2026. The ransomware group Blackwater added Minidoka to a leak site, claiming that they had obtained approximately 2.33 million files of roughly 576 gigabytes.

China-linked group MustangPanda (aka RedDelta/Bronze President/Stately Taurus) targeted the Indian financial sector and political circles in South Korea with an updated LOTUSLITE backdoor, titled LOTUSLITE v1.1 by Acronis researchers, in March 2026. In India, the malware was delivered through spear phishing, sending a file named Request for Support.chm to trick workers in the Indian banking sector by impersonating HDFC, the country’s largest private bank. This file opened a fake popup window, which re-directed users to a server which downloaded and executed a malicious JS File. In South Korea, the threat actor impersonated Victor Cha, a former Director for Asian Affairs on the U.S. National Security Council and current Senior Vice President at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS). The actor sent out Google Drive links to folders named March 30 with fake invitation letters crafted to infect target systems, using DLL sideloading to stay undetected. These files were sent to South Korean and U.S. diplomatic and policy communities, in particular those that deal with Korean relations and security dialogues. The Acronis Threat Research Unit informed the public about the campaign in a technical report on 21 April 2026.

North Korea-linked Lazarus Group is suspected of a $290M crypto theft targeting Kelp DAO, an Indian decentralised finance protocol built on the Ethereum ecosystem on 18 April 2026. The attackers compromised RPC infrastructure provided by Candian cryptocurrency firm LayerZero, forcing systems to rely on compromised nodes, and then issued a malicious command to drain funds. Approximately $293M in cryptocurrency were stolen. Kelp DAO informed the public about the attack on 18 April 2026. LayerZero stated on 20 April 2026 that the attack was likely conducted by Lazarus Group, specifically TraderTraitor.

The ransomware group ShinyHunters breached Amtrak's systems, accessing and releasing at least 2.1 million customer records online in April 2026. In a post dark web post on 11 April 2026, ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for the attack. The exposed dataset contained personal details, including names, email addresses, physical addresses, and customer service records, such as support tickets and potentially travel-related details. The breach was added to Have I Been Pwned on 17 April 2026, after data attributed to Amtrak appeared online.

Unknown perpetrators stole assets worth approximately $13.7 million (1 billion roubles) from cryptocurrency exchange platform Grinex on 16 April 2026. Grinex, based in Kyrgyzstan but linked to Russia, was sanctioned by the US, UK and EU in 2025 for allegedly helping customers circumvent sanctions via a Russian rouble-backed stablecoin called A7A5. In a statement on its Telegram channel, the exchange accused "foreign intelligence services of unfriendly states" of being involved, claiming that "the digital footprints and nature of the attack indicate an unprecedented level of resources and technologies available exclusively to entities of unfriendly states." The exchange further claimed the attack was "coordinated with the aim of causing direct harm to Russia's financial sovereignty." Reuters was not able to verify these claims. The exchange suspended operations following the incident.

Title (Company): Unspecified Cryptocurrency and Finance Sector Individuals
Description: North Korea-linked threat actor Sapphire Sleet (aka APT38/Trader Traitor) conducted a macOS-focused campaign to steal cryptocurrency assets since at least 2025. The attackers used social engineering, impersonating legitimate software updates to trick users into manually running malicious AppleScript files, bypassing macOS security protections. The campaign targeted individuals and organisations involved in cryptocurrency, digital assets and finance. Microsoft Threat Intelligence published its findings on 16 April 2026 and shared details with Apple, which implemented updates to detect and block associated infrastructure and malware.

An unknown threat actor breached a marine fuel procurement system used by the shipping and trading company NYK Group in March 2026, potentially exfiltrating certain data, including personal information of NYK Group employees and employees of their business partners, such as names, company names, telephone numbers, and email addresses. The NYK Group detected the unauthorized access on 24 March 2026, immediately isolated the system, and suspended its use. The system was restored on 27 March 2026. The NYK Group reported the incident to the Personal Information Protection Commission of Japan and other relevant authorities on 27 March 2026, and to the Japanese police on 31 March 2026. The incident was publicly disclosed by the NYK Group on 15 April 2026, through a publication on their website.

Unidentified threat actors compromised the Franziskusschule, a secondary school in Wilhelmshaven, Germany, in April 2026. The Catholic school operator Offizialat Vechta confirmed the incident and reported it to police on 11 April 2026. The school network "IServ" was rendered inaccessible. According to the operator, no data breach was detected and no lasting damage was anticipated. School operations continued unaffected.

In November 2025, Southern Illinois Dermatology, a healthcare provider in the USA, suffered a ransomware attack. The investigation confirmed unauthorized access to parts of its network. The affected data contained personal information and protected health information, including full names, addresses, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, telephone numbers, email addresses, person numbers, and medical record numbers. Southern Illinois Dermtology informed the public about the incident on 2 April 2026. The ransomware group Insomnia claimed responsibility for the incident on 28 November 2025.

Unknown threat actors breached Bitcoin Depot, the largest US Bitcoin ATM operator on 23 March 2026, by stealing login credentials, which enabled them to drain approximately 50.9 BTC, worth $3.6M, from company wallets. The unauthorized actor gained access to Bitcoin Depot's systems and obtained control of credentials associated with the company's digital asset settlement accounts. Bitcoin Depot discovered the breach on 23 March 2026 and promptly activated its incident response protocols, engaged external cybersecurity experts, and notified law enforcement. The company believed the incident was contained to its corporate environment and did not affect customer platforms, systems or data. The incident was made public in a Form 8-K report with SEC on 6 April, and the company was continuing to investigate the security breach with the help of external cybersecurity experts.

Unknown perpetrators gained access to some systems of Spring Lake Park Schools, a district in Minnesota, on 12 April 2026. The district's technology team confirmed the breach and staff shut down all systems to prevent further access. As a result, classes were cancelled on 13 April 2026, along with child care, community education programs, and after-school activities. The district worked with third-party cybersecurity experts and law enforcement to restore essential systems. The incident was reported by the district in a notice to families on 12 April 2026.

DragonForce ransomware breached Dutch waste management company Saver on 9 April 2026. Some data became inaccessible, and the company preventatively shut down some of its systems, causing an inability to respond to phone calls. Furthermore, the attack caused disruption in the company's pest control operations. On 25 May 2026, Hackmanac claimed responsibility for the incident.

Unknown perpetrators compromised part of the technological infrastructure of the Colombian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, causing intermittencies in information services, including the SITAC platform responsible for issuing passports. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, with the support and coordination of Colombia's Cyber Emergency Response Group (ColCERT), informed the public about the incident on 8 April 2026.

Iran-affiliated APT actors exploited internet-facing operational technology devices in April 2026, including programmable logic controllers (PLCs) manufactured by Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley. This activity has led to PLC disruptions across several U.S. critical infrastructure sectors through malicious interactions with the project file and manipulation of data on human machine interface and supervisory control and data acquisition displays, resulting in operational disruption and financial loss. On 7 April 2026, CISA published a cybersecurity advisory warning of these activities. On 22 April 2026, CISA updated the cybersecurity advisory expanding the manufacturer scope to include observed targeting of Schneider Electric, Siemens and possible other PLC manufacturers.

A hacker calling himself "FlamingChina" allegedly breached the National Supercomputing Center (NSCC) in Tianjin, China, in February 2026, exfiltrating approximately 10 petabytes of internal data including classified information. The data leak was announced on a dark web forum and Telegram, with samples offered for sale. Leaked documents reportedly included PDF reports, handbooks, radar test data, physics simulations, renderings of weapon systems and virtual target simulations, as well as documents labelled as classified, including a 2025 testing report for bunker buster ammunition. A SentinelOne consultant who reviewed the samples assessed the leaked data appeared to be genuine.

Anubis ransomware gang claimed to have hacked Western Australia-based charter service provider Shine Aviation on 4 April 2026, exfiltrating 57 GB of data, totalling more than 68,000 files, including employee credentials, records, and access cards, as well as aircraft registration certificates. The leaked data included a wide range of information, from details about aircraft and flights to access credentials for network infrastructure and various corporate systems used by the company. Anubis shared several documents to prove its claim, including scans of employee security cards, login credentials, and more in its leak post.

The ransomware group World Leaks breached a third-party discovery system used by the Los Angeles City Attorney's Office on 20 March 2026, compromising 7.7 terabytes of sensitive police records tied to the Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD), including internal affairs investigations, unredacted criminal complaints, witness identities, and officers' medical information. The breach, which was noticed by the City Attorney's Office on 20 March 2026, resulted in the exposure of roughly 337,000 files. The hackers posted the leaked data on Distributed Denial of Secrets, a website of a transparency group. The LAPD confirmed the breach in a statement, noting that it did not involve LAPD systems or networks, but rather a digital storage system belonging to the Los Angeles City Attorney's Office.

Unknown threat actors breached one of CareCloud's six electronic health record environments on 16 March 2026, temporarily accessing part of the company's data and partially disrupting functionality for approximately eight hours. The affected system stored patient information, though the extent of patient data exposure remains under assessment. CareCloud's other data environments were not affected, and the affected system was restored the same evening. The company disclosed the incident in an SEC filing on 27 March 2026, noting it had notified its insurer, hired external technical support and informed law enforcement.

Title (Company): Government Institutions (Ukraine, Poland, Romania, Slovakia) - Unspecified Defence Supply Chain Entities (Ukraine, Poland, Romania, Slovakia) - Transport and Aid Networks (Ukraine, Poland, Romania, Slovakia) - Military Units (Ukraine, Poland, Romania, Slovakia) - Unspecified Critical Infrastructure (Ukraine, Poland, Romania, Slovakia)
Description: Russia-linked group APT28 (aka Fancy Bear / Pawn Storm) deployed the PRISMEX malware suite against government institutions, military units and critical infrastructure in Ukraine and allied countries including Poland, Romania and Slovakia since September 2025. The threat actors exploited CVE-2026-21509 and CVE-2026-21513 as zero-days via spearphishing emails themed around military training, weather alerts and weapon smuggling. The attack chain triggered exploitation of CVE-2026-21509, forcing systems to connect to attacker-controlled WebDAV servers and execute malicious LNK files. The PRISMEX malware suite included PrismexSheet, PrismexDrop, PrismexLoader and PrismexStager, employing steganography, COM hijacking and abuse of cloud service Filen.io for command and control. Decoy documents included Ukrainian drone inventories, supplier price lists and military logistics forms. Trend Micro attributed the activity to APT28 with high confidence, noting the campaign reflects a shift toward tactical disruption of Ukraine's supply chain and NATO-linked logistics rather than pure espionage, publishing its findings on 26 March 2026.
Techniques Used: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol, Drive-by Compromise, Phishing

Title (Company): Cabinet of Ministers - Provincial security forces of Misiones - Provincial security forces of Entre Rios - Ministry of Education - Central Bank of the Republic of Argentina (BCRA) - Ministry of Health - National Agency for Disability (ANDIS) - Police of Santiago del Estero - Provincial security forces of Tucuman - Provincial security forces of Cordoba - Provincial security forces of Santiago del Estero
Description: Hacktivist group Chronus Team breached over 30 public and private organisations in Argentina in March 2026. Affected institutions included the National Agency for Disability, the Central Bank of the Republic of Argentina, the Chief of the Cabinet of Ministers, the Ministry of Health, the Ministry of Education, the Federal System for Security Measures and the Institute for Medical Assistance Work. The attack also affected provincial police forces in Córdoba, Entre Ríos, Misiones, Tucumán and Santiago del Estero. Users identified as "adrxx", "L0stex" and "Lizard", alleged members of Chronus Team, claimed responsibility for the attack which resulted in the exfiltration of significant amounts of sensitive data. El Liberal reported the attack on 8 April 2026.

China-linked UNC2814 breached Instituto Costarricense de Electricidad (ICE), a state-owned electricity and telecommunications provider in Costa Rica, on 12 March 2026. The attackers sought to extract information related to contracts made by the institution. Preliminary analysis indicated that the malware used was of Asian origin. The Costa Rican government stated that the extent of the damage and the amount of data stolen remain unknown. The incident is under investigation. The Tico Times reported the incident on 12 March 2026, stating that the Government of Costa Rica has attributed the incident to a threat actor with possible ties to China during a press conference. On 13 March 2026, the Chinese Ambassador Wang Xiaoyao responded to these allegations by asking the government of Cosa Rica to provide evidence to the accusations.

Unknown threat actors deployed ransomware against ChipSoft, a Dutch healthcare software provider that manages patient files for approximately 70 percent of Dutch hospitals, on 7 April 2026. Z-CERT, the Dutch centre of expertise for digital security in healthcare, informed affected institutions in a confidential message on the same day. Various hospitals, including Rijnstate Hospital in Arnhem, Antoni van Leeuwenhoek Hospital in Amsterdam and Franciscus Hospital in Rotterdam, reported no disruption to operations and no compromise of patient data, though later in April 2026 it was clarified that patient data had been extracted but was destroyed. ChipSoft confirmed the incident and took measures to limit the adverse consequences. NOS and NL Times reported the attack on 8 April 2026.

Title (Company): Not available - Unspecified Businesses - Unspecified Private Households - Not available
Description: Russia-linked group APT28 compromised internet routers of private homes and businesses in the United Kingdom and United States between 2024 and 2026. The threat actors rerouted internet traffic through servers under their control, intercepting sensitive data including passwords and access tokens from email and web services. The attackers employed DNS hijacking to redirect users to fraudulent websites designed to harvest login credentials. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) described the campaign as opportunistic, with the attackers initially targeting large numbers of devices before narrowing their focus to individuals or organisations of intelligence interest. The NCSC disclosed the campaign in a technical report on 7 April 2026. The US Department of Justice announced on the same day that they neutralized the U.S. portion of a network in a court-authorized technical operation.

On 6 April 2026, unknown threat actors breached Winona County, Minnesota, disrupting county systems and impairing emergency and municipal services. The Governor signed an executive order authorizing the Minnesota National Guard to assist with the response. The incident was reported to the public on 7 April 2026 through the executive order. In late August 2026, Winona County officials confirmed they negotiated and paid a $128,539.57 ransom.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Since 2023, the China-based group Storm-1175 has exploited zero-day and n-day vulnerabilities in high-velocity attacks to deploy Medusa ransomware payloads, targeting the healthcare, education, professional services, and finance sectors in Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States. The group exploited at least 17 vulnerabilities (CVE-202510035, CVE-202623760, CVE-2026-1731, CVE-2023-21529, CVE-2023-27351, CVE-2023-27350, CVE-2023-46805, CVE-2024-21887, CVE-2024-1709, CVE-2024-1708, CVE-2024-27198, CVE-2024-27199, CVE-2024-57726, CVE-2024-57727, CVE-2024-57728, CVE 2025 31161, CVE-2025-52691) to gain access to victims' networks. Microsoft reported the attacks on 6 April 2026.

Unknown hackers breached the Hospital Authority of Hong Kong and leaked sensitive information affecting approximately 200,000 patient records on 3 April 2026. The compromised data included Hong Kong Identity Card numbers, full names, genders, dates of birth and patient identifiers. The unattributed threat actor claimed responsibility and shared sample content on a dark web forum. The Hospital Authority confirmed a suspected case of patient data theft and leakage on 4 April 2026.

Unidentified perpetrators targeted Signature Healthcare, a hospital provider in Brockton, Massachusetts, US, on 6 April 2026. Signature Healthcare detected the incident, shut down its systems and issued a public notice outlining the service disruptions on the same day. Services were restored by 24 April 2026.

North Korean threat actor UNC4736 likely stole approximately $285 million in cryptocurrency from Drift, a US-based cryptocurrency trading platform, on 1 April 2026. According to the company, the threat actors targeted Drift employees at an in-person crypto conference in autumn 2025, posing as a potential business partner with a verifiable background. After onboarding on Drift's ecosystem and depositing over $1 million, the threat actor built an operating presence in the system and sent links infected with malware. Drift engaged Mandiant to investigate the incident. Mandiant attributed the attack to North Korean state-affiliated UNC4736 (also tracked as AppleJeus and Citrine Sleet) on 5 April 2026.

Unknown threat actors compromised Gritman Medical Center, a health system in Moscow, Idaho, US, on or around 1 April 2026, resulting in the closure of several primary and specialty clinics. The hospital and emergency department remained open throughout. Gritman Medical Center publicly disclosed the incident on 2 April 2026 via Facebook. Electronic systems were coming back online by 5 April 2026. Preliminary findings indicated no successful access to electronic systems and no compromise of patient or secure data.

Iran-linked Handala claimed responsibility for a breach of PSK Wind Technologies, an Israeli defence contractor specialising in integrated systems for defence and critical communications, on 2 April 2026. Handala claimed to have stolen sensitive data including documents on command and control systems and allegedly sent it to Axis of Resistance missile units. The group released confidential files including communications systems documentation, internal documents and location photos. The attack was announced on 2 April 2026, coinciding with the Jewish holiday of Passover.

Unidentified perpetrators deployed ransomware against the water treatment plant of Minot, North Dakota, US on 14 March 2026, forcing staff to switch to manual operations for approximately 16 hours after a server was compromised. The compromised server was unplugged after a ransomware message was discovered, while operations continued. The attack was disclosed in a letter from the City Manager to the City Council on 31 March 2026.

North Korean threat actor UNC1069 compromised the widely used open-source software Axios by inserting malicious code into a software update on 31 March 2026. The attackers likely attempted to exfiltrate data from downstream entities. Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) reported the incident and attributed it to UNC1069, a North Korean threat actor with financial motives. The malicious software was removed on the same day. CISA and Singapore's Cyber Security Agency (CSA) both issued warnings in response to the npm compromise.

Title (Company): Pepperell Fire Department - Pepperell Police Department - Groton Police Department - Patriot Regional Emergency Communications Center
Description: Unknown threat actors breached systems of the police, fire department and Patriots Regional Emergency Communications Center in Pepperell, Massachusetts on 31 March 2026, affecting nearby communities including Ashby and Townsend. Reports suggest that data was compromised and that non-emergency phone lines were disrupted. The incident was disclosed by Pepperell officials.

DragonForce deployed ransomware against Fernheizwerk Neukölln AG, a district heating provider in Berlin, Germany, on 20 March 2026. The attackers reportedly exfiltrated data and issued a ransom demand with a payment deadline of 29 March 2026. The operators declined to meet the attackers' demands. Despite the compromise, heating operations continued without disruption. The full extent of the data breach remains unclear. German authorities have been informed and investigations are ongoing. German media outlets "Die Welt" and "Berliner Morgenpost" suggest that DragonForce is responsible for the attack.

Iran-linked Handala claimed responsibility for a breach of the exile media outlet IranWire on 31 March 2026. According to the Iranian judiciary, large amounts of data were obtained, including correspondence, lists of employees and informants, as well as highly confidential information. Handala published selected materials as proof of the breach. The FBI assesses Handala is operated by Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS).

Qilin ransomware group launched ransomware attack on Maine mental health agency AMHC, the largest behavioural healthcare provider in rural Maine with over 350 employees and 5,500 clients, in March 2026. Qilin added AMHC to its list of victims on its dark web data leak site on or around 24 March 2026. The attack was confirmed in a statement to Bangor Daily News on 25 March 2026, stating that it had recently experienced a network disruption and was investigating the incident with cyber incident specialists. The investigative report, published on 7 April 2026, stated that sensitive data was stolen and found that Qilin had obtained unauthorised access between 11 and 12 March 2026.

On or before 10 March 2026, Iran-linked Homeland Justice group carried out a cyberattack on the digital infrastructure of Albania's parliament. The attackers claimed to have gained access to the correspondences the whole Parliament and later leaked emails belonging to four MPs and also deleted materials from the servers, while the breach caused the parliament's IT team to suspend access to internal email services. Local media reports that the attackers claimed responsibility on 10 March 2026, though they likely gained access much earlier.

An individual hacker dubbed "Breach3d" compromised France's National Agency for Secure Documents (ANTS) website on 15 April 2026, and possibly exposed personal data from users applying for IDs, passports, and drivers licences. The Interior Ministry confirmed the breach in a statement on their website on 20 April 2026, and was investigating the scope and impact on affected users. The security breach may have exposed user details such as login ID, name, email, date of birth, and account ID, as well as address, place of birth or phone number in some cases. Authorities notified impacted users and reported the incident to the French Data Protection Authority, notified prosecutors, and alerted the national cybersecurity agency. On 16 April 2026, the threat actor claimed to be selling a large dataset stolen from ANTS, which included around 18-19 million records with names, emails, phone numbers, birth details, addresses and account metadata in a breach forum. In late April, French authorities arrested a 15-year-old nicknamed "breach3d" for allegedly carrying out the attack.

Unknown threat actors breached the City of Tallahassee, Florida, on 17 April 2026, affecting parts of the city's technology environment and knocking the city website offline. Officials immediately disconnected impacted systems and isolated the threat. The city reported no operational impacts at the time, although periodic downtime was possible during maintenance. The city confirmed the cyberattack on 17 April 2026 but did not disclose whether ransomware was involved or if any data was taken.

Title (Company): Unspecified Hosting Providers - Unspecified Internet Service Providers
Description: China-linked group Salt Typhoon (aka Ghost Emperor / RedMike) targeted smaller internet service and hosting providers in the Netherlands, gaining access to routers but not penetrating further into internal networks. The Dutch Military Intelligence and Security Service (MIVD) and General Intelligence and Security Service (AIVD) conducted an investigation, corroborating some findings of a US investigation with independent intelligence. The Dutch agencies endorsed warnings issued by the NSA, CISA and FBI, along with European intelligence agencies BND (Germany), SUPO (Finland), NCSC (UK) and AISE (Italy). The MIVD and AIVD warned that Chinese cyber activities had become increasingly sophisticated, posing a major challenge to Dutch resilience. The attack was publicly disclosed on 28 August 2025.

The Russian ransomware group REvil disrupted the servers of Brazilian meat processing company JBS S. A. in North America and Australia on 30 May 2021, JBS USA announced in a statement the day after. Media reports noted that the cyber incident disrupted JBS's meat processing facilities in the United States, Canada, and Australia.  On 2 June 2021, the FBI attributed the ransomware attack to the REvil ransomware group (also known as Sodinokibi). White House Deputy Press Secretary Karine Jean-Pierre had announced one day earlier that the White House believed the perpetrators were a criminal organization in Russia. On 3 June, JBS released a statement declaring that in the US the impact of the disruption had been limited to one day's equivalent of meat production. The company expected to return to regular production levels at the end of the following week. On 9 June, JBS USA issued a follow-on press release admitting to paying $11 million in ransom to the ransomware group. JBS USA CEO Andre Nogueira explained this step with efforts to prevent potential risks to customers..  In response, the chairwoman of the House Oversight and Reform Committee, Carolyn Maloney (D-N.Y.), sent a letter to Andre Nogueira one day later demanding all documents related to the decision to pay the ransom. In the letter, Maloney also expressed her disapproval of JBS USA's decision to pay the ransom.  On 9 July 2021, US President Joe Biden reported to have demanded in a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin that he "take action" against cybercriminals in his country and that the United States reserved its right to "defend its own people and it's critical infrastructure".  Soon after, on 13 July 2021, the websites and other infrastructure of REvil went offline and group's spokesperson, going by the monicker 'unknown', disappeared. Media reports later revealed that a foreign partner of the US government had compromised REvil infrastructure. Following a brief period in hiding, the group sought to relaunch in September, apparently relying on backups that had previously been infiltrated by the foreign partner. REvil became aware of this compromise when US Cyber Command blocked its website and redirected traffic in October, following to which the group disbanded.
Techniques Used: Content Injection, Drive-by Compromise, Valid Accounts

Title (Company): Unspecified Turkish Private Organisations - Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey (TÜBİTAK) - Unspecified Turkish Government Entities
Description: Iran-linked group MuddyWater (MERCURY, Static Kitten), attributed to Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS) by US Cyber Command, targeted Turkish private organisations and governmental institutions including the Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey (TÜBİTAK) in a campaign operating as recently as November 2021. The threat actors distributed malicious PDFs and Microsoft Office documents masquerading as legitimate documents from the Turkish Health and Interior Ministries, delivering PowerShell-based downloaders as initial footholds.  Cisco Talos attributed the campaign with high confidence to MuddyWater based on technical indicators and TTPs

Title (Company): Unspecified Transportation Sector Organisations - Unspecfied Financial Sector Organisations - Unspecified High-Tech Sector Organisations - Unspecified Global Government Agencies - Unspecified US Defence Industrial Base Companies
Description: China-nexus groups UNC2630 and UNC2717 exploited vulnerabilities in Pulse Secure VPN appliances to compromise dozens of US and EU organisations between August 2020 and March 2021. The threat actors deployed custom malware to maintain long-term access, collect credentials and steal proprietary data.  UNC2630 targeted US defence industrial base companies with malware families including SLOWPULSE, RADIALPULSE, THINBLOOD, ATRIUM, PACEMAKER, SLIGHTPULSE and PULSECHECK. UNC2717 targeted global government agencies using HARDPULSE, QUIETPULSE and PULSEJUMP. FireEye later identified four additional malware strains deployed by UNC2630: BLOODMINE, BLOODBANK, CLEANPULSE and RAPIDPULSE.  Targeted organisations operated in defence, government, high-tech, transportation and financial sectors, aligning with Beijing's strategic objectives outlined in China's 14th Five Year Plan. The threat actors exploited CVE-2021-22893 along with previously disclosed vulnerabilities CVE-2019-11510, CVE-2020-8260 and CVE-2020-8243.  FireEye observed UNC2630 removing webshells from compromised devices between 17 and 20 April 2021, displaying sensitivity to publicity following FireEye's initial reporting. FireEye published the findings on 27 May 2021, and CISA updated its alert with the new TTPs and indicators of compromise.

In April 2026, the ultra-luxury hotel brand Aman was named by ShinyHunters as the target of a "pay or leak" extortion campaign, with the data allegedly obtained from their Salesforce CRM. The data was subsequently leaked publicly and contained over 200k unique email addresses. Whilst not present on all records, the data also included genders, physical addresses, phone numbers, nationalities, dates of birth, spouse names and VIP status codes.

In April 2026, the commercial real estate brokerage firm Marcus & Millichap was named as one of multiple alleged victims of the ShinyHunters hacking and extortion group. Data alleged to have been obtained from the company was subsequently released publicly and included 1.8M unique email addresses, along with names, phone numbers and employment-related information including employer, job title and physical company address. In their disclosure notice, Marcus & Millichap advised that data which may have been accessed appeared limited to "company forms, templates, marketing materials, and general contact information".

In April 2026, the gaming community Reborn Gaming suffered a data breach due to a vulnerability in cPanel and WebHost Manager (WHM). The breach exposed 126 unique email addresses along with IP addresses and Steam IDs. Reborn Gaming self-submitted the data to Have I Been Pwned.

In April 2026, the ShinyHunters extortion group listed Vimeo on their extortion portal as part of their "pay or leak" campaign. They subsequently published hundreds of gigabytes of data, predominantly consisting of video titles, technical data and metadata. The data also included 119k unique email addresses, sometimes accompanied by names. Vimeo attributed the exposure to a breach of Anodot, a third-party analytics vendor, and advised the incident does not include "Vimeo video content, valid user login credentials, or payment card information".

In March 2026, the hacker and extortion group "ShinyHunters" claimed to have obtained a substantial corpus of data from ZenBusiness, a business formation and compliance platform. The group claimed the data had been exfiltrated from platforms including Snowflake, Mixpanel and Salesforce, and threatened to publish it if a ransom was not paid. The following month, after claiming payment had not been made, ShinyHunters publicly released the data. The collection amounted to many terabytes across thousands of files that appeared to originate from multiple systems and business functions, including leads, support records and other CRM-related data. The data contained approximately 5M unique email addresses, often accompanied by name and phone number depending on the source file.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available -  China Railway Society Electrification Committee - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
