Description: An unknown threat actor exploited a critical zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-41940) in the web hosting software cPanel and WebHost Manager (WHM) to target government and military organizations in Southeast Asia, as well as Managed Service Providers (MSPs) and hosting providers in countries including the Philippines, Laos, Canada, South Africa, and the U.S. since May 2026. The attackers used the flaw to bypass authentication checks, granting access to the control panel without valid credentials, and potentially allowing them to manage hosting settings, access sensitive data, or take control of the server. The vulnerability was first disclosed by researchers at watchTowr on 29 April 2026. On 2 May, researchers at Ctrl-Alt-Intel detected attacks exploiting CVE-2026-41940 in Southeast Asia and other regions. Among other things, the researchers found stolen map, technical, organisational, and personal information from a railway electrification ecosystem that is closely linked to China’s state rail infrastructure on an exposed attacker server.

The ransomware group Payload carried out a cyberattack on the B3 school cluster in Bruck an der Mur, Styria, Austria, on 23 April 2026, affecting hundreds of pupils and teachers. The group claimed to have obtained 21 GB of data and threatened to publish sensitive information on the darknet. The Styrian Education Directorate refused to negotiate with the attackers and took swift action to resolve the IT outage, with systems rapidly restored and no lasting damage reported. A report was filed with the data protection authority.

A group of hackers linked to China breached the systems of the Cuban Embassy in Washington in January 2026, accessing internal communications of dozens of officials, including Ambassador Lianys Torres Rivera and Deputy Chief of Mission Alejandro Pila, as reported by cybersecurity firm Gambit Security on 30 April 2026. The intruders bypassed embassy security by exploiting two old vulnerabilities in Microsoft Exchange email servers and compromised the emails of 68 officials.

Unknown threat actors hit Columbia Surgical Partners, a surgery center in Maury County with a ransomware attack in April 2026. The attackers compromised patient medical records and made it difficult to access them. The clinic informed its patients about the attack on 29 April and stated that the clinic was unable to access electronic medical records.
In April 2026, the commercial residential and ISP proxy network LegionProxy suffered a data breach. The incident exposed 10k email addresses, bcrypt password hashes, names and purchases.

In March 2026, the AI-driven merchant data platform Woflow was named as a victim by the ShinyHunters data extortion group. The group subsequently published tens of thousands of files allegedly obtained from the company, comprising more than 2TB of data. The trove included hundreds of thousands of email addresses, names, phone numbers and physical addresses, with the data indicating it related to Woflow customers and, in turn, the customers of merchants using their platform.

Iranian state hacking group Handala (aka Handala Hack Team, Hatef) stole 430.000 documents from Fujairah Port in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) on 4 May 2026. The group stole documents concerning contracts, marine traffic, financial information and maps of the port's oil infrastructure and subsequently leaked them on its website. It also released a statement threatening further attacks if the UAE did not cease its support for the United States and Israel. Handala stated it had shared the stolen maps of oil infrastructure with missile units of what it called the “Resistance Axis”. Shortly after the incident, the port was subject of an air attack, which Handala attributed to the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). According to Al Jazeera, the UAE’s Ministry of Defence stated it had engaged ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as drones launched from Iran on 4 May 2026. The cyber incident was reported by News.Az on 5 May 2026.

An unknown threat actor breached US cybersecurity software vendor Trellix giving them unauthorized access to its source code. The actor exploited software development and security infrastructure to place trojans in updates and extensions, which allowed it to steal access credentials and Trellix’ source code. The company said it had notified law enforcement and was working with forensic experts to investigate the incident in a statement on 4 May 2026.

An unknown threat actor targeted San Diego Miramar College on 4 May 2026. The college's IT team identified and stopped the attack, but users faced intermittent disruptions as systems and websites were restored. The attack affected students, employees, and applicants who relied on campus websites and district portals for email, Canvas, class schedules, registration, and other services.

An unknown threat actor breached the servers of the police of City of Ardmore, Oklahoma, deploying ransomware on 7 April 2026. The actor gained unauthorized access via a phishing email. The city did not pay the $300,000 that the threat actor demanded for not leaking the data. The city informed the public about the attack in a social media post on 29 April 2026. In a media statement,  Chief Information Officer Robert Newell stated that the breach was contained within hours, but personal information including names, addresses, and phone numbers may have been exposed for anyone in the police department's database tracing back five years. The city has since upgraded its security and is continuing its investigation.

In April 2026, the fintech software company Abrigo was targeted in a "pay or leak" extortion attempt by the ShinyHunters group. Shortly after, data allegedly taken from the company's Salesforce instance was published publicly and contained over 700k unique email addresses belonging to both Abrigo staff and external contacts. Whilst separate from Abrigo's Salesforce compromise via the Drift application connector the previous year, the data fields described in that incident are consistent with the ShinyHunters data, namely that it was "business contact information" including "institution name, employee name, email addresses, and phone numbers".

In March 2026, the Colombian fintech company Addi identified unauthorised activity on its platform and advised customers that "it is possible that your personal information may have been compromised". The "pay or leak" extortion group ShinyHunters subsequently claimed responsibility and published a large trove of personal data allegedly obtained from Addi. The data included 34M unique email addresses from credit scoring requests, credit bureau records, customer identity records and email validation logs. It also contained government issued IDs (Cédula de Ciudadanía), estimated income, socioeconomic levels, purchases and other credit-related data points.

In April 2026, Canada Life was the victim of a "pay or leak" extortion campaign by the ShinyHunters group. The group subsequently published the data which contained over 200k unique email addresses along with names, phone numbers, physical addresses and, in some cases, customer support tickets. In their disclosure notice, Canada Life advised that "it is a small proportion of our customers who may have been impacted". In the wake of the incident, Canada Life also published an alert cautioning customers to be wary of phishing attacks, a pattern often seen after the public release of breached data.

In April 2026, data allegedly obtained from CTT, Portugal's national postal service, was posted to a public hacking forum. The data included 468k unique email addresses along with names, phone numbers and parcel tracking numbers which can be used to retrieve the tracking history of the parcel.

In May 2026, the real estate services firm Cushman & Wakefield was the target of a "pay or leak" extortion campaign by the ShinyHunters group. Following the threat, the group publicly published data they alleged had been obtained from the firm, consisting mostly of C&W email addresses along with tens of thousands of external email addresses and corporate contact records. The exposed data was primarily business information, including names, job titles, company addresses and phone numbers.

In April 2026, the fashion brand Zara was among a number of organisations targeted by the ShinyHunters extortion group as part of their "pay or leak" campaign. The group claimed the breach was related to a compromise of the Anodot analytics platform and subsequently published a terabyte of data allegedly including 95M support ticket records. The data contained 197k unique email addresses alongside product SKUs, order IDs and the market the support ticket originated in. Zara's parent company Inditex advised that the incident didn't affect passwords or payment information.

The Lapsus$ Group breached Vodafone, a major international telecom provider, and gained limited access to some files in March 2026. After the company allegedly refused to negotiate within a 15-day deadline, Lapsus$ publicly dumped 7.1GB of Vodafone's internal source code. The breach originated from a compromised internal GitHub account, and the leaked code contained hardcoded PostgreSQL database credentials that could enable unauthorized backend access. Vodafone confirmed the incident occurred in March but stated no customer data was affected, attributing the breach to compromised third-party development software.

Mustang Panda aka Twill Typhoon, a China-linked group, was observed targeting organisations across Japan and the Asia-Pacific region (APJ), starting in late September 2025. The group used fake Apple and Yahoo sites for espionage, and was discovered when several computers connected to fake content delivery networks (CDNs). The hackers used DLL sideloading, where they took a real, safe piece of software and tricked it into running a hidden, malicious file at the same time. They also used real Windows tools, such as dfsvc.exe and vshost.exe, to stay hidden. They used a framework called FDMTP to send new commands and updates to the infected computer, and set up scheduled tasks or hid code in the computer's registry to ensure they didn't lose access if the computer restarted. The attack was first discovered by security experts at Darktrace, who disclosed their findings in a report published on 14 May 2026.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: North Korean state-sponsored hacking group Kimsuky obtained initial access to target systems by delivering spearphishing emails containing malicious attachments disguised as documents to South Korean organizations and individuals. The group used a variety of droppers in different formats, such as JSE, PIF, SCR, EXE, etc., to deliver malware mainly belonging to two big clusters: PebbleDash and AppleSeed. The attackers used legitimate tools, including Visual Studio Code (VSCode) and DWAgent, for post-exploitation activities. Kaspersky identified multiple infection logs uploaded to the Dropbox storage used for httpMalice’s C2 server. They assess with medium-high confidence that attacks associated with these malware families are conducted by Kimsuky-affiliated clusters.
Techniques Used: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel, Phishing, Replication Through Removable Media

Description: Salt Typhoon (aka FamousSparrow), a Chinese-linked threat actor, targeted an Azerbaijani oil and gas company between late December 2025 and late February 2026, exploiting a vulnerable Microsoft Exchange Server using the ProxyNotShell exploit chain. The attackers deployed two distinct backdoor families, Deed RAT and Terndoor, across three separate waves of activity, and returned to the same compromised entry point three times despite remediation attempts. The intrusion was attributed to FamousSparrow with moderate-to-high confidence, based on observed TTPs, malware families, and execution flow. Bitdefender researchers reported the incident on 14 May 2026.

The Nitrogen ransomware group claimed to have stolen 8 terabytes of data, including 11 million files, from Taiwanese electronics manufacturer Foxconn, a critical supplier for major hardware companies including Apple and Nvidia. The stolen information allegedly included confidential instructions, internal project documentation, and technical drawings related to projects involving Intel, Apple, Google, Dell, and Nvidia, among others. The cyberattack caused a network outage at Foxconn’s Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin facility, disrupting production for about a week. Nitrogen claimed responsibility for the attack and posted a collection of sample files on the dark web. Foxconn confirmed the incident but did not comment on the scope of the breach or verify Nitrogen’s claims about the volume and nature of the stolen data.

Iranian state-sponsored hacker group Handala allegedly gained access to existing WhatsApp business accounts, or created fake ones, sending threatening messages via WhatsApp to tens of thousands of Israelis on 27 April 2026. The messages were sent directly to users through the messaging platform, with the content of the messages threatening Jewish Israelis to prepare for weeks of missile barrages, should they not put an end to Benjamin Netanyahu's "foolishness".

Title (Company): West Pharmaceutical Services - West Pharmaceutical Services - West Pharmaceutical Services
Description: An unidentified perpetrator targeted West Pharmaceutical Services, a Pennsylvania-based supplier of packaging and drug delivery products, on 4 May 2026, resulting in the disruption of global operations, including shipping, receiving, and manufacturing processes. The company detected the intrusion on 4 May 2026 and later determined it was a cyberattack, which involved data exfiltration and system encryption. West Pharmaceutical Services proactively took systems offline for containment, notified law enforcement, and brought in outside cyberforensic experts, including Palo Alto Networks Unit 42. The incident was disclosed in a Form 8K and press release on their website on 7 May 2026. The incident affected West's sites worldwide, including its site in Eschweiler in Germany and in Nouvion-en-Thiérache site in France.

Unknown threat actor compromised online shop of Czech carmaker Škoda in May 2026. The attackers exploited a software flaw to gain unauthorized access to its online shop, potentially exposing customer data including names, contact details, order history, and logins, although passwords and payment card data were reportedly not affected. The online shop was disabled for a short time.

An unknown threat actor breached DeFi platform TrustedVolumes, stealing $6.7 million in May 2026. The attacker extracted approximately 1,291 WETH, 206,282 USDT, 16.93 WBTC, and 1.26 million USDC. The root cause of the breach was a combination of permissionless signer registration, broken replay protection and an unvalidated transfer source field. The attacker acted as a trusted signer and drained victims without valid authorization, with funds routed through high-risk no-KYC exchange ChangeNow before being swapped to ETH. TrustedVolumes confirmed the breach and published three wallet addresses holding the stolen funds in a social media post on 7 May 2026.

North Korean state-sponsored APT37 (aka ScarCruft, Ricochet Collima) carried out a multi-platform supply-chain attack targeting a video game platform in China since late 2024. The threat actor targeted Yanbian-themed games, played by ethnic Koreans in the Yanbian region of China by trojanizing Windows and Android components with a backdoor named BirdCall, which was capable of collecting personal data and documents, taking screenshots, and making voice recordings. ESET researchers assessed the actor's goal to be espionage in a technical report on 5 May 2026.

Title (Company): Laboratoria Medyczne Optimed Sp. z o.o.
Description: A Belarusian cybercriminal group breached Medical Laboratory Optimed on 3 May 2026. The attackers had access to identification data, health data, and laboratory test results. The company reported the incident to the President of the Personal Data Protection Office and relevant law enforcement agencies and released a statement to the public on 7 May 2026.

Title (Company): Unspecified Municipal Water And Sewage Utility
Description: An unknown threat actor used commercial large language models to aid in planning and conducting a cyberattack against municipal water and sewage utility’s OT of City of Monterrey in Mexico. The attackers used AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic. The threat actor used AI to generate malicious scripts, conduct the attack faster and more efficiently, and to provide feedback during the attack. The incident was reported by Dragos on 7 May 2026.

Qilin ransomware group carried out a ransomware attack on the Ahorramas supermarket chain in Spain in May 2026. The threat actor stole IDs, financial records, customer complaint forms, signed contracts, bank details, store plans and images of video surveillance systems. The incident caused delays in administrative processes and internal management over a time period of a few days. In a statement released by Escudo Digital, the company stated that it had notified the National Institute of Cybersecurity (INCIBE) and the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD), and had activated its incident response protocols.

Title (Company): Instructure - Unspecified Affected Schools and Universities
Description: ShinyHunters breached US-based education technology firm Instructure and claims to have exfiltrated data from 8,800 schools and over 280 million individuals across multiple countries on 1 May 2026. The cybercriminal group claimed responsibility on its leak site on 3 May 2026 and subsequently defaced Canvas login pages of over 330 institutions on 7 May 2026. The exfiltrated data included user records, private messages, and enrollment data, harvested via Canvas-native export features including DAP queries, provisioning reports, and user APIs. Instructure confirmed the existence of a cybersecurity incident on 1 May 2026. On 11 May, Infrastructure announced that it reached an agreement with the "unauthorized actor" and all data has been returned.

Iranian state-sponsored APT MuddyWater group affiliated with the Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS) likely conducted an intrusion under the guise of the Chaos ransomware-as-a-service group in early 2026. The attackers used social engineering via Microsoft Teams, where they utilized screensharing to harvest credentials and manipulate Multi-Factor Authentication. Once it gained access, the group exfiltrated data via remote management tools like DWAgent, and custom malware. The attackers claimed to have stolen data and initiated ransom negotiations. After data was leaked, the victim confirmed it was legitimate. Researchers from cybersecurity company Rapid7 published the incident and provided technical evidence, attributing it to Iran’s MOIS.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Unknown threat actors compromised the installers of Daemon Tools, a widely-used disk imaging software, in a supply-chain attack that affected users in more than 100 countries on 8 April 2026. Among the affected countries are Russia, Brazil, Turkey, Spain, Germany, and China. The attackers tampered with the installers and distributed them through the software's official website, embedding backdoors into core software components that executed automatically at system startup. The malicious versions, which were first observed in early April 2026, affected multiple releases of the software installed on thousands of machines. Most victims received only a basic information collector designed to gather system data, while a second, more advanced payload was deployed to a handful of targets, including organizations in government, science, manufacturing, and retail sectors in Russia, Belarus, and Thailand. The attackers likely used the initial data collection to profile infected systems before selectively deploying more sophisticated malware, including a lightweight backdoor used to deliver a more complex implant dubbed Quic RAT. Kaspersky researchers informed the public about the attack on 5 May 2026, and the company Disc Soft, which produces Daemon Tools, disclosed that it was aware of the findings and was investigating. Disc Soft stated that the issue had been successfully addressed within less than 12 hours of identifying it and recommended that all users update their Daemon Tools Lite software to the latest version.

Title (Company): Authority for Public Services Regulation - Office of Public Prosecution (Oman) - Information Technology Authority (ITA) - Royal Oman Police - Ministry of Justice and Legal Affairs - Royal Fleet of Oman - Civil Aviation Authority - Ministry of Finance (Oman) - Ministry of Transport, Communications & IT (MTCIT) - Tax Authority of Oman - Royal Court Affairs - State Audit Institution
Description: An Iranian-nexus threat actor carried out a targeted attack against Oman's government, specifically against the Ministry of Justice and Legal Affairs, on 8 April and 10 April 2026. In an effort to comprimise judicial records and citizen identity data, multiple government entities were infiltrated. The attackers exploited a custom webshell deployed on mersaltest.mjla.gov.om, which provided persistent access to the ministries' network. The group used various tools, including C2 code, session logs, and exfiltrated data, to compromise the network and extract over 26,000 Ministry of Justice user records, judicial case data, committee decisions, and both SAM and SYSTEM registry hives. The attack was discovered by AttackCapture scans on 8 April 2026, and a second directory was captured two days later on 10 April. The attackers used a dedicated gov.om folder, which included 12 exploit scripts, to target multiple Omani government entities. The IT-security company Hunt.io disclosed the incident to the public on 5 May 2026.

In April 2026, 7-Eleven was the victim of a "pay or leak" extortion campaign by ShinyHunters, with the data later published that month. The incident exposed 185k unique email addresses, along with names, physical addresses, dates of birth and phone numbers. A small number of records also contained additional exposed data fields. The company later advised the breach was limited to "certain 7-Eleven systems used to store franchisee documents", a statement consistent with the exposed data.

In March 2026, the financial services firm Ameriprise Financial was named by the ShinyHunters group in a "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group claimed possession of more than 200GB of compressed data exfiltrated from Ameriprise's Salesforce environment and internal SharePoint infrastructure, and subsequently published the data after negotiations allegedly failed. The published data contained 500k unique email addresses as well as names, phone numbers, physical addresses and employer information. In their disclosure to state attorneys general, Ameriprise reported 47,876 affected people; the larger email address population represents contacts from Ameriprise's broader operational systems, including internal staff. Ameriprise further advised that they have "implemented heightened monitoring of your account(s) to include enhanced identity verification procedures".

In May 2026, the GTA V and CS2 cheat service Atlas Menu suffered a data breach. An attacker claimed to have gained access to all Atlas systems and published the service's database to a public GitHub repository. The incident exposed 64k unique email addresses along with usernames, IP addresses, support tickets and passwords stored as bcrypt hashes.

In May 2026, the telecommunications company Charter Communications (the parent company behind the consumer broadband and cable brand Spectrum) was named by the ShinyHunters group in a "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group later published the data, which exposed 4.9M unique email addresses along with names, phone numbers and physical addresses. A subset of approximately 85k records originating from an internal employee directory also included job titles. Charter confirmed the incident, but stated that no sensitive personal information or customer proprietary network information (CPNI) was exfiltrated.

In December 2025, the European Dragonica private server Dragonica Lunaris suffered a data breach. The incident exposed 126k email addresses, usernames, dates of birth and bcrypt password hashes. The service operator confirmed the breach and advised it has since been fixed.

In April 2026, the American insurance holding company Kemper Corporation was named by the ShinyHunters ransomware group in a "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The attackers allegedly accessed Kemper's Salesforce environment via social engineering as part of a broader campaign targeting hundreds of organisations using the same method. The group later published tens of gigabytes of data they claimed included internal directory data, Salesforce records and Stripe payment logs. Among the 269k unique email addresses were names, phone numbers, physical addresses and partial payment card data including the last 4 digits, expiry dates and card brands. Kemper confirmed the incident and stated they had engaged third-party cybersecurity experts and notified law enforcement.

In April 2026, the luxury fashion e-commerce platform Mytheresa was listed as a victim of the ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion group. After the ransom deadline passed, the group publicly released the data which contained 84k unique email addresses. The exposed data also included names, phone numbers, physical addresses, purchases and partial credit card data including card type, last 4 digits and expiry date.

In January 2021, the parody site Windows93 suffered a data breach of the Myspace93 sub-site after a beta application was exploited to download server files. The compromised data was later leaked in June and included 46k Myspace93 accounts containing email and IP addresses, usernames and passwords stored in plain text.

A hacking group with the alias Korenvy breached the website of Tierra del Fuego legislature in Argentina on 23 May 2026. The homepage of the website showed messages in both English and Spanish, warning of a alleged breach of the system. The messages were accompanied by the signature „Hacked by Korenvy“.

Ransomware group Payload attacked GTF Freese, a Bremen-based ship supplier with approximately 250 employees, in late May 2026. The group claimed to have exfiltrated 200 GB of company data and posted a countdown on their darknet site threatening to publish the data. GTF Freese confirmed the incident, stating that despite extensive IT security measures, parts of the IT infrastructure were encrypted in a "professionally executed criminal ransomware attack." The company activated prepared emergency plans and worked with external specialists to implement security measures while maintaining core business operations. Production was restored and normal customer service resumed, though the company website remained offline.

Title (Company): KZ-Gedenkstätte Osthofen - KZ-Gedenkstätte Hinzert - NS-Dokumentationszentrum Osthofen - Landeszentrale für politische Bildung Rheinland-Pfalz
Description: Unknown threat actors breached the Landeszentrale für politische Bildung (State Agency for Civic Education) in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, rendering several websites inaccessible. The attack affected the agency's main website as well as the websites of the concentration camp memorials Hinzert (Trier-Saarburg district) and Osthofen (Alzey-Worms district) and the NS Documentation Centre in Osthofen. The agency described the incident as a "security incident" and stated it was working to restore the websites. The Landeskriminalamt (State Criminal Police Office) is investigating whether user data, such as newsletter subscriber email addresses, was stolen. The incident was disclosed on 29 May 2026.

A suspected state actor compromised over 600,000 records from the Lithuanian public register system starting in early 2026. Lithuanian authorities became aware of the attack in April 2026. The director of the Register Centre, Adrijus Jusas, stated that the stolen data included information from real estate extracts and personal identification numbers. According to the Lithuanian Prosecutor General's office, the attack was conducted by a foreign state. On Facebook, the conservative leader of the opposition, Laurynas Kasčiūnas, warned that the exposed data could include information about intelligence agents, military personnel, diplomats, politicians, and officials. Kasiunas claimed that the leak bore the hallmarks of a Russian intelligence operation and that the residential address data of intelligence and military personnel could be used for surveillance, phishing campaigns, identity theft, or coercion attempts. The Lithuanian Prosecutor General's office did not confirm or deny the accusations of Russian involvement and did not reveal the foreign state allegedly linked to the attack.

An unknown threat actor compromised networks of Chelan County, Washington, resulted in a precautionary shut-down of government networks, computers, and phones across all departments on 24 May 2026. The attack was detected by county IT staff on 24 May 2026. The attack did not affect 911 services, which remained available.

Title (Company): Unspecified Service Provider - University hospitals in Tübingen - University hospitals in Heidelberg - University hospitals in Freiburg - Ulm University Hospital
Description: An unknown threat actor compromised a service provider that processes invoices for private medical services resulted in the theft of sensitive patient data, including names, dates of birth, addresses, and billing-relevant data, from approximately 61,000 patients at Ulm University Hospital and other clinics in Baden-Württemberg in May 2026, including university hospitals in Freiburg, Heidelberg, and Tübingen. The hospital management was informed of the data theft a few days prior to the publication date. The attackers exploited the service provider’s systems, but the full extent of the attack is still unclear. The Ulm University Hospital made the cyberattack public in a press statement on 21 May 2026. The hospital has stopped transmitting data to the service provider and is demanding clarification on the criminal offense with the hospital management. The Federal Office for Information Security was contacted and notified by the hospital.

An unknown threat actor hijacked Tunisian telecom operator Tuni Tunisie Telecom's application MyTT and sent messages with the title “A Cry for Tunisia: Freedom is not a crime” to customers. Tunisia Telecom initially reported maintenance on its application, but later acknowledged the cyberattack in a second statement published on the same day.

An unknown threat actor breached Vietnamese ministerial systems in a major cyberattack in May 2026, potentially stealing millions of user records. The National Cybersecurity Center, led by Lieutenant Colonel Tran Trung Hieu, Deputy Director of the National Cybersecurity Center and Director of Vietnam Cyber Emergency Response Teams (VNCERT) under the Ministry of Public Security’s Department of Cybersecurity and High-Tech Crime Prevention, made the attacks public on the Vietnam Security Summit 2026. Initial investigations conducted by VNCERT between 21 May and 22 May 2026 showed that the affected agencies already operated Security Operations Center systems, but the monitoring systems failed to detect the attacks.

Unknown cybercriminals stole thousands of patient data from hospitals in Northern Germany, including the University Hospitals in Schleswig-Holstein and Hamburg-Eppendorf, by attacking an external service provider based in Saarland. The attack, which was reportedly an attempt at extortion, resulted in the theft of data from around 9,000 patients at UKSH and over 5,000 patients at UKE, including names, addresses, and treatment information. The data was stolen from the external service provider, which handles the billing of private and self-paying services. The incident was informed to the Schleswig-Holstein State Centre for Data Protection and the Federal Office for Information Security on 16 April 2026. The clinics announced that they would individually notify the affected patients. The attack was reported on 23 May by NDR.

Title (Company): MGEN - Almerys - Alan - Harmonie Mutuelle - AG2R
Description: Unidentified perpetrators breached Almerys, a third-party payment provider for mutual insurance companies including Alan, MGEN, Harmonie Mutuelle and AG2R, on 22 May 2026. The attack resulted in the leaking of sensitive data, including up to 15 million social security numbers alongside other information such as civil status and contract numbers. The incident was disclosed by Alan in a statement released online on 23 May 2026.

Title (Company): Zali Steggall - Zali Steggall's staff members
Description: A foreign state actor, believed to be affiliated with the Russian government, hacked into the WhatsApp account of Australian Independent MP Zali Steggall and three of her staff members, on 6 March 2026, as part of a phishing scheme. The incident was reported to the Department of Parliamentary Services, who temporarily blocked WhatsApp access on parliamentary devices. The hacking was revealed during a Senate estimates hearing on 26 May 2026, where officials from the Department of Parliamentary Services confirmed that the accounts were breached by a foreign state actor. Zali Steggall confirmed that her WhatsApp account was targeted as part of a broader cyber incident affecting parliamentarians and staff. The incident was reported by various news outlets, including on 24 May 2026 and 25 May 2026.

Unknown threat actor compromised Scottsboro Police Department in Alabama, United States in May 2026, but the attack was quickly detected and systems were shut down by the department before any records or sensitive information were accessed or taken. The department, citing the newspaper WAFF, stated that there was no evidence that identifying information, photographs, videos, reports or other sensitive records were exported or compromised.

Iran-nexus APT Screening Serpens (aka UNC1549, Smoke Sandstorm and Iranian Dream Job) deployed malware to an entity in the Middle East in a social engineering campaign in mid-February 2026. The hackers used fake job offers and recruiter outreach to deliver malware, with the primary aim of cyber espionage and intelligence gathering. The campaign, which was reported by Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 on 24 May 2026, focused on software engineers and IT workers with privileged access to internal systems. The attackers used fake interview invitations and video conferencing tools embedded with malicious software to steal credentials or gain access to company infrastructure. In the campaign, six new remote access Trojan (RAT) variants deployed between February and April 2026 based on samples uploaded to VirusTotal, potentially including further victims in the U.S. and Israel in late March 2026, as well as an organization in the UAE and another Middle Eastern entity in mid-April 2026.

An unknown threat actor compromised email accounts of the Northern Mariana Islands government according to the Office of Information Technology (OIT). OIT has initiated systemwide security protocols and corrective actions to restore full functionality and ensure the continued safety of government systems.

An unknown threat actor calling itself 'Black Matter' conducted a DDoS attack against web hosting platform 1-Grid in South Africa on 18 May 2026. The attack affected the company’s infrastructure and services. In a later statement, the company reported that it had restored the functionality of its services.

Title (Company): TuId - Carlos Negro - Alejandro Sánchez - Luis Lacalle Pou - Antel
Description: LaPampaLeaks claimed to have breached the TuId platform of Uruguayan state company Antel, allegedly stole data of hundreds of thousands of Uruguayan citizens and leaked the personal data of Uruguayan political figures on 7 May 2026. The group offered the data for sale on the dark web, including data from former president Luis Lacalle Pou, Interior Minister Carlos Negro, and Alejandro Sánchez, Secretary of the Presidency. Antel authorities announced that they were investigating the cyberattacks and had filed a criminal complaint with the Attorney General’s Office. The company acknowledged that there may have been an impact on a limited group of up to 163 users, mostly Antel officials.

In June 2026, telecommunications tower infrastructure company American Tower was the target of a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group subsequently published data allegedly taken from the company containing more than 200k unique email addresses belonging to employees, contractors, customers, and leads. Exposed data also included names, addresses, and phone numbers.

In May 2026, the HVAC/R wholesale distributor Baker Distributing Company was added to the ShinyHunters data extortion group's "pay or leak" site. In early June, the group publicly published data they claimed had been obtained from Baker's SharePoint and Salesforce infrastructure including 103k unique email addresses along with names, physical addresses, phone numbers and tickets relating to the company's HVAC contractor customer base. The exposed data was largely corporate contact and support information with limited sensitivity.

In May 2026, the corporate travel management company BCD Travel was claimed as a victim of the ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. Data allegedly obtained from BCD was subsequently published publicly in early June and contained 396k unique email addresses. Other exposed data included names, addresses, phone numbers, job titles and employer names, spanning a variety of different data sets including leads, internal staff and support tickets.

In March 2026, the commercial real estate finance company Berkadia was the target of a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group subsequently published data they alleged was taken from Berkadia's Salesforce instance, including over 300k unique email addresses as well as names, physical addresses and phone numbers, among other data.

In March 2026, the financial consulting and advisory firm CFGI was the target of a ShinyHunters "pay-or-leak" extortion campaign. The group subsequently publicised data allegedly obtained from CFGI comprising corporate contact information, including 243k unique email addresses, names, phone numbers and physical addresses.

In May 2026, the dental benefits administrator DentaQuest was the target of a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign that resulted in the group publicly publishing hundreds of gigabytes of data allegedly obtained from the company. The data included 2.6M unique email addresses along with names, addresses and phone numbers. Much of the data appeared in healthcare enrollment files (ASC X12 transaction sets) with some containing Medicaid IDs, while additional data appeared in member records and related files. DentaQuest acknowledged "a cybersecurity incident involving unauthorized access to a limited portion of our network", and advised they had contained the attack and mitigated the threat.

In January 2026, the automotive research and car-shopping platform Edmunds was listed by the ShinyHunters hacking group as having been breached. Data purportedly obtained in the incident was later published publicly and included 178k unique email addresses, usernames, passwords, IP addresses, phone numbers and vehicle-related records.

In March 2026, the student information system Infinite Campus was targeted in a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group subsequently published data they alleged was taken from Infinite Campus, containing 137k unique email addresses along with names, phone numbers, physical addresses and support tickets. Infinite Campus subsequently sent notifications, advising that the exposed data largely consisted of "names and contact information for school staff" and that "the majority is directory information commonly found on school websites".

In June 2026, retailer JCPenney and associated brands were targeted in a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. Data allegedly obtained from JCPenney through the exploitation of a critical zero-day vulnerability in Oracle PeopleSoft was later published publicly. The exposed records indicated they primarily related to internal HR systems and impacted current and former employees. The data included 368k corporate and personal email addresses, names, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, phone numbers and home addresses.

In June 2026, a collection of accumulated stealer logs from various sources was added to HIBP. The corpus comprised 56M unique email addresses across hundreds of millions of stealer log records. The data also contained 124M unique passwords, which have been added to Pwned Passwords and are now searchable. Individuals can view any records captured against their email address in the stealer logs section of their dashboard. Organisations can see logs affecting their domain via the stealer logs API.

In June 2026, the sports and entertainment company Madison Square Garden Sports was the target of a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group later published the alleged data, which included almost 10M unique email addresses spanning staff and customers, along with extensive personal, employment and customer relationship information.

On 18 June 2026, the latest phase of Operation Endgame targeted the SocGholish malware operation, a prolific malware distribution network used to compromise systems and facilitate further cybercrime. Coordinated by international law enforcement agencies with support from Europol and Eurojust, the operation remediated almost 15,000 compromised websites and disrupted more than 100 servers and domains used to distribute malware. Authorities initially provided HIBP with 154k impacted email addresses and more than half a million previously unseen passwords. The following week, a further 4M email addresses and 9M passwords relating to the StealC malware operation also targeted by Operation Endgame were provided, followed by another 131k email addresses the following month, bringing the total to more than 4.3M unique email addresses.

In June 2026, fashion retailer Ralph Lauren was targeted in a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group subsequently published hundreds of gigabytes of data they claimed was obtained from the organisation's Salesforce instance, including 140k unique email addresses along with names, phone numbers, genders and age groups.

In June 2026, the food distribution company Sysco was targeted by a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. Data was subsequently published containing 2.7M unique email addresses belonging to staff and customers. The data also contained largely corporate contact information including names, phone numbers, physical addresses, internal job titles, and customer feedback.

In June 2026, the University of Nottingham was the target of a cyber attack, later linked to a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. Tens of gigabytes of data were subsequently published online and included 455k unique email addresses along with extensive personal information including names, addresses, phone numbers, ethnicities, disabilities, passport numbers and information relating to academic enrolments and fee payments. In a post about the incident, the university advised that the breach affected both "current students, and alumni".

Ransomware group ShinyHunters breached the National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC), a US insurance regulatory standards body, in June 2026. The attackers claimed to have stolen 3.1 TB of data, including more than 264,000 insurer regulatory filing documents, 2,000 customer and bulk orders containing personally identifiable information, approximately 45,000 files from major credit rating agencies, statutory annual and quarterly financial statements, production AWS infrastructure logs, cloud configuration files, workload automation data, and SQL scripts. On 17 June 2026, NAIC disclosed unauthorised access to their PeopleSoft systems on 11 June. In an update, NAIC acknowledged that an unauthorised party obtained information to gain temporary access to certain data storage areas and that the stolen data was published. NAIC linked the breach to a broader exploitation campaign using a known zero-day vulnerability in Oracle's ERP software suite PeopleSoft.

Title (Company): Unspecified Third-Party Vendor - NSW Rural Fire Service (RFS)
Description: The Nova ransomware group infiltrated the systems of New South Wales (NSW) Rural Fire Service (RFS).  Originally, the group claimed to have exfiltrated over 200GB from NSW government in mid-June via the remote service Citrix, but the government disputed these claims, stating that there was no evidence of any sensitive information being accessed. The only sample files provided by Nova were publicly available and historical information, including PDFs of regional topographic maps and emergency response programs. In late June, an RFS spokesperson confirmed that a hacker gained access to its system initiated from a compromised account via a remote system involving a third-party vendor. Nova did not specify which government agency was compromised in the first place, but it later named RFS explicitly.

Qilin ransomware group disrupted the systems of the public utility company GSW in Germany on 28 June 2026, which resulted in internal networks and the customer portal being unavailable. The energy and water supply were not affected. GSW is a local energy and water supplier which also operates local swimming pools. Following the discovery of the attack, a crisis team was convened, and the IT systems were disconnected from the network. The State Criminal Police Office and relevant authorities were informed and are involved in the investigation. On 17 August 2026, Qilin ransomware has listed GSW as a victim in its dark web portal.

Unidentified hackers compromised personal data of railway operator Trenitalia's clients in Italy in June 2026. The breach, detected on 26 June 2026, involved personal and identifying data, contact information, travel details, loyalty card codes, employer data, type of offer used, identity document details, and other technical data related to ticket generation. Payment data and account access credentials were not compromised.

Title (Company): Biglobe - STNet - JCOM - KDDI - Chubu Telecommunications - KDDI Web Communications - Nifty
Description: Unknown threat actors exploited vulnerabilities in third-party software to improperly access KDDI's email system in Japan on 17 June 2026, potentially leaking up to 14.22 million pieces of personal information including email addresses and passwords. The email system was provided to internet connection operators including STNet, KDDI Web Communications, JCOM, Chubu Telecommunications, Nifty and Biglobe. KDDI became aware of the situation on 17 June 2026 and implemented system modifications to prevent further damage. Affected companies were informed and users were urged to update their passwords. KDDI publicly disclosed the incident and reported it to the Personal Information Protection Committee and the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications on 23 June 2026.

An unknown threat actor exploited a vulnerability in cryptocurrency platform Raydium, a Solana automated market maker (AMM), and stole $1.34 Million on 10 June 2026. An analysis released by blockchain security firm GoPlus confirmed that the attackers successfully exploited a critical verification flaw inside Raydium’s legacy AMM V3 smart contracts to manipulate liquidity accounting, enabling them to bypass security parameters and drain $1.34 million from Raydium.

Unknown threat actors using the pseudonym "xMetah" breached e-health platform Pulsy, which centralises the exchange of medical data in parts of France, and stole health data on 18 June 2026. A database presented as belonging to Pulsy.fr was put up for sale on the dark web, containing over 35 GB in volume. The stolen data included names, birth names, first names, sex, dates and places of birth, nationality, marital status, and patient coordinates, such as postal addresses, cities, postal codes, fixed and mobile phones, emails, and countries of residence. Administrative and care-related data were also reportedly recovered, including patient identifiers, INS references, valid identity status, file histories, identity matches, care pathways, technical references, and application metadata. The potentially stolen data concerned patients treated in Grand Est establishments, users of Pulsy's digital health services, or anyone with a patient file integrated into the regional system. The attack was reported to the regional authorities and the CERT Sant, the national cyber surveillance organization dedicated to the medical sector, on 23 June 2026.

Unknown threat actors breached healthcare technology campany Xsolis and accessed files containing sensitive personal infomation impacting nearly 1.4 million individuals on 20 January 2026. Xsolis is a U.S.-based healthcare firm that develops AI-powered software used by more than 600 hospitals and health insurers for utilization management, medical necessity reviews, patient status determinations, discharge planning, and reimbursement decisions. The compromised data included names, addresses, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, health insurance details, and medical treatment information. The company discovered and contained the breach on 22 January 2026 and notified affected individuals by mail. Media outlets like Bleeping Computer informed the public about the breach on 23 June 2026.

Title (Company): Capital Development Authority (CDA) - National Radio Telecommunication Corporation
Description: Unattributed hackers compromised the Capital Development Authority (CDA) billing system for property, conservancy charges and water in Islamabad on or around 16 June 2026, disrupting online payments for three days. The attackers demanded ransom in Bitcoin and allegedly threatened to publish compromised data on the dark web. The CDA, along with its vendor NRTC and the Information Technology Department, worked to restore the system. CDA spokesperson Shahid Kiani confirmed the attack, stating that backup records remained protected and that online payments processed through 1-Link or authorised banking channels were safe. Pakistan Today and Dawn reported the incident on 19 June 2026.

Unknown threat actors exploited a previously unknown vulnerability on the website of the Productivity Commission of Australia to send unsolicited emails appearing to originate from a PC email address on 9 June 2026. The vulnerability was subsequently patched. The Productivity Commission disclosed the incident publicly on 10 June 2026.

A hacker collective known as APT73 aka Bashe threatened to publish documents from Vienna Airport, which they claimed to have obtained through a phishing attack, on 24 June 2026. The hackers gained access to an employee's computer and stole old freight documents from 2025, including Load Sheet forms, but did not obtain security-sensitive or passenger-related data. The airport confirmed the incident and stated that their operations were not affected. The attackers offered the stolen data for sale on the darknet and threatened to publish it if a ransom was not paid.

A threat actor named "misere" breached jeveuxaider.gouv.fr, a French government website dedicated to volunteering, and leaked personal data from approximately 550,000 accounts on 15 June 2026. The data concerned includes names, email addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, and user engagement histories. Misere claimed responsibility for the attack on a dark web forum, where alleged leaked data was published. On 16 June 2026, the French Ministry for Sports confirmed the incident.

The cybercriminal group The Gentlemen carried out a ransomware attack on major Australian sugar producer Mackay Sugar starting around the 10 June 2026. The attack disrupted operations and forced the shutdown of Mackay Sugar's Farleigh and Racecourse mills in Queensland. Mackay Sugar disclosed the attack on 10 June 2026. The Gentlemen ransomware group claimed responsibility for the attack on 15 June 2026. The attack affected the company's cane supply and logistics systems, and some operations were resumed in a controlled manner from 12 June 2026.

Unattributed hackers compromised a database of the French National Police Sports Federation in June 2026, potentially exposing the data of 224,000 police officers. The cyberattack, which was claimed by a cybercriminal using the pseudonym "Misery", resulted in the leak of sensitive documents, including medical certificates, summons, and sports licenses, on a dark web forum. The data leak was confirmed by the National Police Sports Federation on 21 June 2026.

Unidentified perpetrators breached the digital infrastructures of a supplier of hunting and fishing licence systems in Texas in June 2026, compromising sensitive data, including driving licences, passports, email addresses, phone numbers, and home addresses, of over 3 million people. The incident was confirmed by Texas Parks & Wildlife on 19 June 2026.

An unknown threat actor accessed personal data of users of the MesVaccins.net website, a platform from the company Syadem allowing individuals and healthcare professionals to manage an online vaccination record, in June 2026. The affected data includes identification and contact information (e-mail address and telephone number), civil status data, residence address and social security number, as well as vaccination data and health profile information. On 25 June, the company stated on their website that they are aware of the incident since 15 June. The CNIL was notified, and a complaint has been filed with the competent authorities.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - NATO-aligned Defense Contractor - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: An unknown threat actor stole 110M credentials from over 80,553 FortiGate devices in a sophisticated brute-force campaign, known as FortiBleed, in many countries since February 2026. An exposed directory of the attackers exposed login data tied to tens of thousands of Fortinet firewalls and VPN systems around the world. The campaign was first identified by the security researcher Volodymyr Diachenko on 13 June 2026, and later analysed by Hudson Rock and SOCRadar Threat Research Unit (STRU). The attacker used a complex infrastructure with 250 additional operation servers and relied on lists with stolen credentials for their brute-forcing operation. After successful initial access, the operators systematically pivot directly into internal Active Directory environments to establish deep network persistence. Since at least February 2026, the attacker actively sniffs over 19,000 devices. Several national cyber agencies have published advice follwoing the targeting of Fortinet Firewalls including UK NCSC, CCCS, CISA, and CSA.

The cyber extortion group „PEAR“ aka „Pure Extraction and Ransom“, breached the data of Optimum First Mortgage, a California direct lender, and claimed responsibility for the cyberattack on its dark web site, threatening to leak 9.3 terabytes of sensitive data, on 19 June 2026. The compromised data included highly sensitive information from mortgage applications, such as Social Security numbers, bank account details, tax records, employment history and income data.

China-Nexus threat actor UNC5221 compromised the Belgian civil intelligence service, State Security, by infiltrating the software of an external company responsible for securing the mobile phones of Security Services personnel between May 2025 and spring 2026. The attackers accessed personal data of agents, including names, phone numbers and potentially data of people contacted by State Security members via official mobile phones. The threat actors exploited vulnerabilities in the Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile (EPMM) to access telephone and email data. RTBF reported the incident on 19 June 2026. Cybernews.com reported that "some news outlets have attributed the breach to UNC5221" a group based in and sponsored by China.

Unknown threat actors compromised 75,000 firewalls of the same type used by the town administration of Oranienburg, Germany, on 18 June 2026. CERT Brandenburg, the state's central office for security-related incidents in computer systems, informed the town of the attack. Although Oranienburg's administrative network was not directly affected, the town precautionarily shut down its network on 18 June 2026 at 6 pm, with the shutdown expected to continue on 19 June. During this time, the town administration and municipal facilities were only reachable by phone, and consultation hours of the citizens' registration office were cancelled. The town's website remained accessible with a note on service restrictions.

Title (Company): Export Development Bank of Iran - Unspecified Financial Messaging System - Bank Melli - Bank Saderat - Bank Tejarat
Description: The hacktivist group Black Wolves disrupted electronic banking services of state-owned banks in Iran on 14 June 2026. The incident temporarily prevented online payments by targeting a financial messaging system used by Bank Melli, Bank Tejarat, ​Bank Saderat and ​the Export Development Bank of ‌Iran. The Iranian hacktivist group Black Wolves claimed responsibility for the attack on their Telegram channel. The attack affected numerous ATMs in the capital, Tehran, with residents reporting that electronic payments stopped working in supermarkets, restaurants, and gas stations. The Banking Coordination Council of Iran confirmed the incidents and stated that the disruptions had since been resolved and online transactions were functioning normally again. The attack was reported by Reuters on 14 June 2026.

An unidentified perpetrator breached Mount Royal University in Calgary, Canada, on 17 June 2026, disrupting several systems including the main website, online service MyMRU, on-campus internet access and telephone services. The university retained external cybersecurity experts to assist with the response and investigation. The investigation had not yet determined whether any personal information or data was accessed or taken. Mount Royal University disclosed the incident on 18 June 2026.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: China-nexus threat actor UNC6508 stole data from government and private organizations in the United States and Canada, including a medical research university, clinical providers, academic medical centers, and U.S. military health institutions from September 2023 to November 2025. The threat actor exploited externally facing REDCap servers and using a custom backdoor called INFINITERED to steal administrative credentials and data. Google Threat Intelligence Group reported attributed the campaign.

Title (Company): Ministry of Integration and Regional Development (Civil Defence Alert System)
Description: Unknown threat actors compromised Brazil's national Civil Defence alert system between 19 June and 20 June 2026, sending false emergency messages to approximately 30 million people across eight states and the Federal District. The attack targeted the Civil Defence Alert system operated by the Ministry of Integration and Regional Development. The National Secretary for Civil Protection and Defence Wolnei Wolff confirmed that ten different notifications were issued during the intrusion: nine via Cell Broadcast and one via SMS. The messages contained terms such as "misanthropy" and "alien invasion." The Federal Police and the National Telecommunications Agency (Anatel) launched investigations. Anatel reported that the alerts did not go through the official channels of the system's technical platform operated by ABR Telecom. The system was temporarily suspended following the incident.

Unknown threat actors stole patient and proprietary data from iRhythm Technologies, a U.S.-based digital healthcare company on 8 June 2026. The attack was followed by a ransom demand on 9 June 2026. The company disclosed the cyberattack in an SEC Form 8K filed on 10 June 2026. The threat actor claimed to have stolen proprietary data, protected health information, and other personal data, and demanded payment in exchange for not publicly disclosing this information. The company confirmed the data breach from third-party-hosted business applications via a social engineering attack.

Ransomware group RansomHouse breached Prince George County's computer network in Virginia on or around 10 June 2026, disrupting administrative and phone systems while the 911 emergency system remained operational. RansomHouse listed Prince George County as a victim on 17 June 2026. The county activated response protocols, engaged external cybersecurity experts and notified law enforcement. Critical data backups enabled rapid restoration, with a "vast majority" of the network operational by 18 June. The county is assessing whether personal information was affected. County spokesperson Hannah Thomas disclosed the incident on 18 June 2026.

Title (Company): Unspecified third-party file-storage system - One Medical
Description: The ransomware group ShinyHunters breached One Medical, an Amazon subsidiary, and exfiltrated archived patient data from One Medical Seniors and Iora Health on 8 June 2026. ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen 8.8 terabytes of data, threatening to publish it if negotiations fail. The company confirmed that they learnt on 13 June that an unauthorized person gained access to a third-party file-storage system used used to retain archived information between 8 and 11 June. The affected information contains files with demographic and clinical records from a certain number of patients at designated One Medical Seniors (formerly Iora Health) clinics in Atlanta, Cape Cod, Charlotte, Piedmont Triad, Denver, Houston, Phoenix, Tucson, and Seattle.

Unknown threat actors exploited a vulnerability in the deprecated Aztec Connect decentralised finance platform, draining approximately $2.1 million in crypto on 14 June 2026. The vulnerability stemmed from a mismatch between transaction verification and settlement on Ethereum, allowing attackers to create unbacked balances by crediting value without validating the transactions on-chain, which could then be withdrawn. Aztec Connect disclosed the attack on 14 June 2026.

Unidentified perpetrators disrupted the Russian dairy company Ufagormolzavod on 24 June 2026. The attack affected the IT systems of the company, forcing it to process shipments and paperwork manually. The company’s chief executive, Ildar Faizullin, informed the public about the attack. The attack did not interrupt production, but slowed down the processing of documents and shipments. The incident was reported in the local media.

Ransomware group ShinyHunters stole 297 GB of sensitive employee data from the Council of Europe (CoE) in June 2026, exposing nearly half a million HR and payroll records. The compromised data included names, dates of birth, home addresses, phone numbers, employee IDs, salaries, bank account details, tax and social security information and medical records. ShinyHunters claimed the breach on their dark web blog and made the data public after a deadline on 16 June 2026.

Title (Company): Unspecified Software Company - Not available - Not available - Unspecified Software Company - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Unspecified Software Company - Diplomatic Organization
Description: An unknown threat actor targeted several organisations worldwide with undocumented malware in an ongoing campaign discovered by Kaspersky in 2026. Targets included diplomatic entities in Indonesia, government agencies in Taiwan, software development companies, and businesses in Hong Kong, Lebanon, Syria, Colombia, North Macedonia, Nepal and Serbia. The attackers used a previously undocumented malware loader called SharkLoader to infiltrate targeted systems, exploiting known vulnerabilities in internet-exposed applications including Microsoft Exchange, Microsoft SharePoint and Openfire servers. They also distributed malicious droppers masquerading as legitimate software such as Google Update and Cisco AnyConnect installers, and used PDF documents in phishing campaigns. The malware employed advanced evasion techniques including DLL sideloading to load encrypted malicious modules, with the final stage injecting and executing Cobalt Strike Beacon for command and control. Kaspersky does not attribute the activity to any known APT group and published its findings on 24 June 2026.
Techniques Used: Exploit Public-Facing Application, Phishing, Replication Through Removable Media

Description: Unidentified perpetrators breached the careers platform CareerConnect of Oxford University by exploiting one of its third-party providers, Group GTI in May 2026. On 28 May, GTI informed the University the platform had been accessed by an unauthorised third party that was able to access users' first name, last name, e-mail addresses and, for users who do not sign in using Single Sign-On (SSO), encrypted passwords. GTI has confirmed that the security vulnerability has been fixed, and additional security measures have been put in place.

The ShinyHunters cybercriminal group breached the University of Nottingham on 9 June, accessing a significant amount of student data, including financial information and personal details, from the University of Nottingham’s Campus Solutions system. The university reported the unauthorized activity in a statement on their website on 10 June 2026, and immediately took the affected systems offline to contain the incident. The university apologized to those affected and is working with the third-party platform maintainer to lead a forensic investigation. On 11 June, Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) made an extortion campaign public attributed to UNC6240 (ShinyHunters) targeting Oracle PeopleSoft application infrastructure by exploiting a zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-35273) between 27 May and 9 June. Later, the university released further details on the incident saying that 450,000 email addresses are affected, and the attackers exploited the Oracle vulnerability. The university has reported the incident to Action Fraud and the Information Commissioners Office, and is offering advice and support to affected students.

Unknown threat actors stole the personal information of employees of the city of Nantes in France on 9 June 2026. The data theft was limited to city employees, while the data of citizens remained unaffected. The city mobilized technical teams and set up a crisis unit and notified the French National Commission on Informatics and Liberties. The city disclosed the incident in an internal memo, which was made available to news outlet Ouest France on 13 June 2026.

Iran-linked hacking group Handala (aka Handala Hack Team/ Hamsa) breached and leaked data of water utility provider California Water Service in the United States on 11 June 2026. The attacker published a 5GB proof-of-concept data dump to prove its access to the company's customer billing database and its RTKBase system. The customer billing database contained names, service addresses, phone numbers, account numbers, and payment histories across multiple Cal Water districts, and the internal RTKBase deployment is an open-source GNSS base station platform used by field crews to receive GPS data when mapping and maintaining water infrastructure. Dataminr researchers stated that the RTKBase platform was the entry point and the group merely used it to access the customer information database. Handala’s public release shows access to at least seven operational districts of California Water Service, including Bakersfield, Chico, Salinas, Stockton, Visalia, San Mateo and a regional engineering segment. The group stated that its attack was a response to US attacks on Iran. The breach was reported by Dataminr on 11 June 2026.

An unknown threat actor targeted Great Marlow School in Buckinghamshire with malware, forcing the school to partially close on and after 9 June 2026. The attack disrupted its IT systems and communications, prompting staff to shut down parts of the system as a precaution while an investigation was carried out, resulting in the school being unable to contact parents and carers through its usual email system, and teachers being unable to work. The school is working with cybersecurity professionals to restore normal operations and responding in line with guidance from the Department for Education and the National Cyber Security Centre.

FulcrumSec breached the network of and stole data from pharmaceutical manufacturer Novo Nordisk in Denmark on 11 June 2026. The attacker gained unauthorized access to data from the company’s clinical trials and gained access to a limited number of internal computer systems, compromising personal data, including patient identifiers, year of birth, sex, and health or immunogenicity data. Novo Nordisk stated that no patient's name could be linked directly to the stolen data. It reported that while some of the company’s systems were taken down as a precautionary measure, its core business operations remained intact. The company made the incident public in a statement to Reuters on 11 June 2026.  On 16 June 2026, FulcrumSec claimed responsibility for the attack exfiltrating 1.3 TB of data.

An unknown threat actor breached the City of Rennes on or before 10 June 2026, where the professional data of Rennes Métropole and City of Rennes agents were targeted, compromising information such as civility, name, first name, profession email addresses, phone numbers, function, and technical identifiers. The city confirmed the incident, but considers the stolen information as not sensitive. The 5,500 affected agents were informed and warned about the risks. The attack was discovered by the information system management service, which immediately took measures to limit the impact and notified the CNIL.

The Filipino hacktivist group Nullsec Philippines defaced the website of the Philippine Senate on 10 June 2026. The hacktivist group identifying as “Nullsec Philippines” claimed responsibility for the defacing attack in a social media post, accusing the government of not doing enough against corruption. On 11 June, the Senate confirmed that its official website was recently subjected to an “unauthorized modification” or website defacement but said that initial assessment showed “no indication that confidential or sensitive information had been compromised.” The Senate President Pro Tempore and Acting Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian condemned the act and called for a unified government response to identify and prosecute those responsible. An investigation was launched by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), and the Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC).

Title (Company): Stock Investors - Not available - FireAnt MetaKit
Description: The Vietnamese state-sponsored hacking group APT32 (aka OceanLotus) carried out a supply-chain attack on stock investors, leveraging the widely used software platform FireAnt MetaKit, between October 2025 and March 2026, and compromised the network of a Vietnamese infrastructure and transport construction corporation with its signature implant, SPECTRALVIPER, between November 2024 and February 2026. Both operations were reported by ESET on 11 June 2026. Despite the broad potential impact of such an attack, only a few individuals were observed who ultimately received SPECTRALVIPER, indicating selective targeting. SPECTRALVIPER is a self-developed sophisticated backdoor with orchestration capabilities.

Unknown threat actors breached and deployed ransomware on the network of Kyushu University Hospital. The actor gained unauthorised access to a terminal for research laboratory management and infected the terminal with ransomware, granting the intruder access to 43 patients' personal information and surgical videos. The hospital blocked the terminal from the network to prevent further damage and is working with the police to investigate the cause. The hospital contacted the affected patients and stated that the incident did not affect electronic medical records or other medical systems. The hospital reported the incident in a statement on 10 June 2026.

Unknown threat actors breached the Central Bank of Libya on 10 June 2026. The attack was detected in some information technology systems and digital services, prompting the bank to put in place emergency protocols and disconnect affected systems from the network. The bank's management stated that customer accounts and the operation of payment systems remained unaffected.

Iranian state-sponsored hacking group Handala (aka Handala Hack Team/ Hamsa) breached  News Agency NûJINHA on 6 June 2026. According to the agency, the attack deleted many published materials in the agency's Persian, Arabic and English sections and temporarily disrupted the broadcast by targeting the technical infrastructure. The attacker confirmed the incident in a tweet, threatening violence if the agency did not cease publication. The agency reported the incident in a statement on 6 June 2026 and confirmed that it would continue its work.

A previously unknown cyber espionage group, dubbed SiribClone by Russian cybersecurity firm F6, stole information from Russian military personnel between Mid 2025 and May 2026. The group primarily targeted members of the Russian armed forces stationed in border regions and combat zones, with the campaign appearing to be aimed at gathering battlefield intelligence by stealing files, monitoring communications and collecting sensitive military information from Russian troops deployed near the front line. The hackers impersonated women seeking romantic relationships or volunteers offering humanitarian assistance to initiate conversations with servicemen on Telegram and other messaging platforms before persuading them to download malicious applications or enter their Telegram credentials on fake websites. Victims were tricked into clicking malicious links under various pretexts, including being asked to test a new application or exchange intimate photographs through a secure photosharing application, which installed previously undocumented Android spyware named SafeLoveStealer. The malware can steal photographs, videos, documents, location data and other information from infected devices while also allowing attackers to remotely activate the targets microphone and record conversations.  In addition to mobile spyware, the group deployed previously undocumented malware for desktop computers, dubbed SiribGrabber, whose primary purpose is to steal files from infected systems. Researchers from F6 informed the public about the attack in a technical report on 4 June 2026.

Title (Company): Ministry of Foreign Affairs - Ministry of Economy - Tchap - Ministry of Interior - Ministry of Education - Ministry of Armed Forces - Ministry of Justice
Description: A threat actor named Misère breached the Tchap, a messenger used by the French government and administration, on 7 June 2026. According to a post the threat actor made on a forum, the breach occurred via a compromised account linked to the Ministry of Education. Data from 2023 to 2026 was then harvested from unencrypted public forums on the app. The attacker claims to have accessed data from the Ministries of Interior, Armed Forces, Justice, Foreign Affairs, and Economy, resulting in the exposure of 643,459 messages, 59,386 files, and 13.51 GB of data,  including some documents classified as "diffusion restreinte", or restricted distribution. On 8 June 2026, the French government confirmed the breach, stating that 73,467 individuals had been affected.

An unknown threat actor attacked Evanston Township High School in Illinois with ransomware that disrupted district systems, internet services, and computer infrastructure on 7 June 2026. The attack led to the closure of the school on 08 June 2026 and 09 June 2026, and the cancellation of summer school classes, sports camps, and other on-campus activities. The attack also affected phone systems, staff email access, and online resources, including Home Access Center. The district activated incident response procedures, hired external cyber breach attorneys and cybersecurity forensic experts, and cooperated with the FBI. The incident was disclosed on the website of the school.

ShinyHunters breached DentaQuest, a U.S. dental benefits administrator owned by Sun Life, and claimed to have stolen 234 GB of data in May 2026. On 30 May, the criminals stated that negotiations failed and thereby leaking the stolen data, exposing 2.6 million accounts, including names, emails, government IDs, and health insurance details. On June 2, DentaQuest confirmed on its website that its networks had been breached, and the incident caused “limited disruption” in customer service.

Russian state-sponsored group Gamaredon launched a long-term espionage campaign on Ukrainian targets by exploiting a WinRAR vulnerability to drop nearly fileless malware. The group used a weaponized XHTML file, likely delivered as a spearfishing attachment, to trigger a tracking request and deliver a RAR archive that exploited the CVE-2025-8088 vulnerability. The malware, which included components such as GammaPhish, GammaLoad, GammaWorm, GammaSteel, and GammaWipe, was designed to be highly evasive and persistent, using techniques such as HTML smuggling, path traversal, and NTFS Alternate Data Streams to hide its presence. The campaign was discovered by Sekoia’s Threat Detection Research team based on forensic artifacts recovered from compromised hosts, proactive threat hunting, and live payload acquisition, reconstructing a significant portion of an infection chain deployed in January 2026. The report was published on 1 June 2026.

An unidentified perpetrator breached self-registration application of World Food Programme for Palestine on 14 May 2026, exposing sensitive personal information belonging to some 600,000 households in Gaza. The attackers accessed the WFP's self-registration application for Palestine, compromising names, ID and mobile numbers, and location data. More than 2 million people in Gaza have submitted their personal information to WFP’s self-registration application, known as People Portal, which the WFP credits for cutting registration red tape and response times. The spokesperson said the compromised data is “isolated to the SRA application used only in Palestine”. The breach was only disclosed to the public on 31 May 2026, via a Telegram message to affected Gazans. The WFP confirmed the data breach on 2 June 2026.
