The German-speaking threat actors, using the pseudonym StrikerDE, breached the University of Saarland's Moodle learning platform in April 2026. The breach happened through exploiting an IDOR vulnerability, compromising over 40,000 user profiles, including names and additional information such as private email addresses, hobbies, or links to social media accounts. The attacker further attempted to blackmail the university. The university reported the incident to the police and the relevant data protection authority, and improved their security measures. The incident was first reported by the online magazine Tarnkappe.info on 07 June 2026.

China-linked threat actor targeted government agencies, research institutions, universities, technology companies and financial institutions using spear-phishing techniques in the Czech Republic, Taiwan, India, Cambodia, Panama, and South Korea. The victims were sent an email with a compressed malicious file attached to it. Users were tricked into opening a Windows shortcut file that looks like a PDF document. After the user opens the document, a Powershell script is activated. The attacker used Microsoft Azure's storage as intermediate storage for the stolen data in a ‘dead drop’ system. On 29 May 2026 Indian security software company Sqrite Labs reported the activity, naming the campaign “Operation Dragon Web”.

An unknown threat actor exploited a validation vulnerability in the bridge process of Syscoin (SYS) blockchain and generated approximately 5 billion unauthorized SYS on the networks UTXO blockchain in early June 2026. The attacker created the unauthorized tokens by exploiting the bridge relay path, which verifies transactions between two blockchains, and the system treated the fraudulent transaction as valid. The funds were initially sent to a single address and later distributed to various wallets. In an update posted on X Syscoin said that it paused its bridge and is working with exchanges to prevent the affected credits from entering open markets.

Unidentified perpetrators compromised the credentials of two company employees of Eversource Energy via phishing and social engineering attacks on 14 April 2026. The attack resulted in the exposure of personal information of more than 3,000 customers in Connecticut, Massachusetts and New Hampshire. The breach was identified on 27 April and additional security measures were implemented. The company notified utility regulators in all three states as well as state and federal law enforcement agencies on 21 May. The accessed information included names, mailing and service addresses, account information, phone numbers, email addresses, Social Security numbers, drivers license numbers, and financial account information.

NightSpire carried out a ransomware attack on Krum Public Library around 14 May 2026. The library detected unusual activity on its computer network on 14 May 2026, and the city disclosed the incident as a ransomware attack in a public notification on 3 June 2026. The attackers demanded an extortion payment and threatened to publish stolen data. A forensic investigation found that some files on the library network were accessed without authorization. NightSpire claimed to sell 50 GB of data taken from the library on its leak site.

Unknown threat actors launched a DDoS attack on the service portal of the Nigerian Data Protection Commission between 25 and 31 May 2026. The attacks were disclosed by the organisation’s National Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer Dr Vincent Olatunji, who reported that the portal had been subjected to over 2000 attacks within the span of a week. The Commission reported that the incident could be motivated by financial extortion or other motives. The incident was reported by the newspaper Punch.

Cybercriminal group ShinyHunters breached US telecommunications giant Charter Communications on 1 April 2026, resulting in stolen records contain customer names, email addresses, addresses, phone numbers, phone type, plan information, and some CPNI data. ShinyHunters said to BleepingComputer that they breached Charter on 1 April through a voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account. ShinyHunters claimed responsibility by adding Charter to their data leak site on 23 May 2026. Charter has confirmed the attack and stated that no sensitive personal information or customer proprietary network information (CPNI) data was exfiltrated by the threat actor as a result of recent activity.

Unknown threat actors compromised the personal computer of a nurse working at Fujita Health University Hospital in Toyoake, Aichi Prefecture, with ransomware on 25 May 2026. The nurse had stored patient data on the personal computer in violation of compliance rules, including names, dates of birth, hospitalisation dates and test data of patients with terminal renal failure, peritoneal dialysis and renal replacement therapy. The computer was compromised while browsing a website, and the stored data of 1,365 patients who visited the hospital between 2004 and 2025 may have been leaked externally. The hospital disclosed the incident publicly.

Title (Company): Meta - US Space Force Lieutenant John Bentivegna's Instagram Account - Archived US President Barack Obama's Instagram Account
Description: Unknown threat actors hijacked multiple high-profile Instagram accounts in late May 2026, including the personal account of US Space Force Lieutenant John Bentivegna and former US President Barack Obama's inactive Instagram account from his time in the White House. US Space Force Lieutenant John Bentivegna was misused to share images of Vietnamese radio host 'Hanoi Hannah' and spread anti-American content and Iranian propaganda produced by artificial intelligence. From Obama's account shared images with a comment 'The White House is under the control of Shiites'. Journalists from 404 Media reported that hackers used Meta’s AI support chatbot to break into a host of high-profile Instagram profiles by asking the support bot to change the email address associated with the target account. The accounts were later recovered by American authorities. On 5 June 2026, Meta revealed in a breach letter filed with Maine's Office of the Attorney General that 30 Instagram users had their accounts hijacked. The attacker exploited a flaw in the company's High Touch Support (HTS) tool, an AI-assisted support system that helps users regain access after being locked out of their Instagram accounts. In total, the accounts of 20,225 Instagram users are affected.

Iranian state-sponsored hacking group Handala hacking group breached the Holocaust Victim Support Centre's information systems on 31 May 2026, and leaked over two million documents. The group claimed that during the operation it extracted all the databases, documents, emails and confidential communications from the center with a volume greater than one terabyte. The group claimed responsibility for the attack in a statement on 31 May and argued that analysis of these documents reveals links and financial support from certain Israeli defense industry companies to the center’s activities.

Title (Company): IMSS - IMSS Bienestar - Conagua - Ministry of Public Education - Federal Civil Protection platform
Description: An individual hacker named azazeljakel breached the Federal Civil Protection platform in Mexico in 2026. In May 2026 officials’ data, including institutional emails and access passwords of public officials linked to various agencies, such as IMSS, IMSS Bienestar, Ministry of Security and Citizen Protection, Ministry of Public Education, and Conagua were leaked. The threat actors gained administrative access to the system and published user records. The affected portal was taken down after the attack, but the exposure of data had already occurred.

Title (Company): Göttingen University Hospital - University hospitals in Tübingen - Augsburg University Hospital - Ulm University Hospital - Unimed - Bonn University Hospital - Hannover University Hospital - Hamburg-Eppendorf University Hospital - Schleswig-Holstein University Hospital - University hospitals in Heidelberg - Pirmasens Hospital - University hospitals in Freiburg
Description: An unknown threat actor compromised the service provider Unimed based in Saarland that processes invoices for private medical services resulted in the theft of sensitive patient data in mid-April 2026, including names, dates of birth, addresses, and billing-relevant data, from approximately 61,000 patients at Ulm University Hospital and other clinics in Baden-Württemberg in May 2026, including university hospitals in Freiburg, Heidelberg, and Tübingen. The hospital management was informed of the data theft a few days prior to the publication date. The Ulm University Hospital made the cyberattack public in a press statement on 21 May 2026. The hospital has stopped transmitting data to the service provider and is demanding clarification on the criminal offense with the hospital management. In late May 2026, the State Commissioner for Data Protection of Baden-Württemberg confirmed that, until now, 17 hospitals in Baden-Württemberg reported a data breach. The Federal Office for Information Security was contacted and notified by the hospital. The breach also affected hospitals in Northern Germany, including the University Hospitals in Schleswig-Holstein (UKSH) and Hamburg-Eppendorf (UKE), resulted in the theft of data from around 9,000 patients at UKSH and over 5,000 patients at UKE. Moreover, the public broadcaster NDR reported that at least 6 clinics in Lower Saxony are affected by the breach of Unimed. In late May, the SPD faction in the Schleswig-Holstein state parliament calls for transparency and a complete clarification after the cyberattack. On 28 May, the president of the UKSH said in front of the Schleswig-Holstein state parliament that Unimed reached an agreement the hackers making it very unlikely that sensitive data will be published.

Title (Company): Unspecified Municipal Water And Sewage Utility
Description: An unknown threat actor used commercial large language models to aid in planning and conducting a cyberattack against municipal water and sewage utility’s OT of City of Monterrey in Mexico. The attackers used AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic. The threat actor used AI to generate malicious scripts, conduct the attack faster and more efficiently, and to provide feedback during the attack. The incident was reported by Dragos on 7 May 2026.

Unknown hackers stole emails from a senior executive's Outlook mailbox at a major global stock exchange between October 2025 and March 2026. On 10 October 2025, first malicious activities were observed on the target host. The attackers tried to conceal their activities and used legitimate cloud services (Dropbox and OneDrive) for exfiltration and their command and control (C2) infrastructure. The emails were exfiltrated in incremental batches. The researches from Symantec, who published the activities in a report on 3 June 2026, stating that espionage is the likely motivation of the attackers.

An unattributed threat actor breached Murray County, Georgia’s (USA) government network, which resulted in the closure of several county offices, including the Tax Commissioner, Tax Assessor, Probate Court and Juvenile Court offices on 13 May 2026. The ransomware attack affected public-facing county services, such as tax, assessment and court offices, but did not impact 911, public safety and primary voting operations. The attack was disclosed to the public through the Murray County Commissioners Office Facebook posts and public notices, according to WTVC. Murray County officials later confirmed that the incident was a ransomware attack and that the county paid approximately $200,000 to prevent the publication of the stolen data.

On 29 January 2026, HarfangLab published a report describing a new Iranian state-sponsored campaign dubbed "RedKitten" in which attackers were observed conducting a cyber espionage campaign targeting regime-critical individuals living outside Iran via WhatsApp, Instagram, and Telegram since December 2025, coinciding with anti-regime protests in Iran. The attackers used phishing tactics, including sending fake WhatsApp verification codes or links, and a fake web page that mimics the WhatsApp Web login screen with a QR code that belongs to the attackers' own WhatsApp Web page. This allowed them to gain full access to targets' WhatsApp accounts, including messages, browser, camera, microphone, and location information. The attack was initially reported by Nariman Gharib, an Iranian cyberespionage researcher based in the UK, on 13 January 2026, who described the techniques on GitHub and linked it to the IRGC.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: According to Kaspersky ICS CERT experts, a Chinese APT group known as TA428 (APT TA428/Colourful Panda/Vicious Panda/BRONZE DUDLEY) utilized Windows malware in targeted attacks on military-industrial-complex enterprises; public institutions; and government entities, such as agencies, ministries, and departments in various Eastern European countries (Belarus, Russia, and Ukraine) as well as Afghanistan. The bad actors penetrated and, in some cases, hijacked the IT infrastructure. The goal of this activity was for cyber espionage purposes. Penetration was achieved via spear-phishing emails, which in some cases utilized not publicly available information. The bad actors utilized five backdoors simultaneously, such as: PortDoor, nccTrojan, Logtu, Cotx, and DNSep. These five backdoors were used in previous attacks by APT TA428, while the sixth backdoor (CotSam) was newly observed.

In June 2026, Moody Bible Institute was targeted by a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. Over 2.3M unique email addresses and other personal data were later published publicly, including names, physical addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth and other information relating to donors, supporters, students and alumni. In their disclosure notice, Moody advised that they had "engaged both internal and external cybersecurity experts to thoroughly investigate the matter".

Unknown Threat Actors launched an attack on US-based River Bank Trust from 16 to 19 June 2026. The attackers deployed ransomware across portions of River Bank Trust's server environment. The attack was discovered on 19 June 2026 and disclosed to the SEC by River on 25 June 2026.

Unknown Threat Actors disrupted the administration of Furtwangen in Germany between 29 June and 3 July 2026. The attack caused a widespread IT disruption. Municipal committees, and several meetings were cancelled as officials could not access documents. The attack was reported by the town administration on 30 June 2026.

Russian cybercriminal group "The Gentlemen" exfiltrated data from TKMS subsidiary Atlas Elektronik, a marine defense supplier, between 26 and 28 June 2026. The company is a supplier to the German and US navy, among others. The Gentlemen listed TKMS / Atlas Elektronik on their leak site and published a contract between a Thyssen and an Atlas manager, as well as excel and word files on 25 June 2026. A TKMS spokesman confirmed the attack, stating that a North American company site working with the US military had been attacked, and that no security relevant data had been stolen.

Threat actors using the alias „ChimeraZ“ breached the municipal police of Le Pontet, in the Vaucluse department of France, by infiltrating their network and publishing sensitive data, including postal addresses, phone numbers, and administrative elements, on the darknet on 30 June 2026. The data leak, which contained nearly 60,000 elements of files, including registrations, reports, and intervention data, user identifiers, and other personal information, covered the period from January 2022 to 29 June 2026.

Unknown threat actors breached Aflac Japan, stealing data of 4,38 million customers on 15 June 2026. The attackers accessed the Aflac Yoriso Net customer portal and other systems, exfiltrating personal data, including names, addresses, dates of birth, sex, phone numbers, banking information, and coverage details. For about 230,000 customers, information about premium payment accounts was also compromised. The company detected the intrusion on 25 June 2026 and reacted by immediately suspending the affected systems.

Unknown threat actors breached the Homeland Security Information Network (HSIN) in the United States in June 2026. HSIN is an official plattform of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and is used to share sensitive but unclassified information between a variety of government- and private partners. The DHS took action to isolate the affected systems, mitigate the vulnerability, and launch a comprehensive forensic investigation. Nextgov/FCW informed the public about the incident on 30 June 2026.

The ransomware group ShinyHunters breached employee data from a Nissan subsidiary in United States in May or June 2026. On 25 June 2026, Nissan published a breach notification in which they say that they were notified by Oracle that Nissan was specifically targeted in a campaign with widespread exploitation of a zero-day in Oracle's PeopleSoft software. Thereby, Nissan believes some personal information has been accessed, including contact and banking information, Social Security Number, Social Insurance Number, National Identification Number, financial and tax data, and dependent beneficiary information. Particularly former Nissan employees from U.S.A., Canada, Mexico, and Brazil are likely to be affected. BleepingComputer links the incident to ShinyHunters who are believed to be responsible for the campaign between 27 May and 9 June 2026.

The Blackfield ransomware group breached a subsidiary of Nidec Corporation, a Japanese manufacturer of electronic components for automotive and computing applications, in Taiwan in June 2026. The group claimed on their leak page that they have stolen more than 2TB of data. Nidec confirmed a ransomware attack in a Taiwanese subsidiary. Moreover, the company said that to prevent the spread of the damage, emergency measures were taken, including shutting down the affected server and network. The incident was reported to external specialised agencies and relevant administrative organs which launched an investigation to identify its cause.

An unknown threat actor exploited a vulnerability in code of a third-party vendor of Polymarket, one of the world's largest cryptocurrency-based prediction markets, and stole $3 million from 15 customers on 25 June 2026. Polymarket says it will fully reimburse customers who lost an estimated $3 million after hackers injected a malicious script into the platform's frontend following a breach at a third-party vendor. During the attack, unsuspecting users were tricked into approving fraudulent transactions on the official Polymarket website after malicious JavaScript was injected through a frontend vendor. Polymarket’s own servers and backend infrastructure were not impacted by the incident. The security firm PeckShield said that the incident was a phishing campaign that stole approximately $3 million worth of ParyonUSD from users. The stolen funds were later swapped for 1,893 Ether.

The Kairos extortion group breached the Council of Valdemoro on 05 May 2026. The attack affected the council's computer systems, leading to the suspension of municipal services, including the tax payment gateway and electronic document registration. The council modified the fiscal calendar for the Property Tax (IBI) and the Solid Urban Waste Collection Rate to guarantee the correct functioning of the collection process and offer legal security to taxpayers. Various cybersecurity portals reported that the attackers obtained up to 1.8 terabytes of documentation, including personal data, Local Police reports, identity documents, and administrative files. The group publicly claimed the attack and demanded a ransom on 11 May 2026.

In July 2026, Brinks Home was targeted in a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group subsequently published data they alleged was taken from the company, including 732k unique email addresses and other personal information relating to leads, customers and Brinks staff such as name, phone numbers and physical addresses. The data also included purchases from Brinks along with partial credit card data (last 4 digits, card type and expiry). In Brinks' disclosure notice, they acknowledged the incident and risk of disclosure, and advised that they would notify impacted parties "consistent with applicable law".

In August 2026, clothing retailer Carhartt was the target of a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group subsequently published data allegedly obtained from the company including 12.9M unique email addresses, names, phone numbers and physical addresses. The published corpus also contained millions of synthetic records that did not relate to real individuals and were excluded from the breach.

In August 2026, the Alcon eye care company was named in a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group subsequently published data allegedly sourced from Alcon containing 218k unique email addresses along with other largely corporate B2B contact fields, including name, phone number and physical address.

In July 2026, Exact Sciences (now owned by Abbott Laboratories) was the target of a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group claimed to have obtained data from the company's cancer diagnostics business, which they later published publicly. The breach contained 10.9M unique email addresses belonging to customers, patients and healthcare providers, along with names, addresses, phone numbers and health records. Abbott subsequently published a public notice advising that "some of the impacted files contain personal information and/or personal health information" and that more specific information would follow once their review of the incident was complete. For context, Exact Sciences is the maker of the Cologuard at-home colorectal cancer screening test.
LINDDUN categories: Linkability, Identifiability, Disclosure of information, Non-compliance

Description: In August 2026, the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW) identified unauthorised access to the Fanlore wiki it operates. The breach resulted in the exposure of 145k unique email addresses along with usernames and passwords stored as either MD5 or PBKDF2 hashes. OTW self-submitted the exposed data to HIBP.

In July 2026, electronic test and measurement equipment company Fluke was targeted in a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group subsequently published more than 100GB of data allegedly taken from the company. The corpus contained largely corporate contact information, including over 800k unique email addresses, names, phone numbers and physical addresses. A large collection of support cases was also present.

In June 2026, Glendale Community College was the target of a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. Data allegedly obtained from Glendale was later published online and included almost 800k unique email addresses along with various other data fields, including names, addresses, phone numbers, Social Security numbers and other information relating to student enrolments. In its disclosure notice, the college advised that "the potentially impacted information may vary for each individual and may include all or just one of the above-listed types of information".

In mid-2026, hundreds of thousands of user records allegedly sourced from Golf Canada began circulating via Telegram. The data included 569k unique email addresses along with names, usernames, dates of birth, genders and approximate geographic locations (city, province and postcode). It remains unclear whether the data was obtained via unintentionally exposed website features or a security vulnerability.

In June 2026, a party claiming to have access to data from Goose Creek Candle Company sent emails to a number of the company's customers, claiming the company had a security vulnerability and suffered a data breach. The data was subsequently sent to Have I Been Pwned and contained 6.6M unique email addresses along with names, phone numbers, physical addresses, order IDs and total spent. The data appears to have been obtained from the company's Shopify instance. Goose Creek is aware of the reports but was unable to provide Have I Been Pwned with any further information at the time of publication.

In June 2026, Houston City College was the target of a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. Data allegedly obtained from the college was later published publicly and included 832k unique email addresses along with names, addresses, phone numbers, academic records, and other personal information relating to both current students and alumni.

In June 2026, Inter-Con Security was targeted in a ShinyHunters “pay or leak” extortion campaign. The group subsequently published data it alleged was taken from the company, including 276k unique email addresses along with names, physical addresses, job titles and phone numbers. The data encompassed a combination of contacts, internal users and leads.

In July 2026, the cloud-based business communications platform RingCentral was the target of a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group subsequently published data they claimed was obtained from the platform, which included 1.6M unique email addresses along with names, physical addresses and phone numbers. In their disclosure notice, RingCentral advised that the incident affected "a limited portion of RingCentral customers" and that it was communicating directly with those affected.

In March 2026, hackers claimed they had obtained data from the gig economy platform Paidwork which they then listed for sale. Almost 11GB of data allegedly obtained from the platform was subsequently posted publicly in July and contained over 23M unique email addresses. The breach also included a broad range of other data relating to the operation of the platform including user profile data, banking information, payout history for workers and passwords stored as bcrypt hashes.

In August 2026, Australian beauty retailer Oz Hair and Beauty was the target of an xpl0itrs extortion attack. The group subsequently published data allegedly obtained from the company, which included 2M unique email addresses along with names, phone numbers, geographic locations (suburb and postcode) and purchases.

In July 2025, the German news service NIUS suffered a data breach which was subsequently leaked publicly. The data included 6k unique email addresses along with names, physical addresses and payment details for purchases including either IBANs or partial credit card data (masked card number, type and expiry).
LINDDUN categories: Linkability, Identifiability, Disclosure of information, Non-compliance

Description: In July 2026, the Russian VPN service SplitVPN (previously known as NotVPN) suffered a data breach. The incident exposed millions of customer records, including 865k unique email addresses. Other impacted data included IP addresses, the user's country, and partial payment card data (first 6 and last 4 digits plus expiry date).

In November 2025, AI music generation tool Suno suffered a data breach that later came to light in July the following year. The data contained over 55M unique email addresses. Phone numbers were also present where they had been used as the sign-up method. Although representing a small portion of the corpus, the breach also included tens of thousands of Stripe records relating to purchases, containing names, physical addresses, purchase amounts and partial credit card data including the card type, expiry date and last 4 digits. The company advised that "Suno does not have access to customers' full credit card numbers in Stripe".

Unknown threat actors gained unauthorised access to the business email system of the municipal secretariat of Martigny-Combe in Switzerland on 18 August 2026. The attacker sent fraudulent messages to be contacts of the administration. The affected access was blocked immediately after the incident was detected, and technical security measures were taken.

The pro-Russian hacker group "Server Killers" launched a series of DDoS attacks against Norwegian institutions, disrupting services used by citizens, businesses, and public agencies starting on 24 August 2026. The DDoS attacks, which began at 03:38 CEST, targeted infrastructure operated by the Norwegian Digitalisation Agency, Digdir, together with its service provider Vivicta. The attack affected several shared services, including IDporten, MinID, Maskinporten, eFormidling, and eInnsyn. The disruption also affected parts of Norway’s health infrastructure, with several health services relying on IDporten for authentication. Digdir reported that several shared services became completely unavailable for short periods, while others remained accessible but suffered connection failures, slow responses, and longer-than-usual login times. Server Killers self-attributed the attack in a Telegram post on 26 August 2026, declaring "cyber war" against the Norwegian government for its renewed support for Ukraine on 23 August 2026.

Title (Company): SickKids Foundation - Hospital for Sick Children
Description: Unattributed hackers breached the careers website of the Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids) in Canada, stealing employee data in August 2026. The threat actor exploited a vulnerability in a third-party software application used by SickKids and other organisations, briefly taking down the hospital's careers website and exfiltrating personal information belonging to current and former employees, job applicants, and employees of related organisations including Boomerang and the SickKids Foundation. Clinical systems and patient information were not affected, and patient care continued as usual. SickKids launched an investigation with the support of external cybersecurity experts, offered affected individuals 24 months of complimentary credit monitoring and identity protection services, and disclosed the incident publicly on 20 August 2026.

Unknown threat actors breached the eProtec platform of French civil defence organisation Protection Civile, exfiltrating data belonging to several thousand volunteers in March 2026. The stolen data included civil status information, phone numbers and profile photos, including photos of minors. Frenchbreaches reported that over 525,000 profiles had been exfiltrated from the database, though the Civil Protection association disputed this figure, citing duplicate entries in the file. The National Civil Protection Federation discovered the breach on 17 August 2026..

An Iran-linked threat actor disrupted a small British gas-fired peaker power plant for four days in July 2026, in what was reported as the first successful cyberattack of its kind to bring down a UK power generation facility. The incident, first reported by The Sunday Telegraph, was confirmed by the British government, which declined to identify the affected facility or provide further detail, citing security reasons, though it did not dispute the attribution to Iran. Energy Minister Michael Shanks and other government spokespeople stated that the national energy system was never at risk. He further noted that the plant was small-scale, fell well below the legal threshold requiring generators to notify authorities of cyber activity and was not essential to the wider electricity supply. The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) reportedly received no notifications of power outages in connection with the incident.

Title (Company): Velilla de San Antonio Town Hall
Description: Cybercriminal group Kairos claimed to have breached the municipality of Velilla de San Antonio in Spain, stealing 77.6 GB of information on 21 August 2026. The group claimed on social media to have accessed administrative and personnel records, electronically signed official documents, municipal motions, personal data and national identity documents. On 28 August, the municipality confirmed that the threat actors had published the exfiltrated data. Municipal services continued operating normally throughout. The council notified the National Cryptologic Centre and other relevant authorities.

Cybercriminal group xpl0itrs claimed to have compromised the infrastructure of Gruppo Spaggiari Parma, one of Italy's main technology providers for the education sector, and to have stolen 6.1 TB of data belonging to more than 3,000 schools between 30 June and 20 August 2026. The claimed breach targeted the Modulistica Smart component of the Bergantini platform, used for compiling and submitting forms online, within Spaggiari's ClasseViva electronic register ecosystem. The group claimed the stolen data included identity documents, contact details, and personal information belonging to students and teachers, as well as medical information concerning students, and set a ransom deadline of around 27 August 2026. Spaggiari confirmed an intrusion had occurred and notified the Data Protection Authority, the National Cybersecurity Agency, and the Judicial Police Authority, stating that school data belonging to teachers and children remained safe.

Title (Company): Unspecified Private Certification Agency - Blue House
Description: Unknown threat actors breached a private certification agency server in South Korea, exposing personal information belonging to key figures including high-ranking officials at the presidential office, known as the Blue House, on 20 August 2026. Police confirmed that only basic information, such as names, affiliations, and phone numbers, was exposed, and clarified that the Blue House's own server had not itself been breached. The National Police Agency's National Investigation Headquarters disclosed the incident and stated that an investigation was ongoing.

Unknown threat actors conducted a governance attack on decentralised finance lending protocol Term Labs, resulting in the loss of approximately $8.5 million from its vaults on 23 August 2026. The threat actor stole 2,843 Ether (ETH), valued at approximately £6.87 million, and 1.68 million of the stablecoin USDC, which was subsequently exchanged for around 1.68 million DAI. The attacker's wallet had initially been funded with 2 ETH from the Tornado Cash privacy mixer. Term Labs confirmed the incident via a statement on its social media channels, stating that all Term Meta Vaults had been shut down and DAO governance roles revoked, and that its direct borrowing and lending markets had not been affected based on its investigation so far.

Title (Company): Russian Railways - VTB Bank - Microolap - NEK.TECH - Goznak
Description: Pro-Ukrainian hacktivist group Black Spark, reportedly based in Russia, claimed to have breached Russian network traffic analysis provider Microolap between July and 19 August 2026. In a Telegram post, the group claimed to have compromised several systems, including an outdated version of Microolap's website and an old Bitrix24 customer management system. Black Spark also claimed to have exfiltrated and then deleted data belonging to several Microolap clients, including Russian Railways (RZD), Goznak, VTB Bank, VTB Leasing and NEC.TECH, and to have accessed Microolap's EtherSensor network monitoring platform. Microolap confirmed that some systems had been compromised but disputed the scope of the claim. The company stated that EtherSensor had not been accessed, that no sensitive information had been stolen and that the affected systems were isolated from its core infrastructure.

Unknown threat actors conducted a ransomware attack on Cameron Regional Medical Center in the United States on 18 June 2026. The hospital said it had no evidence that any exposed information has been misused, but that the breach could have exposed patients' protected health information, including patient names, addresses, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, drivers license numbers, financial account information, medical diagnosis and treatment details, dates of treatment, provider names, patient and agency identification numbers, treatment cost information, health insurance information and electronic signatures. The hospital took steps to secure its systems and engaged third-party forensic specialists to investigate the incident's scope, remediate the damage and restore access, and notified the public about the incident on 17 August 2026.

Unknown threat actors breached the cloud system of Heights Finance, a debt consolidation loan company, on 7 May 2026. Through gaining access to a cloud-bsed platform hosted by a third party, the attackers stole sensitive financial information and personal data of approximately 750,000 customers, including contact information, banking data, government IDs, and personal information shared during customer service interactions. Heights Finance published a warning to customrs and informed regulators in Texas on 17 August 2026.

Unknown threat actors breached the French telecommunications operator SFR on 2 July 2026. The threat actors targeted a management tool for analyzing fibre connections, which may have resulted in temporary access to data related to fibre subscriber lines, such as addresses, emails, or phone numbers. The operator immediately cut off the concerned access and put in place additional protective measures. The breach was notified to the National Commission for Information Technology and Civil Liberties (CNIL) and a complaint was filed with the Public Prosecutor.

Unknown threat actors encrypted files in a ransomware attack on Colombia’s Ministry of Justice on 2 August 2026. The attack affected part of its technology infrastructure and disrupted public services related to illicit drug monitoring and legal processes. The ministry confirmed the ransomware attack on 3 August 2026, but denied claims of a data theft.

Unknown threat actors targeted the Asset Recovery and Management Agency (ARMA), Ukraine's agency responsible for managing assets seized from criminals and sanctioned individuals, on or around 18 August 2026. The agency was preparing to select a manager for seized corporate rights in IDS Ukraine, one of the country's largest producers of bottled mineral water and beverages, when the cyberattack occurred. The attackers and their methods were not identified by the agency. Ukraine's security service, the SBU, investigated the attack, which was disclosed to the public on 18 August 2026.

Unknown threat actors stole data from the Latvian Road Traffic Safety Directorate (CSDD) on 8-9 August 2026. The attackers seized the data of 1.2 million private individuals and 200,000 companies, including names, surnames, payment information, vehicle registration plates, and addresses, with Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs ordering an investigation into the incident, warning of the risk that the stolen data could be misused by fraudsters, and that the involvement of a state actor could not be excluded. President Edgars Rinkēvičs called the leak "a significant threat to national security".

ShinyHunters carried out an extortion attack on US-based cloud-based communications platform RingCentral, resulting in the theft and leak of data from approximately 1.6 million accounts on 27 July 2026.  Affected data included email addresses, names, physical addresses, and phone numbers. On 28 July, RingCentral stated that it had been the victim of a social engineering campaign, and that they had stopped all unauthorised activity on its systems. ShinyHunters stated that they used voice phishing to trick an employee into giving them their password. After RingCentral failed to pay a ransom, ShinyHunters leaked the data on 3 August 2026.

Title (Company): Berlin Senate Department for Mobility, Transport, Climate Protection and the Environment - Berlin Senate Department for Urban Development, Construction and Housing
Description: Rhysida ransomware breached the department of mobility and the department of housing of the Senate of Berlin in August 2026. On 16 August, employees in two departments were notified that the internal IT has been interrupted due to IT problems. On 18 August, Berlin's Senate Chancellery announced that a forensic analysis revealed an infiltration of the closed network used by Berlin's administration and the IT of both departments has been shutdown to prevent further damage. The services of the district offices in Berlin were also disrupted. Moreover, the Senate of Berlin is working with the State Criminal Police Office (LKA), the Berlin Public Prosecutor's Office and the Federal Office for Information Security (BSI). On the same day, the public broadcasting RBB reported that sensitive data has been stolen, which was later denied by the Senate stating that only publicly available information was exfiltrated. On 28 August 2026, Rhysida ransomware group claimed responsibility for the attack by adding the Berlin Senate to it dark web leak side, demanding a ransom of 2 million Euro in Bitcoin. The Senate of Berlin refused to pay the ransom and subsequently 5.8 terabytes of data was leaked in early September. In response to the hack, the opposition has accused the Berlin Senate of not taking the consequences of the hacking attack seriously enough and the AfD demands an investigation committee for the cyberattack.

An unknown threat actor breached Bits of Gold, Israel’s largest cryptocurrency broker, through unauthorised access to a third-party data analytics network in August 2026, resulting in the theft of personal information of 200,000 customers, including names, national ID numbers, email addresses, phone numbers, IP addresses, bank account information, and open wallet addresses. The breach was detected by Bits of Gold, which then blocked access to the system and severed its connection to the data analytics networks information sources. The company reported that funds, private keys, passwords, CVV codes, and scanned ID documents were not affected. Bits Of Gold disclosed the incident on 16 August 2026.

Unknown threat actors conducted a ransomware attack on the Health Sciences Centre (HSC) in Canada in August 2026, affecting certain facility maintenance systems, such as heating, ventilation, and air conditioning, as well as door access. The attack was made public by the regional health minister Uzoma Asagwaraon, who said that the HSC is dealing with a cyberattack on 10 August 2026. Clinical services continued uninterrupted and patient care was unaffected. The incident was investigated by Shared Health, who engaged with expert third parties to resolve the incident as soon as possible.

An unknown threat actor launched a large-scale Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack on Threema, a Swiss paid secure messaging service, which disrupted its secure messaging service and caused severe communication issues between 11 and 12 August. The attacks targeted Threema's infrastructure, but not its OnPrem deployments, which run on their own infrastructure. The company communicated the service disruptions through social media, while Threema Work customers received updates by email. The attacks were reported by Threema on its blog and status page, with the company apologising for any inconvenience caused.

An unknown threat actor breached Cook Medical, when one of its employees was deceived by a social engineering attack, inadvertently giving an outside party access to certain company systems. The attackers compromised customer contact information for U.S. and Canadian customers, records of customer communications with Cook employees in Salesforce, employee names and company email addresses, and certain internal business files accessed via SharePoint. Cook Medical disclosed the incident on 12 August 2026, and reported that they had identified and contained the unauthorized access quickly on the same day it occurred. The company stated that they had no evidence that sensitive or protected data was accessed.

Unknown threat actors breached Sogang University in South Korea on or before 14 August 2026, resulting in the subsequent leak of approximately 180,000 personal information records of students and faculty members. The data included names, student IDs, affiliations, email addresses, mobile phone numbers, and encrypted integrated passwords. The leaked information is believed to have affected not only current students, graduates, and faculty members but also those who attended the university in the past. The university's Digital Information Department took emergency measures, including blocking the attacker's IP and restricting access to the service, and reported the incident to the Personal Information Protection Committee and the Ministry of Education.

Ukraine's Main Intelligence Directorate (HUR) breached the digital infrastructure of the Russian e-commerce company Wildberries, resulting in large-scale disruptions to the company's main remote customer service channel and partial destabilisation of its payment infrastructure on 10-11 August 2026. The attack, conducted by the Cyber Corps, was disclosed by the HUR itself on Facebook, stating it was part of an effort to disrupt an entity that helps sustain the Russian economy and its war effort against Ukraine. The attack followed a series of Ukrainian kinetic strikes against Wildberries facilities across Russia.

An unknown threat actor stole contact details of nearly 80,000 people by breaching the database of an online ordering platform for documents associated with Public Health France's prevention campaigns, hosted by a service provider in August 2026. Public Health France is a French public administrative establishment under the supervision of the Ministry of Health. The platform, moncoupon.santepubliquefrance.fr, was completely independent of the agency's other sites and only included contact data, such as email and postal addresses and phone numbers, for the delivery of ordered products, but no health data. According to French Breaches, the data appeared in criminal forum on 11 August 2026. Public Health France confirmed the figure and stated that as soon as the cyberattack was reported, the platform was put into maintenance and all passwords were deleted for security reasons. A notification was made to the National Commission for Information Technology and Civil Liberties (Cnil) for data breach. The teams at Public Health France were actively working to restore access to the service.

Title (Company): Witold Pilecki Institute of Solidarity and Valour
Description: Russian or Belarussian threat actors defaced the websites of the Polish Witold Pilecki Institute of Solidarity and Valour, as well as its branches in Berlin, Warsaw, and Augustów on the night of 13 to 14 August 2026. According to a statement by the institute, the attackers posted content that echoed Russian propaganda and promoted anti-Ukrainian narratives. The institute's IT team blocked the attack and took the affected websites offline. The Pilecki Institute informed the public about the attack on 15 August 2026.

A cybercriminal group known as ZeroBytes claimed to have infiltrated the official portal of the Directorate General of Public Finances (DGFiP) in late June 2026 and extracted the tax data of 678,438 French taxpayers, including 392,867 individuals and 285,570 professionals. The attackers claimed responsibility for the hack in a cybercriminal forum and published authentic samples of the stolen data on 12 August 2026. On 13 August, DDGFiP confirmed access and extraction of data concerning individuals and professionals, but does not disclose the number of affected people. DGFiP said that they immediately implemented new restrictive measures to stop it and prevent further illegitimate access. Thorough investigations are ongoing to accurately determine the data and the number of users involved. The attacker claimed to have accessed an internal search tool via a VPN access obtained after infiltrating servers. The exposed data included highly sensitive information such as names, dates and places of birth, postal addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, reference tax income, tax withholding rates, family situations, and numbers of dependents. Some records also contained a history of requests addressed to the tax administration. On 17 August, Agenzia Nova reported that French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu assembled a crisis inter-ministerial cell dedicated to the cyberattack. In early September 2026, French authorities detained an 18-year-old suspected member of the ZeroBytes hacking group.

On 3 August 2026, the systems of PharmaEssentia company and its subsidiary Panco Healthcare Co., Ltd. were breached by The Gentlemen ransomware group. The companies were listed on The Gentlemen's leak site on 10 August 2026, with the group demanding a ransom from Pharmaessentia. Pharmaessentia activated its defense mechanisms in response to the breach, called in external cybersecurity experts, and informed the relevant authorities. The attack had no significant impact on the company's operations, according to their initial assessments.

Title (Company): Municipality of Sithonie - Municipal Port Fund of Sithonia
Description: An unknown threat actor launched a ransomware attack on the municipality of Sithonie and the Municipal Port Fund of Sithonia in Greece in August 2026, which simultaneously affected the central administration and the management of ports and boat shelters in the region. The Hellenic Police's Electronic Crime Directorate investigated the attack, and the Personal Data Protection Authority was informed.

Unknown threat actors carried out an attack on the local government of Mitchell, South Dakota (USA), forcing local officials to shut down government networks on 6 August 2026. County officials were ordered not to open any emails sent from Mitchell's town government. Local newspaper "Mitchell Republic" reported the first reported incident after receiving a tip from a reader. Mayor Jordan Hanson declared on 13 August that the city's systems were up and running again.

Cybercriminals stole patient data from Polish medical software provider, MyDr at an unknown point before 8 August 2026, according to Zaufana Trzecia Strona, an IT security news service who had been contacted by the alleged hackers. The attack, which affected nearly 19 million Polish citizens, resulted in the theft of around two terabytes of data, including information related to medical consultations, prescriptions, and other documents used in patient follow-up, all from 2024 and before; samples of the data were sent to Zaufana Trzecia Strona. The incident was announced by Polish authorities, including Digital Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski, who stated that the attack was one of the largest cybersecurity incidents ever recorded in Poland. Around 12,000 medical facilities used the services of the targeted company.

Title (Company): Autonomous University of San Luis Potos (UASLP)
Description: An unknown threat actor breached the Autonomous University of San Luis Potos (UASLP) in Mexico in August 2026, which compromised several of its university systems, including virtual classes, and temporarily took the corresponding platform out of service. Through a notice to the university community, the Computer Science Division noted that the incident started on 5 August 2026 and that work continues to restore services and get systems to operate normal. The UASLP announced the extension of the deadline for payment and reenrollment, but did not disclose any additional details on the nature of the attack or the affected systems.

Cybercriminals breached the French Government's anti-telemarketing platform Bloctel, stealing 3 million telephone numbers on 11 August 2026. The Director-General of Competition, Consumer Affairs, and Repression of Frauds (DGCCRF) informed the public about the incident in a statement on 12 August 2026. Bloctel notified the affected consumers via email. The incident occurred the day before the planned closure of Bloctel.

Title (Company): Canton of Grisons - Federal Office of Computer Science and Telecommunications (BIT)
Description: An unknown threat actors compromised 200 SharePoint accounts managed by the Federal Office of Computer Science and Telecommunications (BIT) in Switzerland on 28 July 2026.  A similar attack occurred on the Canton of Grisons' SharePoint servers, which hosted the cantonal administration's website. In contrast to the attack on the BIT, there were no indications of compromised accounts or data loss, as confidential information and sensitive personal data were not stored on the affected servers. Nevertheless, the BIT announced that a detailed analysis revealed no data loss. The Computer Office of the Canton of Grimson assured that detailed analyses were ongoing and announced an extraordinary update to correct security vulnerabilities, resulting the website being inaccessible for several hours from 7 pm on 05 August 2026. The ePortal and specialist applications of the Canton of Grisons remained operational during the update. The Cantonal Computer Office informed the public about the attack in a statement on 05 August 2026. The incident was made public by the BIT and the Canton of Grimson on 4 and 5 August 2026.

Hackers with suspected ties to the Chinese government launched a "near-autonomous" AI-enabled cyberattack on government of Taiwan, extracting over 2,500 personnel records and compromising at least 85 government accounts from 1 July to 4 July 2026. The attackers used two popular open-source AI frameworks, Hermes and OpenClaw, to set up the operation, which was discovered by Israeli cyber firm Dream through an online archive of 160 megabytes and nearly 1,400 files. The attack employed up to eight autonomous agents simultaneously to map 21 government systems, and expanded to hit a nuclear safety agency and at least seven energy companies. The attackers bypassed the agents' safety guardrails by framing the work as authorised penetration testing, and the tool continuously ranked and reprioritised possible attack paths based on available evidence. The attack was initially reported by Israeli cybersecurity company Dream on August 12, which attributed the attack Chinese-speaking threat actors; Dream specified that the attackers used simplified Chinese characters (spoken mostly in the PRC) for internal status reports. Dream also stated that the receiver government was located in Asia, and that traditional Chinese was used in target-facing analysis; Financial Times therefore reported that a person with knowledge of the attack stated that Taiwan was the target. The Taiwanese Ministry of Digital Affairs declined to comment on the incident.

Title (Company): Croatian Interior Ministry - Croatian Automobile Club - Croatian Pension Insurance Institute - Central Register of Pension-Insured Persons - Croatian Regulatory Agency for Network Activities - Croatian Tax Administration - Croatian Health Insurance Fund
Description: On or around 28 July 2026, Serbian businessman, Georgije V., was arrested in Croatia for allegedly hacking into the computer systems of various Croatian state institutions and public agencies from 1 April to 30 April 2026.  The targets included the Croatian Interior Ministry, the Central Register of Pension-Insured Persons, the Croatian Health Insurance Fund, the Croatian Regulatory Agency for Network Activities, the Croatian Pension Insurance Institute, the Croatian Tax Administration, and the Croatian Automobile Club. The matter was reported by Croatian daily Jutarnji list on 6 August 2026, after Croatia's Chief State Attorney, Ivan Turudic, initially sparked public interest announcing work on a case related to national security. According to Jutarnji (citing unnamed sources), the suspect raised suspicion of ties to Serbian Intelligence Agency (BIA) which are being investigated as of 13 August 2026.

An unknown threat actor carried out a ransomware attack on AME, the technology provider of the Vincennes Community School Corporation in the United States. The Vincennes Community School Corporation shut down its servers as a precautionary measure, resulting in phones and internet being unavailable at the school corporation building. The district reported that none of its data had been compromised. The attack was disclosed to the public by the Vincennes Community School Corporation through a social media post on 4 August 2026.

An unknown threat actor launched a ransomware attack on the City of Coweta in Oklahoma in the United States on 5 August 2026. The threat actor used a ransomware known as Anubis and encrypted local files, including Word documents and Excel spreadsheets as well as multiple municipal financial systems. The attackers demanded a ransom, but city officials refused to communicate with them or pay the ransom. Emergency services were not affected as they run on separate networks. The city said it was working with IT professionals, cyber insurance, local police, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation to investigate the incident. The city reported the incident to the public on 7 August 2026.

The RansomHouse launched ransomware attack on Techventures Bank S.A. in Romania in August 2026. The Romanian National Directorate of Cyber Security (DNSC) announced on 4 August 2026 that it provided assistance to the bank after the incident was reported to DNSC on 2 August. The authorities collaborated with the bank to limit the effects of the attack and investigate the incident. On 6 August 2026, RansomHouse claimed responsibility for the attack on its leak site.

An unknown threat actor launched a ransomware attack on the Indian hosting provider Host DZire on 5 August that affected several VMware ESXi virtualisation nodes, resulting in the encryption of virtual disks and total loss of data on the affected nodes. The attack, which occurred around 2 AM UTC, is believed to have exploited a recently disclosed VMware vulnerability, affecting VMware-based services in India, the Netherlands, and the United States. The hosting provider subsequently initiated a complete rebuild of its infrastructure and deployed replacement services, although lost data could not be recovered without external backups. KVM and Leaseweb VPS services remained unaffected.

An unknown threat actor breached two New Jersey municipal water systems in the United States in the week from 31 July to 1 August 2026. The attackers targeted internet-exposed control systems, temporarily limiting operators' ability to monitor or manage them remotely. Staff was forced to shift to manual operations. Officials stated that service remained uninterrupted and drinking water was safe throughout the incident. The New Jersey Cybersecurity and Communications Integration Cell (NJCCIC) is working with the affected utilities, along with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to investigate the attacks.

Title (Company): Department for Education (DfE) - Police National Legal Database (PNLD)
Description: Previously unknown ransomware group ExfilSquad breached the UK's Department for Education (DfE) and the Police National Legal Database (PNLD), which provides legal assistance to UK police forces, in July 2026. According to the group's leak site, the breach exposed approximately 607,000 records relating to the department's helpdesk and the Turing Scheme, an international education funding programme, including names, email addresses, phone numbers, and job titles, alongside 135,000 records from the police database. The DfE confirmed the incident and stated it was working with the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO), the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), and the National Crime Agency (NCA) to investigate. The PNLD also confirmed the incident, stating that the stolen data included the names, employing force or organisation, and work email addresses of police officers and criminal justice personnel, but that no confidential victim, witness, or offender information was held on the database. ExfilSquad is reportedly demanding payment from the DfE and PNLD in exchange for not publishing the remaining data.

On or around 1 August 2026, the Panama Metro detected a cybersecurity incident of unknown origin in part of its technological infrastructure, and subsequently activated its response protocols to contain possible effects, with a technical investigation being conducted to determine the extent of the incident.

An unknown threat actor launched ransomware attack on the National Administration of Penitentiaries (ANP) in Romania on 28 July 2026, which affected several workstations and servers. The ANP's IT team immediately contacted the National Directorate of Cyber Security (DNSC), which intervened to limit the impact of the attack by physically isolating all equipment. The cyberattack started on 28 July around midnight and the first confirmed encryptions were detected in the early morning of the next day. The attack was reported by the ANP on the same day. Cybersecurity experts from the DNSC and ANP worked to limit the impact, remedy the problems, and investigate the attack. As a result of the attack, several services were unavailable due to precautionary measures.

Unknown threat actors disrupted the Constitutional Court of Guatemala, which affected the electronic mailbox and other key systems on 10 August 2026. The perpetrators demanded a sum of money to end the attack. The Court initially stated that it was experiencing temporary technical difficulties, but  confirmed on 11 August that its systems had been the object of a cyberattack, with temporary affects on some technological services.

Title (Company): Unspecified Organisations - Unspecified Organisations in the Aviation Sector - Unspecified Organisations - Unspecified Organisations - Unspecified Organisations - Unspecified Organisations in the Financial Sector - Unspecified Organisations - Unspecified Organisations in the Telecommunications Sector - Unspecified Organisations - Unspecified Organisations - Unspecified Organisations - Unspecified Small and Medium-Sized Businesses; Government Entities
Description: The Iran-nexus threat actor Mirage Kitten (aka UNC1549, Smoke Sandstorm, Screening Serpens) used spear-phishing to breach critical infrastructure in the Middle East and Africa from April 2026, according to researchers with Kaspersky. The actor targeted small and medium-sized businesses and government entities in Jordan, unidentified organisations in Egypt, aviation targets in Pakistan, telecommunications companies in Ethiopia, and financial sector entities in Burkina Faso. The attackers sent recruitment-themed messages and fake job offers to targets, which, when opened, would install the group’s malware titled NightLedger. The group used previously undocumented malware, including a Windows backdoor known as NightLedger and two network tunnelling programs called ArcBridge and BridgeHead, to maintain stealth and persistent access. The attack was reported by Kaspersky researchers on 28 July 2026.  On 26 August 2026, Group-IB researchers published a subsequent report on the threat activity (tracked as Tortoiseshell); Group-IB expanded upon Kaspersky's initial reporting and stated that Mirage Kitten/Tortoiseshell was further observed targeting European states and the Gulf States: namely the UK, France, Albania, and Belarus, alongside Israel, Türkiye, and GCC member states.

Title (Company): South St. Paul water utility - Plymouth water utility - Maple Plain water utility - City of Braham water plant
Description: An unknown threat actor breached multiple water utilities in Minnesota in the United States on 26 and 27 July 2026. The actor targeted the operational technology systems of dozens of water utilities in Minnesota, including those in Braham, Plymouth, Maple Plain and South St. Paul. The attackers targeted the automated control functions of the utilities, however water and wastewater operations remained operational in most cases. The City of Braham briefly took its water plant offline after the cybersecurity incident was detected, urging residents to minimise water use. Plymouth reported that the issue was limited to equipment connected via cellular communications within the system. The attack was reported in a statement published by the affected cities on 27 July 2026. On 30 July, the NYT reported the cyberattack is believed to be carried out by Iranian hackers referring to unnamed U.S. and state officials and others familiar with the matter.

An unknown threat actor breached the inbox of an employee of IEH Corporation, a US defence and aerospace manufacturer, in a phishing attack that exposed its Microsoft 365 inbox, including emails and potentially export-controlled military data on 4 August 2026. The attack occurred when an employee clicked a link disguised as a Microsoft document-sharing link from a prospective business contact, entering their Microsoft 365 credentials into a fake login page, and handing an attacker full access to their inbox. The attacker accessed the company's mailbox, exposing emails, attachments, customer data, engineering documents, and potentially export-controlled information. No data exfiltration was confirmed. The incident was reported to the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in an 8K filing.

Title (Company): Departmental Fire and Rescue Services (SDIS) of Alpes-de-Haute-Provence - Departmental Fire and Rescue Services (SDIS) of Marne - Departmental Fire and Rescue Services (SDIS) of Alpes-Maritimes - Departmental Fire and Rescue Services (SDIS) of Landes - Departmental Fire and Rescue Services (SDIS) of Aisne
Description: An unattributed hacker breached five Departmental Fire and Rescue Services (SDIS) in France, namely those of Aisne, Alps-de-Haute-Provence, Alpes-Maritimes, Landes, and Marne, and exfiltrated at least 700 megabytes (MB) of employee data in July 2026. The cybercrime unit of the Paris prosecutors office was informed and an investigation was opened for fraudulent access to an automated data processing system and extraction of this data, which was entrusted to the Anti-Cybercrime Office. Two suspects were identified on 26 July.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - SonicWall
Description: INC Ransomware group (aka UTA0533) exploited two vulnerabilities in Remote Access Gateway SonicWall SMA 1000 as zero-days, affecting private and governmental organizations in multiple countries including Australia, the US, UAE, Colombia, Switzerland in June 2026. The vulnerabilities, respectively tracked as CVE-2026-15409 and CVE-2026-15410, were used to gain root access on VPN appliances before patches became available. The threat actor combined these vulnerabilities to compromise SonicWall SMA VPN appliances and obtain root-level access, allowing them to access stored or cached credentials, capture network traffic, and potentially intercept credentials processed by the appliances. SonicWall disclosed on 14 July 2026 that they are investigating multiple incidents related to these vulnerabilities. Between 17 July and 1 August, INC Ransomware added multiple victims to their leak site. The activities were attributed to INC Ransomware on 17 July 2026.

Possibly Chinese-speaking threat actors compromised Thailand's Ministry of Finance using an autonomous AI agent named "Hermes," running with minimal human oversight, alongside a custom implant referred to as "Hades," between 26 June and 13 July 2026. The threat actor exploited known software vulnerabilities to compromise several systems within the ministry's network, deploying webshells and gaining internal network access, with stolen credentials used to target the ministry's data infrastructure. Cybersecurity firm Hunt.io uncovered the activity after identifying exposed staging infrastructure hosted in Hong Kong, including logs showing the AI agent autonomously navigating the ministry's network and files. Hunt.io assessed the threat actor as Chinese-speaking with low to medium confidence and disclosed the incident on 23 July 2026.

An unknown threat actor disrupted the public safety communications systems of Suisun City in California in the United States on 7 August 2026. The attack forced the city to shut down its IT systems, halting emergency call routing, police and fire dispatch, records, and other city services. The city council declared a state of emergency on 8 August 2026 allowing for quick access to emergency support services and reimbursement for costs associated with the incident. Emergency services were rerouted through the Solano County dispatch center to maintain police and fire services.  The Federal Bureau of Investigation, Department of Homeland Security, and California Office of Emergency Services were informed about the attack and are working with the city to contain and investigate the incident.

Ransomware group "The Gentlemen" breached Portuguese public transport company Metro Mondego and copied customer data on 6 July 2026. The compromised data may include identification and contact information such as name, date of birth, address, telephone number, email address, photograph, and official identification numbers, alongside data belonging to individuals who had exchanged emails with the company. Payment card data was not affected, as it was processed on isolated systems. "The Gentlemen" listed Metro Mondego on its victims list and threatened to publish the compromised data on 16 July 2026. Metro Mondego disclosed the incident in a statement on 25 July 2026 and notified the National Cybersecurity Centre, the National Data Protection Commission, and the authorities responsible for criminal investigation.

Title (Company): Instituto Nacional de Antropología e Historia (INAH)
Description: The hacking group BlackHexBrotherHood stole and leaked confidential documents of students at the National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH) in Mexico on 5 August 2026. The group breached the systems of INAH and leaked 1.2 gigabytes of confidential documents of students with scholarships, including birth certificates, identification, ID numbers, proof of address, and bank statements on its Telegram channel. The incident was reported by journalist Ignacio Gómez Villaseñor on his X account on 7 August 2026. The INAH responded by issuing a statement on their X account stating that they were conducting technical analyses to determine the situation.

Unknown threat actors using the pseudonym "B133DR00T" defaced the website of Argentina's Mendoza Senate around midday on 24 July 2026, displaying a photograph of Argentine Football Association president Claudio "Chiqui" Tapia alongside a message criticising the country's justice system. The activity was reportedly conducted from outside Argentina and was accompanied by a post on X from the group, warning that they had arrived in Argentina and questioning what Interpol would do about it.

Unknown threat actors launched a ransomware attack on the City of Drancy, located in Seine-Saint-Denis, France, causing municipal systems to malfunction on 3 July 2026. The attackers demanded a ransom in bitcoin, which the city refused to pay, following recommendations from the state. The attack was discovered during routine surveillance by the city's IT agents, who filed a complaint with the specialised prosecutor's office, and technical teams disconnected all municipal servers to prevent the malware from spreading. The incident disrupted the city's computer services, causing complications, slowdowns, and degradation of public services, with data leaks considered likely although their extent remains unknown. Mayor Jean-Christophe Lagarde disclosed the incident on 21 July 2026.

The North Korea-linked threat actor Kimsuky targeted South Korean corporate Infrastructure between 2025 and early 2026. Kimsuky compromised vendor infrastructure by exploiting vulnerabilities in internet-facing mail servers or by conducting spear-phishing against employees. After the initial compromise, Kimsuky aggressively pursued lateral movement, including compromising customer groupware servers and stealing the vendors’ infrastructure credentials. The threat actor used known malware like Gomir and HttpTroy, which were attributed to Kimsuky in the past. Specifically, one compromise of a company was observed in November 2025 and another compromise of a second company was observed in December 2025. The activities were attributed and reported by the South Korean security company ENKI on 20 July 2026.
Techniques Used: Exploit Public-Facing Application, Phishing, Valid Accounts

Title (Company): X - Account: Marine Le Pen - Website of National Rally
Description: An unknown threat actor defaced multiple websites of the French Party National Rally on 21 July 2026. A visible modification of several pages of the RN website occurred, where Marine Le Pen's face had been replaced by a cat illustration surrounded by Algerian and Moroccan flags. The leader's X account was also hacked, with the dissemination of a message related to a cryptocurrency, deleted a few minutes after its publication. The incident was reported by the party to several media, including Le Parisien, France Télévisions and BFMTV, which confirmed the filing of a complaint for cybercrime. The party said in a statement to BFMTV that no massive exposure of personal data has been observed, but the accounts of a municipal candidates might be affected including information about his running mates.

An unknown threat actor breached the cryptocurrency wallet Zeus Wallet in the United States on 5 August 2026. The company reported that no loss of customer funds had been found and no vulnerabilities were found in the Lightning Node software. The company stated that it suppressed the attack but took its infrastructure offline out of an abundance of caution. Zeus posted an official security update to it’s official X account on 6 August.

An unknown threat Actor breached the large energy provider Origin Energy in Australia in July 2026. On 22 July 2026, the company published a press statement, saying that they are currently investigating a potential security incident which may involve unauthorized access to some customers' data, but do not  believe the impacted data includes customer credit card or bank details. Furthermore, the Australian Cyber Security Centre and the Australian Federal Police have been notified and the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner has been engaged.

An unknown threat actor breached multiple North Carolina ports in the United States on 4 August 2026. A spokesperson for the port confirmed that an outside actor or group had gained unauthorised access to the IT systems of North Carolina Ports in Wilmington, Morehead City, and Charlotte. The breach forced the organisation to shift to manual processing and enact a contingency plan. The port announced that it expected delays in the days after the incident. The US Coast Guard and multiple state agencies were informed about the incident.

The Gentlemen ransomware group compromised Oldelval, the company operating Argentina's main oil transportation network, affecting its administrative systems. The company, whose main shareholder is YPF, reported the incident to the National Securities Commission (CNV) and activated its cybersecurity protocol, containing the attack and restoring administrative tasks without interrupting oil transportation. On 23 July 2026, the Gentlemen ransomware group claimed responsibility for the attack listing the company on their website.

Title (Company): National Agency for Cadastre and Real Estate Advertising (ANCPI)
Description: ByteToBreach, an individual hacker, breached Romania's National Agency for Cadastre and Real Estate Publicity (ANCPI) and, after extortion attempts failed, deleted data from the agency's systems in July 2026. The incident became public on 14 July 2026, when all of ANCPI's IT systems and services were disrupted, including the land registry service, the e-Terra cadastre, its website and email service. Some of the stolen data, including employee credentials, internal documents and details on the agency's IT network, was put up for sale on a hacking forum on 15 July 2026. On 17 July 2026, security firm KELA claimed that the individual behind ByteToBreach was Zakaria Mahdjoub, allegedly based in Oran, Algeria. On 19 July 2026, ANCPI published a statement on its restored website confirming that its IT infrastructure was undergoing large-scale reinstallation and consolidation following the incident, whilst disputing claims that all backups had been deleted.

An unknown threat actor breached the Hungarian State Treasury's computer network, specifically the Division for Agriculture and Rural Development, in August 2026. The attacker encrypted files on some employees' computers, affecting internal systems. Authorities isolated the affected servers to limit the spread of the attack. The investigation, conducted by the national cyber security centre and security services, suggests the attack may have originated from servers in Russia. The Treasury notified the institution responsible for data protection, and some electronic services are operating with restrictions. Daily News Hungary reported on the incident on 3 August 2026, citing the Treasury's announcement that there is no evidence of compromised or lost beneficiary data.

An unknown threat actor breached Intermarché, a large retail chain, which resulted in a significant data leak affecting approximately 300,000 customers of its Drive service. The attackers gained unauthorised access to personal data, including names, dates of birth, billing addresses, telephone numbers, and loyalty card numbers, as well as certain information related to online orders. However, banking data and details of products ordered were not affected. The attack was detected and blocked by Intermarché's teams, and an alert email was sent to the affected customers. The incident was confirmed by a spokesperson of the company to French Breaches.

Unknown threat actors hijacked an institutional email account of the Municipality of Piovene Rocchette's using phishing on 29 July 2026. The attackers sent a fraudulent message to contacts in the address book, containing a link to malicious software. The Municipality informed the public about the attack through a note from the municipal secretariat. The incident was resolved, and the unauthorised access was revoked on 31 July 2026.

An unknown criminal actor breach telecommunications company WindTre in Italy in February 2025. The criminals gained access to the company’s systems by posing as technical support staff and convincing operators at two retail outlets to grant access, resulting in the exposure of personal data of over 365,000 customers, including IBANs and credit card numbers for 41,359 users. The Italian Data Protection Authority imposed a fine of 1.7 million Euros on WindTre for violating the principles of integrity and confidentiality of data under the GDPR. The incident was publicly disclosed by the Italian Data Protection Authority on 17 July 2026.

Unattributed hackers disrupted the Loyalist College in Ontario, Canada, on 9 July 2026. The attack impacted various systems and services, including email, on-campus internet access, myLoyalist, Canvas, and college systems that support student registration and tuition and fee payments.
