The college confirmed the incident with a post on their website and notified provincial authorities and alerted its community through a website announcement. Online classes were suspended until further notice, but in-person classes continued, and the campus remained open.

The criminal group Anubis conducted a ransomware attack against Coca-Cola’s dairy subsidiary Fairlife, compromised parts of its IT systems, including production-relevant systems on 16 July 2026. The group claimed responsibility for the hack on 20 July, claiming to have stolen 1TB of data. After detecting the incident, Fairlife temporarily suspended production operations in the United States. Later, the company confirmed that data has been stolen.

A Russian threat group, allegedly linked to Russia's Military Intelligence Service GRU, targeted the drinking water plant of the 500-inhabitant municipality Saint-Noël in Canada on 23 July 2026. The attackers breached the plant's systems for less than an hour, which went into safe mode before the attack was detected by a municipal employee. The plant resumed its activities the following day. Mayor Gilbert Marquis informed the public about the attack in an interview with La Presse. According to Saint-Noël's Regional County Municipality of La Matapédia, a cybersecurity expert attributed the attack to an organized hacker group based in Russia. CBC reported that Z-Pentest, a group allegedly linked to the GRU, claimed responsibility with a video allegedly showing a cursor adjusting chlorine dosage settings in the water plant.

The criminal group ShinyHunters breached medical technology company Abbott’s Cancer Diagnostics Business in the United States on 16 July 2026. The threat actor stated that it had gained access to the company’s systems by compromising an employee’s Microsoft Entra single sign-on account using vishing tactics. Once the group had gained access to the account, they stole data from connected Software as a Service (SaaS) applications including Salesforce, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, SAP, Slack, Adobe, Atlassian, Zendesk and Dropbox. They claimed to have stolen internal documents, contracts and over 30 million rows of customer personally identifiable information from multiple datasets, including names, email addresses, phone numbers, home addresses, dates of birth and more than one million Social Security numbers. Additionally, ShinyHunters claimed that the stolen data included over 22 million client notes containing doctor-patient conversations and more than 20 million medical orders and customer agreements and NDAs. While the actor sent a sample of the data to BleepingComputer as proof of the compromise, the claims are not further verifiable. The company released a statement acknowledging the incident on 16 July. The threat actor claimed responsibility for the attack in a statement in BleepingComputer on 17 July 2026.

Unknown threat actors breached and exfiltrated data of a large number of employees of France's Ministry of National Education on 25 July 2026. The attacker took control of an account of the ministry, targeting the information system dedicated to staff training. The attackers may have exfiltrated personal details, including professional information, status, functions, postal addresses, phone numbers, and social security numbers of ministry employees who have worked in education since 2001. The ministry's information system security operational centre was alerted on 26 July 2026, and external access to the system was suspended.

Unknown threat actors targeted the town administration of Wriezen, Germany, on 17 July 2026. The attack compromised the administration's ability to work. Mayor Karsten Ilm confirmed the incident. The affected IT systems were taken offline as a precautionary measure to protect the systems and limit further damage.

Title (Company): Unspecified Organisations in the Hospitality Sector - Unspecified Organisations in the Telecommunications Sector - Unspecified Organisations in the Financial Sector - Unspecified Government Entities - Unspecified Organisations in the Transportation Sector - Unspecified Government Entities
Description: Russia-aligned threat actor TA488 (aka LAUNDRY BEAR, Void Blizzard) targeted US and European government entities, as well as organisations in the telecommunications, financial, hospitality and aerospace sectors, exploiting a bug in Microsoft Outlook Web Access (OWA), tracked as CVE-2026-42897, to steal emails and account credentials since around 22 July 2026. The threat actor used a novel infection chain culminating in a previously unknown JavaScript browser-based implant named OWAReaper, purpose-built for persistent access inside OWA, marking an improvement in the group's capabilities. Proofpoint disclosed the campaign on 29 July 2026, a week after the joint cybersecurity advisory attributing LAUNDRY BEAR's separate Zimbra Collaboration Suite campaign. Proofpoint noted that the earliest infrastructure used in this campaign was set up in March 2026, two months before Microsoft's out-of-band patch for CVE-2026-42897, raising the possibility that TA488 exploited the vulnerability as a zero-day.

The Everest ransomware group stole technical data from a supplier of the Eastern Swiss train manufacturer Stadler by gaining access to the data exchange platform using compromised login credentials in mid-July 2026. Stadler refused to pay a ransom of CHF 10 million and filed a criminal complaint with the Thurgau cantonal police. According to Stadler, the cyberattack did not cause any data loss for Stadler Rail, and the company’s internal systems remained unaffected. The stolen data has no relevance to train safety and does not include sensitive personal information. The incident was made public by Stadler in a press statement on 21 July 2026.

Unknown threat actors stole patient data from Partnered Health, an operator of over 57 clinics in Australia, on 23 June 2026. The attack was disclosed by Partnered Health on 15 July 2026, and the company listed 16 possibly affected clinics. The attackers stole personal data, including name, date of birth, address, contact details, insurance information, and sensitive medical records like pathology and diagnostic results, consultation notes, and referral letters. On 30 July 2026, the ransomware group INC Ransomware claimed responsibility for the incident on their leak page.

An unknown threat actor disrupted mobile voice, data and internet services of Unitel, an Angolan telecommunications company, across the country on 28 July 2026, affecting both individual and business customers. The incident was detected in the early morning and coincided with the eve of the company's share admission to the Angola Debt and Securities Exchange (BODIVA). Unitel's fixed telecommunications services, supported by fibre optics and radio links, remained operational, ensuring continued communication for various public institutions and companies. The company's technical and cybersecurity teams activated internal response and containment protocols, bringing the incident under control and beginning a gradual recovery of services. Unitel reported the following day that it had begun a phased restoration of the disrupted services.

An unknown threat actor stole £18 million from DeFi exchange Ostium via an exploit, by using a registered PriceUpKeepforwarder and predated authorised Oracle reports to generate artificial trading profits on 15 July 2026. The incident was first reported by the blockchain security firm Blockaid on X. Some of the stolen USDC coins were exchanged for Ethereum via the Kyber Network. The attack occurred shortly after Ostium's partnership with Nasdaq was announced.

Title (Company): Hachioji Academy's Hachioji Junior and Senior High School
Description: Unknown hackers launched a ransomware attack on Hachioji High School in Japan in July 2026, resulting in unauthorised access to and damage of some of the school's servers. The school disclosed the incident on 13 July 2026 and set up a countermeasures headquarters, working with the Hachioji Police Station, external experts, and legal counsel to investigate the cause and extent of the damage. The school's representative email address was unavailable during the investigation and restoration process.

An unknown threat actor breached Analog Devices, a Massachusetts-based semiconductor chip manufacturer, gaining access to certain systems and exfiltrating data on 23 June 2026. The company activated its incident response process, engaging outside cybersecurity experts and law enforcement, and disclosed the incident publicly in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on 29 July 2026. On 26 July 2026, ransomware group ExfilSquad claimed to have stolen over 570,000 customer records from Analog Devices, though the company denied any link between this claim and the breach detected on 23 June.

An unspecified perpetrator breached Séneca, a platform operated by Andalusia's Ministry of Education and used by regional educational centres in Spain, in July 2026. The threat actor exploited a security lapse after a user accessed the platform from a personal computer outside the region's protected digital environment. The regional cybersecurity centre detected the incident and secured the affected systems, and the investigation was transferred to the police.

An unidentified perpetrator breached two network operators, Netze BW and Stuttgart Netze in Germany in July 2026, affecting thousands of households. The attackers gained access to customer data records through a vulnerability in the systems of a third-party provider, which had taken over the installation of modern electricity meters in Baden-Württemberg households on behalf of the network operators. The compromised data included full names, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers and serial numbers of the installed meters, as well as recordings of the metering units. The attack was reported by the German regional public broadcaster SWR.

Unknown threat actors disrupted the systems of AnMed, a hospital system operating across the Upstate region of South Carolina and Northeast Georgia, forcing the closure of dozens of departments on 26 July 2026. AnMed disclosed the incident via a statement on its website, confirming that malware was impacting its network, and notified state and federal authorities. AnMed Medical Group offices and Imaging Services closed on 27 July 2026, whilst Urgent Care, Kids Care, Integrated Therapy locations and Laboratory Services remained open as scheduled. Offices were expected to reopen on 29 July 2026.

Unidentified hackers carried out a DDoS attack on the website of German public transport company Nah SH, disrupting access from around 10am on 13 July 2026. The attack made www.nah.sh intermittently unavailable, disabling the online information service, whilst the Nah SH app and shop remained unaffected. Spokesperson Dennis Fiedel confirmed appropriate measures had been taken, though the source could not be identified and the disruption was ongoing at the time of reporting.

Unattributed hackers breached US auto insurer AssuranceAmerica, stealing the personal information of up to 6.9 million people, after a targeted phishing attack compromised a single employee's credentials on 16 March 2026. The threat actor accessed parts of the insurer's IT systems and copied files containing customers' names, contact information, driver's license numbers, auto insurance policies and accounts, driver and vehicle details, and accident claims information, with some customers' Social Security numbers and tax identification numbers also compromised. AssuranceAmerica discovered the breach on 17 March 2026 and disclosed the incident publicly, sending notification letters to affected customers on 10 July 2026 following completion of its file review on 15 June 2026.

Chinese state-sponsored threat actors infiltrated Paraguayan government networks in 2026. The Paraguayan Ministry of Technology and Information (MITIC) announced on 10 July 2026 that in a joint cybersecurity review with the United States multiple threat actors were identified in Paraguayan government networks, which are linked to the Chinese government. A MITIC spokesman explained that while they continue to make the diagnosis of the impact, it can confirm that an exfiltration of data occurred.

Title (Company): Unspecified External Card Provider - Health Service Executive (HSE)
Description: Unidentified threat actors breached an external card provider of the Health Service Executive (HSE) and accessed a small number of HSE records on 26 May 2026. The HSE reported the breach to the Data Protection Commissioner (DPC) on 27 May 2026. The production of plastic cards, including EHIC cards, was paused, but provisional replacement certificates were provided instead. The HSE reportedly ensured that there was no reduction or change in the service that people received, and applicants were notified of their eligibility for the relevant scheme through a letter.

The cybercriminal group TripleX compromised the email account of a Bank of Baroda employee and leaked approximately 1TB of customer data on a dark web forum on 24 July 2026. The leaked data reportedly included savings account records, loan application documents, further identity numbers and internal records such as branch audit reports and vigilance investigation files. TripleX claimed responsibility for the leak, stating it had targeted the bank over weak passwords and security failings. Bank of Baroda confirmed the breach, stating that an employee's email account had been compromised, and that it had implemented containment measures and initiated a forensic investigation.

The ransomware group RansomHouse disrupted the operations of subsidiaries of Nichirei, Japan's top frozen food supplier, on 15 July 2026, causing system failures through unauthorised access. The disruption affected deliveries to clients including Kentucky Fried Chicken Japan and Kura Sushi Inc, a popular rotary sushi chain, prompting both businesses to warn of possible shortages and store closures. Supermarkets, pastry chefs, and elderly care centres were also affected by resulting shortages, according to local media. Nichirei disclosed the incident in a statement on 15 July 2026 and announced it was investigating and taking measures to restore its systems, with plans to gradually resume disrupted operations from 19 July 2026.

The threat actor GrayBravo (aka TAG-150) installed malware DenoRat and NightShadecC2 on the systems of a organization in finance sector in June 2026. The attack chain started with a ClickFix social engineering lure that ran a command from the Windows Run prompt when clicked, leading to an MSI file being downloaded and executed, which wrote and launched Griffin20.ps1, an AI-generated PowerShell. This stage installed or located Deno, then used it to fetch and run the next-stage called DinDoor, ultimately loading NightshadeC2 for command and control. The attack was reported by eSentire's Threat Response Unit in June 2026, which reported its findings to the public on 15 July 2026.

Unknown threat actors conducted a ransomware attack on Kootenai County, Idaho and exfiltrated data from the County's network on 30 March 2026. The affected information included name, address, date of birth, Social Security number, individual taxpayer identification number, driver’s license or state identification card number, medical information, health insurance identification number, and financial account/payment card information. For a small number of individuals, the impacted information contained a biometric identifier, such as fingerprints. The county immediately informed the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Chief Information Security Officer for the State of Idaho and the Idaho Attorney General of the incident and published a statement to inform the public on 22 July 2026.

Title (Company): Unspecified Drone Manufacturers - Database of Government Employees - Government application - Unspecified Shipping Companies
Description: A China-nexus actor compromised various organizations in Taiwan, Thailand and Afghanistan in June 2026. The attacker used the Large Language Models (LLMs) Claude Code and DeepSeek-v4-pro to assist in the intrusion. While Claude Code executed code, DeepSeek assisted with the offensive reasoning. The tools generated scripts, adapted failed exploits, created credential-harvesting pages, and executed commands. The targets included shipping companies and drone manufacturers in Taiwan, a database of personal information of Thai government employees and a government application in Afghanistan. The compromise was reported by Hunt.io on 14 July 2026.

An unknown threat actor breached South Korean pharmaceutical IT provider Cresoty on 7 July 2026, compromising its "EasyScanner" prescription automatic recognition service and leaking pharmacy and patient information. The threat actor stole pharmacist names, pharmacy business registration numbers, pharmacy phone numbers and email addresses, whilst the company's POS and payment services continued operating normally. Cresoty reported the incident to the Personal Information Protection Committee and the Korea Internet & Security Agency after becoming aware of it on the morning of 7 July 2026, and completed emergency measures pending a further investigation into the leak. The company disclosed the incident to the public via a report published on its website on 8 July 2026.

Title (Company): Unspecified External Service Provider - Industrie Werke Basel (IWB)
Description: Unknown threat actors breached an external service provider of Industrielle Werke Basel (IWB), the electricity and drinking water utility for the canton of Basel City, Switzerland, stealing data belonging to around 40,000 customers on or around 15 July 2026. The stolen data included names, addresses, and technical information related to energy meters but did not include telephone numbers, email addresses or bank details. The third-party provider promptly informed IWB, which restricted data exchange and initiated security checks, whilst the company's internal systems remained unaffected. IWB Board Chairman Claus Schmidt confirmed the incident and announced additional controls.

North Korean APT37 is suspected of having compromised the online education system of the South Korean National Diplomatic Academy (KNDA) in South Korea between April 2025 and February 2026. The KNDA trains candidates for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, as well as serving diplomats and senior officials. The threat actor gained access to the system by exploiting a zero-day vulnerability in the server software and misconfigured security settings. The attacker maintained access to the system for approximately 9 months, enabling the compromise of personal information, including IDs, names, emails, and encrypted passwords, of former and current employees of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The Foreign Ministry was informed about suspicious activity on the system by a related government authority in early February 2026 and immediately shut it down. The investigation is ongoing, and the ministry has not yet determined precisely what information was accessed or exfiltrated during the period of compromise. The attack was reported by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on 20 July 2026. According to media reports, the IT security company Genians Security Center assessed that the attack was likely conducted by the North Korean-linked APT37.

Members of Unit 61240 of the 16th Centre of the Russian Federal Security Service (FSB) (aka TURLA/ Venomous Bear/ Uroburos) gained unauthorised access to a server belonging to an entity in the judicial sector in France in 2019. Using custom malware tracked as TURLA, the FSB gained unauthorised access to the server. The breach was disclosed in a joint attribution statement by the EU and France on 13 July 2026.

The ransomware group World Leaks breached the systems of Reliance Infrastructure, a contractor for the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant, by exploiting a server hosted by third-party data centre provider Yotta on 29 May 2026, and leaked around 19,000 files, totalling nearly 14.3 GB, onto the dark web, including engineering drawings, vendor details, inspection records, and other project-related files, which were reportedly accessible online since 11 June 2026. The breach was reported by independent cybersecurity researcher Rakesh Krishnan, and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) is investigating the incident alongside the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) and Reliance Infrastructure. Yotta said in a statement it had noted suspicious activity on May 29 on a server it hosts that belongs to Reliance Infrastructure. World Leaks claimed responsibility for the breach, and the leaked information is believed to have originated from Reliance Infrastructure's systems. The Nuclear Power Corporation, which commissions and operates the country's nuclear power plants, said in a statement to Reuters that the ‌information said to ⁠be available in the public domain pertains only to common service facilities and does not relate to any nuclear safety or nuclear security-related systems.  On 16 July 2026, Jintendra Singh, Union Science minister, rejected reports that sensitive nuclear data has been compromised and stated that nuclear safety and security systems were unaffected.

Members of Unit 61240 of the 16th Centre of the Russian Federal Security Service (FSB) (aka TURLA/Venomous Bear/Uroburos) exfiltrated a significant amount of data from a research institute specialised in sensitive technologies and working for the French defence industry in February 2025. Using custom malware tracked as TURLA, the FSB gained unauthorised access to the institute's network and exfiltrated the data. The incident was disclosed in a joint attribution statement by the EU and France on 13 July 2026.

An unattributed hacker defaced the official website of the Kenyan presidency, replacing the homepage with a message targeting President William Ruto and demanding a ransom of five bitcoins on 18 July 2026. The attackers threatened to disclose unspecified information if the ransom was not paid. Kenyan Minister of Information, Communication and Digital Economy, William Kabogo, confirmed the cyberattack, stating that government cybersecurity teams were mobilised to respond to the incident. The website's functionality was fully restored on 19 July 2026

An unknown threat actor compromised the Low Emission Zone application of municipality through credentials that granted sufficient privileges to be able to steal user data in June 2026. Users of the application were notified by City Council of Ciudad Real. The City Council announced that they activated all security protocols to isolate the system and safeguard the affected information, and recommended those affected to be vigilant for suspicious communications.

The Gentlemen ransomware group stole and threatened to publish data stolen from Colombian Ecopetrol’s information systems on 17 July 2026. The attack affected cloud file storage environments of approximately 15 companies in the Ecopetrol Business Group, with around 3,300 user accounts affected. The attacker's attempt to hijack the company's IT systems was blocked by cybersecurity controls. The external actor made extortion demands, threatening to publicly disclose the illegally extracted information. In response, Ecopetrol activated its incident response and management protocols, revoked unauthorised access, blocked mechanisms associated with mass downloads of information, filed a complaint with the Attorney General’s Office, and deployed cooperation activities with national specialised entities. On 28 July, the company reported that external actors have published the information that was illegally copied from 15 companies of the Ecopetrol Group.

Homeland Justice, an Iran-linked threat actor, claimed to have breached Albanian Post's systems and published leaked internal staff emails on Telegram in March 2026. The attackers framed the action as retaliation against the postal service's alleged support for the Mujahedin-e-Khalq's presence in Albania. The leaked emails contained data on postal deliveries to individuals along with other internal information. Albania's Minister for Local Governance, Ervin Demo, stated that postal services continued to operate normally and that no evidence had emerged of systems or data having been compromised or encrypted, pending a detailed analysis by the National Agency for Information Society. The incident followed a claimed intrusion by Homeland Justice against the Albanian parliament's digital infrastructure earlier the same month.

Unknown threat actors carried out a sophisticated cyberattack against Delaware County in the United States on 26 June 2026. The attackers gained limited access to the county's network and some of the data stored on it. In a proactive step, Delaware County shut down their network, causing disruptions to the sheriff's office, district attorney, libraries, and county council. The county informed the public about the attack in a statement on 2 July 2026.

An unspecified perpetrator breached Champaign-Urbana Public Health District in the United States between 6 May and 7 May 2026, copying certain files from the district's computer network. The district reported that the accessed data may have included names, addresses, birth dates, treatment information, diagnostic information, health insurance information (including policy numbers), Social Security numbers and financial account information. The district noticed suspicious activity on its network on 7 May 2026 and subsequently notified state and federal regulators. The incident was disclosed through a public notice issued by law firm Mullen Coughlin LLC on 8 July 2026.

Title (Company): Leipzig Group - Leipzig Municipal Utilities (Leipziger Stadtwerke) - Leipzig Public Transport (Leipziger Verkehrsbetriebe/LVB) - Leipzig Waterworks (Leipziger Wasserwerke)
Description: Unidentified perpetrators carried out DDoS attacks against several internet pages of the Leipzig Group in Germany on 12 July 2026, overloading servers with a high volume of requests. The attack affected the websites of the Leipzig Group, Leipziger Stadtwerke, Leipziger Verkehrsbetriebe (LVB) and Leipziger Wasserwerke. The "Leipzig Move" timetable app continued to function without restriction. Technicians restored the websites on the same day. The Leipzig Group stated that no data was accessed during the incident.

Title (Company): Unspecified Polish Researchers - Unspecified Polish Journalists - Unspecified Polish Law Enforcement Employees - Unspecified Polish Political and Public Figures - Unspecified Polish Public Administration Employees
Description: UNC1151 aka Ghostwriter conducted a sustained phishing campaign targeting Gmail accounts of Polish citizens, with CERT Polska observing high-intensity activity since March 2026. The threat actor sent fraudulent emails in Polish imitating official Gmail administrator communications, directing recipients to fake login pages capable of harvesting both passwords and two-factor authentication codes (SMS-based and application-generated). Targets included individuals in political and public life, researchers, journalists, and public administration and law enforcement employees, alongside their family and social contacts. The group used dedicated phishing domains (registered under TLDs including .icu, .digital, and .top) as well as subdomains hosted on the Netlify platform and in some cases compromised Polish organisations' websites to host fake login panels. UNC1151/Ghostwriter has been linked to Belarus by Mandiant and other cybersecurity researchers in previous reporting

Unknown threat actors breached the district secretariat of mobility of Bogotá in June 2026. The hackers accessed an old database and stole personal data, licence numbers, SOAT policy, vehicle details, as well as photos and videos of infractions. The hackers claimed to have obtained data of more than 4.5 million users and published a sample of the data as proof. In July 2026, the secretariat of mobility of Bogotá confirmed that an old database was accessed and data was exfiltrated, but did not confirm the number of users affected.

A suspected Chinese threat actor tracked as UNK_MassTraction breached the systems of U.S. and Canadian universities to steal sensitive data and establish persistent access via webshells and backdoors starting in May 2026. The attackers targeted physics and engineering departments, focusing on administrators and professors with national security links or organisations researching astrophysics and particle physics. Cybersecurity firm Proofpoint informed the public about the attack on 07 July 2026.

An unknown threat actor breached Latvijas valsts meži (LVM), Latvia's state-owned forestry company and IT service provider, in June 2026. LVM took several systems offline including the LVM GEO platform, map services and the Mednis hunting application. CERT.LV head Baiba Kaškina stated the attack appeared commercially motivated. Minister for Smart Administration and Regional Development Edgars Tavars warned that the incident demonstrated vulnerabilities in Latvia's strategic infrastructure and called on government institutions to identify cybersecurity weaknesses. He confirmed that the electronic voter register, developed by LVM for upcoming parliamentary elections, was transferred to the state before the attack and was not compromised. LVM filed a report with the State Police.

Title (Company): US Army Artificial Intelligence Integration Center (ai2c.army.mil) - US Army Open Innovation Lab (oil.army.mil)
Description: Hacker "Kurdish sr" defaced multiple US Army subdomains on 6 July 2026 in a 404 hijacking campaign. The affected subdomains oil.army.mil (Army's Open Innovation Lab) and ai2c.army.mil (Artificial Intelligence Integration Center) displayed pro-Kurdish sentiments and insults directed at President Donald Trump and US Ambassador to Türkiye Tom Barrack. The defacement messages called to "FREE KURDISTAN" and included "Kurdish sr was here." The attackers exploited the websites' error-handling system to insert unauthorised content on error pages while the rest of the sites appeared untouched. The affected sites run on WordPress and Microsoft cloud infrastructure. Independent cybersecurity researcher Ronald Lovelace discovered the defacements and notified US Army officials. The Army took immediate action to secure the affected pages and investigate the incident. CyberScoop reported the incident on 6 July 2026.

Title (Company): Unspecified Israeli Government Entities - Unspecified Israeli Defence Sector Entities
Description: Iran-nexus threat actor Cavern Manticore breached government and defence sectors in Israel between March and July 2026. The threat actor gained access to target systems via a supply chain vulnerability, compromising trusted SysAid software. Cavern Manticore operated a modular command-and-control framework against its targets, utilising a .NET-based framework with uncommon compilation formats and anti-analysis measures. Check Point Research identified and named the threat actor in their findings.

An unknown threat actor stole $6 million from DeFi protocol Summer.fi on 06 July 2026. The attackers exploited the protocol's Lazy Summer contracts, specifically the LazyVaultLowerRiskUSDC pool, by using a flash loan to distort the internal liquidity and then withdrawing user funds. The attackers' address, exploit smart contract, and affected contracts were published by security company Blockaid. The incident was reported by Kamina Bashir on Yahoo finance on 6 July 2026. On 15 July, Summer.fi announced to wind down operations as a consequence of the hack.

Unattributed hackers deployed ransomware against the University of Alicante in Spain on 2 July 2026 in what the university described as the largest cyberattack the institution has suffered to date. The university's monitoring systems detected suspicious activity and alerted the Information Technology Security Division, which immediately activated preventive measures and deactivated certain services to stop the spread. The attack was limited to a few secondary servers. As a precaution, the university shut down UACloud (the intranet), remote access for workers and electronic administration, resulting in the suspension of legal deadlines for procedures. Essential services were restored within 24 hours. The university confirmed there was no data breach and that personal, economic and academic data remained safe. Diario de Alicante reported the incident on 6 July 2026.

An unknown Russian threat actor launched a DDoS attack on the website of an unidentified Ukrainian television channel in 2025. The attack lasted three hours, with the attacker using a botnet of compromised devices in Asia, Europe and the United States to launch up to 200,000 requests per minute. Head of the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) Cyber Security Department Brigadier General Volodymyr Karastelov disclosed the attack in a press release on 1 July 2026.

A threat actor using the pseudonym "Cenfecracked" breached the Citizen Attention System (SAC) of the Municipality of León in Mexico in July 2026, stealing a database containing personal information of approximately 250,000 citizens. The compromised data included citizen IDs, full names, phone numbers, dates of birth, address details and exact coordinates. The hacker posted the database on a dark web forum. The attack caused the institutional portal of the Municipality of León to be shut down for more than 24 hours to prevent further incidents, disabling digital platforms for paying fines and services, reporting urban issues, and access to scholarships and social programmes.

Title (Company): Unspecified Media Organisations - Unspecified Organisations in the Defence Industrial Base - Unspecified Law Enforcement Organisations - Unspecified Organisations in the Energy Sector - Unspecified Organisations in the Technology Sector - Unspecified Organisations in the Education Sector - Unspecified Federal and Local Government Organisations
Description: The Russian state-supported APT group LAUNDRY BEAR (aka TA488, Void Blizzard, CL-STA-1114) exploited a zero-day vulnerability in email software to steal sensitive information from various western government and commercial organizations since July 2025. To gain initial access, LAUNDRY BEAR sent phishing emails that trigger a zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2025-66376) in the webmail client of the Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS), once a user views the malicious email without requiring further interaction. After successful exploitation, LAUNDRY BEAR established persistent access to the systems and exfiltrated sensitive user information including Last 90 days of emails, email address, password, Global Address List (GAL), two-factor authentication (2FA) tokens, and newly-created Application Passcodes. LAUNDRY BEAR targeted and compromised users in various organizations in NATO countries and Ukraine, including those associated with: the Defence Industrial Base (DIB), the federal and local government, education, energy, law enforcement, media, non-governmental organizations, and technology. The activities were made public and attributed in a joint cybersecurity advisory released by various intelligence agencies and with contributions from Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 and Proofpoint on 22 July 2026.

Unknown threat actors breached one of CareCloud's six electronic health record environments on 10 March 2026, temporarily accessing part of the company's data and partially disrupting functionality for approximately eight hours. The affected system stored patient information, though the extent of patient data exposure remains under assessment. CareCloud's other data environments were not affected, and the affected system was restored the same evening. The company disclosed the incident in an SEC filing on 27 March 2026, noting it had notified its insurer, hired external technical support and informed law enforcement. According to a data breach notice filed with California’s attorney general’s office in July 2026, CareCloud said hackers had access to one of its electronic health record data stores for at least six days, between March 10 and March 16. On 30 July 2026, TechCrunch reported that nearly 350,000 people have been affected by the breach so far.

Scattered Spider hackers infiltrated Transport for London's (TfL) computer systems between 31 August and 3 September 2024. The attackers reportedly gained access through TfL's Cisco VPN. The Dial-a-Ride assisted transit service for disabled people was temporarily suspended as a consequence. TfL detected suspicious activity during routine monitoring and limited access. On 16 September 2024, the National Crime Agency and City of London Police arrested Thalha Jubair and Owen Flowers, at their home addresses. Both were members of the online criminal collective Scattered Spider. On 20 September 2024, TfL began notifying around 5,000 customers whose data may have been accessed.  Jubair and Flowers pled guilty on 22 June 2026. The hack caused damages of £39 million.

In August 2026, the French intellectual property software and services company Questel was the target of a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group subsequently published an extensive corpus of data they alleged was obtained from the company, largely comprising corporate contact information associated with sales leads, support cases and marketing activities, with 1.2M unique email addresses. The data also included names, employers and job titles, along with physical addresses and phone numbers.

In June 2019, the France-based art valuation website Artvalue.com (now defunct) left their 158k member subscriber base publicly exposed in a text file on their website. The exposed data included names, usernames, email addresses and passwords stored as MD5 hashes. The site operator did not respond when contacted about the incident, although the exposed file was subsequently removed.

In August 2026, Manchester Airports Group (MAG) disclosed a data breach impacting their services. The incident was later claimed by the FulcrumSec hacking group, who subsequently published email addresses and phone numbers relating to 8.8M customers of Manchester, Stansted and East Midlands airports. The data contained personal information relating to airport services, including vehicle registrations and parking history, Fast Track purchases and lounge bookings. In their disclosure notice, MAG advised that "at no point has passenger safety or aviation security been compromised".

In August 2026, healthcare and pharmaceutical company McKesson was targeted in a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The group subsequently published a substantial corpus of data they alleged was sourced from the company, which included 6.4M unique email addresses among other personal and corporate data attributes. The impacted data related to a range of individuals and roles, including marketing campaign recipients, patients, staff and healthcare provider contacts. In McKesson's disclosure notice, the company advised it had identified unauthorised access to "certain third-party applications and the exfiltration of certain data was associated with a subset of customers within our Oncology & Multispecialty and Medical-Surgical business units", but had "reasonable assurance of no ongoing unauthorized activity".
LINDDUN categories: Linkability, Identifiability, Disclosure of information, Non-compliance

Description: Unattributed hackers gained access to the network of the Springfield School Department in Massachusetts, United States, on 1 September 2026. The intrusion blocked the district's ability to access online programs needed to operate schools. This included student health records and transportation information. School officials first detected malicious traffic that day, though activity had escalated from minor disruptions the prior evening. The incident was classified as a districtwide Level 4 severe incident, forcing school closures for at least two consecutive days. The district asked students and staff to avoid using school networks and laptops to prevent further spread. Officials communicated with the school community via social media and text messages due to the loss of email access. Federal, state, and local law enforcement were involved in the investigation. Springfield city government's own systems were not affected.

Title (Company): Thomson Reuters - U. S. Virgin Islands Supreme and Superior Courts - Ontario Courts (Court of Appeal for Ontario, Superior Court of Justice, Court of Justice) - Multiple US State and Territorial Courts (Alabama, Kentucky, Montana, Nevada, North Dakota, South Carolina, New Hampshire, Wyoming, Pennsylvania county/appellate courts, Ohio Courts of Appeals, Tennessee Appellate Court Clerk's Office)
Description: Unknown threat actors gained unauthorised access to a cloud environment operated by Thomson Reuters between March and 30 June 2026. This affected court records managed through its C-Track case management platform. Thomson Reuters detected the unauthorised activity on 30 June 2026. The company subsequently determined that accessed data included names, Social Security numbers, driver's licence numbers, medical information, dates of birth and health insurance information. Certain confidential, redacted or sealed records may also have been affected at some courts. In the United States, the breach affected appellate and supreme courts in Alabama, Kentucky, Montana, Nevada, North Dakota, South Carolina, New Hampshire and Wyoming, several Pennsylvania county and appellate courts, ten Ohio District Courts of Appeals, the Tennessee Appellate Court Clerk's Office and the US Virgin Islands Supreme and Superior Courts. In Canada, the breach affected Ontario's three main courts: the Court of Appeal for Ontario, the Superior Court of Justice and the Court of Justice. Thomson Reuters stated there was no evidence of resulting identity theft and that systems processing court financial transactions were unaffected. The chief justices of Ontario's three courts disclosed the incident publicly in a joint statement on 2 September 2026.

Title (Company): Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) - Department of Migrant Workers (DMW)
Description: An unknown threat actor breached two Philippine government agencies on 8 September 2026. The Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) website was subjected to unauthorised access, whilst the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) web host was modified without authorisation, prompting both agencies to take their websites offline. The Department of Information and Communications Technology's (DICT) Cybersecurity Bureau and National Computer Emergency Response Team responded to both incidents, deploying access-control hardening and system-isolation measures. Initial assessments found no compromise of sensitive databases or personally identifiable information in the DOLE incident. Both agencies' affected web services remained offline as a precaution while technical teams completed investigations and strengthened security controls.

Ransomware group Brain Cipher claimed responsibility for breaching Golden State Orthopedics & Spine, a large multispecialty medical group serving Northern California, in a dark web forum post on 1 July 2026. The group claimed to have obtained 150 gigabytes of data, including patients' names, addresses, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, health insurance information and medical diagnosis details, stating it intended to publish the data within six to seven days. Golden State Orthopedics & Spine noticed unusual network activity around 2 July 2026 and launched an investigation, later confirming that protected health information may have been subject to unauthorised access. The company disclosed the incident publicly on 27 August 2026.

Hackers believed to be linked to North Korea deployed a new Linux toolkit, targeting organisations in South Korea's automotive and media industries starting in early 2025. The toolkit, which included a trojanised HAProxy instance dubbed "ted backdoor" and trojanised versions of tools like agetty, atd, crond, polkitd, and sshd, was used for long-term reconnaissance and allowed the attackers to spy on their targets while evading detection for extended periods. The attacks involved the exploitation of a vulnerability in a Groupware login portal to establish a foothold in the DMZ, followed by the collection of authentication credentials using an SSH keylogger, which enabled lateral movement into internal systems. The ted backdoor was deployed on top of an HAProxy load balancer, allowing the attackers to intercept and inject HTTP traffic, execute commands, and maintain persistence. The number of trojanized binaries and functionalities found suggest the scope could be long-term cyber espionage and surveillance. Rapid7 assessed on 4 September 2026 with moderate confidence that the newly identified toolkit is likely the work of a North Korean APT group, based on the targeting pattern, simple XOR-based encryption, a custom substitution cipher, and command-server infrastructure already linked to APT37 by other threat intelligence feeds.
Techniques Used: Exploit Public-Facing Application, Supply Chain Compromise, Valid Accounts

Description: Unknown threat actors breached Baylor Genetics, a US clinical diagnostic laboratory between 11 and 17 June 2026. The attackers stole data of approximately 2.8 million patients and employees, including names, birth dates, medical testing and laboratory results, health insurance information, and some Social Security numbers. The company first noticed suspicious activity within a part of its systems on or around 15 June 2026, after which the company conducted a review of the attack, which was completed on 30 June 2026. Baylor Genetics subsequently informed affected individuals of the incident.

Unknown threat actors breached the vice-rectorate of the French overseas territory Wallis-et-Futuna on 28 August 2026, particularly affecting the academic email system and the Pronote platform. The vice-rectorate worked in close coordination with national authorities and associated experts to secure its systems and restore affected services, with investigations and technical operations ongoing. The incident forced the postponement of class councils and, according to the acting vice-rector, a gradual resumption of services was expected by the end of the week following disclosure. Acting Vice-Rector Loetizia Fayolle disclosed the incident to the public on Facebook on 3 September 2026.

A group of self-proclaimed white-hat hacker stole approximately 4,000 Bitcoins (worth around $320 million) from the Liquid Federation wallet, a Bitcoin blockchain network operated by Blockstream, on 6 September 2026. The attackers exploited a software bug in Elements, the open-source code powering Liquid Network, which allowed more LBTC to exist than the system's real Bitcoin reserves should have allowed. The hackers then demanded that Liquid fix a bug. After the company complied, the group returned 3,400 of those crypto coins, worth around $262.6 million, while keeping roughly 598 BTC, close to $47 million, for themselves. The incident was disclosed to the public by Liquid Network on X on 6 September 2026.

An unidentified hacker carried out a ransomware attack against Beaver County Behavioral Health (BCBH) before 8 July 2026. BCBH is a Pennsylvania agency coordinating mental health and substance use services. The threat actor copied data from BCBH's network. This included protected health information such as names, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, medical and treatment information, and insurance details. BCBH discovered the incident on 8 July 2026. The agency worked with federal law enforcement and third-party cybersecurity consultants to investigate. Administrator Lisa McCoy disclosed the incident publicly on 4 September 2026, stating that a review to determine the full scope of affected individuals was ongoing.

Title (Company): Environmental Radiation Monitoring System, Tottori Prefecture
Description: Unknown threat actors launched a ransomware attack on the Environmental Radiation Monitoring System of Tottori Prefecture, Japan, on 2 September 2026, disabling the system's main server and encrypting its files. The system collects and monitors radiation dose rate and related data from monitoring posts around the Shimane Nuclear Power Station and the Ningyotouge Environmental Technology Center. The prefecture confirmed that the system holds no confidential or personal information, and that a backup server at a remote location remained unaffected, allowing radiation monitoring to continue uninterrupted. The prefectural office's CSIRT emergency response team responded quickly, cutting off communication channels and implementing containment measures alongside system maintenance providers and the prefectural police's cybercrime unit. The prefecture disclosed the incident publicly on 3 September 2026.

Qilian ransomware group launched ransomware attack on the Quebec Construction Commission (CCQ) on 24 August 2026, exfiltrating the personal information of 350,000 people, including dates of birth and social insurance numbers. In the course of the attack, the online and telephone services were disrupted. Later, the attack was claimed by the ransomware group Qilin. On 4 September, CCQ confirmed the incident in a statement on their website, saying that they took measures to reduce the risks and opened an investigation.

Title (Company): Opposition Member of Parliament - Individuals in Serbia’s Student Movement
Description: An unknown actor targeted Serbian activists, including a member of Serbia's student protest movement, with Pegasus and NoviSpy spyware ahead of local elections. The use of mercenary spyware such as Pegasus is generally indicative of government-linked deployment, though no specific state actor has been confirmed in this case. After the activists received an Apple Threat Notification, Citizen Lab, in collaboration with the SHARE Foundation, confirmed the infection, tracing it to an iMessage zero-click exploit, and identified high-confidence indicators of compromise. The attack required no action from the victim and gave the attacker full access to the phone, including messages, photos, notes, microphone, and camera. Apple later fixed this specific exploit through security updates in iOS 18.4.1. The SHARE Foundation documented at least 14 individuals in Serbia targeted with advanced spyware since early 2026, spanning student movement members, civil society activists, an opposition member of parliament, and a local councillor. Citizen Lab published a blog post on the surveillance campaign on 3 September 2026.

An unattributed hacker breached global chemical company Lotte Chemical in South Korea, gaining unauthorised access to certain personal information stored within its internal system (ECOMS), on 27 August 2026. The company discovered the incident on the same day and disclosed it publicly on 31 August 2026. Following discovery, Lotte Chemical implemented measures to prevent further harm and launched an investigation into the cause and scope of the incident with the assistance of internal and external cybersecurity experts. Based on initial findings, the potentially affected personal information may vary by individual and could include names, login IDs, mobile phone numbers, email addresses, employee numbers, job grades, positions and other work-related information.

An unknown threat actor disrupted computer systems belonging to Luminis Health, forcing the healthcare provider to cancel some appointments and delaying patient treatment, in August 2026. Luminis Health, which operates Anne Arundel Medical Center, launched an investigation with the support of legal counsel and third-party cybersecurity experts, and rerouted some patients as a result of the disruption. The Maryland Department of Health and other state agencies were informed and met with local stakeholders to assess critical needs and available support. Luminis Health disclosed the incident publicly on 1 September 2026, confirming that certain systems remained unavailable while teams worked to safely restore them, and stated that its investigation into whether patient information was affected was ongoing.

Cybercriminal group Emperador carried out a ransomware attack on the city government of Baguio in the Philippines in August 2026, claiming to have stolen 2.9 GB of documents and personal information, including identification cards, building permits, and construction-related files. The group also claimed to have stolen contracts, legal permits, financial statements, project proposals, procurement records, and other administrative documents. Emperador added the Baguio city government to its leak site on 10 August 2026. The city government confirmed the incident on 14 August 2026 and took BUILDPass, its online system for processing building permits and related construction transactions, offline; the system may contain personal information and documents submitted by applicants. The stolen data was subsequently published on the group's leak site.

Title (Company): U.S. Fintech Company - Asian Technology Company
Description: An unknown threat actor compromised an Asian technology company and a US fintech company between March and July 2026, using the ClickFix technique for initial access and sharing infrastructure across both intrusions. At the technology company, after initial payloads were repeatedly blocked, the threat actor downloaded the legitimate Node.js installer and used it to run an implant that communicated with Ethereum blockchain gateways to retrieve commands, a technique known as EtherHiding. At the fintech company, the threat actor deployed a Rust-based backdoor known as C2Looper, previously linked to ransomware operations. Access was maintained at both organisations until at least July 2026. Symantec disclosed the activity on 3 September 2026, linking both intrusions to the same actor and noting further connections to an initial access broker known as Woodgnat (aka KongTuke).

INC ransom conducted a ransomware attack against the Salus Polyclinic in Trieste, Italy, disrupting the hospital's systems between 31 August and 3 September 2026. The attack caused significant disruptions to the facility, including the suspension of ordinary hospitalisations, postponement of blood tests and laboratory analyses, and interruption of blood collection activities. The incident was reported by the hospital's management after they received the ransom demand, and an investigation is currently underway. The Polyclinic attributed the incident to INC Ransom in a notice to the public on 10 September 2026. Other media reports suggested that an Russian-Albanian national might be responsible for the attack.

Title (Company): Ministry of Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion (France)
Description: Unknown threat actors breached and disrupted France's Ministry of Ecological Transition between 29 August and 3 September 2026. A shared ministerial digital hub first reported a "sophisticated" cyberattack against its messaging tools on 29 August, prompting password resets and service suspensions. On 2 September, a user posted on a cybercrime forum claiming to have exfiltrated two datasets, "controleurs.csv" (14,656 records including names, dates of birth and professional details) and "all_users.json" (data of 8,166 users, including emails, phone numbers and identification numbers), citing a misconfigured API and an IDOR vulnerability as the access route. These claims remain unverified. The Ministry initially described the disruption as a routine IT incident but acknowledged to AFP on 3 September that it had been the target of a sophisticated cyberattack on its messaging services, engaging ANSSI and filing a report with the public prosecutor's office.

Unknown threat actors disrupted the payment software and geographic information system (GIS) of South African bulk water supplier Rand Water on 2 September 2026. The disruption affected the utility's ability to process payments to vendors and contractors, and took down the GIS system used to map and manage its pipeline network, preventing contractors from obtaining infrastructure approvals. The incident was first reported by technology news site MyBroadband, citing an anonymous source, and confirmed by Rand Water on 3 September 2026. The utility stated that its water treatment processes and quality control systems continued to operate normally.

ShinyHunters breached and leaked data of McKesson, a major U.S. healthcare and pharmaceutical company between 21 and 25 August 2026. The attackers stated that they used vishing to compromise McKesson's Okta accounts and accessed Salesforce and Snowflake, allegedly exfiltrating about 1TB of data containing approximately 284 million patient-related records. The hackers demanded a ransom of $55,236,150 and gave McKesson 72 hours to respond after leaking sample data. The stolen data included sensitive information such as names, addresses, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, patient IDs, Medicaid numbers, medical record numbers, information on medications and allergies, illnesses, disabilities, appointments, and data on attending physicians. McKesson became aware of the attack on 25 August 2026.

Title (Company): Ministry of Housing and Urban Renovation (France)
Description: The ZeroBytes hacker group claimed to have stolen data from the “Zero Empty Housing” website, a program of France's Ministry of Housing, on 28 August 2026. The stolen information includes names and first names of property owners or users, their dates of birth, email addresses, phone numbers, postal addresses, financial information, and housing data. ZeroBytes confirmed its responsibility for the attack on a cybercrime forum, stating it had exfiltrated almost 150 million lines of data. The French Ministry of Housing declined to comment on the matter.

The Gentlemen Ransomware Group breached and exfiltrated data from Nutex Health, a for-profit healthcare company operating 28 facilities across 12 states in the US before 24 August 2026. The attackers exfiltrated patient and employee, credentialed provider, business and financial information from the company’s servers. The incident was disclosed by Nutex Health in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on 24 August 2026. The Gentlemen Ransomware Group claimed responsibility for the attack on 31 August 2026, demanding a ransom. On 10 September 2026, Nutex confirmed in a statement that the group published the stolen data on its leak site.

An unknown threat actor compromised the website of Korea City Airport in late August 2026. The Korea City Airport put a notice on its website on 26 August 2026, saying that they detected signs of external intrusion on its downtown airport website and they have taken emergency measures. Customers were advised to take preventive measures, such as changing their website passwords immediately.

Unspecified hackers launched a ransomware attack targeting certain computer networks belonging to the City of Norcross in Georgia, identified by city officials on 1 August 2026. The city engaged external cybersecurity professionals and notified law enforcement to investigate and secure affected systems. Most city services and computer systems had returned to normal operations, though officials warned residents of possible limited ongoing disruptions during restoration efforts. It remained undisclosed whether any sensitive resident or employee data had been compromised, and no timeline for full restoration had been released. The city notified residents of the incident on or around 28 August 2026.

Unknown threat actors exploited Avici's Solana-based smart contract system, calling functions on its authorisation and collateral programs to withdraw funds and drain user accounts on 28 August 2026, affecting around 125 accounts for amounts between roughly $9 and $26,000 each. Separately, a vulnerability in card issuer Rain's smart contract allowed $500,859.22 to be stolen from 1,685 users, whilst over $600,000 was lost to phishing via fake websites deploying wallet-draining malware. Total losses across both vectors ranged between $600,000 and $1 million; Avici reimbursed all affected users automatically. The AVICI token fell around 39-49% following disclosure. Avici engaged the FBI's IC3, and partner platforms Rain, Jupiter, and Tria took precautionary measures, with Jupiter and Tria confirming no direct impact to their own systems.

Ransomware group Safepay claimed to have breached Air Liquide Korea, the South Korean subsidiary of global industrial gas company Air Liquide, and demanded a ransom on 25 August 2026. Air Liquide Korea supplies industrial gases and related services to major domestic industries, including semiconductors, petrochemicals and steel, through a network of over 60 production facilities and 220km of pipeline. Safepay listed the company on its dark web leak site and posted screenshots as proof, stating it would release the stolen data at a later date if negotiations failed. The exact scope of the breach had not been confirmed at the time of reporting.

Title (Company): Unnamed property manager - Unnamed manufacturer - Unnamed food services company - Unspecified IT Service Providers - Unnamed distributor - Unnamed financial services firm - Unnamed manufacturer - Unnamed energy firm
Description: A unknown suspected affiliate of The Gentlemen ransomware-as-a-service operation used Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 4.6 to drive nearly every stage of intrusions against at least eight organisations in or around June 2026, including an Australian energy firm, a food services company in South Africa, a manufacturer in Thailand, an IT services company in Malaysia, a financial services firm in Mauritius, and several entities in the United States, as reported by Gambit Security in a threat report on 23 August 2026. Gambit states that the messages to Claude Code were in Russian, but did not explicitly link the attack to Russian threat actors.

The ransomware group Barracuda breached Micro-Comm, a small maker of water utility technology in Olathe, Kansas, on or around 31 July 2026. Barracuda posted nearly 850,000 company files (roughly 644 GB) from the company on 6 August 2026. The FBI and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency were investigating the breach, which was believed to be an opportunistic attack not specifically targeted at Micro-Comm. The breach was discovered by the company on 31 July 2026, and customers were informed in an August 8 newsletter that the company had experienced a limited malware attack. The incident was reported by various sources, including Dixon Land, a spokesperson for the FBI’s Kansas City field office, and Jim Cote, a co-owner of MicroComm.

Unknown threat actors disrupted the global operations of Boston Scientific, a US-based multinational medical device company, including its ability to process and ship orders to customers, on 25 August 2026. The incident, discovered on 26 August 2026, affected access to certain operating systems and business applications. Boston Scientific engaged a cybersecurity firm to address the incident and, as of 26 August 2026, had not determined the financial impact. No group had claimed responsibility as of 27 August 2026, and investors were informed that full system restoration could take weeks.

A threat actor named "misere" breached Solimut Mutuelle, a French mutual insurance company, on or before 22 August 2026. Misere claimed to possess the data of nearly 1.5 million insured people; some of the data included social security numbers, as well as nearly 3 million postal addresses, over 700,000 international bank account numbers (IBANs) which were put up for sale, and over a million salary declarations.  The company detected the incident on 23 August and quickly isolated its systems, putting an end to the intrusion. Solimut Mutuelle informed its potentially affected members and notified the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (Prudential Control and Resolution Authority) and the Commission nationale de l’informatique et des libertés (CNIL, the French data protection authority).

FulcrumSec breached Manchester Airports Group (MAG), which operates Manchester Airport, London Stansted and East Midlands Airport, accessing personal data belonging to around 8.7 million customers on the weekend of 22 August 2026. The accessed data related to car park, lounge, and fast-track bookings, as well as in-airport WiFi sign-ups, and primarily consisted of email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registration numbers, and postcodes. MAG discovered the incident on 25 August 2026 and disclosed it on 27 August 2026, stating that no payment or banking details were exposed. FulcrumSec told BleepingComputer that it stole approximately 86 GB of data. In early September, the cybercriminals have leaked data on 8.7 million travellers after MAG refused to pay a ransom.

An Iran-linked threat actor disrupted a small British gas-fired peaker power plant for four days in July 2026, in what was reported as the first successful cyberattack of its kind to bring down a UK power generation facility. The incident, first reported by The Sunday Telegraph, was confirmed by the British government, which declined to identify the affected facility or provide further detail, citing security reasons, though it did not dispute the attribution to Iran. Energy Minister Michael Shanks and other government spokespeople stated that the national energy system was never at risk. He further noted that the plant was small-scale, fell well below the legal threshold requiring generators to notify authorities of cyber activity and was not essential to the wider electricity supply. The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) reportedly received no notifications of power outages in connection with the incident.

In October 2024, news of a data breach exposing Burger King Russia customers broke following an August attack on the Mindbox marketing automation platform. The breach exposed 3.2M unique email addresses along with names, genders, dates of birth, phone numbers and approximate geolocations, with the data spanning 2018 to August 2024. Burger King Russia acknowledged the incident and advised it did not include payment or passport details.

In November 2023, over 800k user records were scraped from the Chess.com website and posted to a popular hacking forum. The data included email address, name, username and the geographic location of the user. A further 446k scraped records were later provided and added to HIBP.

In August 2026, millions of records allegedly sourced from Chess.com were posted online. The data contained 7.3M rows with 4.6M unique email addresses, along with usernames, names, countries and data relating to users' Chess.com accounts. Analysis of the data suggested it had been obtained by scraping. When loaded into HIBP, 99% of the email addresses had already appeared in previous data breaches, further supporting the scraping theory. Read more about scrapes and data breaches.

In 2019, the now-defunct B2B marketing leads database service LimeLeads suffered a data breach due to an exposed, unsecured Elasticsearch server. The incident exposed tens of millions of records of largely corporate contact data containing 17.8M unique email addresses, along with phone numbers, employers, job titles and geographic locations including state, city and postcode.

Title (Company): Namiban Ministry of Defence and Veterans Affairs (MODVA)
Description: The RansomHouse ransomware group breached the Ministry of Defence and Veterans Affairs (MODVA) in Namibia in September 2026. On 16 September, the group listed MODVA on its leak site. The Namibia Cybersecurity Incident Response Team confirmed that unauthorised activity occurred within the Ministry’s network environment and said that an analysis of the affected systems revealed an incident associated with the RansomHouse ransomware group.

Unknown threat actors conducted a ransomware attack on the network of the Collado Villalba City Council in Spain, encrypting data from the system on 15 September 2026. The threat actors gained access to the network through a security breach in an external provider and demanded a ransom, which the City Council refused to pay. The systems were isolated and the attack was contained within two days. The city council notified federal law inforcement and cybersecurity experts. The City Council informed the public of the attack and restoration of the systems through a statement on 17 September 2026. On 21 September 2026, all of the municipality's systems were operational again

An unknown threat actor breached the University of Munich (LMU) in Germany in September 2026, accessing a system with student information, including potential health insurance and financial aid data. The university confirmed on 19 September 2026 that they have detected a cyberattack on 17 September. The potentially affected records include students' names, dates of birth, and other identifying information, contact details, and LMU email addresses, bank account information, and details about students' courses of study and previous educational qualifications. Health insurance numbers and identifiers associated with Germany's student financial aid program may also have been affected. After discovering the breach, the university disconnected the affected server and brought in external cybersecurity specialists. It is also working with law enforcement on an investigation.

Title (Company): Unspecified Government Entities - Unspecified Government Entities - Unspecified Telecommunications Organisation - Unspecified Government Entities - Unspecified Government Entities - Unspecified Government Entities - Unspecified Government Entities - Unspecified Government Entities
Description: China-aligned APT group FamousSparrow carried out an espionage campaign targeting government entities across Latin America and a telecommunications organisation in Puerto Rico, deploying a backdoor named SparroWocky since July 2025. The group almost exclusively focused on high-profile targets in Argentina, Ecuador, Guatemala, Honduras, Panama, Peru, Puerto Rico and Venezuela. Since August 2025, FamousSparrow appears to have shifted from its previous SparrowDoor tool towards SparroWocky, a new custom C++ backdoor that manipulates low-level memory structures and patches code at runtime to avoid detection. The group also began incorporating code from open-source projects directly into its malware. ESET disclosed the findings in a report published on 17 September 2026.

Title (Company): DataHub Pvt Ltd - Nepal Stock Exchange (Nepse)
Description: An unknown threat actor targeted DataHub Pvt Ltd, a data centre serving 72 brokers, with a ransomware attack that disrupted trading on the Nepal Stock Exchange (Nepse) on 20 September 2026. The attack affected multiple systems and services, including TMS, CDSC-related systems, payment gateways and other interconnected services. Nepse suspended trading at the request of the Stock Brokers Association of Nepal after DataHub reported the cyberattack, with regulators halting trading to prevent further damage.

Unknown threat actors conducted a ransomware attack on the IT systems of Ellis County, Kansas, United States, on 17 September 2026. County officials became aware of the incident early that morning and immediately took steps to contain the disruption, including isolating affected systems and engaging cybersecurity specialists. An investigation was launched with the assistance of local law enforcement, the Kansas Highway Patrol, and the Kansas Bureau of Investigation. Some county services were unavailable, delayed or operating under temporary procedures, though 911 and emergency public safety response remained unaffected. The county stated there was no evidence at the time of personal or sensitive information having been accessed.

Foreign actors breached the computer systems of two small water utilities in Colorado, United States, in late August 2026. Both utilities are privately operated and serve fewer than 200 people each. The threat actors changed equipment settings, disabled remote access and alarms and altered pumping cycles. Governor Jared Polis's office stated that treatment processes and water quality were not impacted at either provider, and that the incidents were brief and quickly addressed by the providers themselves, who then alerted the state.

Title (Company): Housing and Redevelopment Authority of Clay County - Moorhead Public Housing Agency
Description: Unknown perpetrators conducted a ransomware attack on the network of the Housing and Redevelopment Authority of Clay County (HRA), Minnesota, United States, gaining unauthorised access between 19 June and 21 June 2026 and copying data affecting the HRA and Moorhead Public Housing Agency. The affected data included names, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, driver's licence or state identification numbers, passport numbers, immigration identification numbers, birth certificates, tribal identification card numbers, financial account numbers, health insurance identification numbers, and medical or health information. The HRA detected the ransomware on 22 June 2026 and immediately launched an investigation with third-party cybersecurity and forensics consultants, notifying federal law enforcement and Minnesota IT Services. The data review concluded on 18 August 2026, and the HRA began mailing notification letters to affected individuals and disclosed the incident publicly on 17 September 2026.

The hacktivist group called CikLeak claimed to have breached the computer systems connected to Russia's election infrastructure, including the Central Election Commission and companies involved in developing Vybory, the state-run platform used to administer elections. The hackers claimed to have stolen internal documents, server configurations, passwords and employee communications from the commission and its contractors, including Russian telecom giant Rostelecom, and provided the stolen material to Important Stories, an independent Russian investigative outlet. CikLeak stated that their goal was to expose how the Russian electoral system works internally and what they described as opportunities for authorities to manipulate election results, and urged Russians to vote in person on the final day of the election. Important Stories authenticated the documents, but it remains unclear how deeply the hackers penetrated the election infrastructure or whether they gained access to systems directly involved in voting or counting ballots.

The Direwolf ransomsware group attacked the Tanjung Pelepas Port (PTP) in Malaysia, a major port in Southeast Asia and a joint venture between Maersk and Malaysian conglomerate MMC that caused container terminal operations to be suspended for several hours on 9 September 2026. The port later restarted systems and resumed business, with Maersk stating that some ships may experience delays as a result. Maersk confirmed that an incident affected the terminals systems, and operations were being gradually restored. PTP detected abnormalities in the late evening of 9 September, mainly affecting the terminals operating system. To control the risk, the port immediately isolated the affected systems and temporarily suspended some container terminal operations, before gradually resuming them on 10 September 2026. PTP stated that it is working with cybersecurity experts to investigate the incident and is taking additional security measures. Currently, there is no evidence that customer data has been accessed without authorization. On 11 September 2026, a cybersecurity information platform reported that the ransomware organization Direwolf had listed PTP on its "victim list" and claimed to have obtained internal data.

Title (Company): Sutton Public Schools - Town of Sutton
Description: An unknown threat actor breached the Town of Sutton and the public schools in Sutton in the United States in September 2026. The town of Sutton posted on Facebook on 17 September 2026 that they identified a cybersecurity incident affecting certain portions of its network environment and, upon discovery, immediately took steps to secure its systems, contain the incident. Despite the incident, town services continue to operate. The Town engaged experienced independent cybersecurity and forensic professionals to assist with the investigation and response efforts. The Town has also notified and is coordinating with law enforcement authorities.

Chinese state-sponsored threat actors UTA0560 and APT31 (aka Violet Typhoon, JungleBamboo, attributed to the MSS Hubei State Security Department) exploited a shared Chrome and Windows zero-day exploit chain against non-governmental organisations from 1 September 2026. Both actors used spearphishing emails directing victims to a legitimate US university website with a cross-site scripting flaw, redirecting them to attacker-controlled servers, where a fake donation form triggered a multistage exploit combining a Chrome V8 vulnerability (CVE-2026-85046), a WebAssembly sandbox escape (CVE-2026-87491), and a Windows kernel vulnerability (CVE-2026-85880). UTA0560 deployed a custom in-memory backdoor named GRIMWEDGE, whilst APT31 deployed a loader that installed a credential-stealing Chrome extension disguised as a Google Gemini assistant, named LONGTALE. Volexity assessed both actors as espionage-motivated and found identical exploit code between the two campaigns, suggesting the chain may have been shared or sold to multiple Chinese end-users, whilst final payloads used distinct toolsets. Volexity published its findings on 15 September 2026, noting similarities to a related campaign reported on 10 September using a separate shared exploit kit dubbed BlueMoon.

The Kairos ransomware gang deployed ransomware against the City of Libercourt in France at the end of August 2026. The actor breached the town’s information systems and exfiltrated personal data, demanding a ransom in return for not publishing the stolen data. The functioning of the town's services remained unaffected. The city stated it was investigating the scope of the stolen data and warned residents about suspicious calls. The attack was disclosed to the public by the city on 15 September 2026.

An unknown threat actor stole personal and health data of patients participating in medical research in Spain on 15 September 2026. The Zamora Care Complex reported that the incident had affected personal information of patients including in the National Study on Inflammatory Intestinal Disease on Genetic and Environmental Determinants. The incident was detected by the Grupo Español de Trabajo en Enfermedad de Crohn y Colitis Ulcerosa, which manages data of patients with Crohn’s Disease for statistical and scientific purposes. The Zamora Care Complex immediately implemented measures to block the attack and reported the incident to the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD). Later, AEPD reported that the hack was conducted to a great extent by an AI agent from a well-known AI company.
