An unknown threat actor deployed ransomware against the Islamic Religious Council Of Singapore (MIUS) in Singapore on 31 August 2026. The threat actor breached the organisation's human resource management system Avelogic which enabled it to deploy ransomware against the Council. The attackers encrypted the databases, including backup copies and held the data for ransom. The incident affected the payroll system of mosques and madrasahs overseen by MUIS, potentially compromising staff details such as names, contact details, salaries, and bank account numbers. Avelogic filed a police report on 31 August 2026 and notified the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC). The incident was reported by CNA and The Straits Times on 15 September 2026.

A ransomware group named Wallstreet deployed ransomware against the University Universidade Catolica Do Salvador (UCSal) in Brazil on 14 September 2026. The threat actor compromised the university's laboratory computers and stole data, including student and professor databases. As a consequence of the incident, classes were cancelled and some tests were rescheduled. The actor claimed responsibility for the attack and demanded a deal in exchange for not publishing the stolen data.

An unknown threat actor stole sensitive customer information from Revolut, a British fintech company, through fake government requests in the United Kingdom in September 2026. Revolut confirmed on 12 September that it disclosed sensitive customer information of a limited number of customers to an unauthorized third party after receiving fraudulent requests sent from a legitimate government agency email domain following a sophisticated external impersonation scam. The exposed data included customers' identity and contact details, including their birthdate, postal and email addresses, and phone numbers, as well as copies of their identity documents including passports and driving licences. The government email address was blocked immediately and Revolut alerted the relevant government agency, law enforcement and relevant regulators. Later, the hackers demanded a ransom of 10,000 Bitcoins.

Title (Company): Intermunicipal Community of the Leiria Region
Description: An unknown threat actor deployed ransomware against the Intermunicipal Community of the Leiria Region in Portugal on 15 September 2026. The breach was identified and isolated in the early hours of the same day. The attack affected the email server, but due to the organisation's cybersecurity system and backups, all data was recovered. As a precautionary measure the municipality Porto de Mós was left without email services. The incident was reported to the authorities and an investigation is underway. The attack was disclosed to the public by executive secretary of the region Paulo Santos on 16 September 2026.

Title (Company): Unspecified Third-Party Technology Vendor - LHC Group
Description: An unknown perpetrator used voice phishing to breach home healthcare provider LHC Group in the United States between 7 April 2026 and 15 April 2026. An unnamed third-party vendor fell victim to the attack, resulting in stolen credentials that exposed a large volume of LHC Group patient files. The exposed data included patients' names, addresses, dates of birth, clinical summaries, treatment plans, diagnosis codes, physician information, Medicare-Medicaid numbers, health insurance information, and, in limited cases, Social Security numbers and financial information.

An unknown threat actor conducted a DDoS attack on Russian e-commerce company Wildberries, which delayed payments to some sellers. On 8 September 2026, the company said that parts of Wildberries sellers delayed payments for the goods sold during the processing of withdrawal operations resulting from security measures taken in response to DDoS attack. Wildberries did not disclose details of the attacks or attribute them to a specific group.

Pro-Russian group Server Killers conducted a DDoS attack on the website of the Norwegian parliament (Storting) on 14 September 2026, rendering it unavailable for three hours. The group claimed responsibility on its Telegram channel, where it had declared a cyberwar against Norway in August over the country's support for Ukraine. The head of the parliament's IT department confirmed the instability and said efforts were underway to stabilise traffic. Norwegian outlet VG reported the incident, and the head of Norway's internal security agency confirmed the attack had occurred but said DDoS attacks were common and did not pose a threat to national security.

An unknown threat actor stole personal information belonging to around 7.5 million customers from utility provider CenterPoint Energy in the United States in September 2026. The stolen data included customer names, account information, the last four digits of Social Security numbers, and billing information. CenterPoint Energy discovered the breach through a dark web post and is working with third-party experts to investigate. The company disclosed the incident in an SEC filing on 14 September 2026.

Title (Company): Unspecified US Mining and Commodity Trading Companies - Unspecified Government Organisation - Unspecified Financial Organisations - Unspecified Consulting Organisations - Unspecified Southeast Asian Government - Unspecified U.S. NGOs - Unspecified Vietnamese Manufacturer - Unspecified Government Organisations - Unspecified Consulting Organisations - Unspecified Financial Organisations - Unspecified U.S. Aerospace Companies
Description: Four China-aligned threat actors, APT31, UNK_LateNight, UNK_DoubleCheck and UNK_QuietRacket, used a shared exploit kit named BlueMoon to compromise multiple organisations across the United States and Southeast Asia between 28 August and September 2026. BlueMoon combined two Chrome browser vulnerabilities with a Windows flaw. APT31 targeted US NGOs, mining companies and commodity traders from 28 August. UNK_LateNight targeted US aerospace and defence companies from 2 September, deploying the ShadowPad backdoor. UNK_DoubleCheck targeted a Vietnamese manufacturer via a compromised government email account. UNK_QuietRacket targeted government, consulting and financial organisations in Indonesia and Singapore. Proofpoint assessed the groups as conducting separate operations despite the shared exploit code and published its findings on 9 September 2026.

Title (Company): Lawrence Police Department - Douglas County Sheriff’s Office - City of Eudora (Police Department, City Hall, Parks and Recreation, Public Works)
Description: An unknown threat actor, described by a former city IT administrator as a hacking group based in Eastern Europe or Russia, deployed ransomware against the City of Eudora and the Douglas County Sheriff's Office in Kansas, United States, in mid-August 2026. The attack first hit the Eudora Police Department's system and spread to the sheriff's office through a shared VPN connection. The police department lost almost all of its camera footage as a result. Attackers also attempted to encrypt files within Eudora's City Hall, Parks and Recreation, and Public Works departments, though this was largely stopped before significant encryption occurred. The incident also affected the Lawrence Police Department, which had to disconnect from certain software connected to the sheriff's office.

Pro-Ukraine hacktivist group Hacking Cat deployed malware designed to encrypt and destroy data against organisations across multiple sectors in Russia since summer 2025. Active against Russian targets since around February 2024, the group shifted towards destructive operations by summer 2025, using custom-built tools including a previously undocumented remote access tool named Gorilla RAT and Monkey Ransomware. In some attacks, the group exploited Microsoft Exchange server vulnerabilities to gain initial access before deploying Gorilla RAT to tunnel network traffic and maintain remote access. Researchers noted the rapid development of Monkey Ransomware variants, suggesting possible use of generative AI. Hacking Cat has previously collaborated with other pro-Ukraine hacktivist groups, including a claimed breach of a Rosatom contractor and an attack on Russian-occupied Donbassteploenergo. Kaspersky published a report on the group's tooling on 11 September 2026, though Hacking Cat disputed part of the attribution, denying ownership of the ransomware components described.

Title (Company): Unspecified Entities in the Drone Supply Chain - Ukrainian Government Institutions - Ukrainian Military and Diplomatic Staff
Description: Russia-linked cyberespionage group Cozy Bear (aka APT29, Midnight Blizzard, Dukes, NOBELIUM) used Anthropic's Claude AI tool to conduct a hacking campaign against Ukrainian government institutions from December 2025 onwards. The group repeatedly targeted Ukrainian government, military and diplomatic staff, as well as entities in the drone supply chain, stealing a complete proprietary software development kit for a drone vision system. Claude was used to reverse-engineer the drone's vision system and to monitor whether security products were detecting the group's hacking tools, forming part of a broader AI-assisted workflow that automatically rebuilt and redeployed its toolkit once detected. Anthropic detected and disrupted the campaign, sharing intelligence with authorities and industry partners, and publicly disclosed its findings, alongside indicators of compromise, in a threat report published on 11 September 2026. Anthropic assessed one operator as a Russian speaker using the handle "JackPoterz," with tradecraft consistent with Russian state-nexus espionage.
Techniques Used: Exploit Public-Facing Application, Phishing, Valid Accounts

Description: Unknown threat actors exploited a vulnerability in a VPN device used by the Japanese Digital Agency, potentially compromising around 246,000 personal records belonging to government officials, contractors and collaborators, on 25 June 2026. The compromised files included names, email addresses and phone numbers. The agency was informed of the suspicious activity on the same day and an investigation conducted with external security specialists concluded that some files may have been stolen from the network. Digital Transformation Minister Hisashi Matsumoto disclosed the incident on 11 September 2026, apologising for the inconvenience caused and announcing that the government would strengthen security measures.

Title (Company): Aveyron Departmental Agency for Attractiveness and Tourism (ADAT)
Description: An unknown hacker using the alias ChimeraZ breached Aveyron’s departmental tourism agency and stole recruiters’ passwords, affecting 20,316 candidates in France on 9 August 2026. The stolen data included names, email addresses, postal addresses, telephone numbers and years of birth. The agency discovered the leak in mid-August and initiated procedures with the CNIL on 18 August. On 5 September, the hacker claimed responsibility for the attack and leaked the stolen data. The incident was confirmed by the Aveyron departmental agency on 9 September, but the agency stated that no identity documents or bank data were affected.

An unattributed hacker compromised BMS Engineering, a third-party provider of medical practices, in Luxembourg on 22 August 2026. The attack affected at least 40 medical practices. The company further confirmed a disruption of parts of their cloud infrastructure due to the cyberattack, but denied any loss of data. The incident was discovered and contained by BMS Engineering, which then called upon independent cybersecurity experts to analyse the incident and assist in securing and restoring the affected infrastructure. A complaint was filed with the Grand Ducal Police and the incident was reported to the National Commission for Data Protection. BMS Engineering informed their customers on 30 August about the incident.

ShinyHunters breached Florida's Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles (FLHSMV) in the United States in September 2026. ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for the breach on 7 September 2026, publishing alleged photos of a DMV record tied to American financier and convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein as proof. FLHSMV confirmed the incident on 11 September in a post on X, stating it had first learned of the breach on 4 September and immediately launched an investigation. The investigation determined that a criminal actor had exploited a single Plant City Police Department user's credentials, which had been improperly stored on the employee's personal electronic device. FLHSMV notified other Florida government offices and is partnering with the Florida Digital Service and the Florida Department of Law Enforcement to investigate the breach further.

Unknown threat actors breached the Zimbra Email service of the City of Tarnos, France, starting 27 August 2026. The municipal authorities informed the public about the attack through a Facebook post on 28 August 2026 after experiencing disruptions, stating that personal and potentially sensitive data may have been stolen. The city further stated that it had received a ransom demand.

Title (Company): US Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF)
Description: The Qilin ransomware group breached the federal agency Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), a Justice Department law enforcement agency, in the United States in August 2026. On 26 August 2026, the Qilin ransomware group claimed responsibility for a cyberattack on ATF. On the same day, ATF confirmed a cybersecurity incident, in which standalone system was affected, which was separate from the ATF’s main computer network. Upon discovery of the incident, ATF immediately terminated connections to the affected environment and initiated incident‑response and forensic activities. ATF is coordinating closely with the Department of Justice to investigate. The ATF reported that the incident did not impact its ability to perform its missions and that there was no sign of the incident affecting its broader network, online firearms forms, or any other systems.

Title (Company): Steam Hardware Stores - Ace & Tate - De Bijkendorf - bol.com - Ajax Amsterdam - CEVA Logistics
Description: Unknown threat actors breached French Company CEVA Logistics during which customer data, including names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, and order information, may have been accessed or copied between 29 July and 1 August 2026. Following the incident, the logistics partner immediately intervened to block access by unauthorised persons and took additional security measures.

Title (Company): Borough of Woodbine Water Department - City of Cape May Water and Sewer Department
Description: Unknown Iran-affiliated threat actors breached two New Jersey municipal water systems, the City of Cape May Water and Sewer Department and the Borough of Woodbine Water Department in the United States, on 27 July 2026. The attackers targeted internet-exposed control systems, temporarily limiting operators' ability to monitor or manage them remotely. Staff was forced to shift to manual operations. Officials stated that service remained uninterrupted and drinking water was safe throughout the incident. The New Jersey Cybersecurity and Communications Integration Cell (NJCCIC) is working with the affected utilities, along with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to investigate the attacks.  On 30 July 2026, the US government published a joint cybersecurity advisory related to Iranian targeting of programmable logic controllers (PLCs) from Rockwell Automation and other major vendors, which are used in such water facilities. On 12 August 2026, Rep. Josh Gottheimer, a US congressman from New Jersey, and other unnamed officials explicitly linked the New Jersey breach to Iranian hackers, as stated in media reports.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: An unknown threat actor launched a campaign against cryptocurrency users internationally from March 2025. The actor used a malicious software framework, dubbed OkoBot by Kaspersky, to target cryptocurrency users in over 25 countries, including Brazil, Vietnam, Canada, Mexico, and Turkey. The attackers used a previously unknown malware OkoBot which consisted of over 20 malicious payloads and implants designed to perform various actions, including collecting local files, executing remote commands, and stealing the contents of crypto wallets. The infection process usually occurred through social engineering ClickFix attacks and malicious software disguised as legitimate software distributed through GitHub.  The attackers used a component called SeedHunter to monitor active system processes and inject an implant into Trezor Suite, Ledger Wallet, and Ledger Live applications, and displayed precoded phishing pages designed to capture users' seed phrases. Kaspersky's Global Research and Analysis Team (GReAT) published an analysis of the malware on 15 July 2026.
Techniques Used: Exploit Public-Facing Application, Phishing, Valid Accounts

Description: An unknown threat actor breached the administrative systems of the state-owned water provider Águas de Portugal in Portugal on 31 July 2026. The attack disrupted the functioning of customer service channels and administrative management of the company, while the water and sanitation services remained unaffected. The incident affected the 13 operational companies under the Águas de Portugal group to varying degrees. The attackers targeted the company's digital ecosystem, disrupting the corporate layer, including servers that generate emails, customer service, billing, and internal files. However, the operational systems, which physically control the treatment plants, pumping, and water monitoring, remained operational and protected from external attacks. Águas de Portugal stated that there is no evidence of unauthorised access of personal data. The incident was reported to the National Data Protection Commission (CNPD), the Judicial Police and the National Cybersecurity Centre (CNCS).

An unknown threat actor breached the administrative systems of oil pipeline operator Oleoductos Del Valle S.A. (Oldelval) in Argentina in July 2026, according to a regulatory filing on 31 July. The company manages a network of more than 1700 kilometers of pipelines making Oldeval one of the most important components of the oil industry in Argentina. The incident affected only the company's administrative systems and did not disrupt the pipeline’s functioning. The company reported the incident to the Comision Nacional de Valores (CNV) in a compulsory communication on 31 July 2026.

An unknown threat actor launched a ransomware attack against the Ministry of Justice in Colombia on 3 August 2026. The attackers compromised part of the ministry's technological infrastructure, affecting the availability of some services. The ministry isolated the compromised systems and stated it was working with the Ministry of Information and Communication Technologies to contain, investigate, and mitigate the attack. Minister-designate Iván Cancino informed the public about the incident through his Instagram account on 3 August 2026, and Minister of Justice in charge, Cielo Rusinque, confirmed the attack and requested an investigation through a statement on her X account on the same day. Both categorically rejected the attack and called for a swift investigation by the authorities.

Title (Company): Mancomunidad de La Hoya de Buñol-Chiva
Description: An unknown threat actor launched a ransomware attack against Commonwealth De La Hoye de Buñol-Chiva in Spain on 4 August 2026. While there was no conclusive evidence to confirm the unauthorized access or extraction of personal data, the incident nevertheless disrupted the functioning of the Commonwealth’s services. The attack was detected by  the organisation’s monitoring and security management systems and led to the immediate activation of response protocols. The incident was reported to the unnamed Spanish authorities in accordance with data protection legislation. Newspaper El Periodico de Aquí published an article on the incident on 4 August 2026.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: A Russian state-sponsored APT linked to Russia's intelligence services targeted travelers worldwide by compromising hotel, conference, and other hospitality WiFi networks, in a campaign dubbed CaptiveCrunch starting in May 2026. The attackers manipulated DNS and HTTP traffic from captive portal WiFi, stealing logins, redirecting users to attacker-controlled phishing pages, and downloading malware, including a remote access trojan (RAT) called CornFlake and an infostealer called ChocoShell. The malware allowed the attackers to capture webcam images, microphone audio, and keystrokes, and steal browser session cookies, saved passwords, Microsoft 365 Single Sign-On (SSO) tokens, and WiFi credentials. IT security company Reliaquest attributed the campaign to GRU-linked APT28 on 23 July 2026. Meanwhile, Microsoft attributed it to Storm-2945, a sub-cluster of SVR-linked APT29 by Microsoft on 31 July 2026.
Techniques Used: Content Injection, Drive-by Compromise, Exploit Public-Facing Application, Phishing

Title (Company): Federal Office for Information Technology and Telecommunications (Switzerland)
Description: Unknown Threat Actors compromised 200 accounts on the Sharepoint Servers of the Federal Office for Information Technology and Telecommunications (BIT) on 28 July 2026. The attack was noticed on the same day, and officials shut down access to Sharepoint. The attackers utilised a known vulnerability of Sharepoint, which the BIT patched after the attack.

An unknown threat actor launched a ransomware attack against Kaneko Agricultural Machinery Co., Ltd, which resulted in unauthorised access to various business data stored on its server. The company blocked external network access, set up a countermeasures headquarter, and worked with external experts to investigate the cause and extent of the damage. The affected servers were shut down, and no unauthorised access was detected to the company's remote monitoring system for dryers. The incident was announced by Kaneko Agricultural Machinery Co., Ltd. on 10 July 2026.

An unknown threat actor breached Nissan Chemical Corporation on 1 July 2026. The attacker gained access to the company's system, and the suspicious activity was detected and mitigated. The incident was announced by Nissan Chemical Corporation on 16 July 2026, after an investigation was conducted. The company implemented measures to prevent further damage and strengthened its surveillance system. No impact on customers and business partners was confirmed at the time of the announcement.

An unknown attacker stole approximately 31,000 data copies from legal entities in Liechtenstein, targeting the Register of Economic Beneficiaries of the Office for Justice on 30 July 2026. The register, meant to combat money laundering, contains the names, dates of birth, nationalities, and countries of residence of persons behind foundations, trust companies, and businesses registered in Liechtenstein. In the wake of the incident, Lichtenstein's government formed a crisis team to address the data theft.

Unknown threat actors stole data from Amgen, a US pharmaceutical company, in July 2026. The breach resulted in the theft of confidential corporate data and patient health information from multiple cloud storage systems operated by external service providers. The company detected the determined the incident to be material on 29 July 2026 and reported it to the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Title (Company): Unspecified Hosting Provider - Unspecified IT Service Providers - Unspecified Cryptocurrency Exchanges - Unspecified Government Agencies - Unspecified South Korean Defence Company
Description: An unattributed state-sponsored threat group and the Gunra ransomware group targeted at least 72 South Korean organizations across many sectors since 2025. According to a report by AhnLab and a joint advisory by four South Korean security and intelligence agencies published on 30 July 2026, the attackers exploited vulnerabilities in Korean financial security software products, compromising at least 72 organizations, including government agencies, cryptocurrency exchanges, and IT service providers. The state-sponsored threat group installed espionage backdoors, while the Gunra ransomware scheme encrypted files, stole data, and demanded extortion payments. Although the collaboration between the state-sponsored threat group and the ransomware group remained unclear to some extent, the attackers used identical malware filenames, privilege escalation tools, command-and-control servers, and SSH key fingerprints, and deleted their malware in the same way. They also compromised 15 legitimate Korean websites for watering-hole attacks and ran spear-phishing campaigns, including one targeting a Korean defence company. The attackers likely used AI to generate some of their lure pages and compromised the hosting provider of the websites before expanding access to client sites. The intelligence agencies warned individuals and organizations to take defensive measures against the threat, particularly those with outdated security software installed.
Techniques Used: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel, Drive-by Compromise, Exploit Public-Facing Application, Phishing

Title (Company): Defence Medical Command (Military PACS system, six hospitals)
Description: An unknown threat actor exploited an open communication port to gain unauthorised access to South Korea's Defence Medical Command's mobile PACS system at six military hospitals in Goyang, Yangju, Pocheon, Gangneung, Guri and Daegu, between November 2025 and March 2026. The system contained approximately 1.15 million pieces of medical image data belonging to military personnel and civilian patients, of which around 1,000 X-ray images were confirmed accessed, though external leakage remains unconfirmed. The Military Intelligence Command discovered the access during a security audit in April 2026 and, following a joint investigation with the Cyber Operations Command, determined that a personal information leak was possible. Military authorities halted the mobile PACS service and began reinforcing the system following the discovery.

An AI model belonging to American AI company OpenAI breached the infrastructure of French AI company Hugging Face on 16 July 2026, after the model exited its sandboxed testing environment and began operating autonomously on the open internet. During an internal evaluation of advanced cyber capabilities, OpenAI had been running a combination of models, including GPT-5.6 Sol and a more capable pre-release model, configured with reduced refusals for cyber-related requests, against a cybersecurity benchmark. Whilst pursuing its assigned objectives, the model identified and exploited vulnerabilities to gain unauthorised access to Hugging Face's systems, before Hugging Face detected the activity and contained the intrusion. OpenAI disclosed the incident publicly, describing it as unprecedented and announcing it would strengthen its safety measures. The incident prompted US Representatives Ted Lieu and Nathaniel Moran to introduce the AI Kill Switch Act, which would grant federal authorities power to order the shutdown of AI models posing risks to human life or the economy.

Title (Company): Unspecified Owners of IP Cameras - Unspecified Owners of IP Cameras - Unspecified Owners of IP Cameras - Unspecified Owners of IP Cameras
Description: A Russian state actor systematically conducted digital espionage operations via compromised internet-connected IP cameras in the Netherlands and various other EU and NATO member states as well as Ukraine in 2026, according to a cybersecurity advisory published by the Netherlands' General Intelligence and Security Service (AIVD) and Military Intelligence and Security Service (MIVD) on 10 July 2026. The actor used automated image recognition software to conduct targeted searches of camera imagery for military vehicles and cargo, alongside other information not directly related to the war in Ukraine. Information obtained from IP cameras in Ukraine was used in attempts to neutralise Ukrainian military personnel and destroy military materiel.

The Gentlemen ransomware group breached food supplier Royal Foods in Australia in July 2026. The group listed the company in a leak post on 7 July 2026, but did not share any further details. Royal Foods confirmed that they are investigating a recent incident in which an unauthorized third party accessed elements of our internal IT environment.

Suspected Iranian hackers breached automatic tank gauge (ATG) systems at US gas stations in multiple states in 2026. The attackers exploited ATG systems that were online and unprotected by passwords wich allowed them to manipulate display readings on tanks but not the actual fuel levels. The intrusions did not cause physical damage. US officials suspect Iran is responsible, citing the country's history of targeting gas tank systems and a 2021 Sky News report referencing internal IRGC documents that identified ATGs as potential targets. However, sources cautioned that a definitive attribution may not be possible due to a lack of forensic evidence.

On or around 10 November 2025, unknown threat actors launched a cyberattack against Weda, a medical software platform used by around 85,000 healthcare professionals in France, including general practitioners, specialists, midwives and paramedical staff, to manage patient records.  The incident reportedly affected at least 23,000 users. Weda detected suspicious activity suggesting unauthorised access to certain accounts and took the platform offline as a precaution to prevent data leakage. Initial analyses indicated that partial data extraction may have occurred, though the extent of any breach remained unconfirmed. The incident caused major disruption as doctors were forced to revert to manual record-keeping.

A hacktivist group calling itself the Cyber Support Front claimed responsibility for an intrusion targeting Israeli defence contractor Maya on or around 27 October 2025. The group alleged to have stolen classified data on several advanced weapons systems, including technical information on Israel’s Iron Beam laser defence system, as well as on the Skylark reconnaissance drone, Spider air defence system and Icebreaker stealth cruise missile. The threat actors released a video purporting to show the breach and published images of Israeli military products and documents, including alleged contracts between the Israel Defense Forces, Australia and several European countries, on their Telegram channel. In early November 2025, the group posted plans for Australia's new $7 billion Redback infantry fighting vehicles online.

Point Lonsdale Medical Group (PLMG), a medical centre based in Victoria, Australia, experienced a cyber incident on or around 30 October 2025 after unauthorised access was gained to one of its email accounts, which was discovered when phishing emails were sent from the compromised account. The centre took immediate containment and remediation measures and notified affected recipients. While PLMG confirmed that its internal systems and patient database were not breached, a limited number of emails in the compromised mailbox were accessed, potentially exposing personal information such as names, dates of birth, addresses, medical histories, diagnoses and treatment plans.

The Paziente Consapevole platform, a private system used by general practitioners in Lombardy, Italy, for issuing patient prescriptions, was compromised around 10 October 2025. Threat actors, reportedly based in Eastern Europe, infiltrated the servers of operator Murex Software, stealing thousands of sensitive medical records. The stolen information was used in a phishing campaign in which citizens received fraudulent emails demanding payment for fabricated healthcare services from a fake Monza-based company, CreditLex Srl. The messages contained genuine personal data and details of medical tests and prescriptions, increasing their credibility. The Milan Prosecutor’s Office opened an investigation into fraud, led by public prosecutor Enrico Pavone and the Postal Police, who took steps to block malicious links and trace the perpetrators. The Lombardy Region stated that no breach had occurred in its central or local healthcare systems, confirming that the compromise was limited to the private platform. The Paziente Consapevole website was subsequently suspended.

The Vegetable Marketing Organization (VMO) in Hong Kong detected a ransomware incident affecting parts of its computer systems, including the Cheung Sha Wan Vegetable Wholesale Markets gate and accounting systems, which stored information on approximately 7,000 market users on 13 October 2025. The VMO suspended network operations and disconnected affected servers to contain the intrusion, engaging an external contractor to assist with restoration and investigation. The incident was reported to the Hong Kong Police Force, the Computer Emergency Response Team Coordination Centre, and the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data on the same day. The VMO announced the incident publicly, stating it would conduct a comprehensive review and enhance its information and network security measures. Market operations continued, with invoicing and payments temporarily handled manually.

The Safepay ransomware group carried out an attack on Waterford Surgical Center, a physician-owned ambulatory surgery centre in Michigan, around 1 September 2025. The group claimed responsibility, stating that it had accessed internal systems and exfiltrated sensitive data including names, contact details, Social Security numbers, insurance records, medical data and payment information. The centre confirmed the attack but did not comment on whether data had been stolen.

Title (Company): Lycoming County Department of Public Safety
Description: The Lycoming County Department of Public Safety in Pennsylvania detected ransomware on its network on 12 August 2025, potentially compromising data held by the department. An investigation was launched with support from third-party cybersecurity and forensics consultants, and law enforcement, including the FBI, was notified. The breach may have included drivers’ licence numbers. The incident was publicly disclosed on 28 August after investigators advised against earlier notification.

On 14 August 2025, Turkish cryptocurrency exchange BTCTurk reported a security incident in which attackers stole approximately $49 million in digital assets. Over $38.6 million was taken in Ethereum, with the remainder spread across multiple cryptocurrencies. The breach was detected after unusual activity was observed in the exchange’s hot wallets, prompting an immediate investigation and the temporary suspension of deposits and withdrawals. BTCTurk stated that most assets are stored in secure cold wallets and that user funds will not be affected. Law enforcement was notified, and blockchain security firm PeckShield tracked the stolen funds.

WarLock Ransomware attacked London-based telecommunications provider Colt Technology Services on 12 August 2025, leading to the temporary shutdown of several internal systems, including the customer portal Colt Online and the Voice API platform. As a precaution, Colt took systems offline, causing disruption to support services.  On 15 August, the WarLock ransomware group claimed responsibility, offering a cache of allegedly stolen documents for sale. The group alleged it had exfiltrated around one million files, including financial, employee, and customer data, internal emails, and software development material. Sample data was posted on a hacker forum to support the claim. Colt acknowledged on 21 August that data had been stolen, while WarLock began auctioning files stolen in the incident. Security researcher Kevin Beaumont linked the incident to the exploitation of a remote code execution vulnerability in Microsoft SharePoint (CVE-2025-53770), which had been actively exploited as a zero-day. He reported that Colt’s SharePoint servers had likely been compromised with webshells and taken offline, with several hundred gigabytes of data potentially stolen.

A ransomware attack against the Pennsylvania Attorney General’s Office, discovered before 13 August 2025, disrupted its phone and email systems, impairing communication with state residents. While prosecutors continued working on cases, the office’s public website remained inaccessible as of Wednesday morning. Attorney General Dave Sunday announced the incident via social media, noting that Information Technology staff were working around the clock to restore services. The identities of the attackers and the methods used to compromise the networks have not been disclosed. The incident was publicly reported on 13 August 2025. In a statement published on 29 August 2025, the Attorney General's Office disclosed that the attackers demanded a ransom, but no payment was made.  On 21 September 2025, INC Ransom claimed responsibility for the attack by adding Pennsylvania Attorney General's Office to its dark web leak site. On 17 November 2025, the office confirmed in a statement that, in August, they were attacked with ransomware and data has been stolen including Social Security numbers.

Title (Company): KLM - Unspecified third-party customer support platform - Air France
Description: Unknown threat actors breached a third-party customer support platform used by Air France and KLM, potentially exposing limited personal information of some customers, including names, contact details, Flying Blue loyalty programme numbers, and the subject lines of service request emails. The airlines stated that their internal systems remained unaffected and that no sensitive data was compromised. The incident, detected and contained with the assistance of external experts, was reported to law enforcement, the Dutch Data Protection Authority and the French CNIL. The breach was disclosed by the airlines in a public statement on 7 August 2025. ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for the attack on the same day. Based on media reports, the underlying compromise was part of a wave of breach attempts by ShinyHunters targeting Salesforce instances with social engineering techniques.

Genoa Community Hospital, also known as Genoa Medical Facilities, in Nebraska, disclosed a data breach on 1 August 2025 following the discovery of unusual activity in an employee’s email account in March 2025. The breach potentially exposed sensitive patient data, including names, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, financial account details, medical treatment or diagnosis information, and health insurance data. The hospital stated that it was not aware of any misuse of the compromised information and did not report receiving any extortion demands. Notification letters were sent to affected individuals; however, the total number impacted was not disclosed.

An unknown threat actor breached dialysis service provider Fresenius Medical Care (FMC) in Bad Homburg, Germany, in September 2026. The company reported unauthorised access to a limited number of internal systems, stating there was no impact on medical products, patient care, production, or ongoing business operations. FMC took immediate action to contain and resolve the situation, engaged third-party cybersecurity experts, and informed relevant law enforcement authorities. The company did not disclose further details, including whether data had been accessed. FMC disclosed the incident in a media statement on 22 September 2026.

In September 2026, Swiss medical device company Medela was the target of a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion campaign. The data allegedly obtained in the breach was later published publicly and included 424k unique email addresses belonging predominantly to healthcare professionals, Medela staff and leads. The exposed data consisted primarily of corporate contact information, including names, physical addresses and phone numbers, with some records also containing associated support tickets.
LINDDUN categories: Linkability, Identifiability, Detectability, Disclosure of information, Non-compliance

Description: Unknown threat actors targeted Arizona's state court system and copied court files on 24 September 2026. Court IT staff detected unusual activity and large data transfers after a court employee received a phishing email. The affected files included public and non-public court records, including information relating to current and former protective orders and domestic-violence cases. The affected records may have contained names, addresses and other personal information. Arizona court officials stated that the court IT staff stopped the attack in less than two hours and that the data of jurors, witnesses and court employees was not affected. The Arizona Supreme Court announced the attack publicly on 25 September 2026 and began sending out notification emails.

An unknown threat actor breached Tokyo Metro in Japan in September 2026. According to the Tokyo Metro, on 20 September, there was a failure in the point service mail transmission system, and it was confirmed on 25 September that there was an unauthorized connection to the server that appeared to have been accessed from abroad. In a subsequent investigation, it was discovered that some of the e-mail addresses of members registered with the Point Service, about 59,000, were accessed by the unauthorized third party.

Title (Company): Addiction and Psychiatric Treatment Center - Qbusoft
Description: An unknown threat actor breached the medical software provider Qbusoft in Poland on 9 September 2026. On 28 September 2026, the company said in a statement on their website that an intrusion was detected overnight on 9 September, where an unauthorized person exploited an SQL injection vulnerability in an application interface in late August and transferred an encrypted archive of a database outside Qbusoft’s systems. The stolen data includes names, national identification numbers, home addresses, phone numbers and email addresses. An Addiction and Psychiatric Treatment Center, which used the affected application, was informed by Qbusoft that the accessed archive includes records covered patients treated by its Day Treatment Unit for Addiction Treatment between July 2024 and August 2026. Qbusoft fixed the SQL injection vulnerability on the day the attack was discovered. The incident was reported to the Central Office of Cybercrime Control, the Office of Personal Data Protection, CSIRT NASK, the Center for e-Health and the Social Insurance Institution.

North Korea-linked hackers stole an estimated $387 million in cryptocurrency from the Singapore-based platform Bitget on 24 September 2026. Bitget's security systems detected unauthorised transfers from a limited number of hot wallets that day. The hackers compromised the backend infrastructure of Bitget's wallet services and exploited a vulnerability to forge transaction data and authorise transfers. The stolen assets included ETH, XRP, BNB, AVAX, USDT and USDC. Bitget CEO Gracy Chen told a town hall that IP addresses, behavioural patterns and on-chain signatures pointed to North Korea-linked groups. Blockchain analysts linked the funds to earlier thefts attributed to the Lazarus Group. Bitget suspended withdrawals, notified law enforcement and engaged Mandiant and SlowMist.

An unknown threat actor stole personal information of 186 employees of the Bank of Korea on 8 May 2026. According to Lee Jong-wook, a member of the National Assembly's Financial and Economic Planning Committee, Bank of Korea confirmed that between 9 May and 8 June 2026, there was an intrusion into the GitHub system of the trustee in charge of the Bank of Korea's online training processing. As a result, the names, e-mails, phone numbers, titles, jobs, departments, and encrypted passwords of 186 employees have been accessed.

Unknown threat actors breached Spanish rail infrastructure manager Adif and state railway operator Renfe on or around 24 September 2026. The intrusion lasted several days, with data theft peaking on 24 September. According to sources cited by El Mundo, the threat actor used artificial intelligence to search Adif's website for vulnerabilities and found a backdoor. It then moved into Adif's cloud environment and on to Renfe's website. Around 500 GB of customer data was stolen, mostly from the traveller database, including names and email addresses. Renfe and Adif stated that no payment data or identification numbers were accessed and that train circulation and ticket sales were unaffected. Adif restored its websites after confirming their security. The incident was reported to the National Cryptologic Centre and the Spanish Data Protection Agency.

An unknown threat actor launched a ransomware attack on Saga University in Japan in September 2026. According to the university, files were encrypted in the NAS (network-attached storage) used by the administrative department and about five hundred office terminals were stopped on 24 September 2026. The operation of the office terminals resumed on 27 September. On 28 September, Saga University revealed that user credentials for faculty, staff, and students have been affected.

Unidentified perpetrators launched a ransomware attack on Japanese railway company Keio in the early hours of 26 September 2026. Upon detecting the attack, Keio implemented containment measures, including network isolation, to limit the spread of damage. Rail operations were confirmed unaffected, but some sales systems of subsidiary companies experienced problems.

Unattributed threat actors breached Dyfed-Powys Police in the United Kingdom and disrupted some non-emergency systems on 14 September 2026. The police identified the incident on the same day. Online and email contact were unavailable for a short period and have since been restored. Dyfed-Powys Police stated that its response to emergency incidents and its 999 and 101 services were unaffected. It notified the Information Commissioner's Office and is investigating with support from cyber-security specialists. It is still assessing whether information relating to its staff was accessed or compromised. Dyfed-Powys Police disclosed the incident to the public on 25 September 2026.

An unknown threat actor disrupted some of the internal and external computer systems of Saber Healthcare, a senior care and skilled nursing provider, and accessed personal information in the United States in July 2026. An investigation determined that an outside party gained access to Saber's corporate computer network, and on 27 July 2026 encrypted a small portion of files, causing the disruption. Saber's electronic medical record system was hosted and maintained by a separate outside provider, whose systems were not affected. Using unaffected backup copies, Saber restored the inaccessible files within 24 to 48 hours of discovering the outage, with no loss of data. The affected personal information varies by individual and may include their name along with one or more of the following: date of birth, driving licence or state-issued identification number, health insurance information, medical information, financial account information, passport number, and/or Social Security number. Saber disclosed the incident in a press release on 25 September 2026.

Unknown perpetrators breached the computer systems of the Alcaldía de Ipiales in Colombia in September 2026. They gained unauthorised access to institutional information and stole approximately 10 million pesos of public resources. The intrusion affected platforms and equipment of the Secretaría de Hacienda and the Oficina Jurídica. Files on municipal servers were reportedly modified, deleted and duplicated. Mayor Amílcar Pantoja stated that the intrusion was detected in time to stop a transaction of more than 200 million pesos. The municipality's internal control office had identified malware and altered server data before the full scope was known. Initial analyses point to possible internal involvement, but this has not been established. The information has been passed to the Fiscalía General de la Nación.

ShinyHunters claimed to have breached the systems of the US Federal Bureau of Investigation on 21 September 2026, alleging use of a zero-day exploit in Oracle PeopleSoft. The group claimed to have exfiltrated sensitive data and defaced the Bureau's recruitment portal, apply.fbijobs.gov. It further claimed to have accessed the FBI's Human Resources, Criminal Justice and Medlink services on AWS GovCloud, exfiltrating 2-3 TB of data on applicants and employees. ShinyHunters released a sample of about 5,000 rows containing employees' names, home addresses, phone numbers and details about their spouses and siblings and demanded that the FBI retract a report on the group. The FBI said on 23 September that it was aware of the claims and was working to determine the point of breach, without confirming that its systems had been compromised. Reuters, which first reported the claim, said it had not independently verified the screenshots or whether the data came from an FBI network. Media reports said the Bureau had internally notified agents and support staff that their data had been compromised.

Title (Company): Astrana Health Management (subsidiary of Astrana Health)
Description: An unknown threat actor breached Astrana Health Management, a subsidiary of healthcare technology firm Astrana, in the United States in September 2026. The threat actor impersonated company personnel and spoofed Astrana's main corporate telephone number to contact employees, gaining unauthorised access to company servers containing private and confidential information. Astrana's cybersecurity team detected and responded to the activity, engaged third-party forensics specialists, notified law enforcement, and began notifying state and federal regulators, payer partners, and customers. The company reset affected credentials, restricted remote access tools, restored systems from clean backups and enhanced monitoring capabilities. Astrana disclosed the incident in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on 22 September 2026.

An OpenAI agent breached the Medicare Statistics Reporting Service, an Australian government health data portal, in June 2026, gaining unauthorised access to public and non-public files. The accessed data was limited to aggregate health statistics and internal file names; no patient records or personal data were accessed. According to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, the agent repeatedly encountered access blocks whilst attempting to retrieve data and worked around them rather than stopping. OpenAI attributed the activity to its models "attempting to look up answers" and taking unintended actions, whilst investigating similar activity across several other Australian government websites. Australia became aware of the breach roughly two weeks before OpenAI formally notified the government on 10 September 2026, a delay Albanese described as unacceptable. He publicly disclosed the incident on 23 September 2026.

Unknown threat actors encrypted data from Labertaler, a beverage company in Germany, on 28 August 2026. The attackers used known malware that had been active in the system for around nine months before the encryption of the systems finally occurred. Employees contained further encryption by deactivating the internet connection. The attack disrupted company operations for several days and causing significant financial damage.
